- **The test helper was a landmine, and defusing it is part of the fix.** `ApplicationDetail.artefactLoading.test.tsx` read this line through a `getByText(/steps completed/)` helper, which *throws* on no match. Suppressing the line would have turned any all-unknown render into a thrown `TestingLibraryElementError` — reported as a broken test, from whichever assertion happened to call it first, rather than as the behaviour under test. It is `queryByText`-based now and returns `string | null`. Confirmed load-bearing: reverting the helper alone turns the new cold-load case red with exactly that throw.
- **The state was uncovered because the two existing phases are mutually exclusive by construction.** Each leaves the other's queries settled — that is what makes them each other's negative control — so between them they sample one unknown row and three, never four. A fourth phase (`all-in-flight`) is *added* rather than an existing one widened, for the same reason WIC-2141 added a third: both controls stay load-bearing. Covered at both layers — the page phase proves the cold load reaches this state, four `WorkflowChecklist` cases pin what the component does in it.
- **Mutation control, run and recorded — five reversions, each restored.** Ungating the count line: **2 red**, one per layer. Restoring unconditional "more": **2 red**. Dropping "more" *unconditionally*: **4 red** — the discriminating direction, since a fix that just deleted the word passes the new assertions and breaks the singular "Checking 1 more step…" that WIC-2141 pins. Suppressing the count line unconditionally: **10 red**, including both of WIC-1630's AC-3 assertions, which are unchanged by this card and still bite. Reverting the test helper: **1 red**, by throw. Each mutant kills a different subset.

### Fixed — the Job Fit Analysis checklist row stated a false negative while its query was in flight (2026-09-06)

WIC-1630 gave three of `WorkflowChecklist`'s four steps an `'unknown' | 'absent' | 'present'` state so they stop asserting "you have none" while their queries are unsettled. It excluded the fourth, Job Fit Analysis, behind a comment reading "backed by no query at all (WIC-1652), so it is never unknown and must stay identical while the other three load". That premise was true when written and false by the time it shipped — WIC-1652 had since given the row a query. The comment, not the code, is what went wrong (WIC-2141).

- **The literal `unknown: false` asserted something the data no longer supported.** `ApplicationDetail` calls `useJobFitAnalyses(...)` and read `data` alone, so `fitAnalyses?.analyses?.[0]` was `undefined` both in flight and when the query came back empty. The page counted the step against the denominator, rendered it unticked, marked it "Recommended" whenever a job description existed, and linked to `/job-fit-analysis?appId=` — inviting the user to run an analysis they may already have had. Measured with the other three queries held settled so only the fit query varied, the in-flight row was **byte-identical** to the settled-and-genuinely-empty row.
- **The existing suite could not see it, in exactly the way the original defect's suite could not.** `ApplicationDetail.artefactLoading.test.tsx` pinned the fit query `isLoading: false` in *both* of its phases on purpose, as the negative control proving the fix was per-query rather than a page-wide loading flag. No value of that mock could exercise the in-flight fit row. The control is load-bearing for the other three rows, so it is kept intact and a **third phase** is added — the fit query unsettled and the other three settled — rather than the flag being flipped.
- **The two phases are now each other's control.** With only the fit query in flight, rows 1-3 must render identically to settled-absent; with only rows 1-3 in flight, the fit row must. A fix keying off a page-wide flag fails both directions, which neither control could pin alone.
- **The tri-state replaced the `hasFitAnalysis` boolean rather than pairing with it.** A `hasX` boolean beside an `xUnknown` flag makes "present *and* unknown" representable and asks every consumer of one to remember the other — the reasoning already recorded on `ArtefactStatus`, applied to the row that had been its exception. `ApplicationDetail` was the only caller passing it. The default stays `'absent'`, so a caller wiring nothing keeps the settled row rather than one that loads forever.
- **WIC-2058's cells were migrated onto the new prop with every assertion unchanged.** That suite pins the create/read/inert link, including the unscored analysis that ticks with no badge — the migration is exactly where that cover could have been dropped, so the link shape is re-asserted against the tri-state rather than assumed to survive. Nothing about which analyses match or how `fitScore` renders changed; the badge still tests `!= null` and not truthiness.
- **Mutation control, run and recorded.** Three separate reversions were each confirmed to turn the new cases red and were then restored: dropping the `isLoading` read at the call site (5 cases), restoring the hardcoded `unknown: false` (3), and ungating the link and "Recommended" from `settled(...)` (4). Each mutant kills a different subset, so no single assertion is carrying the file.

### Fixed — Corrected the prod canary's cadence claims: it is scheduled every 15 min but GitHub *delivers ~5%* of those ticks (2026-09-05)

The `.github/workflows/supabase-keepalive.yml` canary was documented — in its own comments and in the incident issues it files (#414) — as running "every 15 minutes." Measured over its complete 194.5h history it delivered **39 of ~778 expected `*/15` ticks = 5.0%**, median gap **191 min**, with a **67h** window that had no canary at all. Root cause is inherent GitHub Actions throttling of high-frequency `schedule` events: every delivered run succeeded and none were cancelled, so the loss is GitHub never *creating* the run — not the workflow's `concurrency` group and not any `[skip ci]`/`[skip deploy]` marker (those affect push/PR triggers only, never `schedule`) (WIC-2125).

- The cron is offset off the top of the hour (`*/15` → `7,22,37,52`) as a partial mitigation, and every "every 15 minutes" claim in the workflow header, the cron comment, and the #414 incident-issue body template is corrected to state the measured best-effort cadence. Absence of the alert no longer implies prod is healthy.
- The durable fix — a Cloudflare Worker Cron Trigger, immune to Actions throttling — is tracked as a follow-up and is human-gated on a credential no agent holds.

### Fixed — 19 e2e specs that could never run are running again: `personal-info` dark since 2026-05-11, job-fit TC-4 since 2026-04-25 (2026-09-05)

`packages/web/e2e/personal-info.spec.ts` sat behind five `test.describe.skip(...)` blocks for **four months** — 18 specs covering the onboarding personal-info step and all three Settings-page states including **save failure** — behind a commit message promising an "infrastructure fix" that no card tracked. `job-fit-analysis.spec.ts` TC-4 sat behind a bare `test.skip(...)` labelled `FIXME: Test is flaky in CI` since 2026-04-25. Neither was visible to any signal the pipeline had: a skipped spec is not a failing spec, the files still read as covered in any filename-level audit, and the suite's spec **count went up, not down**. Measured on `origin/main` `18d8a183`: 176 specs, 48 skip-annotated, **19 of them carrying no reason string**. After this change: 177 specs, 29 skip-annotated, **0 unconditional**. Both dispositions were "re-enable"; nothing was deleted.

- **The personal-info cause was one glob, not an infrastructure problem.** `setupDashboardMocks` registered `page.route('**\/api/dashboard*', …)`. Playwright's `*` does not cross `/`, but it matches the rest of a filename — so that glob also intercepted the Vite dev server's request for `/src/services/api/**dashboardService.ts**` and answered the JavaScript module with `application/json`. The `services/api` barrel then failed to import and **the whole SPA rendered a blank page**, with no error surfaced to the test. Every block in the file calls that helper, which is why all 17 specs failed identically and why it read as "React components don't render content despite proper mock setup". `setupFallbackApiMocks`'s `**\/api/**` was the same trap, wider — it intercepted six source modules. Both are now URL-**pathname** predicates, which cannot reach `/src/...` at all. One fix, 14 specs recovered.
- **A second, independent cause:** `should-show` was unmocked. `OnboardingContext.loadOnboarding` awaits `Promise.all([getStatus(), shouldShow()])` (WIC-1359), so the unmocked half rejected the pair and the catch set `showOnboarding` to false — the modal the onboarding specs assert on never mounted. Now mocked, derived from the status fixture rather than pinned twice.
- **TC-4 was never flaky.** It failed **12 times out of 12**, deterministically, on a Playwright **strict mode violation**: `JobFitAnalysis.tsx` renders `results.summary` both in the summary block and again as the empty-catalog panel's body copy, and the fixture's `summary` *is* that sentence, so the unscoped `getByText` matched two elements. Assertions are now scoped to the panel, which also pins the CTA's real role — it is a `<button>`, and the old `link`-or-text assertion passed on the text arm without ever checking.
- **Three validation assertions were rewritten to assert reachable behaviour.** The URL/email inputs are `type="url"` / `type="email"` on a form with no `noValidate`, so the browser's own constraint validation fails the field and **the submit event never fires** — React Hook Form is never invoked and the Zod strings those tests waited for (`Must be a valid URL`) can never render. Verified directly: with `not-a-url` in a `type="url"` input the form's `submit` handler runs 0 times. They now assert the field is reported invalid *and that no `PATCH` is issued*, which holds whichever layer does the rejecting.
- **New CI gate, `scripts/e2e-skip-floor-check.py`**, wired into `lint-and-test`. It fails the build on any skip annotation with **no reason string** — the one shape a gated `test.skip(cond, 'why')` cannot produce, and therefore the signature of a hard-coded skip. It deliberately does **not** pin a skip *count*: the credential-gated band is expected to drain to zero when WIC-2122's `E2E_TEST_USER*` secrets land, and a pinned count would fight that. Graded against the pre-fix `origin/main` report it exits **1 and names all 19**; against this branch it exits 0. `--list` launches no browser, so the check needs neither browser binaries nor credentials, and it lives in `lint-and-test` rather than `e2e-tests` because that job runs even on a `[skip deploy]` push.

⚠️ The source card's arithmetic did not close and is corrected here: it put the credential-gated band at **24** and the unconditional set at 19, which sums to 43 rather than the 48 it also reported. Measured both ways at `18d8a183`, the split is **29 gated + 19 unconditional = 48**. The "24" figure should not be used as an acceptance threshold; `0 unconditional` is the durable one.

⚠️ Un-skipping surfaced a live defect that is **not fixed here** (WIC-2126): `packages/web` resolves `zod@4.3.6` — nested, and invalid against its own declared `^3.23.8` — against `@hookform/resolvers@3.10.0`, which only understands zod 3's `ZodError`. The resolver rethrows instead of mapping, so `formState.errors` stays empty and **every client-side validation message in `PersonalInfoForm` and `ApplicationForm` is dead**; an invalid submit throws an uncaught `ZodError` and the form silently does nothing. `npm ls zod` exits non-zero with `ELSPROBLEMS` on a clean `npm ci` today. Native constraint validation masks it for exactly the URL/email fields, which is why it went unnoticed. One spec here documents the broken behaviour explicitly and names the card.


### Documentation — Prod's DB fault is an accept-then-close spin loop, not a refused connection; three docs quoted a stale `db` signature (2026-09-06)

Documentation only. No code, no tests, no runtime change — and **no prod deploy is required or requested by this entry**.

Two things were settled about the ~10-day WIC-2092 data-plane outage, and three sites were carrying a `db` string that production stopped emitting two days ago.

- **The fault is *accept-then-close*, not *refused / blocked / DNS-failed*.** postgres-js `error(err)` → `errored(err)` nulls `initial` (`connection.js:381-393`), and the Cloudflare socket polyfill turns a rejected `tcp.raw.closed` into exactly that `emit('error', e)` (`cf/polyfills.js:117-119,152-158,214`). Any real socket error would therefore end the initial dial loop after **one** dial and surface its own message. `describeDbFailure` prefixes `connect deadline exceeded:` only when our own watchdog set `ctx.dbUnreachable`. So prod reporting the deadline rather than an error string **proves no socket `error` event arrived inside 1500ms** — a free narrowing out of a string we already ship, and it rules out a whole upstream goose chase. (Caveat: `error()` returns early without calling `errored()` when `options.host[retries + 1]` exists. `DATABASE_URL` is single-host, so it falls through — re-check if it ever gains a host list.)
- **The spin loop is CONFIRMED, and the argument that it was not is retracted.** WIC-2169 §3 reasoned that prod returning a clean deadline trip rather than `Too many subrequests by single Worker invocation` leaned against a fast spin — and therefore that raising `DB_CONNECT_DEADLINE_MS` might connect. Backwards: prod emitted `Too many subrequests` for days (2026-08-26/27/30/31, 09-01) and stopped only because WIC-2043's deadline landed 2026-09-04 (#364) and cuts the loop off before the budget runs out. Under the competing "one slow dial" shape an invocation spends exactly **one** subrequest and can never exhaust the 1000-budget; prod exhausted it repeatedly. WIC-2170 carries the retraction.
- **⭐ A symptom that vanished because you installed a mitigation is not a negative result.** Reasoning from its absence measures the mitigation, not the fault. `git log` the mitigation before treating a missing symptom as evidence — WIC-2043 was cited three paragraphs above the inference it invalidated.
- **⛔ Do not raise `DB_CONNECT_DEADLINE_MS`, and the arithmetic is why.** ADR-007 records budget exhaustion at a 4.04s response, i.e. ≥1000 dials in ≤4.04s ⇒ **≥250 dials/s on prod's own path** (a lower bound; the response also covers routing and serialisation). The 878 dials/s in `connect-bound.ts` was synthetic and local — this is the same quantity measured against prod. At ≥250/s the current 1500ms deadline already spends **≥375 of the 1000** subrequests per DB-dialling invocation, and the budget is exhausted again at a deadline of ≈**4.0s**. A raise toward 4s re-arms the WIC-2043 failure on *every* endpoint, and under a confirmed spin loop no finite deadline connects anyway. The experiment's informative range is empty and its unsafe range is reachable.
- **Three stale-signature sites corrected.** Prod's `db` string has changed three times without the fault changing — `Too many subrequests …` → `write CONNECTION_DESTROYED …:6543` (WIC-2043 teardown collateral) → `connect deadline exceeded: no connection within 1500ms (…:6543)` (WIC-2163, #428, current). `deploy-drift.mjs` quoted the middle one as "CONNECTION_DESTROYED against the us-west-2 pooler", which reads as a far-end fault WIC-2163 disproved; `supabase-keepalive.yml` quoted it as "the live outage signature"; ADR-007's `## Open decision` block quoted the first. All three now carry the current string plus the full drift history. **No check was keyed on the string** — the canary asserts `.status == "ok"`, which is invariant under all three — so nothing was silently broken, and each site now says explicitly that the string is an example and must not become a matcher.
- **Net effect on the P1: the Hyperdrive ask is strengthened, not competed with.** Something accepts the Worker's TCP connect and closes it with no error event, while CI reaches the same pooler in ~29ms with a green `SELECT 1`. That difference is Worker egress, and Hyperdrive is the supported Worker→Postgres path. The human gate on a Cloudflare credential carrying Hyperdrive scope (WIC-2097) stands; no agent action closes it.

Verified live 2026-09-06T08:2xZ and T08:3xZ against both `app.careerpin.app` and `jobtrail.al-23f.workers.dev`: `503`, ~1.85s, byte-identical bodies.


### Fixed — `/api/health` reported our own connect-deadline trip as postgres-js `CONNECTION_DESTROYED`, pointing every reader at Supabase (2026-09-06)

Production's `/api/health` rendered a DB failure as `write CONNECTION_DESTROYED aws-1-us-west-2.pooler.supabase.com:6543`, which reads as "the pooler dropped us". It is ours: when the WIC-2043 connect deadline expires (`DEFAULT_CONNECT_DEADLINE_MS = 1500`), `connect-bound.ts` calls `sql.end({ timeout: 0 })`, and postgres-js `terminate()` (`connection.js:425`) rejects the in-flight query with that string. The true meaning is "the Worker did not finish TCP + TLS + the Postgres startup handshake inside our own 1500ms deadline" — a statement about our egress that carries no information about the far end, aimed at the one place the fault is not (WIC-2163, during the WIC-2092 outage).

`describeDbFailure` now reports the cause. The circuit already knew — `tripDbCircuit` sets `ctx.dbUnreachable` **synchronously** before `sql.end()`, so it is always populated by the time the destroyed query rejects, and the watchdog is its only caller — but that reason never reached the health payload. A trip now surfaces `connect deadline exceeded: no connection within 1500ms (<host>:<port>)`; a genuine server-side disconnect leaves `ctx.dbUnreachable` unset and keeps its own message, so the two never collapse into one string.

⚠️ The endpoint is read from postgres-js's `address`/`port` fields, which are **arrays** (`['host']`, `[6543]`), not strings — the driver parses the connection string that way for multi-host failover and `Errors.connection` passes them through, then renders `host + ':' + port`, where a single-element array stringifies without brackets and hides the array. A `typeof x === 'string'` guard rejects every real postgres-js error and silently drops the host:port, so the message loses the half that makes it actionable while every hand-built test fixture still passes.

HTTP status, `status` and `hyperdrive` are unchanged. The WIC-2123 canary asserts `http == 200 && status == "ok"` and captures `db` for display only, so its predicate is untouched by this change.

### Added — The 15-min prod canary now asserts the data plane, not just auth: `/api/health` must be 200 with `status:ok` (2026-09-05)

`.github/workflows/supabase-keepalive.yml`'s 15-min canary job gains a second, independent probe alongside the auth check: it GETs `${PROD_BASE_URL}/api/health` and fails the run unless HTTP `200` with body `status:ok`. Production's data plane returned `503` for ~10 days (WIC-2092) while every monitor stayed green — the auth canary proves only that Supabase Auth REST is up (it never dials Postgres), `GET /api/*` returns `401` before Postgres is reached, and the keep-alive `SELECT 1` runs only on the 3-day schedule. `/api/health` became a real liveness check under WIC-1296 but nothing polled it, so the outage was invisible to CI (WIC-2123).

- Both probes run every fire via `if: always()`, so a data-plane failure never masks an auth-plane failure or vice versa; each records an independent verdict and the run goes red if either regresses.
- The failure message names the observed `hyperdrive` and `db` fields verbatim, so the incident issue is self-diagnosing (e.g. `hyperdrive=false`, `db="write CONNECTION_DESTROYED ..."`).
- Failure reuses the existing deduped incident reporter — one standing issue with comments across a multi-day outage, never one issue per 15 minutes.
- This makes the outage *visible* only; fixing it (production Hyperdrive provisioning) is human-gated under WIC-2092 and out of scope here, so the alarm is expected to stay red until that lands.

### Added — A read-only probe for whether the live `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` can replace the revoked `CLOUDFLARE_CAREERPIN_API` in the marketing deploy (2026-09-05)

`.github/workflows/cf-marketing-token-drop-in-probe.yml` measures, against the live credential, each capability `deploy-marketing.yml` depends on: `GET /accounts`, zone reads and DNS record lists on `careerpin.app` + `careerpin.io`, and a Pages project read for `careerpin-marketing`. It is `workflow_dispatch`-only, `environment: production`, and issues **GETs exclusively** — no POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE and no `wrangler`, so unlike the WIC-2097 probe it has no write call at all.

`CLOUDFLARE_CAREERPIN_API` is **revoked** (403 / code 9109) and has exactly two consumers, of which `deploy-marketing.yml` is the only production one. That workflow fires on `push: main` touching `packages/marketing/**`, so the next marketing content change auto-fails at "Resolve Cloudflare account ID"; it last ran green 2026-06-12, which is why nothing has surfaced. The probe decides whether repointing removes the human rotation gate outright, or names the exact missing scopes so the ask pending on WIC-2100 becomes specific.

Two design points are load-bearing. It carries a **positive control** — the account-scoped `tokens/verify` — because `403/9109` (revoked) and `403/10000` (live-but-unscoped) are otherwise indistinguishable in a table of bare 403s, and conflating them is what confounded the board record on approval `d61d200b` clause (i). And because a GET-only probe proves *Read* but never *Write*, the verdict rests on a **token self-policy read** that enumerates permission groups by name; without it `DROP_IN=yes` would be a success condition the probe could never return, which reads as a clean negative. Scope inference is otherwise one-directional and stated as such: Cloudflare's write permission groups grant read, so a denied read is decisive against write, while a successful read is not evidence for it (WIC-2118).

### CI — the `e2e-tests` job now fails loud instead of going green while its multi-user isolation specs silently skip (2026-09-06)

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`'s `e2e-tests` job gains an `Assert isolation-test credentials are present` preflight that fails the job when any of the six values the data-isolation specs need is empty: the `SUPABASE_URL` / `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` vars and the four `E2E_TEST_USER*` secrets. The multi-user isolation specs (`packages/web/e2e/multi-user-isolation.spec.ts`) self-skip on an empty `TEST_USER_EMAIL`, and none of the six exists at any level today (the secrets are unset; the Supabase vars live on the `dev`/`production` environments and this job declares no `environment:`). So the job passed **green while skipping the isolation coverage `ADR-005` / `WIC-201` claim for it** — run `33986788859` reported **48 skipped / 128 passed**, and that green check was being read as RLS-isolation coverage that never ran. With the preflight it is now impossible for the job to report green on that silent skip: green means the specs actually ran. This is `WIC-2122` route 2 (pure engineering, no credentials). **Consequence:** because `deploy-production` needs `e2e-tests`, the push-triggered production deploy stops until the credentials land — that is `WIC-2122` route 1 (provision the four `E2E_TEST_USER*` secrets and `SUPABASE_URL` / `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` on the `dev` environment and add `environment: dev` to the job), which needs a human to mint live test-user credentials and stays open on `WIC-2122`. The specs were not deleted or weakened.

### CI — split the isolation-coverage preflight into its own job so it stops blocking deploys and every PR (2026-09-06)

`WIC-2131`'s credential preflight (previous entry) sat inside `e2e-tests`, **before** `- name: Run E2E tests`, so `exit 1` aborted the job before `npx playwright test` ran at all. That did two things beyond the intended honest-red on isolation coverage: it dropped the **128 real, passing specs** from the deploy gate, and — because `deploy-production` needs `e2e-tests` — it made every push to `main` and **every open PR** permanently red, stranding four merged commits (`db3b93d4`, `9be22c1c`, `a488932a`, `afebcc76`) out of production (`WIC-2157`). This moves the `Assert isolation-test credentials are present` step verbatim — same names-only discipline, same `::error` copy — into a new standalone job, `e2e-isolation-coverage` (`needs: lint-and-test`). `e2e-tests` runs the suite again (~128 passed / 48 self-skipped); the new job stays **red for the documented reason** until `WIC-2122` route 1 lands. `deploy-production`'s `needs: [lint-and-test, e2e-tests]` is unchanged and the new job is deliberately **not** added to it, nor to the `skip-ci-sweep-required` ruleset — it is a visible-but-harmless red, never a deploy or merge blocker. Net: deploys resume on the next merge (the four stranded commits ship with it), PRs go green on the suite, the 128 specs gate prod again, and the missing-credential state stays loud and separately visible. The real fix remains `WIC-2122` route 1 (a human mints the six credentials). No specs deleted or weakened; no placeholder credentials invented.

### Decided — No automated detector for stacked-child auto-close: an hourly sweep would be slower than the humans already are (2026-09-05)

A stacked-child close detector was scoped for `.github/workflows/evil-merge-sweeper.yml` and **deliberately not built**. Root `CLAUDE.md`'s **Merging a PR** section gains the verdict so the question is not re-scoped a fourth time (WIC-2106, closing WIC-2095 / WIC-2089 item 2). No workflow, no code, no permission change.

- **The decisive number is latency, not precision.** Both known instances were recovered by hand in **2m02s** (#34, re-landed as #35) and **17m08s** (#126, reopened and retargeted). The sweeper's cron is `17 * * * *` — mean latency ~30 min, worst case 60 — so the detector would have fired *after* the recovery on both instances it exists to catch. Prevention (retarget children before merging the parent) already dominates detection, and was documented earlier today.
- **Precision was never the obstacle.** The correlation the card proposed does discriminate cleanly: child `closedAt` − parent `mergedAt` is **+2s** for #34 against `-11.21h`, `-30.30h`, `+41.45h`, `+73.10h` for the four other closed-unmerged non-`main`-base PRs. Four orders of magnitude of margin, and two of the four are negative — closed *before* the parent merged. A naive "branch still exists" check is what returns all five.
- **⚠️ The card's own population query undercounts by half, and the correction is recorded.** `closed-unmerged with a non-`main` base` finds #34 but **not** #126, because #126 was recovered and now reads `MERGED` with base `main`. Current-state queries are blind to recovered casualties; only `GET /issues/{n}/timeline` sees them. The premise "one true positive in the repository's entire history" was measured that way and is wrong — there are two.
- **The sweeper was the wrong host regardless.** It enumerates `state: 'open'` and publishes a per-head commit status the ruleset gates on, so a closed PR offers no data to reuse and no output channel. Its closing `core.setFailed` means *"a PR could not be evaluated"*; a permanently-red historical finding routed through it would corrupt that fail-closed signal.
- Re-measured at `origin/main` `9dabae34` over all **399** closed PRs (up from the 390 the card cites), with a positive control so a zero would read as a real zero. Documentation only — no code, no tests, no schema change.





### Documentation — One runbook for the two production data operations that have been parked waiting on a human (2026-09-05)

`docs/runbooks/prod-data-operations.md` collects the exact commands, safety properties and decision trees for **WIC-1464 AC-a** (`audit-foreign-star-text.mjs`) and **WIC-1929** (`migrate-project-storage-keys.mjs`). Both scripts have been merged and green on `main` for days; neither card is waiting on code. Both are waiting on the same scarce resource — a human holding production credentials — and each previously required its own investigation to act on. Documentation only: no code, no tests, no schema change.

- **The read-only half can be run immediately, by anyone with `DATABASE_URL`.** The WIC-1464 audit executes entirely inside a `BEGIN READ ONLY` transaction, so Postgres itself rejects a write. That is *enforced* read-only rather than *documented* read-only, which is what makes it safe to run while the AC-b disposition is still open — it needs no approval, and there is a real chance it returns zero and closes the card's remaining scope outright.
- **The exit code is the decision point for WIC-1929, and it is documented as such.** `0` = all artefacts attributable, safe to `--apply`; `2` = commingled slugs and/or occupied destinations, which is precisely the data-attribution judgement the card's pending ask is asking for; `1` = environment error. The script refuses to guess and exits non-zero rather than let a deploy read "partially migrated" as "done".
- **Two safety rails are called out because getting them wrong is expensive and silent.** `--samples N` on the audit prints the leaked STAR text itself and must never reach a ticket (it writes to stderr so a `> file.json` redirect cannot capture it by accident). And the audit's `indeterminate` verdict — one side's owner `NULL` or the 0017 placeholder — is **not** a leak; `NULL <> NULL` is not a mismatch, which is the exact case WIC-1464 predicted would be got wrong.
- **The migration touches no rows.** Its only statement is a `SELECT`; all mutation is against object storage, which bounds a bad run to stored objects rather than data. It is idempotent — a second run finds nothing and exits 0.
- Verified against `origin/main` `6ebf1a2b`: both scripts and both test suites present (predicate 20/20, migration 41/41 as re-validated 2026-09-04). Recorded separately: WIC-1464's *"Also flagged"* tail — `generateInterviewPrep`'s unscoped `applications` read — is **closed**; all three reads now carry `ownerScope(applications, userId)`. Do not re-file it.


### Documentation — `CREDENTIAL_REGISTRY.md` misstated `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`'s scopes: `Pages: Edit` was claimed but is absent, DNS was unclaimed but reads fine (2026-09-05)

The registry row claimed *Pages: Edit; Workers Scripts: Edit; Account: Read*. Measured against the live credential by run `33989995418` (`cf-marketing-token-drop-in-probe.yml`, read-only, 20:24:11Z), that was **inverted on both counts it spoke to** — the capability it named is absent, and one it did not name reads fine. Aliveness corroborated by run `33989113004`.

- **`Pages: Edit` is claimed but ABSENT.** The `careerpin-marketing` project read returns **403 / code `10000`** — an authorization error, not a `404`. Cloudflare's Pages *write* group grants read, so a **denied read is decisive against write**.
- **DNS is not claimed but reads fine** — record lists return **200 / 200** on both zones (5 and 4 records). That proves **`DNS: Read` only**. **`DNS: Edit` is recorded as unverified in either direction, not as present**: the token cannot read its own policy (**403 / `9109`** on the API-tokens endpoint), so permission groups could not be enumerated, and a GET-only probe can never establish write.
- The verdict rests on a **positive control** — account-scoped `tokens/verify` returned 200 `active` — so every 403 above is a scope gap rather than a dead credential, the distinction that confounded the `CLOUDFLARE_CAREERPIN_API` record.

The row appears to have been inferred from a green production deploy, and the note now says why that does not follow: **`deploy.yml` runs `wrangler deploy` against Workers, a different Cloudflare product from Pages.** The string `pages` does not appear in `deploy.yml` at all — `wrangler pages deploy` and `/pages/projects` appear only in `deploy-marketing.yml`, under the *other* token. So the 19:19:59Z green run (`33986788859`) is strong evidence for `Workers Scripts: Edit` and none whatsoever about Pages. The same falsified claim is corrected in `CI_CD.md` and `CLOUD_ENV_SECRETS.md`; ADR-005's table is left as the historical record of what was decided.

This also resolves the open question the `CLOUDFLARE_CAREERPIN_API` note left hanging: WIC-2118 asked whether this token could stand in for the revoked one, and the answer is **`DROP_IN=no`** — it clears accounts and DNS reads but is denied exactly the Pages capability `deploy-marketing.yml` exists to exercise. Documentation only; the remediation stays on WIC-2100 (WIC-2121).


### Documentation — The two "dangling" `CONTENT_STYLE.md` section references were never dangling; they point at their own documents (2026-09-05)

`JOBFIT_CAPS_DECISION_WIC1122.md:292` and `ROUTE_TITLE_CONVENTION.md:325` each name `CONTENT_STYLE.md` and then cite a bare `§1.3` / `§4`. WIC-2112 classified both as **Group E — dangling**, on the reading that the `§` pointed *into* `CONTENT_STYLE.md`, which has named headings and no numbered ones. That diagnosis was wrong. Both `§`s point at **their own** documents, where both targets exist (WIC-2117, delivering WIC-2115). Documentation only — no code, no tests, no UI copy.

- **The convention is measurable and both files hold it without exception.** Across their 31 and 71 `§` uses: a bare `§N` in prose means *this document*; a `§` attached to a filename (`COMPONENT_SPECS.md §10`, `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md § Enforcement`) means *that* file. `JOBFIT:287–288` uses both forms in a single bullet — `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md § Gap Severity Scale` alongside *"which cites §3 of this document"*. The two sites sit in `## Related` lists, so the bullet's subject is a filename while its trailing `§N` is internal; that placement is what makes them misread, and it misread the author of the original classification.
- **The targets are the ones the prose already implies.** `JOBFIT` §1.3 is `### 1.3 Consistency check`, whose closing line is *"This decision is that rule applied"* — exactly what the bullet compresses. `ROUTE_TITLE` §4 is `## 4. Why this does not wait on the casing standard`. **No `§` was repointed at `CONTENT_STYLE.md`**: the defect was ambiguity, so each reference now names its own document in the idiom that file already uses (`§1.3 of this document`, `§4 above`).
- **⚠️ `doc-reference-audit.py` was deliberately not extended to validate `§` anchors**, taking WIC-2115's stated escape hatch on a measurement. Of 378 numeric `§N` refs in `docs/design/`, adjacency — the only signal a parser has — classifies 335 as internal, and **51 of those do not resolve against their own file's headings**: a 15% false-positive rate on a script that gates `deploy.yml` and `docs-audit.yml`. Nearly all 51 are outbound refs whose referent is fixed by *discourse*, not adjacency — `COVER_LETTER_PANE_LABELLING.md` uses bare `§10` **eight times** meaning `COMPONENT_SPECS.md` §10, named once at its own `## 5.` heading, and its own headings stop at `## 6.`. The named form is no better: `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md:518` cites a **truncated** heading. A validator would fail 51 correct references to catch two ambiguous ones.
- Group E's entry in `CASING_MIGRATION_INVENTORY.md` is corrected in place rather than deleted, since the original wrong diagnosis is the reason the card existed. The 10 Group D citations, `CONTENT_STYLE.md`'s status and adoption sections, and the known `Back to dashboard` error are untouched — all await the WIC-1066 ruling. `doc-reference-audit.py` passes, 353/353.



### Decided — `runtime-paths.cjs` keeps its two-predicate allowlist: the shared predicate is tuned to the stricter consumer on purpose (2026-09-05)

`.github/scripts/runtime-paths.cjs` gains the **decision** on top of the rationale it already carried, so the next reader meets a settled question rather than a puzzle (WIC-2113, ruling on WIC-2101). `ALLOWED` is unchanged — comment-only, zero behaviour change.

- **The two consumers' errors are not symmetric in cost, and that is what decides it.** A wrong answer costs `deploy-drift.yml` a page with no remedy; it costs `skip-ci-guard.yml` a PR that adds a gitleaks allowlist entry — one suppressing a leaked secret — merging under a CI-skip marker with **zero check runs**. A nuisance page is recoverable; a suppressed secret scan is not. So `.gitleaks.toml`, `.gitleaks-baseline.json`, `.gitattributes`, `.github/secret-scan-allowlist.json` and `.github/scripts/**` all stay runtime-bearing, and the over-alerting on CI-only paths is a price knowingly paid.
- **Both alternatives were rejected in writing, not merely passed over.** Per-consumer allowlists model the asymmetry honestly but reintroduce the two-lists-that-drift hazard this module was extracted to kill; allowlisting for both consumers weakens secret-scan posture and would need a security sign-off that is not obtainable from an agent seat today (WIC-2018). The revisit trigger recorded in the file is **frequency data, not a date**.
- **⚠️ WIC-1271's "14 commits behind, zero runtime paths" acceptance figure does not reproduce, and the detector is not being tuned to it.** Re-measured this run at `origin/main` `bde665db`: the 2026-08-19 → 2026-08-25 window is **17 commits behind, 4 runtime-bearing, 7 undeployed runtime paths, ALARM** (T1 only — T2 needs 5). The count is never 14 under any framing: excluding the commit that closed the gap gives 16, not 14.
- **No allowlist change makes that window quiet**, measured as a counterfactual rather than asserted. `332856f9` (WIC-1069) changes four `packages/web/src/**` files and is genuinely runtime code. Allowlisting all of `.github/**`, `.gitattributes` and `.gitleaks*` still alarms (4 → 1 runtime-bearing); it goes quiet only if that allowlist is combined with excluding the closing commit — i.e. only under the exact policy change this ruling rejects. A detector that alarms on that window is behaving correctly.
- Guard clause confirmed rather than assumed: the predicate is untouched (`ALLOWED.length` 2, comment-only diff, identical classification on eight probe paths), PR #394's skip-ci-guard verdict harness rebuilt and re-run **8/8** (4 PASS, 4 BLOCK, shared module resolving), and `deploy-drift.mjs --selftest` **14/14**.



### Accessibility — the `jsx-a11y` ratchet is finished: `A11Y_BASELINE` is empty and `--max-warnings` is 0 (2026-09-05)

The last of the 47 findings baselined when `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` was adopted (WIC-1483) is retired. `A11Y_BASELINE` in `packages/web/src/test/jsxA11yBaseline.test.ts` and `BASELINED_RULES` in `packages/web/eslint.config.js` are both empty, and `lint` and `lint:fix` in `packages/web/package.json` both run at `--max-warnings 0` (WIC-2110, closing WIC-2085 and WIC-1589's AC-1/AC-2/AC-3).

- **This is an exemption, not a fix, and the distinction is the whole point.** `ApplicationCard`'s `<article tabIndex={0}>` keeps its tab stop and now carries an `eslint-disable-next-line jsx-a11y/no-noninteractive-tabindex` with its rationale at the line. Every spelling the rule would accept — a real `<button>` inside the `<h3>`, or `role="button"` on the article — trips axe's `nested-interactive` instead, because `SortableApplicationCard` wraps each card in a dnd-kit `div[role="button"][tabindex="0"]`. WIC-2077 shipped the button form, measured it, and reverted it; WIC-1942 measured the role form on `ResumeVariantCard` and removed it. Two ratchets pull against each other at that site and axe measures the more serious defect.
- **It is a net tightening, and that is why the exemption is the right exit.** `no-noninteractive-tabindex` (1 → 0) leaves `BASELINED_RULES` and returns to `error`, taking the enforcement surface 31/1/2 → **32/0/2**. A new `tabIndex` on a non-interactive element anywhere in the tree now fails `npm run lint` outright instead of being absorbed by the ceiling.
- **The promotion is forced, not chosen.** `jsxA11yBaseline.test.ts`'s *states its enforcement surface exactly* asserts the resolved `warn` set equals exactly the rules the baseline records, so a zero-finding rule cannot stay baselined — leaving the line in `eslint.config.js` reds the suite. The same guard binds in the other direction through the 32/0 severity counts.
- **⚠️ The directive sits on the `tabIndex` attribute, not on `<article>`.** This rule reports at the attribute; the `no-noninteractive-element-interactions` directive four lines above reports at the element. Measured both placements — an element-level directive does not suppress it, and the wrong placement looks right.
- Verified by running it rather than predicting it: `npm run lint` exits **0** at `--max-warnings 0` with no residual warnings, `jsxA11yBaseline.test.ts` is **5/5**, and `routeAxe.render.test.tsx` + `ApplicationCard.keyboardNav.test.tsx` are **20/20** — the axe suite being the check that killed both obvious fixes.
- **⭐ Reaching zero COST the ratchet a cross-check, and the suite now says so.** With one entry, narrowing the lint glob was caught twice — by the `toEqual` on the map and by the surface test, because a narrowed `{}` baseline disagreed with a non-empty `warn` set. An empty baseline agrees with *any* narrowing: `{} === {}`, `total` and `BASELINE_TOTAL` both 0, `warn` set empty on both sides. Measured by mutating the glob to `src/pages/**` — the suite fails on `expect(filesLinted).toBeGreaterThan(100)` **alone** (`expected 61 to be greater than 100`, 4 of 5 passing) where it previously failed two tests. That assertion is now the only thing separating "nothing is wrong" from "almost nothing was read"; the note in the file that called it doubly-covered is corrected rather than left to rot.
- **⛔ An empty baseline does not mean the tree has no accessibility debt.** It means no finding is unadjudicated. Restructuring the dnd-kit wrapper so the card can be a genuinely interactive element remains open, and needs an axe measurement in both directions.
- **⚠️ WIC-1589's AC-2 is met in substance but not in its literal wording**, and the wording is what is wrong: it reads *"`BASELINED_RULES` is empty, so all 34 `recommended` rules are at `error`."* The list is empty, but the surface is **32 at `error`, 0 at `warn`, 2 deliberately `off`** — `control-has-associated-label` (opt-in upstream, 3 findings) and `label-has-for` (deprecated upstream, superseded). Emptying the baseline was never going to promote those two. Reported rather than tuned to match.

### Fixed — `cd packages/infra/redirect-worker && wrangler deploy` no longer deploys the production `jobtrail` app (2026-09-05)

`packages/infra/redirect-worker/wrangler.toml` is renamed to `wrangler.jsonc`, and `SHADOWED_ALLOWLIST` in `scripts/wrangler-config-resolution-check.py` — which carried it as the one known shadowed config — is now empty (WIC-2109, closing WIC-2108). Filename precedence beats directory proximity in wrangler's resolution, so as a `.toml` this file lost its own directory to the repo-root `wrangler.jsonc`.

- **Measured as an A/B, not reasoned about.** `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run --env=""` run from `packages/infra/redirect-worker` under wrangler **4.129.0**, identical conditions on both sides. **Before:** `Total Upload: 8084.57 KiB`, bindings `env.R2_BUCKET (jobtrail-documents)`, `env.ASSETS`, `env.NODE_ENV ("production")`, `env.ANALYTICS_SINK ("posthog")`, `env.POSTHOG_HOST` — the production app, reproducing WIC-2108's measurement exactly. **After:** `Total Upload: 0.29 KiB`, `No bindings found.` — this Worker's own bindingless shape.
- **The resolved file is named by what wrangler tried to bundle, not by a `Processing …` line.** That warning only prints for a config outside the cwd, so post-fix it is correctly absent and cannot serve as the evidence. Run without the `node_modules` symlink, the pre-fix control fails on `Could not resolve "@aws-sdk/client-s3"` in `packages/api/src/services/storage.service.ts` — it was bundling the API Worker's `main`, from the redirect Worker's directory.
- **The ratchet was confirmed non-vacuous before it was satisfied.** With the file renamed and the allowlist entry still present, the check exits 1 on the `no longer exists` branch. The entry was removed only after that positive control fired; the guard forced the cleanup rather than tolerating a stale entry.
- **The rename arms a different footgun, so the file now documents it.** `deploy` from that directory previously misfired onto `jobtrail`; it will now correctly deploy `careerpin-redirects`, installing Worker routes on three hostnames that `.github/workflows/deploy-marketing.yml` assigns to the `careerpin-marketing` Pages project on every marketing deploy — CNAME upserts at `:112-114`, `add_domain` at `:178-180`, with the same `/* … 301` served by `packages/infra/redirect-pages/_redirects`. A header comment records the supersession and says not to deploy without checking the dashboard first. `docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md` carried the now-false instruction to deploy that Worker with an explicit `--config` and is corrected in the same commit.
- **Not measured, and deliberately not asserted in either direction:** whether the `careerpin-redirects` Worker exists in Cloudflare at all. No agent seat holds a Cloudflare credential. That is why the config was renamed rather than deleted — deleting it would convert a possible deployment into an undocumented one.


### Added — A read-only probe that answers the careerpin redirect-ownership question from CI, and a correction: the Pages redirect is not where the last entry said it was (2026-09-05)

`.github/workflows/careerpin-redirect-ownership-probe.yml` reads the Cloudflare control plane to answer whether the `careerpin-redirects` Worker exists and whether it holds routes on `www.careerpin.app`, `careerpin.io` and `www.careerpin.io` — the question WIC-2111 was filed to route to a human dashboard session (WIC-2111, following WIC-2109). `workflow_dispatch` only, every request a GET.

- **The "no agent seat holds a Cloudflare credential" premise is true of the agent seat and false of CI.** `CLOUDFLARE_CAREERPIN_API` is a repo-level secret that `deploy-marketing.yml` already spends against these exact zones, so the three dashboard steps reduce to three API reads. The probe follows `cf-token-capability-probe.yml`'s safety fence — the token reaches curl through a `0600` config file so it is absent from `ps` argv as well as the log, and no `set -x` runs while it is in scope. It is strictly stricter than that predecessor: it has no POST at all, so unlike the Hyperdrive probe it cannot create anything even in principle.
- **⚠️ The previous entry named the wrong file as the live Pages mechanism.** It cited `packages/infra/redirect-pages/_redirects`. That directory is deployed by **nothing** — the only `pages deploy` in the repository targets `packages/marketing` (`deploy-marketing.yml:136`). The redirect is performed by `packages/marketing/_worker.js`, a Pages advanced-mode worker that serves assets for the apex and 301s every other hostname, with `packages/marketing/_redirects` carrying the same three rules as a fallback. `packages/infra/redirect-pages/` is a second orphan sitting beside the Worker config, which the card scoping the cleanup did not account for.
- **No external probe can ever attribute the redirect, so do not spend a run trying.** `packages/marketing/_worker.js` and `packages/infra/redirect-worker/worker.js` build the identical expression — `https://careerpin.app${url.pathname}${url.search}` into `Response.redirect(…, 301)`. Measured live: all three hostnames 301 to the apex preserving path and query, and the apex serves the site (`200`). Both implementations predict exactly that, so the HTTP surface is evidence about behaviour and never about ownership. The Cloudflare control plane is the only discriminator, which is what the probe reads.
- **A dead credential and a missing scope fail identically, so the probe controls for it first** (the WIC-2097 lesson). It lists accounts before anything else and aborts rather than reporting a verdict if that fails; only after the control passes is a `403` on `workers/scripts` attributable to a missing `Workers Scripts:Read`. A non-200 there is reported as `UNDETERMINED` and never as "the Worker does not exist" — absence of the Worker is a claim the probe will only make from a `200`.
- Worker existence and route ownership are read as **separate** questions, because a Worker holding no routes is harmless while one holding routes on those hostnames genuinely contests the Pages custom domains. Nothing is deleted and no cleanup is performed here; the header comment in `packages/infra/redirect-worker/wrangler.jsonc` is corrected and now points at the probe instead of at a dashboard session.


### Added — A read-only probe that measures whether the CI Cloudflare token can provision Hyperdrive, so a 4-day-stalled board approval turns into a decision (2026-09-05)

Production's API has answered `503 {"status":"degraded","hyperdrive":false}` for logged-in users since 2026-08-26. The remedy is agreed (ADR-007 opt 1: give prod a Hyperdrive binding), and the blocker was never technical — board approval `d61d200b` had sat pending since 2026-09-01 on a question nobody had answered: either (i) confirm the CI `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` carries `Hyperdrive:Edit`, or (ii) create the config in the Cloudflare console. `.github/workflows/cf-token-capability-probe.yml` measures clause (i) (WIC-2097).

- **Clause (i) is a fact, not a judgement**, so it is measured rather than asked. The workflow is `workflow_dispatch`-only and prints one unambiguous verdict line — `HYPERDRIVE_EDIT=yes|no`, or `HYPERDRIVE_READ=no` when the token has no Hyperdrive scope at all.
- **It does not fix production and does not deploy.** No Hyperdrive config is created, `wrangler.jsonc` is untouched, there is no `wrangler deploy`. The prod deploy stays board-gated under `d61d200b`.
- **Edit scope is tested without creating anything**, by POSTing a deliberately-invalid `{}` body: if authorization clears, the request dies on schema validation instead. `403` means no Edit scope; `400` means the scope is present.
- **That trick rests on Cloudflare checking authz before schema, so the workflow tests that assumption rather than trusting it.** A control fires the same invalid POST at an account the token certainly cannot reach. An authz-shaped answer proves the ordering and validates the real test; a `400` proves schema runs first, and the verdict is reported as **undetermined** rather than inferred. Reporting a scope the probe cannot actually see would be worse than reporting nothing.
- **The no-side-effect claim is asserted, not assumed.** The config list is read before and after, and the job fails loudly if the id set moved or if the create POST ever returns `2xx`.
- **`environment: production` is load-bearing.** `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` exist only as `production` environment secrets, so without it both interpolate to empty and every call fails in a way that reads exactly like a dead token — the job refuses to report a verdict from empty credentials. The environment has `protection_rules: []`, so this adds no human gate.
- **Secret hygiene is enforced at the source.** The token reaches curl through a `0600` config file rather than `-H`, so it is absent from `ps` argv as well as the logs; only status codes, CF error codes, and config ids/names are printed. A config's `origin` block carries the database host and user, so response bodies are never echoed wholesale.
- **Verified against a mock Cloudflare before shipping**, driving the workflow's own extracted script through all six paths — Edit yes/no, no read scope, the schema-first undetermined case, and both failure fences (a `2xx` create and a changed config list, which exit non-zero). A run seeded with a token id, an account id and a database host confirmed none reach the log or the step summary.



### Fixed — A second Worker config redefined `preview` as production; it was inert, and the reason it was inert is not the one anyone would guess (2026-09-05)

`packages/api/wrangler.toml` declared `[env.preview] name = "jobtrail"` — the **production** Worker — while the root `wrangler.jsonc` maps `--env preview` to `jobtrail-preview`. `set-worker-secrets.yml` ran its `wrangler secret put` step under `working-directory: packages/api`, which reads as "this step uses the adjacent config" and would have meant a dev-scoped credential writing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to production. WIC-2107 was filed on that reading. **It is wrong**, and the deleted file was never resolved by anything (WIC-2107).

- **Wrangler resolves config by three independent find-up walks, one per _filename_** — `wrangler.json` → `wrangler.jsonc` → `wrangler.toml` (`findWranglerConfig`). Each walk runs to completion before the next begins, so **filename precedence is evaluated before directory proximity**: a `wrangler.jsonc` at any ancestor beats a `wrangler.toml` in the cwd itself. Proximity only breaks ties within one filename's pass.
- **Confirmed behaviourally, not by reading the source.** CI run `33972023673` — the WIC-2099 verification dispatch, `target_env: preview`, with the `working-directory` line still in place — logged `Processing ../../wrangler.jsonc configuration` and `Creating the secret for the Worker "jobtrail-preview"`. Reproduced locally on a second wrangler version (4.129.0 vs CI's 4.86.0) from both directories, which agree byte-for-byte on the resolved bindings. **No secret ever reached production, and the `dev` job-level environment chosen in WIC-2099 was correctly scoped.**
- **Inert is not safe when the gap is invisible.** Nothing was broken, but the repo carried two configs disagreeing about what `preview` means, and only wrangler's filename-precedence rule kept the dangerous one from winning. Converting the root config to `.toml`, or adding a `packages/api/wrangler.jsonc`, would have flipped it live with no diff to review. The dead file is deleted and `working-directory: packages/api` is gone, so the step now matches every other wrangler caller.
- **`scripts/wrangler-config-resolution-check.py` holds both closed**, wired into the required `Lint & Test` job. It asserts every wrangler call site under `.github/workflows` resolves the root config, and that no config in the tree is shadowed by an ancestor. It is keyed on the **hazard** — which config actually resolves — not on the proxy: restoring `working-directory: packages/api` alone leaves it green, because that genuinely is harmless, and it fires only when the resolution changes.
- **Graded by mutation, and two of the mutants found real bugs in the check itself** — a missing `re.MULTILINE` that blinded the `cd`-in-a-run-block detector, and a ratchet that iterated discovered configs rather than the allowlist, so renaming the allowlisted file made the stale entry permanent. A blinded scanner exits 2 rather than 0: an unparsed call site must never read as a clean one.
- **One shadowed config remains, allowlisted rather than fixed.** `packages/infra/redirect-worker/wrangler.toml` loses to the root config the same way. No CI path deploys it, but `cd packages/infra/redirect-worker && npx wrangler deploy` deploys the production `jobtrail` app instead of `careerpin-redirects`. Use an explicit `--config` there; tracked separately.


### Fixed — `set-worker-secrets.yml` offered two Worker targets nothing dispatches, one of which does not exist (2026-09-05)

`.github/workflows/set-worker-secrets.yml` let a dispatcher pick `preview`, `dev` or `staging` and passed the choice straight to `npx wrangler secret put --env`. Only `preview` is reachable work; the list is now `preview` alone (WIC-2105, carrying WIC-2102).

- **`dev` and `staging` have zero consumers.** Every `--env` occurrence under `.github` at `a9d7186` is the literal `preview` — three in `deploy.yml`, four in `remediate-worker-secret-leak.yml` — except the parameterized one in this workflow. The sweep was run with a positive control (`--env preview`), so the zero is a measured zero and not an anchored-regex artifact. Nothing schedules, dispatches or documents a `dev` or `staging` secret push.
- **The two load-bearing details from WIC-2099 are untouched, and a comment now says why.** The input is still named `target_env` rather than `environment`, so `grep 'environment:'` still means the job key and nothing else; the job-level `environment: dev` — which is what GitHub resolves `secrets.*` against, and without which all three credentials interpolate to empty — is unchanged. One is a *Cloudflare Workers* environment, the other a *GitHub* environment; narrowing the first must not touch the second.
- **The premise that `dev`/`staging` were "undeclared" was wrong, and the fix stands without it.** WIC-2102 reasoned from the root `wrangler.jsonc`, which declares only `env.preview`. But the secret-put step runs `working-directory: packages/api`, so wrangler resolves `packages/api/wrangler.toml` — which declares `[env.dev]`, `[env.preview]` **and** `[env.staging]`. The options were removed for having no consumer, which is the measurement that was actually taken, not for being undeclared. A comment at the input records this so the next reader does not re-derive the claim from the wrong file.
- **That same `working-directory` points this workflow at a different Worker than every other caller, which is filed separately as WIC-2107 and is not fixed here.** `packages/api/wrangler.toml` names its preview env `jobtrail`, while the root config names it `jobtrail-preview` and reserves `jobtrail` for production. `deploy.yml` and `remediate-worker-secret-leak.yml` declare no `working-directory`, so their `--env preview` resolves the root config. Narrowing the options list neither causes nor cures that; it is called out here so the two are not conflated.


### Added — A scheduled detector that notices when production stops running `main`, and a single shared definition of "runtime path" (2026-09-05)

WIC-1271 documented production sitting **14 commits behind `main` for six days**: 14 consecutive `[skip ci]` merges suppressed the `push` event, `deploy.yml` never fired, and nothing in the repo compared what prod serves against what `main` says it should serve. `.github/workflows/deploy-drift.yml` is that comparison (WIC-2098, carrying WIC-2088).

- **The deployed revision comes from Actions run history, because the app cannot answer.** `/api/health` returns `{status, hyperdrive, db}` and no version, no SHA, no build id — verified live rather than assumed, which is the trap this AC existed to catch. So the detector resolves the most recent `deploy.yml` run whose **`Deploy Production` job** concluded `success`. Job level, never run level: that job is `skipped` on every `pull_request` run, so "latest successful run" would happily return a SHA that never went near production. The stated limitation is in the script header — this proves what CI last pushed, so a `wrangler deploy` from a laptop would be invisible.
- **Proven to fire, not just to stay quiet.** A detector only ever verified in its green state is indistinguishable from a broken one. `node .github/scripts/deploy-drift.mjs --selftest` drives the same decision function the scheduled run uses through eight cases, four of which must alarm — including the WIC-1271 shape — and refuses to pass if none of them do. It was also run against **real repository history** with the deployed SHA set back four merges, where it correctly went red on one runtime-bearing commit while reporting three docs/CI-only commits quietly. `workflow_dispatch` carries a `deployed_sha_override` input so anyone can re-demonstrate that in CI without merging bad code.
- **Loud on runtime code, quiet on prose.** WIC-1271 point 3: a monitor that pages for a docs commit gets muted and is then worse than nothing. Two stated thresholds — undeployed runtime code older than 90 minutes, or 5+ runtime-bearing commits at any age — and a docs/workflow-only gap is reported and never alarmed. The tree diff, not the per-commit union, decides: a runtime change reverted before it shipped leaves nothing undeployed and raises nothing.
- **It reports `/api/health` and can never alarm on it.** A monitor saying "prod is 0 commits behind" while prod returns `503` is telling a true and useless thing (WIC-2088), so health is surfaced as context. But the 2026-09-05 outage is **not** drift — prod was running current code and failing on connectivity (WIC-1386 / WIC-2092 / WIC-2097) — so health is explicitly barred from turning the job red. A health-regression alarm is a different detector and belongs on its own card.
- **The runtime-path allowlist now has one definition instead of two.** WIC-1271 warned that a second copy would drift. It was inline in `skip-ci-guard.yml`; it now lives in `.github/scripts/runtime-paths.cjs` and both workflows `require()` it. The skip-CI guard gains an `actions/checkout` pinned to the **default branch** for that — trusted, already-merged code, never the PR head, with `persist-credentials: false` — and the guard's six verdicts were re-run against stubs before and after the change to confirm they did not move.
- **Read-only.** No deploys, no production writes, no repo writes, and no Paperclip auth (a run-scoped key is a 1h JWT and would be expired on nearly every scheduled firing — WIC-1252). `permissions:` is read-only on every scope; the alert channel is the scheduled job going red, which GitHub already emails on.


### Fixed — `set-worker-secrets.yml` ran unauthenticated because its job declared no `environment:`, and the input named `environment` made the omission read as present (2026-09-05)

`.github/workflows/set-worker-secrets.yml` referenced `secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from a job with no job-level `environment:` key. None of the three exists at repo level — measured 2026-09-05, the repo-level secret list holds only `CLOUDFLARE_CAREERPIN_API` — so all three interpolated to the empty string and `npx wrangler secret put` ran with no credentials (WIC-2099, found while measuring the token's Hyperdrive scope for WIC-2097).

- **The bug was camouflaged by a name collision, so the rename is the fix and not tidying.** The `workflow_dispatch` input was called `environment`, so `grep -n 'environment:'` hit line 6 and the absent job key read as present. The input is now `target_env` — it selects the Cloudflare Workers env for `wrangler --env` and has nothing to do with the GitHub key that resolves `secrets.*`. A `grep` hit now means the job key and nothing else.
- **The predicted failure mode did not reproduce, and is recorded here rather than tuned away.** The card expected wrangler to emit an auth error reading like a revoked or expired credential. Measured on the pre-fix workflow (run `33972091515`), wrangler 4.86.0 instead names the variable: *"In a non-interactive environment, it's necessary to set a `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` environment variable."* The revoked-token misread is real for WIC-2097's **curl** probe, where an empty token returns `403/10000`, but not for wrangler. What wrangler cannot say is *why* it is empty — it has no way to know the job is missing an `environment:` key — which is the part the guard supplies.
- **The job now declares `environment: dev`, not `production`.** The workflow only ever targets preview/dev/staging, and `deploy.yml`'s `deploy-preview` job — which performs this same push in its "Sync preview Worker secrets" step — already runs under `environment: dev`. `dev` carries all three secrets, so this is the least-privilege choice rather than the widest one. It adds no human gate: `dev` has `protection_rules: []`.
- **A guard names the cause wrangler cannot.** The three secrets are asserted non-empty in a preceding step whose failure message points at the job-level `environment:` key and flags the `target_env` decoy. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is covered for a second and stronger reason: wrangler only refuses on an empty *token*, so with credentials present but the key empty it would upload an empty secret and report `✨ Success!`, silently disabling the Worker's AI features. The guard was driven through all-empty (the exact pre-fix state), all-present, and one-missing before shipping.
- **Verified by dispatch in both directions, not by reading.** Fixed workflow against `preview` from this branch: guard passed and wrangler reported `✨ Success! Uploaded secret ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (run `33972023673`). Pre-fix workflow on `main`, same input: failed, with the step's own env block printing `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID:` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:` empty (run `33972091515`).



### Added — The changelog union-corruption detector now runs in CI, with synthetic fixtures because there is no live traffic to validate it against (2026-09-05)

`CHANGELOG.md` is `merge=union`, so the driver resolves by concatenating both sides at each differing hunk and reports success. Four corruptions ride through silently — a `### ` heading welded to the previous entry's last bullet, a bullet kept twice, a whole entry kept twice, and a bullet filed under an entry *neither parent filed it under*, where a correction reads as a claim about an unrelated change. All four have reached `main` or an open PR. A correct, threshold-free detector has sat in root `CLAUDE.md` as prose since WIC-1778 and nothing ran it: `grep -li changelog` over all 16 workflows returned zero. `scripts/changelog-union-check.py` and `.github/workflows/changelog-union-guard.yml` close that (WIC-2103, carrying WIC-2087 and WIC-1792).

- **Fixtures are the load-bearing evidence, not the sweep.** `gh pr list --state open` returns 0 today, so a run reporting 0/0 is byte-indistinguishable from a detector that does nothing. `selftest` builds real commits in a scratch repo and runs the same `git --attr-source=<ours> merge-tree` path the PR check uses, reproducing one weld, one duplicate bullet, one duplicated entry and one misfiled bullet, with **two** clean controls asserted as hard as the positives. It runs on every trigger, including the ones that will find no PRs.
- **It also reproduces two real corrupted PRs, against answers published before this code existed.** `replay` re-measures PR #129 at `97989e6` and PR #115 at `7890a2c` and matches `CLAUDE.md`'s hand measurements exactly — including the wrong-orientation row, where #129's single corruption presents as 2 misfiled instead of 1 duplicate. Not wired into CI: it depends on pull refs and a base branch this repo does not control, and a GC'd ref would turn the gate red for a reason unrelated to the detector.
- **It never consults `mergeable` or a merge ref.** GitHub computes mergeability with the default text driver, so a PR touching `[Unreleased]` flips to CONFLICTING routinely and benignly; the merge ref is frequently stale. The detector runs its own three-way simulation from `refs/pull/N/head` and the base tip. A tokenizing scan of the script's own executable source fails the build if that ever changes — the first, hand-rolled version of that scan silently stopped reading two thirds down the file, which a mutant exposed.
- **`pull_request_target`, not `pull_request`.** A CONFLICTING PR runs no `pull_request` workflows at all, because they build the merge ref and there isn't one — so the trigger would have gone quiet on exactly the population this check exists for. No PR head code is ever checked out or executed; the job reads blobs and nothing else, which is also why fork PRs need no special case.
- **Each of the four WIC-1792 constraints is pinned by a test.** `ours = PR head`; each PR against its own base; findings keyed on normalised text with the line number only as a locator; and `--attr-source` as a **global** option. That last one gets three assertions, because "the flag is accepted" and "the flag is doing anything" are different claims: global works, after the subcommand git exits 129, and a head that deleted the `merge=union` line is refused rather than silently unioned off the working tree.
- **Every check is `union − ours − theirs`, subtracted by content.** A weld already committed on the branch that the merge merely shifts down the file is not a finding. Graded by mutation: 11 mutants — reversed orientation, line-number subtraction, each check disabled, the flag dropped, a mergeability gate — 11 killed.



### Documentation — The casing standard's migration inventory is a script now, and "8 docs cite it" was three different rules wearing one label (2026-09-05)

`CONTENT_STYLE.md` proposes sentence case for every UI string and has never been ratified; the board decision is live on WIC-1066. The work needed under *every* outcome is the measurement, so WIC-2112 (carrying WIC-2096) lands `docs/design/ui-string-casing-inventory.py` and `docs/design/CASING_MIGRATION_INVENTORY.md` and changes **no UI copy and no document's status**. Migrating now, or hedging the citations now, would pre-empt the board and be reverted under a ratify ruling.

- **Report-only on purpose, and a sibling rather than a mode.** The script always exits 0 and is deliberately not wired into `deploy.yml` or `docs-audit.yml`: a check that fails the build enforces a rule, and this rule is not adopted. The card predicted `wireframe-casing-audit.py` was the right host and asked for that to be falsified cheaply — it is. That script reads markdown wireframes for positional ALL-CAPS labels and is the *enforcing* gate at `deploy.yml:81`; this one reads TSX for per-word casing. No shared scope, parser or verdict, and a mode flag that changes exit semantics does not belong inside a build gate.
- **Comment stripping is the whole game, and it arbitrates two disagreeing hand counts.** Raw `git grep -F` reads JSDoc prose as shipped strings — `types/jobFit.ts:181` alone discusses `Job fit analysis` in a comment. Re-measuring `CONTENT_STYLE.md`'s own five ❌/✅ pairs shows each prior count was right about something: WIC-2096 was right that the `Job fit analysis` ✅ hits are prose, and wrong that `Back to dashboard` has none.
- **`Back to dashboard` does appear in the codebase.** `CONTENT_STYLE.md`'s adoption-status section says it "does not appear ... at all"; it is at `pages/NotFound.copy.ts:23`, rendered at `NotFound.tsx:103`, and the whole 404 block is already sentence case. That section was fenced from edit by the card because the board is reading it, so the correction is recorded in the inventory doc instead. The doc's argument is unaffected — ❌ still outnumbers ✅ at all five pairs.
- **Three buckets, because a flat count would misdirect the migration.** `constants/title.ts` (20 strings) is the §5 route-title mirror table, enforced by `route-title-table-audit.py`; migrating it independently turns the build red, so it is `derived`. `e.g.` placeholders, hardcoded `<option>` records and `mock*` fixtures are user data standing in for records, so they are `sample`. Chrome measures **352 title / 429 sentence** at `0922bed9` — a wider population than WIC-2096's 77/13, and a smaller *fraction* than its framing implies.
- **"8 docs cite it as authority" was an overcount as work and an undercount as sites** — 8 files but 24 lines, of which only 10 treat the unadopted sentence-case rule as settled. Fourteen are correct as written: three cite the ALL-CAPS clause (in force, WIC-1209), six cite Exception 1's product-name ruling (in force, WIC-1102), three already hedge it as pending. Scoped as "fix all 8", about nine edits would have been wrong.
- **Two citations are broken regardless of the ruling.** `JOBFIT_CAPS_DECISION_WIC1122.md:292` cites a `§1.3` and `ROUTE_TITLE_CONVENTION.md:325` a `§4`; `CONTENT_STYLE.md`'s headings are named, not numbered, so neither resolves. `doc-reference-audit.py` validates cited filenames, not section anchors, which is why they survived.


### Fixed — A failed database connect re-dialled ~1000 times and spent the whole Worker subrequest budget (2026-09-04)

`getDb()`'s two Workers branches could not bound postgres-js's *initial* connect loop, and the comment above `WORKERS_CONNECTION_OPTIONS` claimed they capped an unreachable database "at one wasted subrequest". Production disproved that on every request: `/health` answered `503 {"db":"Too many subrequests by single Worker invocation"}` in 4-6s (WIC-2043, under WIC-1916).

- **The loop needs a close with no `error` event, which is why it never reproduced locally.** `postgres@3.4.9` `connection.js:441-458` takes `if (initial) return reconnect()` — `setTimeout(connect, 0)`, no backoff, no ceiling, query never rejected. An `error` event would reach `errored()`, null `initial` and stop it after one dial, which is exactly what a Node `ECONNREFUSED` does. The Cloudflare socket polyfill instead resolves `tcp.raw.closed` into a bare `close()`, so a host that accepts and closes re-dials until the budget is gone.
- **Neither existing option could ever have bounded it.** `max: 1` bounds the pool; the loop is inside one `Connection`'s socket lifecycle. `connect_timeout: 5` bounds a dial that *hangs*, and `closed()`/`connect()` cancel and re-arm that timer every iteration — it cannot fire while dials keep failing fast, which is the failing case. `backoff` is only read below the `return`.
- **Bounded from outside instead** (`db/connect-bound.ts`): a deadline armed with the pool, disarmed by the first `ParameterStatus` — the earliest available proof a TCP connect *and* startup handshake completed. On expiry the pool is ended with `{timeout: 0}`, which reaches `terminate()` and nulls `initial`, and a circuit opens on the request context so no later `getDb()` in the same invocation re-enters the loop. Rejecting the caller alone is not enough; the loop outlives the rejection unless the pool is actually torn down.
- **Measured, both directions.** Against a socket with the polyfill's clean-close shape, `main` issues **428 dials in 500ms with the query still unsettled**; with this change it issues **1** and rejects. `test/db-connect-bound.test.ts` (13 tests) drives the real `getDb()` on both Workers branches and asserts the dial count, that dialling stops after teardown, and that a second `getDb()` costs zero further dials.
- **`subrequest-budget.test.ts` is preserved, not replaced.** That suite tests the classifier and the 503 + `Retry-After: 5` shaping from #148, which are correct; it mocks the services, so no line of `getDb()`'s Workers path ran under it and it reported nothing about budget consumption. The new deadline error is classified alongside it, so it answers 503 once rather than retrying into the loop it just stopped.
- **Bound, not a guarantee of one dial.** postgres-js exposes no per-dial hook (`socket` is the only candidate and supplying it makes `connect()` skip the dial entirely, so the factory must return an already-connected socket — on Workers that means reimplementing the `cloudflare:sockets` shim and its TLS upgrade). The dial count is bounded by the deadline, tunable via `DB_CONNECT_DEADLINE_MS`, default 1500ms.
- **This does not create the production Hyperdrive binding**, which needs a Cloudflare token and stays with WIC-1916 / WIC-1386. No schema, migration or wire change.




### Fixed — Testing Library's async-util budget is now configured repo-wide, so a slow query stops reading as a missing element (2026-09-05)

`packages/web/src/test/setup.ts` never called `configure(...)`, so every `waitFor` and every `findBy*` in the suite ran against Testing Library's default **1000 ms** `asyncUtilTimeout`. Three files had grown per-site `{ timeout: 5_000 }` constants to work around it, each carrying a comment noting that the repo configured no default (WIC-1827 / PR #332). This sets the default those were standing in for and deletes all three (WIC-2086).

- **This is a different timer from the one WIC-1889 raised, and that is the whole point.** `testTimeout` bounds a whole test; `asyncUtilTimeout` bounds a single query, and they nest. A query can blow the 1000 ms async-util budget while sitting far inside the 15 s `testTimeout` PR #322 set — and when it does it fails as `TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find role="…"`, not as a timeout, so it does not even look like the WIC-1889 family. Raising `testTimeout` could never have covered it.
- **Measured across the whole suite, not inferred from one query.** Testing Library routes every async util through `getConfig().asyncWrapper`, so wrapping it — delegating to RTL's existing act-aware wrapper rather than replacing it — times the entire population. The instrumented runs set the budget to 60 s so the measurement was **not censored by the limit being measured**, and the three per-site overrides were removed first so those call sites were uncensored too. 91 files, 831 tests, ~730 async-util calls per run, 4 cores:

| condition | p50 | p99 | max | calls > 1000 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| idle, cold cache, default pool | 27.8 ms | 831 ms | **1289 ms** | 4 / 733 (0.5%) |
| cold cache, `--maxWorkers=8` (2x) | 51.8 ms | 1444 ms | **2928 ms** | 23 / 733 (3.1%) |
| cold cache, `--maxWorkers=8`, load avg ~17 | 104.0 ms | 2941 ms | **5578 ms** | 69 / 728 (9.5%) |

- **Individual waits breach 1000 ms even on an idle box** — 4 calls, worst 1289 ms, no contention and the default worker count. That is marginal rather than fatal, and the distinction is measured, not hedged: a full-suite run at the stock default, idle, is **831/831 green**, because those same calls land under 1000 ms on another run. Idle leaves no headroom; load is what converts it into a failure.
- **8 s is the measured worst case plus stated headroom:** 1.43x over the 5578 ms observed under contention heavier than CI's, and ~6x the idle worst case — the same ratio WIC-1889 chose for `testTimeout`. It is deliberately well below that 15 s ceiling. A query that genuinely never resolves must still fail as a Testing Library error carrying the rendered DOM, and it only does that if the async-util budget expires *before* the test budget; at 15 s or above every such failure degrades to a bare vitest timeout that says nothing about why.
- **Zero cost when green.** These utils poll and return as soon as the condition holds, so a larger ceiling only changes how long a genuine failure takes to report. The idle full-suite run at a 60 s budget took 145 s, in line with the runs at the stock default.
- **The three workarounds are removed, not kept.** Their worst measured site — `ProjectDetail.outline.test.tsx`'s EMPTY branch at **2855 ms** under load avg ~17 — is covered by the default with 2.8x to spare, so none of the six call sites needs a local override.
- **Paired negative control, full suite, identical load** (`--maxWorkers=8` + 8 CPU burners, cold cache): reverting the `configure(...)` line with the workarounds still gone produces **4** `TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find role="…"` failures; restored, **0**. Both runs also carry the same 2 vitest `testTimeout` failures — those are the WIC-1889 family, appear identically at a 60 s async-util budget, and are an artifact of that deliberately extreme load rather than of CI or of this setting. No test depends on the old default either: both instrumented full-suite runs were 831/831 green at a 60 s budget.
- **The hazard was never confined to the three files that had noticed it.** Two of those four failures — `CatalogBrowseView.keyboardNav.test.tsx` and `WizardContainer.discardGuard.test.tsx` — are in files that never carried a per-site workaround. The card predicted "a fourth author will hit it the same way"; two already had, and were being carried by luck.
