- **⛔ A narrow repro is not a valid control here.** Running just the three outline files under the same load is **6/6 green even at the stock default** — the cost is full-suite contention, not anything local to those files. Two full-suite runs are what separates the two states; a targeted re-run reports clean in both.
- Test configuration only. No production code, no schema, no wire change.


### Fixed — The skip-CI allowlist treated `docs/` as documentation, so a PR could edit a CI gate script and skip the gate it just changed (2026-09-05)

`skip-ci-guard.yml` and `skip-ci-sweeper.yml` each carried `(p) => p.startsWith('docs/')` as the first entry in their `ALLOWED` list — paths exempt from the "runtime code shipped under a skip marker" check. But `docs/` is not documentation-only: **four of the scripts that constitute the `lint-and-test` gate live under it**, and `deploy.yml` invokes all four with no `continue-on-error` (`:81`, `:106`, `:115`, `:125`). A PR editing `docs/design/wireframe-casing-audit.py` under `[skip ci]` was classified as having no runtime surface and could merge without the gate it modified ever running (WIC-2084, dispatched as WIC-2094).

- **The sweeper's copy is the load-bearing one; the guard's is advisory.** Enforcement on `main` is the ruleset `skip-ci-sweep-required` (id `21489705`, `enforcement: active`, `include: ["~ALL"]`), which requires **two** contexts — `skip-ci-sweep` and `evil-merge-sweep`. Only `skip-ci-sweeper.yml` publishes a commit status (`createCommitStatus`, `CONTEXT = 'skip-ci-sweep'`); `skip-ci-guard.yml` publishes none, emitting only its own `pull_request_target` check run (`Skip-CI vs runtime code`), which no ruleset requires. Both are fixed — they carry an explicit `KEEP IN SYNC` note — but only one of them was gating merges.
- **Classic branch protection is absent, and that reads like "no gate".** `GET /branches/main/protection/required_status_checks` returns **404**. The gate is entirely in the ruleset API. `skip-ci-sweeper.yml:30` asserted in prose that `skip-ci-sweep` was the *only* required context; that went stale when `evil-merge-sweep` was added (WIC-2055) and is corrected here.
- **Verified by executing the shipped predicates, not by re-typing them.** The control extracts the `ALLOWED` array out of each YAML and evaluates it, asserting the anchor matches exactly once first — a non-matching anchor would otherwise grade an unmutated tree green. Against unfixed `main` it fails **8/8** (four gate scripts × two files); against the fix it passes, with `docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` still ALLOWED via the surviving `endsWith('.md')` predicate. The two files' verdicts were **identical on all 9 probe paths** both before and after — previously assumed, now measured.
- **Blast radius is 14 files, and the collateral is fail-safe.** All 84 paths under `docs/` were classified both ways: 14 non-`.md` files change ALLOWED → RUNTIME (the 4 gate scripts plus 10 under `docs/analytics/`), and all 70 `.md` files are unaffected. The 10 collateral files now demand *more* CI, never less, so the cost is a slower merge and not a weakened gate.
- **The `.github/workflows/` predicate is deliberately kept** — a workflow-only change is the intentional no-deploy merge route (WIC-1686 declined to call it a defect). This entry is solely about `docs/`.
- CI configuration only. No production code, no schema, no wire change.


### Documentation — `gh pr merge --delete-branch` closes stacked children, and the repo setting does not stop it (2026-09-05)

Root `CLAUDE.md` gains a **Merging a PR** section. `--delete-branch` is a per-invocation override that deletes the head branch regardless of `delete_branch_on_merge` (currently `false`), and when that branch is another PR's base, GitHub **closes the child unmerged** rather than retargeting it (WIC-2089 item 1, under WIC-1625).

- **It has happened twice, and the board's citation is confirmed.** **#126** was closed at `2026-08-27T04:55:10Z`, **2 seconds** after parent **#124** merged at `04:55:08Z` — stranding the WIC-238 AC-10 returning-user bypass. A second, previously unrecorded instance: **#34** closed at `2026-08-04T18:43:06Z`, **2 seconds** after parent **#33** merged at `18:43:04Z`. #126 was recovered in place (reopened `05:12:18Z`, retargeted `05:12:20Z`); #34 never was, and its work re-landed as a fresh **PR #35**.
- **⚠️ `gh pr view` cannot see this — check the timeline.** #126 today reports `MERGED` from a `main` base and looks healthy, because the recovery retargeted it; only `GET /issues/126/timeline` shows the `closed` → `reopened` → `base_ref_changed` sequence. An earlier draft of this entry mis-read that post-recovery state as evidence the board's citation was wrong. It was not.
- **One board-side detail does not hold: #126 carried no reviews.** It was described as having "two `APPROVED` reviews"; `GET /pulls/126/reviews` returns empty. This generalises — **agents cannot approve PRs here** (every agent authenticates as `alwick`, the PR author, and GitHub 422s a self-approval), so no merge recipe should wait for one.
- The section gives the ordering that avoids it — retarget children first, then merge the parent with the flag omitted — plus a one-liner that lists any open PR naming a given branch as its base.
- Documentation only. No code, no tests, no schema change.


### Accessibility — Four keyboard-unreachable click targets, and one toggle that silently did nothing (2026-09-05)

`A11Y_BASELINE` drops **18 → 10** (WIC-2073, continuing WIC-2062's 26 → 18 under WIC-1589). Both `--max-warnings` ceilings in `packages/web/package.json` move with it. Four files reach zero findings and their baseline entries are deleted rather than zeroed, each with a comment recording the transition.

- **Three were the established shape** — a bare click handler on a non-interactive element, fixed the way `ResumeVariantCard` (WIC-1942) and the four `Reports*` pages (WIC-2062) fixed it: a real `<button>`, never a `role=` on the wrapper. `CatalogBrowseView.tsx`'s pending-diff card, `STARStoryBank.tsx`'s `<h3 onClick>` expand toggle (now carrying `aria-expanded`), and `StarEntryPicker.tsx`'s `StarEntryCard`.
- **`StarEntryPicker` needed no new control**, unlike the other two: the card already contained a real checkbox wired to the same `onToggle`, so the wrapper went inert and the checkbox became the control — named with `aria-label={entry.title}`, where it previously had no accessible name at all. Its `onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}` existed only to escape the wrapper handler and is deleted as dead code. Clicking the card *body* no longer toggles selection; that affordance was keyboard-unreachable, so it was never part of the accessible contract, but it is a real change for pointer users.
- **`FilterPanel.tsx`'s "Active Only" label was a live functional bug, not a keyboard gap** — and it was measured rather than assumed. `<button>` is a labelable element, so `htmlFor` already forwarded a label click to the switch, and the label's own `onClick` ran the handler a second time. On a stateful host one label click wrote `{activeOnly: true}` and then `{}`: the control did nothing at all. Deleting the `onClick` retires both findings and fixes the toggle, with no markup restructured.
- **`no-static-element-interactions` reached zero and is promoted off `BASELINED_RULES` back to `error`** — a genuine ratchet tightening, and a forced one: the suite asserts the `warn` set equals exactly the rules the baseline records, so a zero-finding rule cannot remain baselined. Enforcement surface goes 27/5/2 → **28/4/2**. Measured per-rule: `click-events-have-key-events` 5 → 1, `no-noninteractive-element-interactions` 5 → 3, `no-static-element-interactions` 2 → 0, `no-autofocus` 5 and `no-noninteractive-tabindex` 1 unchanged.
- **Keyboard reachability is pinned per component** by three new `*.keyboardNav.test.tsx` files following the `Reports*` precedent, plus three cases on `FilterPanel.test.tsx`. Each was mutation-checked against restoring the handler it replaced, and the counts are recorded as measured: the `StarEntryPicker` mutant reds 3 of its 4 tests, not the 1 first predicted. The ratchet itself got the same treatment — reintroducing a fixed handler reds `jsxA11yBaseline` and names the file.
- **Scope was held deliberately.** The remaining 10 are four different shapes and are *not* "leave forever": `no-autofocus` ×5 (a per-site design judgement), `ApplicationCard.tsx` ×2 (already has `onKeyDown`/`tabIndex`/`aria-label`, entangled with `draggable`), `ResumeUpload.tsx` ×2 (a drag-and-drop zone) and `WizardStep.tsx` ×1. `AXE_BASELINE` is a separate ratchet and is unchanged at 8.





### Accessibility — The five `no-autofocus` findings were never defects, and the rule is now `error` (2026-09-05)

`A11Y_BASELINE` drops **10 → 5** (WIC-2077, continuing WIC-2073's 18 → 10 under WIC-1589), and both `--max-warnings` ceilings in `packages/web/package.json` move with it. **No focus behaviour changed.** All five sites were read individually and all five are correct as written, so they are recorded as reviewed exceptions at the line rather than "fixed".

- **The rule was over-firing on the case it is known to over-fire on** — a user-initiated focus move into a newly-revealed input. Four of the five are inside a Radix `Dialog.Content`, where WCAG 2.4.3 *requires* focus to enter the dialog (`CommandPalette.tsx`'s Cmd+K search, `wizard/WizardContainer.tsx`'s first wizard field, `pages/ProjectsList.tsx`'s create-modal name field); the fifth pair are panels revealed by a button press (`SavedFilterShortcuts.tsx`'s "Save current filters as:", `pages/ResumeVariantDetail.tsx`'s inline title edit). Each now carries an `eslint-disable-next-line jsx-a11y/no-autofocus` stating *why that site* is exempt.
- **⛔ `ProjectsList.tsx:234` would have been actively harmful to "fix".** Its `autoFocus` is what suppresses Radix's `onOpenAutoFocus`, which is what makes `useDialogFocusRestore`'s `focusin` fallback capture the trigger — deleting it silently changes the focus-restore path pinned by WIC-1931, and the lint finding it retires says nothing about focus restore. The reasoning was already written down at `ProjectsList.tsx:52-54`; the disable comment now cites it.
- **This is a tightening, not an exemption.** `no-autofocus` reaches 0 findings, so it leaves `BASELINED_RULES` and returns to `error` — forced, not chosen, because the suite asserts the `warn` set equals exactly the rules the baseline records. Before, a new `autoFocus` anywhere in the tree was a warning absorbed by the ceiling; now it fails `npm run lint`, with five justified exemptions. Enforcement surface goes 28/4/2 → **29/3/2**. Verified by positive control in both directions: a fresh `autoFocus` lints as an **error**, and deleting any one directive reds the ratchet and names the file.
- **The baseline header's central claim had gone false and is replaced, not patched.** It read "every entry here is a real defect, not an accepted exception" while half the map was accepted exceptions. The invariant is now one the file can keep — *an entry here is a finding nobody has adjudicated yet* — so a reviewed finding leaves the map in one of two directions, fixed or exempted at the site, and "reviewed and accepted" has a spelling that costs a line of justification where the next reader needs it.
- **Two stale prose counts were corrected while in the file.** `eslint.config.js`'s header said "5 rules / 26 findings today" (truth at `main`: 4 / 10) — it had rotted through WIC-2062 and WIC-2073 with nothing able to contradict it, and is now marked as prose the entries below it supersede. The anti-no-op guard's worked mutation was re-measured rather than re-read: narrowing the glob to `src/pages/**` now yields **0** findings, not 1, because `no-autofocus` was the only rule surviving the narrowing.
- **Scope held.** The remaining 5 are three shapes and are not "leave forever": `ApplicationCard.tsx` ×2 and `ResumeUpload.tsx` ×2 — both the established precedent shape, and WIC-2077's second slice — and `wizard/WizardStep.tsx` ×1, which is genuinely fenced (its handler is a Ctrl+Enter shortcut, not a mouse-only affordance, and every obvious remedy trades one finding for another). `AXE_BASELINE` is a separate ratchet and is unchanged at 8.


### Accessibility — The resume drop zone had no keyboard path at all, and a precedent that failed on its sixth site (2026-09-05)

`A11Y_BASELINE` drops **5 → 4** (WIC-2077 slice 2, continuing slice 1's 10 → 5 under WIC-1589), and both `--max-warnings` ceilings in `packages/web/package.json` move with it. `click-events-have-key-events` reaches 0 and is promoted off `BASELINED_RULES` back to `error`; enforcement surface goes 29/3/2 → **30/2/2**.

- **`ResumeUpload.tsx` was a genuine WCAG 2.1.1 failure, not a lint artifact.** Unlike the `FilterPanel`/`StarEntryPicker` cases, no real control existed to promote: the `<input type="file">` is `className="hidden"`, the drop zone's `onClick` was the only pointer path to the picker, and the copy said "or click to browse" while there was nothing to press — so there was **no keyboard path to uploading a resume at all**. A real "browse files" `<button>` now carries the activation; the `<div>` keeps `role="region"`, its accessible name and the drag handlers, and remains the drop target. Pointer users lose the whole-zone click target, the same trade documented for `StarEntryPicker`.
- **⛔ `ApplicationCard.tsx` was scoped into this slice, implemented, measured and then REVERTED — the prescribed fix trades a lint warning for a *serious* axe violation.** Moving its activation onto a real `<button>` inside the existing `<h3>` is the `ResumeVariantCard` (WIC-1942) / `Reports*` (WIC-2062) precedent, correct on all five earlier sites. On this one it reds `routeAxe.render.test.tsx` with **`nested-interactive` on `/applications`**, because the cause lies outside the component: `SortableApplicationCard` wraps every card in a dnd-kit `<div role="button" tabindex="0" aria-roledescription="sortable">`, so a real button inside the card nests an interactive control inside a widget. Isolated by bisection — the `ResumeUpload` half alone is axe-clean; the `ApplicationCard` half alone reproduces it.
- **The two ratchets pull in opposite directions here, and axe is measuring the more serious defect.** This is the WIC-1942 lesson inverted: there, deleting an `<article role="button">` cleared an axe finding and a `jsx-a11y` finding at once. Here the lint finding stays, the card keeps its `tabIndex`, and the tree is left accessible-enough rather than lint-clean. A precedent that has held five times can still be wrong on the sixth site, and only the *other* baseline could say so — which is the argument for running both.
- **⚠️ A scoping prediction was measured false and is recorded rather than worked around.** It held that `no-noninteractive-element-interactions` carries a default `handlers` option of `onClick,onMouseDown,onMouseUp,onKeyPress,onKeyDown,onKeyUp`, so retained drag and hover handlers would not re-trigger the rule. On this config the resolved options carry **no `handlers` key at all** — they are `{body: ['onError','onLoad'], iframe: […], img: […]}` — and probed one at a time on a bare `<article>`, **each** of `onDragStart`, `onDragEnd`, `onMouseEnter` and `onMouseLeave` trips the rule by itself. So `ResumeUpload`'s own `onDrop`/`onDragOver`/`onDragLeave` keep it in the baseline at 1, and the rule stays at 3.
- **The remaining survivors are deliberately not exempted.** Writing disable directives per slice 1's pattern would be working around a measurement rather than answering it; each is a real design question. Tracked as WIC-2078, together with a defect found in passing and *not* fixed here: `ApplicationCard`'s quick-action bar is gated on `isHovered`, so its Edit and Delete buttons are mouse-only — a keyboard gap larger than the lint finding beside it, and one `jsx-a11y` is structurally blind to, so no baseline number moves when it is fixed.
- **Keyboard reachability is pinned** by `ResumeUpload.keyboardNav.test.tsx` (5 tests), mutation-checked against restoring the wrapper `onClick`: 4 of the 5 red.


### Accessibility — The kanban card's Edit and Delete were mouse-only, and the last three lint survivors are adjudicated (2026-09-05)

`A11Y_BASELINE` drops **4 → 1** (WIC-2078, closing the tail WIC-2077 split out). Both `--max-warnings` ceilings in `packages/web/package.json` move with it. `no-noninteractive-element-interactions` reaches zero and is promoted off `BASELINED_RULES` back to `error`; enforcement surface goes 30/2/2 → **31/1/2**.

- **The defect with real user impact moved no ratchet number, which is why it needed its own card.** `ApplicationCard`'s quick-action bar was gated on `isHovered`, so its Edit and Delete buttons did not exist in the DOM unless a mouse was over the card — on the kanban board the only path to either action, so both were unavailable to a keyboard user outright (WCAG 2.1.1). `jsx-a11y` is a per-file static lint and cannot see a control that is absent, and `routeAxe` renders at rest where the bar is correctly absent, so **both existing ratchets were green before the fix and after it**. The bar now reveals on focus as well as hover, pinned by a new `ApplicationCard.keyboardNav.test.tsx`.
- **Fixing that exposed a second, latent defect the first one had been hiding.** The card's `onKeyDown` calls `preventDefault()`, and `keydown` bubbles — so it also ran for events originating on the quick-action buttons and **cancelled their activation**: pressing Enter on Edit navigated to the application instead of editing it, and Space did nothing. It could not have been observed before, because with the bar mouse-only no keyboard event could originate below that element. Guarded with `e.target !== e.currentTarget` and pinned by three cases asserting the handlers *fire*, not merely that focus arrives.
- **The reveal is React state, not a CSS `group-focus-within` variant, and the test is the reason.** jsdom applies no Tailwind, so a CSS-only reveal would leave the buttons queryable whether or not the fix were present — the pinning test would pass against the unfixed component. Conditional rendering also keeps the buttons out of the DOM at rest, which is what keeps `routeAxe` clean.
- **The card's native HTML5 drag is deleted as dead code.** `handleDragStart` called `dataTransfer.setData('application/json', …)` and nothing ever read it back: `dataTransfer.getData` appears **zero** times in `packages/web/src`, and the kanban columns are dnd-kit `useDroppable` targets, not native drop targets. The real drag is dnd-kit's `PointerSensor`/`KeyboardSensor` one level up on `SortableApplicationCard`, which also already supplies the `opacity-50` styling the removed `isDragging` state applied. The `draggable` prop goes with it, at all three call sites. Stated as measured: this removes dead code that was competing with dnd-kit's pointer handling, and does **not** claim to repair any pointer-drag misbehaviour, which was not measured.
- **All three lint survivors are EXEMPTIONS, not fixes** — the same shape as WIC-2077's `no-autofocus` block, and the distinction is the point: no markup became more operable. The rule fires once per element on the presence of any handler, measured rather than assumed — on a bare `<article>`, `onClick` alone and `onKeyDown` alone each trip it independently, so `ApplicationCard`'s finding could never have been retired by deleting its drag and hover handlers. Each carries its reason at the line: the card's own activation (a real `<button>` or `role="button"` there trips axe's `nested-interactive` instead, per WIC-2077/WIC-1942); the resume drop *target*, which cannot be given a keyboard equivalent and instead has one on the sibling "browse files" button; and the wizard's Ctrl+Enter, a container-scoped shortcut delegated from focusable descendants, where `tabIndex` would add a dead tab stop and a `document` listener would widen the shortcut's scope.
- **The one remaining finding is the one this ratchet cannot drive to zero.** `no-noninteractive-tabindex` on `ApplicationCard`'s `<article>` is load-bearing: every spelling that satisfies it trips axe's `nested-interactive`, because `SortableApplicationCard` wraps each card in a dnd-kit `div[role="button"][tabindex="0"]`. The next move on it is a dnd-kit wrapper question, not a `jsx-a11y` one. `AXE_BASELINE` is a separate ratchet and is unchanged at 8 findings over 8 entries.


### Fixed — The kanban card's Delete asked for confirmation and then did nothing (2026-09-05)

Clicking Delete on a kanban card raised "Are you sure you want to delete this application?", and confirming did **nothing** — no request, no error, no feedback (WIC-2079). `ApplicationsList` is the only page that mounts `<KanbanBoard>`, and it passed no `onDelete`, so `ApplicationCard.handleDelete` ran the confirm and then called `onDelete?.(id)` on an undefined prop. The user was walked through confirming a destructive action that could not happen.

- **This supersedes the "real defect found in passing" note in the WIC-2078 entry above, which was wrong in both halves.** That note said Edit and Delete were "unreachable by keyboard entirely". The render-gating it described was real and is fixed above, but neither button was a *keyboard* gap in the sense claimed. Edit navigates to the same route as the card's own Enter/Space activation, so a keyboard user could always reach that destination — it is a redundant affordance, not an unreachable one. Delete was not a keyboard gap either: it was **dead for everyone, pointer included**. The a11y framing pointed at the smaller of the two problems, the [Group B] shape from WIC-2073 (`FilterPanel`).
- **`useDeleteApplication` already existed and had never been called.** It is wired now, following `ResumeVariantsList.handleDelete` verbatim: `mutate` with an `onError` that logs and alerts. The alert is deliberate rather than the `console.error`-only shape used by `handleStatusChange` on the same page — a failed status change leaves the board visibly unchanged, so the user can see nothing happened, whereas a **failed delete is indistinguishable from the bug being fixed here**. Silence on the error path would reintroduce it.
- **The native `confirm()` stays.** There is no `ConfirmDialog`/`ConfirmModal` component in the repo, so it is the house style; building one was out of scope for this fix.
- **The gap was structurally invisible to the existing test.** `ApplicationCard.keyboardNav.test.tsx` supplies its own `onDelete={vi.fn()}`, so it pins the card's half of the contract and stays green no matter what any caller does. The defect lived entirely in the seam between component and page, which is exactly what a mock injected at that seam cannot see. New `ApplicationsList.deleteWiring.test.tsx` mounts the **page** and asserts at the `fetch` boundary instead — nothing below the network is stubbed. Confirmed as a falsifier before the fix was written: against `9cdccb0a` it fails with zero DELETE requests issued.
- **Edit is kept, deliberately, and the reasoning is recorded at the call site.** It duplicates the card's own destination, so dropping it was the live alternative. It stays because it is the only *labelled* affordance of the pair — the card's activation is implicit, and "Edit Staff Engineer" is what actually announces the action to a screen reader — and because it keeps a non-destructive control first in the bar's tab order, ahead of Delete. If the detail route ever grows a distinct `/edit` mode, the duplication resolves itself.
- **`stopPropagation` on the pointer path is now pinned, in both places it can be.** The keydown guard from WIC-2078 was covered; the `e.stopPropagation()` calls in `handleEdit`/`handleDelete` were not, and deleting either left the suite green. Delete's is pinned end-to-end at the page level (a leak would navigate away from the board mid-delete); Edit's can only be pinned with separable spies at the component level, because in production a leak navigates twice to one destination and is indistinguishable from working.
- No API, schema or migration change. `A11Y_BASELINE` and `AXE_BASELINE` are both untouched — this defect is invisible to `jsx-a11y`, which is the point.

### Security — The last two agent-dispatchable owner signatures are narrowed, closing the ADR-010 D2 burndown (2026-09-05)

ADR-010 **D2**, fifth and final agent-dispatchable slice (WIC-2076, closing WIC-2068 after WIC-2070/2071/2072 and the catalog slice below). `[SIG]` **23 → 21**, `[COND]` unchanged at **3**, `[NOWNER]` 0, `[LAUNDER]` 0; the guard baseline is regenerated **downward**, 26 → 24 entries, by deletion only.

- **Two signatures, both runtime no-ops by construction.** `dialogue.service.ts`'s `captureProjectFile` and `resume.service.ts`'s `addCompanyToCatalog` take `userId: string` instead of `userId?: string`. Both write tables whose `user_id` is `.notNull()` (`projects`, `company_catalog`), so an owner-absent predicate already selected the empty set — what changes is that an absent owner is no longer *representable* at the signature. No call site changed.
- **Both runtime guards are retained, and that is a deliberate departure from the card.** The dispatching card asked for the `!userId` half of `addCompanyToCatalog`'s early return to be dropped once the type forbade absence. It is kept. The type is not a runtime guarantee — these are reachable from JS callers and from a JWT with no `sub` claim, where `userId` is `null` however the signature reads (the belt-and-braces rationale at `project.service.ts:752`). Dropping it would have sent `eq(companyCatalog.userId, undefined)` into the read as an unscoped match, and would have failed the existing tenant-isolation test outright.
- **`overrideFileName` moves from `?` to `string | undefined`.** A required parameter cannot follow an optional one (TS1016), so narrowing `userId` forces the preceding parameter's spelling. This is the same idiom as `getOrCreateProjectBySlug`, and the sole call site plus both tests already passed it positionally — so it is a spelling change, not a caller change.
- **Both guards were mutation-checked rather than assumed.** Deleting `addCompanyToCatalog`'s `!userId` half reds exactly the test asserting the select and the insert are never reached; deleting `captureProjectFile`'s throw reds the AC-R5 case on its *message*, because `getOrCreateProjectBySlug` answers the same `BAD_REQUEST`/400 and a code-and-status assertion alone would have passed. Each mutant compiled and ran (`passed + failed` equal to the unmutated total), so neither graded a tree it had failed to change.
- **The guard's positive control was run after the baseline regen, not before.** Reintroducing the fallback exits **1** naming the exact site; the unmutated tree exits **0**. Mutating before `--write-baseline` would have baked the fallback into the baseline and made a green run meaningless.
- **The remaining 24 baselined findings are not deferred work.** 10 are forbidden by in-file headers (`interviewPrep.service.ts`, `resume-variant.service.ts`), 12 are on nullable tables and need a backfill plus `SET NOT NULL` behind a human-gated `DATABASE_URL`, 1 is a guard false positive (`analytics.service.ts`'s pre-auth telemetry, where an absent owner is the documented session-scoped case), and 1 is entangled with a nullable-table caller. None is actionable from an agent seat.



### Security — The six catalog list endpoints paged every tenant's rows when the owner was absent (2026-09-05)

ADR-010 **D2**, first slice (WIC-2068, continuing WIC-2070/2071/2072). `catalog.service.ts` is now clear: `[SIG]` **29 → 23**, `[COND]` **10 → 3**, `[NOWNER]` and `[LAUNDER]` unchanged at 0. `scripts/owner-predicates.baseline.json` is regenerated downward — 12 deletions, zero additions.

- **The defect shape.** `listCompanies`, `listJobFitTags`, `listTechStackTags`, `listBullets`, `listThemes` and `listDiffs` each built their predicate as `if (userId) conditions.push(eq(<table>.userId, userId))`. With the owner absent that line does not run, and because every remaining conjunct is a *filter* rather than a *scope*, `.where(and(...))` still renders a valid query — one that pages every tenant's catalog and answers HTTP 200. The owner parameter is now required and the tenancy term unconditional.
- **This was reachability, not a guarantee, and that is the whole point of D2.** D1.3 had already closed the only route-level source of an absent owner (`catalog.routes.ts` passes `requireOwner(c)`, which 401s), so these arms were unreachable — held one layer away, by a function the services never see. Requiring `userId` makes absence unrepresentable at the signature, so the compiler enforces it instead of a convention about who calls whom.
- **The card's own numbers were stale and were re-measured before any code changed.** WIC-2068 cites `[SIG] 71 / [COND] 29` at `a64554a`; `main` had advanced six PRs since, and the true starting point was **29 / 10** — WIC-2070/2071/2072 had already burned the rest. The 71 was never 71 units of work.
- **`generateDiff`'s ownership probe was a residual guard.** Its `userId` was *already* required, so the `if (userId)` wrapping the resume/application probe could not be false — dead code that made the probe read as optional to a human and to the audit alike. It now runs unconditionally, matching the `conditions.push` at the foot of the same function, which was made unconditional for the same reason.
- **"Single-user mode" is retired, not merely untested.** Eight tests pinned the fail-open arm as intended behaviour. They are replaced by their fail-closed counterparts: an absent owner reaching a service now renders the *same* scoped clause binding NULL, and reads **zero rows** — asserted against a stub that honours the clause, per ADR-010 AC-4, not against a response code. `generateDiff` refuses at the probe rather than waving a foreign resume through to auto-apply.
- **`test/` is outside `packages/api/tsconfig.json`, so tightening a signature breaks no test at compile time.** That is what lets these tests reach past the signature and measure the predicate — but it also meant six `pagination.test.ts` call sites were silently binding NULL into every tenancy term. They now pass a real owner.
- **Mutation matrix: 7 sites × 2 graders, 14/14 killed.** Restoring `if (userId)` at any one site trips the audit (exit 1) *and* reds exactly 2 tests. Two traps were hit and recorded: the `listDiffs` mutant initially did not apply at all (its anchor string occurs twice — a `count == 1` assertion caught what would otherwise have read as a clean pass), and the first `generateDiff` mutant did not compile, producing no test line rather than a failure. Mutants were applied **after** `--write-baseline`, per WIC-2072.


### Security — An authenticated request with no owner is now rejected at the route, not laundered into "no owner filter" (2026-09-05)

ADR-010 D1.2 + D1.3 (WIC-1600). Every authenticated route read its caller as `c.get('userId') ?? undefined`, which turned *absent owner* into *absent owner filter* and pushed the decision down into each service predicate. All 66 such sites across 11 route files now call `requireOwner(c)`, which 401s instead: adoptions reach **77 in all 11 route files**, and `packages/api/src/routes` holds **zero** of the old shape. Five of the 66 are the `reports.ts` sites the entry below closed independently while this was in flight — the two changes converged on the same call, so the totals here count them once, not twice.

- **`HonoVariables.userId` narrows from `string | null` to `string`.** The two places that relied on the wider type are handled rather than deleted: the three `PUBLIC_PATHS` routes now leave the variable unset instead of setting it to `null` — they run before an owner exists, and `undefined` and `null` are already treated identically by every consumer — and `requireOwner` reads through the wider type on purpose, since it is the guard that *makes* the narrowed type true rather than a consumer that may assume it.
- **The type is not the mechanism, and that was measured, not assumed.** With `userId` narrowed to `string`, reintroducing the laundering in `routes/dashboard.ts` still gives `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 — a redundant `??` is legal, and 81 service signatures still accept `userId?: string`, so the argument typechecks at every call site. `[SIG]` and `[COND]` cannot see it either; they key on signatures and predicates, and a route call argument is neither.
- **So the guard gained a fourth check, `[LAUNDER]`**, keyed on the *fallback* rather than on the literal `undefined`, so `?? null`, `|| ''` and `?? 'anonymous'` are caught too. A bare `c.get('userId')` with no fallback is not flagged — that is what `requireOwner` itself does. Baseline holds it at 0. This pass touched routes and not predicates, so it moved neither `[SIG]` nor `[COND]`; both stand at `76` / `37` after merging WIC-2065, which narrowed the five `reports.service.ts` signatures independently.
- **Behaviour is unchanged for real callers.** No route reachable here could already produce an absent owner: D1.1 rejects a token that verifies without a `sub`, and D3 gives local dev a real owner. This makes that guarantee structural instead of an invariant three layers from the predicate — the request now stops at the edge rather than relying on every downstream predicate to be written correctly.
- **Verified with both controls.** `test/require-owner.routes.test.ts` grows to 18 entry points, one per migrated route file, asserting 401 `OWNER_REQUIRED` *and* that the service was never called — a response code alone cannot separate a not-found guard from an ownership guard. Reverting a single migrated site flips that test from pass to a 200, and the four `[LAUNDER]` cases in `test/audit-owner-predicates.test.ts` pin the guard's own detection.
- **What this does and does not close.** It removes the route-level absence; it does not narrow the 71 service signatures that still accept `userId?: string` (D2 stays partial, `[SIG] 71` / `[COND] 29`). The four cross-tenant `catalog.service.ts` UPDATEs this entry was originally written against were fixed independently by WIC-2067 while it was in flight, together with the `[NOWNER]` ternary blindness that hid them — so that class is now closed at both ends rather than at one, and no claim about those four sites survives here.

### Security — The catalog diff apply path rewrote one row per tenant, and the guard written to catch that scored it clean (2026-09-05)

`catalog.service.ts` `applyChange` scoped its four UPDATEs with `const whereClause = userId ? and(eq(t.slug, s), eq(t.userId, userId)) : eq(t.slug, s)`, and all four uniques are **composite** `(userId, slug)` (`schema.ts:225`, `:250`, `:274`, `:315`). No single-column unique on the slug means the fallback predicate carried no LIMIT, so an absent owner rewrote one row *per tenant* (WIC-2067, from WIC-1672 Finding 2; ADR-010 AC-T0).

- **Not exploitable on `main` today, and it was not reachable when filed.** `middleware/auth.ts` `requireSubject` throws 401 on an absent `sub`, and `PUBLIC_PATHS` is the three `/api/auth/*` routes. This is defence-in-depth restoration. It reopens the moment anything joins `PUBLIC_PATHS`, or `applyDiff` is called from a queue consumer or backfill script — neither of which touches this file, which is the reason to close it at the predicate rather than rely on the caller.
- **The `[NOWNER]` check was structurally blind to the shape it was written for.** `classifyPredicate` scanned both arms of a conditional into one flat result, so the owner-scoped consequent answered for the whole predicate and the owner-less alternate was never weighed. It graded the *same* defect written inline one line away — severity inverted, since the site that looks scoped and degrades silently got the milder grade. A conditional in predicate position is now classified arm by arm and is owner-scoped only if **every** arm carries the owner term; `unique` is the intersection across arms, not the union, or a consequent that happens to touch a pk masks a non-unique fallback.
- **Fixed inside `classifyPredicate`, not by expanding the `where` argument.** The identifier hop already resolves `const whereClause = …; .where(whereClause)`, so recursing at the conditional also weighs a ternary nested inside a combinator — `and(eq(t.slug, s), userId ? eq(t.userId, userId) : …)` — which a top-level expansion returns unchanged and stays blind to. The fail-closed `userId ? eq(t.userId, userId) : isNull(t.userId)` posture stays clean for free: both arms carry the owner term.
- **Seven standing fixtures**, including two negative controls that matter as much as the positive one — an id-scoped fallback must stay counted as pk-scoped rather than reported, or the next reader "fixes the flood" by reverting this. All seven die under a revert-the-fix mutant.
- **Owner required rather than branched.** `getDiff`, `applyDiff`, `applyChange`, `discardDiff` and `resolveDiffItem` take `userId: string`; the four `catalog.routes.ts` call sites move off `c.get('userId') ?? undefined` to the existing `requireOwner(c)`, so the `undefined` is no longer manufactured at the boundary. Three id-only `catalogDiffs` writes now reuse the owner-scoped predicate, and four `userId!` assertions are gone.
- **Guard deltas, measured at `c661d363`:** `[NOWNER]` 0 → 4 (the branch fix exposing the live defect) → **0** (the defect closed); `[SIG]` 76 → **71**; `[COND]` 37 → **29**; pk-scoped writes 18 → **23**, the five newly-visible id-scoped fallbacks. Baseline burned down 113 → 100. Guard exits 0.
- **`or(eq(t.userId, u), eq(t.slug, s))` is the same blindness in the other spelling and is NOT fixed here** — recorded in the script's scope note. Measured 0 occurrences across all 44 write predicates, which is why it is a note and not a finding. Closed in the entry directly below (WIC-2069), together with the `not(...)` spelling.


### Security — `or()` and `not()` inverted owner-scoping in the AC-T0 guard exactly as the ternary did (2026-09-05)

WIC-2069, closing the residual WIC-1672 Finding 3 that the entry above left open as a scope note. `classifyPredicate` set `owner` on the **first** owner column it saw anywhere in a predicate. That is sound for `and`, which narrows, and wrong for the other two members of `PREDICATE_COMBINATORS` — the owner term is present but not load-bearing, which is the WIC-2067 shape in two more spellings.

- **`or(...)` widens and `not(...)` inverts.** `or(eq(t.userId, u), eq(t.tagSlug, s))` rewrites every tenant's row whose slug matches; `and(eq(t.tagSlug, s), not(eq(t.userId, u)))` writes to every tenant **except** the caller, which is strictly worse than dropping the owner term altogether. The guard saw `t.userId` and scored both CLEAN.
- **Each combinator now quantifies the way it composes**, over operands classified independently rather than scanned into one flat result: `and` keeps `some`, `or` requires `every`, and `not` yields neither `owner` nor `unique` — the complement of one row is every other row, so a bare `not(eq(t.id, id))` is now reported instead of filing under pk-scoped.
- **Four-mutant matrix at `extraction.service.ts:109`, against `origin/main` `a64554a`.** Before: the ternary and bare-`eq` controls exit 1, `or` and `not` both exit **0**. After: **all four exit 1** with a `[NOWNER]` finding at the mutated site. Running the two controls first is what makes the `or`/`not` green evidence of a blind spot rather than of a mis-applied patch.
- **The clean tree is unmoved:** guard exits 0, **100 baselined sites / 22 baseline keys**, `[SIG]` 71, `[COND]` 29, `[NOWNER]` 0, 19 pk-scoped, 0 unresolved. The change is monotone — it can only retire an `owner`/`unique` grade, never manufacture one.
- **Nine standing fixtures, three of them negative controls**: `and` with one owner conjunct, `or` with the owner term on every disjunct, and a `not` beside a real owner conjunct are all clean. A rule keyed on the *spelling* — report any `or`/`not` outright — passes every positive case and fails all three. Under a revert-the-fix mutant exactly the six positive cases go red, 38 pass, and the suite total is unchanged at 44.
- **Live exposure is zero** — no write predicate in the tree uses either shape. This is prevention ahead of the ADR-010 D2 rewrite of ~100 owner predicates (WIC-2068), which this guard is the only thing gating; a blind combinator is cheapest to fix before that lands, not after.



### Security — `project.service.ts` no longer represents an ownerless caller, and its storage keys no longer invent a shared `anon` tenant (2026-09-05)

ADR-010 **D2 slice 1** (WIC-2070, under WIC-2068), continuing the D1.2/D1.3 route-layer entry above. All **22** owner signatures in `packages/api/src/services/project.service.ts` narrow from `userId?: string` / `userId: string | undefined` to `userId: string`, and `storageOwner`'s `userId ?? 'anon'` fallback is deleted. `[SIG]` **71 -> 46**, with `[COND]` **29**, `[NOWNER]` **0** and `[LAUNDER]` **0** all unmoved.

- **Zero of the 22 was a live defect, and this entry does not claim otherwise.** Every site was already fail-closed: the 14 DB-access sites route through `projectScope`/`projectIdScope` -> `requireOwner`, which has thrown 400 on an absent owner since WIC-1554, and the 8 storage-key sites were unreachable with `undefined` because each sits behind an `assertProjectOwned` (or, cross-file, a `getOrCreateProjectBySlug`) that throws first. What changes is *representability* — a future caller can no longer write an ownerless path without `tsc` objecting.
- **Every runtime guard is retained.** Narrowing a type is not a mechanism: `tsc` exits 0 on a reintroduced `?? undefined` at a call site, and `userId` arrives from a JWT `sub` claim that can be `null` at runtime however the signature reads. `requireOwner` keeps its throw and carries a comment saying why deleting it would leave the file strictly less safe than before the narrowing. `getOrCreateProjectBySlug` was already in this shape and is the template the rest now match.
- **Deleting `?? 'anon'` needed a new throw, not just a narrower type — the naive deletion is worse than the fallback.** `/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/.test(undefined)` coerces to the *string* `'undefined'`, which passes the character class and contains no `..`, so removing the `??` while leaving the falsy check below the regex would have silently renamed the shared ownerless tenant from `projects/anon/` to `projects/undefined/` with the whole suite green. `storageOwner` now rejects a falsy owner **before** the traversal guard, and `test/project.guards.test.ts` AC-9b pins that ordering by reading the error *code* (`BAD_REQUEST`, not `INVALID_PATH`) across `undefined`, `null` and `''`.
- **AC-9 is inverted, deliberately.** It previously asserted that an absent owner resolved to `anon`; it now asserts a throw. The test reaches the runtime guard through an explicit cast, because the narrowed type makes the call unrepresentable to `tsc` while doing nothing about a JS caller or a `sub`-less token — which is the entire reason the throw has to stay.
- **Objects already stored under `projects/anon/` are untouched.** This closes the code path that creates new ones; the historical data is a separate question owned by WIC-1929 (project-storage-key backfill). Code change here, data question there — stated rather than left to be discovered.
- **Three signatures outside the target file moved, all forced by `tsc` and none of them a caller change.** `resume.service.ts` `writeProjectFile` and `dialogue.service.ts` `enrichProjectFile` / `correctProjectFile` consume the narrowed helpers; every call site already supplied a `string` (the dialogue routes via `requireOwner(c)`, the resume path after its own explicit `if (!userId) throw`). Baseline delta is exactly -25: `project.service` 22 -> removed, `dialogue` 3 -> 1, `resume` 8 -> 7. The other 78 baselined sites, which carry all 29 `[COND]`, are untouched and stay with WIC-2068.
- **Positive control, and one honest negative result.** A mutant that reverts one signature to `userId?: string` and silences every use with `!` **compiles clean (`tsc` exit 0) and still fails the audit** (exit 1, a new `[SIG]`) — the ratchet catches what the compiler cannot. The card's prescribed control, a bare `userId ?? undefined` at a call site with the signature left required, does **not** fail the audit and should not: against a `userId: string` it is a no-op the compiler types as `string`, so there is no defect to detect. Full suite green at 1577 tests across 83 files.



### Security — Five owner ternaries dropped the owner term instead of inverting it, so an absent owner widened the query rather than narrowing it (2026-09-05)

ADR-010 **D2 slice 2** (WIC-2071, under WIC-2068), continuing slice 1 above. Slice 1 closed a cohort whose fallback was already inert; this one closes the opposite shape. Five signatures narrow to `userId: string` and five fail-**open** fallbacks are deleted: `catalog.service.ts` `listStarEntries`, `dashboard.service.ts` `getDashboardStats`, `resume.service.ts` `listResumes` and `listResumeExports`, and `application.service.ts` `updateApplication`. `[SIG]` **46 -> 41**, `[COND]` **29 -> 23**, `[NOWNER]` and `[LAUNDER]` both unmoved at **0**.

- **Fail-open, not fail-closed, and the difference is the whole slice.** Ten other owner ternaries in `services/` resolve an absent owner to `isNull(t.userId)` — a narrower reading over tables where anonymous rows genuinely exist, exempted by shape in the guard's `failClosedOwnerTernary()`. These five instead *dropped* the owner term. Three fell to `: undefined`, which drizzle reads as **no predicate at all** rather than a narrow one, so the read widened to every tenant's rows. Two are the `userId ? and(idTerm, ownerTerm) : idTerm` idiom that `resume-variant.service.ts:55` records as the WIC-1482 / WIC-1500 defect: the fallback still *looks* scoped because the id term survives, so a `: undefined` grep does not find them — `listResumeExports` became an IDOR read by resume id, and `updateApplication` an IDOR **write** by application id plus a guessable small-integer `version`.
- **None of the five was reachable on `main`, and this entry does not claim otherwise.** Each has exactly one route caller and all five already pass `requireOwner(c)`, which returns `string` — so they were held one layer away by the D1.2/D1.3 edge guard, not live cross-tenant leaks. This is D2's target class: *unreachable but representable*. Because every caller already supplied a `string`, **zero call sites change**.
- **Requiring the owner, never repairing it to `isNull()`.** An `isNull()` fallback would be a real reading on the two nullable tables here (`applications.user_id`, `resumes.user_id`, whose `userId ?? null` insert paths are live) — of *somebody else's* anonymous rows. Absence is an error on these paths, not a narrower query, so the branch is deleted rather than inverted.
- **Every runtime guard is retained, and the mutation matrix shows why both halves are load-bearing.** Eleven mutants, each run against the audit, `tsc`, and the 158 affected tests. Deleting any one of the five `if (!userId) throw` guards is **killed by the tests and invisible to both the audit and `tsc`**; restoring any one of the six fail-open fallbacks is **killed by the audit and invisible to `tsc`**. `tsc` exits 0 on all eleven — the type is not the mechanism. The two gates are exactly complementary, and neither alone covers the other's class.
- **The fallback mutants survive the tests, and that is a property of the fix rather than a test gap.** With the guard in place the fallback branch is unreachable, so restoring it changes nothing observable — they are equivalent mutants *given the guard*. Recorded here so the next reader does not mistake the audit for redundant coverage: it is the only gate that sees that class.
- **Three of the card's own predictions were wrong, in the safe direction.** It expected `[COND]` to drop for the three `: undefined` sites only and said the two IDOR sites "will move neither counter". `[COND]` in fact dropped **6**, because `updateApplication` carried *two* owner ternaries — the update predicate and the read that disambiguates 404 from 409. That second one mattered on its own: unscoped, it answered `VersionConflictError` for another tenant's application, confirming the row exists and re-opening the distinction the owner term erases. The audit's pk-scoped exemption list also fell **19 -> 18**, because that UPDATE no longer needs exempting.
- **The card's prescribed positive control is vacuous — the same trap slice 1 hit.** `listResumes(requireOwner(c) ?? undefined)` leaves both the audit and `tsc` at exit 0, because `requireOwner` returns `string` and the coalesce is a no-op. Reporting "the audit fails" from it would have been false. The control that works reverts the signature and the ternary together, which the audit catches as a new `[SIG]` and `[COND]`.
- **Four existing tests pinned the old behaviour and were inverted, not deleted.** `dashboard.service.test.ts` had asked for exactly this: its ownerless case asserted a 16-row cross-tenant aggregate and carried the instruction *"Failing here is the signal that the fix arrived, not that this test broke."* Likewise `catalog.service.test.ts` asserted `.where(undefined)` as "single-user mode". New coverage is `test/owner-required.fail-open.test.ts` (22 tests) over a real migrated Postgres, asserting per site that no query is issued at all — `getDb` is never called — since ADR-010 AC-4 notes a response code cannot separate a not-found guard from an ownership guard. Full suite green at **1599 tests across 84 files**.
- **The remaining fail-open inventory is 13 sites, not 0, and the card's "five" counted functions rather than ternaries.** A comment-aware sweep of every owner ternary under `packages/api/src` — matching on the *fallback shape*, so the dropped-owner-term idiom is included — finds **19** fail-open against 8 fail-closed. This slice closes **6 ternaries across the 5 named functions**, `updateApplication` carrying two. The other **13** sit in `cover-letter.service.ts` (7), `application.service.ts` (3) and `resume.service.ts` (3), every one the same dropped-owner-term shape on a pk-scoped read or write. They are filed as a follow-up rather than folded in, so this PR's counter predictions stay checkable against a fixed set.



### Security — The last 13 fail-open owner ternaries are closed; the D2 dropped-owner-term inventory is now 0 (2026-09-05)

ADR-010 **D2 slice 3** (WIC-2072, under WIC-2068), completing the fail-open cohort slice 2 above opened. All **13** remaining ternaries are the `userId ? and(idTerm, ownerTerm) : idTerm` idiom — the owner term dropped rather than inverted, so the fallback still *looks* scoped because the id term survives. **12** signatures narrow to `userId: string` across `cover-letter.service.ts` (`getCoverLetter`, `updateCoverLetter`, `deleteCoverLetter`, `reviseCoverLetter`, `generateOutreach`, `exportCoverLetter`), `application.service.ts` (`getApplication`, `deleteApplication`, `updateApplicationStatus`) and `resume.service.ts` (`getResumeExport`, `deleteResume`, `getResumeDownloadUrl`). `[SIG]` **41 -> 29**, `[COND]` **23 -> 10**, `[NOWNER]` and `[LAUNDER]` both unmoved at **0**; the pk-scoped exemption list falls **18 -> 15**.

- **13 ternaries, 12 signatures — the counters record which is which.** `updateCoverLetter` carries two, exactly as `updateApplication` did in slice 2: the UPDATE predicate *and* the read that disambiguates 404 from 409. `[COND]` drops **13** (one per ternary) and `[SIG]` drops **12** (one per signature), so the two counters disagreeing by one is the fix being measured correctly rather than a discrepancy. The second ternary is not cosmetic: unscoped it answered `VersionConflictError` rather than `NotFoundError` for another tenant's letter, confirming the row exists and re-opening the distinction the owner term erases — and fixing only the write predicate would have left that oracle intact with every other test still green, so it has a dedicated case.
- **Three of the thirteen were worse than an IDOR read.** `deleteApplication`, `deleteCoverLetter` and `deleteResume` dropped the owner term from a **DELETE**, and `deleteResume` hands the `filePath` from that read to `deleteObject`/`fs.unlink`, so the blast radius included another tenant's object in R2 — which no database rollback recovers. `getResumeDownloadUrl` is the other outlier: it mints a signed URL, so its fail-open branch issued a **bearer credential** over another tenant's file, valid for an hour and usable with no further authentication. `updateApplicationStatus` dropped it from a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, the only ownership check on a path whose every subsequent write keys on `id` alone.
- **None was reachable on `main`, and this entry does not claim otherwise.** The card warned these might not all be `requireOwner(c)`-fed and asked for the call sites to be measured rather than assumed. Measured: each of the 12 has exactly one production caller, all in `routes/`, all already passing `requireOwner(c)`, which returns `string`. **Zero production call sites change.** Unlike slice 2 there were also **no tests to invert** — all 21 test call sites already passed an owner, so the full suite was green before the new coverage was added and stayed at 1599 throughout.
- **Requiring the owner, never repairing it to `isNull()`.** `applications.user_id`, `cover_letters.user_id` and `resumes.user_id` are all nullable with live `userId ?? null` insert paths, so a fail-closed reading here would be a real read — of somebody else's anonymous rows — and on the three DELETE paths a real deletion of them. Absence is an error on every one of these paths, so the branch is deleted rather than inverted. The 8 genuinely fail-closed `isNull()` ternaries elsewhere are untouched, as are the two files whose headers forbid narrowing.
- **The audit's positive control is order-dependent, and run in the wrong order it reads as a false pass.** Reverting a signature and its ternary *before* rewriting the baseline leaves the audit at **exit 0** — the reverted site is still recorded in the old baseline, so it is not "new". Run after `--write-baseline` the same mutant gives **exit 1, "2 NEW site(s) allow an absent owner"**. The control is sound; the order is load-bearing, and the failure mode is silent agreement rather than an error.
- **Complementarity re-measured rather than inherited.** Restoring one fallback while keeping its guard: **killed by the audit, invisible to the tests** (46 pass) — an equivalent mutant *given the guard*, not a test gap. Deleting one guard while keeping the narrowed signature: **killed by the tests** (3 fail, precisely that site's three cases) **and invisible to the audit**. `tsc` exits 0 on both — the type is not the mechanism, which is why every `if (!userId) throw` is retained per ADR-010 AC-2.
- **Coverage and the closing sweep.** New `test/owner-required.fail-open.slice3.test.ts` — 46 tests over a real migrated Postgres (PGlite, the repo's own migrations in journal order), table-driven over all 12 functions with a length assertion on the table itself so a site cannot be quietly dropped. Per ADR-010 AC-4 the load-bearing assertion is that **`getDb` is never called**, since a response code cannot separate a not-found guard from an ownership guard. Full suite green at **1645 tests across 85 files**. The baseline rewrite is purely subtractive — 0 entries appended, 0 counts increased, 3 `[COND]` entries removed entirely and 3 `[SIG]` counts reduced, 64 findings to 39. Re-running the sweep at the end gives **0 fail-open** against the same 8 fail-closed: the dropped-owner-term inventory D2 was opened to burn down is empty.


### Security — The five report endpoints returned every tenant's applications to a caller with no identity (2026-09-05)

`routes/reports.ts` laundered the owner five times with `c.get('userId') ?? undefined`, and each of the five `reports.service.ts` predicates then spelled the owner term as something that absence could switch **off** — `...(userId ? [eq(applications.userId, userId)] : [])`, an `if (userId) conditions.push(...)`, and a `userId ? and(...) : statusTerm` ternary (WIC-2065, serving WIC-1901 / WIC-1600, ADR-010 AC-T0).

- **The owner term was not weakened, it was absent.** Eight helpers elsewhere in this package use `userId ? eq(t.userId, userId) : isNull(t.userId)`, where an absent owner scopes to the orphan rows; `audit-owner-predicates.mjs` baselines those as fail-**closed** preconditions, not defects. These five instead dropped the term from the query, so the predicate reduced to the status filter and the read matched every row in `applications`. `getByFitTierReport` was worse again: its `conditions.length > 0 ? and(...) : undefined` meant `?includeTerminal=true` from an owner-less caller issued a bare `.where(undefined)`, which in drizzle is no predicate at all.
- **The reachable caller is a token that verifies but carries no `sub`**, which `middleware/auth.ts` resolves to `null` (WIC-1554). Not the local-dev bypass — ADR-010 D3 (WIC-1964) gave that a real `LOCAL_DEV_USER_ID`, which is what made the fail-closed narrowing safe to do at all.
- **Fixed at the edge, then at the predicate.** All five routes now resolve the owner with `requireOwner(c)` (401 `OWNER_REQUIRED`); the five service signatures narrow from `userId?: string` to `userId: string` and the owner-absent branches are deleted rather than reordered. Absence is now unrepresentable in this file.
- **Red before green, on the hazard rather than on preserved behaviour.** A test supplying a concrete owner passes against the pre-fix tree — the predicate was already correct for an identified caller — so it is blind to the mutant that reverts this. Both new blocks therefore mutate the absent-owner arm: `reports.tenancy.test.ts` (10 tests) had all five AC-T0 cases returning **both tenants' rows** pre-fix, and the five new `require-owner.routes.test.ts` entries returned **200 with the service called** where they now assert 401 and, load-bearingly, that the service was never called at all — which is what "matches zero rows" means when the read is never issued.
- **Fail-closed by SQL, not by a branch.** `eq(applications.userId, undefined)` binds `NULL`, and `= NULL` is `NULL`, so even a JS caller smuggling an absence past the type system matches nothing. That is why deleting the branch was safe rather than merely tidy.
- **`owner-predicates.baseline.json` burned down 123 -> 113 findings** (SIG 5 + COND 5 removed, 25 entries -> 22), never `--write-baseline`. `audit-owner-predicates.mjs` still exits 0.
- **Scope is the reports vertical only.** Six genuinely fail-open sites remain — `application.service.ts:155,269`, `cover-letter.service.ts:471`, and the three `.where(undefined)` sites in `catalog`, `dashboard` and `resume` — and are deliberately left for follow-on cards. The other 113 baselined findings are overwhelmingly the fail-closed `isNull` shape and must not be mass-converted.
- **AC-N2b got stronger, not weaker.** `stale.definition.test.ts` compared the report's clause against a bare `staleWhere()`; both surfaces now emit `and(<stale>, user_id = $n)`, so it compares the composed predicate and the dashboard and report must agree on the owner scoping as well as on the stale definition. No schema, migration or wire change.



### Fixed — Completing a Job Fit Analysis removed the only way to look at it (2026-09-04)

`WorkflowChecklist`'s "Job Fit Analysis" row read `link: hasFitAnalysis ? undefined : …`, so
ticking the step turned the row into a plain `<span>`. The other three rows do not behave this
way — Cover Letter and Tailored Resume *repoint* at `/cover-letters/:id` and
`/resume-variants/:id` on completion, and Interview Prep links unconditionally. This one had
nowhere to repoint to (WIC-2058, dispatching WIC-1860).

- **The state it actually cost the user is the unscored analysis.** `fitScore === null` — an
  empty catalog, or a job description naming no required skills — ticks the step with no badge
  *and*, before this, no link. The user was told they had done it, shown nothing, and given
  nowhere to go. The new link is therefore keyed on the analysis id and not on the score:
  gating it on a score would link exactly the rows that already show something.
- **`GET /catalog/job-fit/analyses/:id` is new, and the list route could not have stood in.**
  The list's only exact narrowing is `applicationId`, which `/job-fit-analysis/:id` does not
  carry, so resolving an id through it means fetching the newest `MAX_ANALYSIS_LIMIT` (100)
  rows and scanning them in the browser — a client filter over a server-chosen page, which can
  only remove rows and never recover one the server did not send (WIC-1533, WIC-1652). An
  analysis outside that page would have read as "not found" while sitting in the table.
- **A miss and a cross-tenant hit are the same 404.** `getJobFitAnalysis` ANDs the owner term
  into the read rather than checking the row afterwards, so a stranger's id is
  indistinguishable from a nonexistent one and the endpoint is not an existence oracle over
  other users' ids. Asserted structurally with `expectScopedTo` — including the id half, bound
  by column — so `and`→`or` reds rather than passing a presence check (4 of 20 cells red on
  that mutant).
- **`/job-fit-analysis/:id` renders the summary contract, not the whole analysis.** The four
  JSONB payloads are deliberately off that DTO. Every one of the page's four branches renders
  the `<h1>` through one frame, so a fifth return inherits it rather than shipping a headingless
  outline (the class `routeOutline.render.test.tsx` inventories).
- **`ApplicationDetail` gains a "View Fit Analysis" header link as well as the checklist row.**
  Not decorative: the checklist renders `<Link to={item.link}>` from a computed field, which
  `route-integrity.test.ts`'s static route→link audit cannot see, so the route would be
  reported as an orphan page nothing links to. `/applications/:id/prep` has carried the same
  button-and-row pair since WIC-1536. Verified by deleting the link and watching the audit red.
- The route sweeps move 30 routes / 120 pairs → **31 / 124**; `AXE_BASELINE` is unchanged at
  8/8 and `MISSING_H1` stays empty.



### Fixed — Four report pages navigated on a bare `<div>`, so their cards were mouse-only (2026-09-05)

`ReportsClosedLoop`, `ReportsNeedsAction`, `ReportsPipeline` and `ReportsStale` each rendered an
application card as a `<div>` whose only affordance was `onClick={() => navigate(…)}`, styled
`cursor-pointer`, with no `tabIndex`, no `role` and no key handler. The card was unreachable by
keyboard and absent from the accessibility tree — a WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) failure, recorded by
`jsx-a11y` as one `click-events-have-key-events` + one `no-static-element-interactions` per file
(WIC-2062, under WIC-1589).

- **Navigation moved onto a real `<button>` inside each card's existing heading**, following the
  `ResumeVariantCard` precedent (WIC-1942). A `role="button"` on the wrapper is *not* the fix and
  was not attempted: that shape tripped axe's `aria-allowed-role` and `nested-interactive` when it
  was tried there. A heading may contain a button where the heading itself may not become one.
- **`ReportsStale` got smaller, not larger.** It was the only file with nested interactives — a
  "View job posting" `<a>` and a "Set Next Action" `<button>` — and both carried
  `onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}` purely to escape the wrapper's handler. With the wrapper
  inert both are dead code and are deleted. Removing the workaround rather than adding one is the
  tell that the shape is right.
- **`A11Y_BASELINE` 26 -> 18**, the four entries deleted outright rather than zeroed; both
  `--max-warnings` ceilings move to 18, and `BASELINED_RULES`' trailing counts go
  `click-events-have-key-events` 9 -> 5 and `no-static-element-interactions` 6 -> 2. Neither rule
  reaches zero, so both stay `warn`. `AXE_BASELINE` is unchanged at 8/8.
- **These four pages had no tests at all**; `ReportsByFitTier.test.tsx` was the only test on any
  report page and covers empty-state copy on a different route. 18 new tests across four files pin
  role, Tab reachability, Enter activation, the preserved mouse path, and that the card body is
  inert. Every file reds on the pre-fix tree (4/4 each).
- **One guard was caught being vacuous and rewritten.** "Navigates exactly once" cannot be checked
  by observing the location: React batches a duplicated `navigate()` to the same URL into one
  render, so a recorder sees a single entry either way. Verified against a mutant restoring the
  wrapper's `onClick` — the recorder-based assertion stayed green. The check is now on the history
  *stack* (one Back must return to the report), which reds on that mutant, as do the inert-body and
  outbound-link guards.


### Tests — The onboarding panel's own focus restore was deletable with a green suite; it is now pinned (2026-09-05)

`OnboardingModal.tsx:311` spreads `{...outerFocusRestore}` onto the panel's `Dialog.Content`. Deleting that
spread left `npx vitest run src/components/onboarding/` fully green — 36 passed (36) — so the binding was held
in place by nothing (WIC-2060, split out of WIC-1868 when that card closed for its `aria-hidden` fix).

- **The two existing focus-restore tests structurally cannot reach it.** `OnboardingModal.step-actions.test.tsx:187`
  and `:300` pin `resumeSkipFocusRestore` and `dismissFocusRestore`, and both open and close a *nested*
  confirmation while the panel stays mounted. The panel's own `Dialog.Content` never unmounts under either, so
  its `onCloseAutoFocus` — the half of the binding that does the restoring — never fires.
- **The new test opens and closes the panel itself**, driving `showOnboarding` on the mocked context across two
  rerenders, and asserts focus returns to the control that opened onboarding. The opener is captured by the
  hook's `focusin` mechanism rather than `onOpenAutoFocus`, which works because `OnboardingModal.tsx:89`'s
  `!showOnboarding` early return sits *below* the hooks: the component stays mounted while the panel is closed,
  so focusing a control then is exactly the "last element focused while no dialog was open" case.
- **The deliverable is the mutant dying, not the test existing.** Baseline 36 passed (36) → **37 passed (37)**
  with the test added; with `{...outerFocusRestore}` deleted, **1 failed | 36 passed**, total still 37 — so the
  mutant compiled, which is the gate WIC-1610 exists for (a mutant that fails to compile reports green and makes
  the kill count meaningless). Restoring the line returns 37 passed (37).
- Under the mutant focus lands on `<body>`, exactly as `useDialogFocusRestore`'s header predicts: dropping the
  spread does not leave the panel unhandled, it leaves Radix's own `onCloseAutoFocus`, which `preventDefault()`s
  and focuses `context.triggerRef` — populated only by a rendered `Dialog.Trigger`, of which there is none.
- Test-only. No component, route, schema or wire change; `outerFocusRestore` itself was already correct.

### Added — A sweeper-shaped companion makes the evil-merge gate requirable, which `pull_request` structurally cannot be (2026-09-04)

The WIC-1979 detector is sound and unchanged. What this adds is a gate around it that a repository
ruleset can actually name (WIC-2055).

- **The guard could not be made required, and could not be reshaped either.** `evil-merge-guard.yml`
  is `pull_request`-triggered because it is the one check that runs `actions/checkout` on PR head
  code, so `pull_request_target` would hand untrusted code a base-repo token. That trigger is
  unreachable when the PR's base predates the workflow file, does not retro-fire onto already-open
  PRs, and does not run at all on a CONFLICTING PR — so naming it required would leave PRs pending
  forever. The two constraints collide, which is why the remedy is a second workflow rather than an
  edit to the first.
- **`evil-merge-sweeper.yml` runs from the default branch with no `actions/checkout` and no `run:`
  step**, publishing the commit status `evil-merge-sweep`. It reads commit parents and git trees over
  the API only, and the rule is a pure blob-sha comparison that never needs file contents — which is
  what makes `pull_request_target` safe here, the same property `skip-ci-sweeper.yml` relies on.
- **Parity is exact on the gated class and deliberately not claimed elsewhere.** Over all 594 merge
  commits on `main`, the API-shaped detector returns the identical `invented` set as the git-driven
  script — 1 by default (`d59c74bf packages/web/vite.config.ts`), 2 with `--include-tests` (adding
  `6f2b8f21`) — with nothing the script reports and it misses. The non-gated class is not in parity
  and is not published: `git show --cc` is a *dense* combined diff that suppresses hunks sourced from
  a single parent, so an ordinary clean auto-merge differs from both parents by blob yet prints
  nothing. Same corpus, the script reports 75 such files and a blob-only rule sees 161. Telling those
  apart needs line content, so the class is named `contested`, documented as a strict superset, and
  left out of the status.
- **The corpus is recorded, because a live-git parity test would pass for the wrong reason.**
  `deploy.yml` checks out with no `fetch-depth`, so CI runs at depth 1, `git rev-list --merges`
  returns nothing, and the test would compare two empty sets and go green — the same trap that makes
  `fetch-depth: 0` load-bearing in the guard. `scripts/record-evil-merge-parity-corpus.mjs` records
  all 594 merges and 28,537 per-path decisions against the real script's verdict, and the test pins
  the corpus size and both known instances so an emptied fixture fails loudly.
- **The workflow's inlined copy is pinned, not trusted.** No checkout means it cannot import the
  module, so the detector is duplicated inside the `github-script` block; the block between the
  `SHARED-CORE` markers is compared byte-for-byte against the module by the test suite, rather than
  left to a "keep in sync" comment.
- **Budgeted from measurement.** Merge counts per PR range are bimodal (p50 5, p90 246, max 390)
  because stacked PRs carry their parent stack in `base...head`. A sha-keyed tree cache turns a
  100-PR sweep from 10,849 reads into 811, so the cap is 900 and the cron is hourly rather than
  `*/15`. Running out defers the remaining PRs — leaving their status `pending`, which is fail-closed
  — and says so in the job summary; it never publishes a verdict from a partial read.
- **Admin bypass still overrides it**, and the workflow header says so. Both bypass actors on the
  ruleset are `bypass_mode: always`, so `gh pr merge --admin` goes straight through. This is a
  durable signal on the PR, not an enforcement boundary.
- **Validated end to end by executing the workflow's real script against stubbed API data**: it posts
  `failure` on PR #143's actual CI range, and across 120 historical PR ranges it fires on exactly the
  8 that transitively contain `d59c74bf` — 0 false positives. The status context is added to ruleset
  `21489705` only after the sweeper has reported at least once on `main`, so a never-reported context
  cannot wedge the queue.


### Fixed — Browser Back silently discarded a half-filled dialogue wizard; the app now mounts a data router (2026-09-04)

`/projects/new/dialogue` confirmed before discarding on five paths — Escape, the header ×, an
overlay click, the ⌘K palette and in-wizard anchor clicks — and on none of them was the browser's
own Back button. WIC-1765 could not reach it: a `popstate` has already been committed by the time a
listener runs, so the location has changed and the route has re-rendered, leaving nothing to confirm
*before*. Intercepting it after the fact needs a fake history entry, which breaks Back for the whole
page. React Router ships the correct mechanism as `useBlocker`, and it throws `useBlocker must be
used within a data router` under the plain `<BrowserRouter>` the app mounted (WIC-1924).

- **`App.tsx` now mounts `createBrowserRouter`/`RouterProvider`.** One catch-all data route mounts
  the existing route tree unchanged; the router is built at module scope, since building it in the
  component body would discard history state on every render.
- **The route table stays JSX, deliberately.** `useBlocker` reads `DataRouterContext` from
  `RouterProvider` at the top and does not care how the tree below matched, so descendant `<Routes>`
  keep working and blocking still covers every `navigate()` and `popstate` — there is only one
  router. Converting the 30 routes to route objects would instead take five source scrapers to zero
  matches at once (`route-integrity`, `route-title-coverage`, `routeOutline.render`,
  `routeOutline.source`, `routeHeadingOutline`), and this app has no `loader` or `action` to migrate
  because every page fetches through React Query. The route inventory is worth more than the shape.
  Per-route `loader`/`action`/`lazy` remain unavailable until that conversion happens; nothing wants
  them today and it is purely additive.
- **Two bespoke interception mechanisms are deleted, not joined by a third.**
  `hooks/useInAppNavigationGuard.ts` (a capture-phase document click listener) is gone, and so are
  `registerNavigationGuard`/`requestNavigation` on `CommandPaletteContext` — the palette is back to a
  plain `navigate()` and no longer has to know guarded routes exist. `App.dataRouter.test.tsx` greps
  every `src` file for all three identifiers, over comment-stripped source so the prose recording why
  they went is not what keeps it green.
- **The exit path needed care.** `onCancel` itself navigates, so the guard would have blocked the
  app's own confirmed discard and re-opened the confirmation over it. The blocker is disarmed a
  *render* before that navigation, not a line before it.
- **The WIC-1765 suite passes unchanged against `useBlocker`** — 19 tests, no assertion rewritten.
  The fixtures move to `createMemoryRouter`, which is forced by the same fact that forced the
  production change, not a rewrite to match the new implementation.
- **Five new tests, each confirmed load-bearing by mutation.** Four red when the blocker is unwired
  (`useBlocker(false)`), which is the pre-fix state. The fifth is the AC-3 control — untouched
  wizard, Back goes straight through — which by design passes both before and after; it is red
  instead under `isDirty = Object.keys(data).length > 0`, the seeded-state bug from WIC-1621 that
  the untouched-wizard controls exist to catch. `AXE_BASELINE` (8) and the lint ceiling (0 errors /
  26 warnings) are both unmoved.


### Fixed — Four a11y defects behind 18 of the 26 baselined axe findings, dropping `AXE_BASELINE` 26 -> 8 (2026-09-04)

`packages/web` route sweep. The WIC-1926 ratchet is a two-way pin — a new finding fails, and a
*fixed* one fails too until its entry is deleted — so every number below is a test failure that
had to be answered, not a tally taken by hand.

- **Four defects, 18 findings, 14 keys.** Two `<select>` filters on `/resume-variants` with no
  accessible name (8 findings, all four branches); the hidden `<input type="file">` on
  `/resumes/upload` (4); the wizard `role="progressbar"` on `/projects/new/dialogue` (4); and an
  `<article role="button">` in `ResumeVariantCard` that tripped `aria-allowed-role` and
  `nested-interactive` at once (2). Findings, not bugs — the four fixes are four edits.
- **The card is now a plain `<article>`, and its navigation moved into the heading.** The
  interactive role made a widget that still contained the card's own two buttons, so the role and
  the nesting were one defect. A `<button>` inside the `<h2>` carries the click instead: reachable
  by mouse and keyboard, no role on a non-interactive element, `h2` count unchanged at 1.
- **That retired a `jsx-a11y` rule as well, so it is back at `error`.**
  `no-noninteractive-element-to-interactive-role` had exactly one finding tree-wide and it was this
  `<article>`. `BASELINED_RULES` drops it, the file leaves `A11Y_BASELINE` entirely, both
  `--max-warnings` ceilings go 27 -> 26, and the enforcement surface goes 26 -> 27 rules at `error`.
- **The remaining 8 are third-party and stay baselined on purpose.** All 8 are `aria-hidden-focus`,
  `incomplete` rather than a violation, on Radix's own
  `<span data-radix-focus-guard tabindex="0">` sentinels — verified by dumping the offending node,
  not inherited from the previous comment. They are how `FocusScope` traps and returns focus, so the
  fix would be a patch to `@radix-ui/react-focus-scope`. Left as 8 pinned keys rather than an
  `EXCLUDED_RULES` entry so a *real* `aria-hidden-focus` defect written anywhere else still fails.
- **Two unmeasured progressbars named while in the file.** `ResumeUpload`'s upload-progress bar only
  renders in the `uploading` state, which the four sweep branches never reach, so it carried the same
  defect invisibly. Named it too; it moves no baseline number.
- Web only. No API, schema, migration or wire change.


### Added — `useState` seeded from a prop is now a lint error, unless the prop name says it is mount-only (2026-09-04)

`packages/web`. Copying a prop into `useState` snapshots it: the initialiser runs on mount only, so
the parent goes on updating the prop while the component keeps its mount-time copy and nothing
reports the divergence. WIC-1612 / PR #211 deleted four such sites from `FilterPanel.tsx`; WIC-1583
rewrote `OutreachComposer.tsx` after a second platform picker wrote to a value the composer read
once and then ignored.

- **`local/no-usestate-from-prop`, at `error`, with zero findings and no allowlist.** The exemption
  is the repo's own convention rather than a list: a prop named `initial*` declares the mount-only
  contract in the name, which is the decision `main` already made when WIC-1583 renamed
  `OutreachComposer`'s seed prop to `initialContext`. A name-based exemption cannot go stale the way
  WIC-1440's did, where 6 of 8 allowlist entries were dead within two merges.
- **Landed at `error`, not `warn`, so neither `--max-warnings 26` ceiling moves.** WIC-2053 showed
  how coupled those ceilings are to the a11y baselines; `error` plus zero findings touches neither.
  Lint is 0 errors / 26 warnings before and after.
- **The rule reproduces the hand inventory exactly.** Run with its exemptions disabled it reports 5
  sites — `OutreachComposer.tsx:56,57,58,59` and `hooks/useRouteFocusHandoff.test.tsx:55` — matching
  an independent grep-based scan. With the `initial*` exemption on, 2 remain; both are out of scope
  below. `FilterPanel.tsx` is confirmed clean.
- **Boolean-predicate seeds are out of scope, deliberately, and that is the substance of the card.**
  `useState(!!fitAnalysisId)` and `useState(readyAfterMs === 0)` do not copy a prop — they hold a
  boolean whose *default* was conditioned on one — so "the prop and the state have diverged" has no
  reading: the boolean can be false while the prop is set, and that is a legitimate state. Renaming
  either prop to `initial*` was not available: **both props are read live elsewhere in their
  component** (`fitAnalysisId` at `OutreachComposer.tsx:100` and `:223`), so the name would have been
  false. The narrowing has a real cost and is stated in the rule's KNOWN GAPS rather than hidden.
- **The behaviour test is tree-state-independent, because the rule lands at zero findings.** That is
