  exactly the WIC-1903 failure mode: no-op `no-literal-caps-jsx-text`'s single `context.report(...)`
  and its baseline test stayed green, so a dead rule and a working one were indistinguishable.
  `src/test/useStateFromProp-rule.test.ts` lints 31 synthetic snippets through the real resolved
  config. Verified by mutation: no-op this rule's `context.report(...)` and **`npm run lint` stays
  green while 25 of the 31 go red** — the 6 survivors are precisely the assertions that do not depend
  on reporting. Every "must not flag" case carries a differential control, so no exemption can be
  satisfied by a rule that reports nothing.
- **Every KNOWN GAP is pinned, not prose**: laundering through an intermediate local, `memo()`,
  positional-param hooks (`useDebounce.ts:12` seeds `useState(value)` *correctly* — it resyncs in an
  effect), nested components reading a parent's props, and the boolean narrowing above.
- **Test files are in scope on purpose**, stated in `eslint.config.js`: a test-helper component is
  exactly the shape the rule reads, so a carve-out would put the blind spot where nobody looks.
- **`OutreachNew`'s remount key is now enforced.** The comment at `OutreachNew.tsx:38-49` called the
  key deliberate defence-in-depth and then said "nothing in the suite enforces it." Two cases now do,
  pinning its composition from both sides — a change to `fitAnalysisId` must discard a user's edit
  (remount), and a change to `applicationId`, which is absent from the key, must not. Verified by
  mutation in both directions: narrowing the key fails the first and only the first, widening it
  fails the second and only the second. This is the half of the hazard a lint rule structurally
  cannot reach, since the safety lives at the call site and the rule runs at the definition.
- Web only. No API, schema, migration or wire change.


### Fixed — Eleven pages rendered no `<h1>` at all while loading or on error, closing the last 21 route/branch pairs (2026-09-04)

Every route now opens at a single top-level heading on **all four** of its render branches. `MISSING_H1` in `routeOutline.render.test.tsx` is empty and its size pin is **0**, so the `<h1>` rule joins the heading-skip rule as unconditional over all 120 (route, branch) pairs — no allowlist, no exemptions (WIC-2050, under WIC-1864).

- **One defect class, three shapes, and the third is the one worth naming.** Fifteen pairs were pages whose `<h1>` sat below an `isLoading` / `isError` early return, so those branches returned with no heading at all. Four more (`/projects`, `/projects/:projectId`, its file editor) stood a grey skeleton block where the heading goes — but a heading is static copy, or comes off the URL, so there was never a response to wait for; only the subtitle keeps a skeleton. The two `/applications/:id/prep` data branches were the odd shape: the page opened at its own `<h2>`, which is the same WCAG 2.1 AA (SC 1.3.1) failure wearing different markup.
- **The parent card's "Class B" — 6 pairs said to need more than a lift — does not exist.** It came from a `grep <h1` that matched a *comment*: `ApplicationDetail`, `ProjectDetail`, `ProjectFileEditor` and `ResumeVariantDetail` each carry a `// Mirrors the page <h1>` note above `useDocumentTitle`, which sits above the early return because a hook cannot be called conditionally. The JSX `<h1>` is 30-180 lines further down in all four. All 21 were the same mechanical lift, which is why all 21 closed in one pass rather than the 15 the dispatch scoped.
- **Where the heading is genuinely unavailable, the branch shows the same string the tab does.** `ApplicationDetail` and `ResumeVariantDetail` read their `<h1>` off fetched data, so their loading and error branches fall back to `DYNAMIC_TITLE_FALLBACKS`. That is the existing convention rather than new copy: `ROUTE_TITLE_CONVENTION.md` §0.3 makes a route's title its `<h1>` verbatim, so the two must not diverge on the branch where neither has real data yet. Both files now resolve one `heading` const and pass it to both the hook and the element, so they cannot drift.
- **Each fix is a shell component, not a duplicated heading, and that is forced rather than stylistic.** `routeOutline.source.test.ts` pins five of the touched files at exactly one literal `h1`; two copies of the same markup would read there as the page growing a second top-level heading. `CoverLetterNew`'s existing layout component is the pattern each one follows.
- **Lifting the header surfaced a real critical defect that no check could previously see.** `InterviewPrepPage`'s back control is an icon-only `<button>` with no accessible name — axe `button-name`, critical. It went unflagged because the header rendered on *no* branch the route sweep could reach: loading and error returned before it, and the branch the harness calls `loaded` fell through to the not-yet-generated state. It now has an `aria-label` and an `aria-hidden` glyph. Fixed rather than baselined, per that suite's own instruction; `AXE_BASELINE` is unchanged at 22 keys / 26 findings.
- **Verified by the ratchet, in both directions.** The inventory went 21 -> 15 -> 0 across the run, each step failing `has no stale MISSING_H1 entry` with exactly the pairs just fixed and no others — so the count is measured by the suite rather than asserted here. Full `packages/web` suite: **705 passed**, unchanged from `main` except the tests this entry describes.
- Web only. No API, schema, migration or wire change.


### Added — Source content that enters `main` inside a merge commit is now caught, instead of appearing on no review surface at all (2026-09-04)

`packages/api/scripts/detect-evil-merges.mjs` plus an `Evil-Merge Guard` workflow fail a PR whose branch carries a merge commit that *authored* source content — content held by none of the merge's parents (WIC-1979).

- **The blind spot is the finding; the line that exposed it was benign.** Merge `d59c74bf` added three lines to `packages/web/vite.config.ts` present in neither parent. `git log --oneline` between two heads shows only the merge; `git log -S` skips merges unless given `-m`; and GitHub attributes merge-only content to no reviewable commit. So a source file changed between board approval and merge with nothing for a reviewer to look at.
- **Gated on the narrow signal, so the check stays credible.** A hunk that merely differs from every parent also covers ordinary hand-resolutions: over all 594 merges on `main` at `e1bda4e8` that looser rule flags 75 files across 47 merges (7.9%). The gate instead requires every parent to have held the *same* blob — nothing was in conflict, so any difference is content the merge invented. Same 594 merges, that is **2**: `d59c74bf`, and `6f2b8f21`, which created a 329-line `dashboard.metrics.test.ts` present in neither parent. Resolutions are reported under `--report`, never failed.
- **Tests exist for the decision, not the plumbing.** `test/detect-evil-merges.test.ts` (29 tests) runs the parser over `git show --cc` output pasted verbatim from this repository rather than hand-written fixtures, since reading git's grammar is the whole job. `inspectMerge` and `mergesIn` take an injectable runner, so no test needs a repo or depends on this history. Six mutants — including `every` weakened to `some` and the parent list left unsplit — were each killed with the total case count held at 29, so none passed by failing to compile.
- **Non-test source only by default**, widened with `--include-tests`; a test invented in a merge is a review-visibility problem, not a runtime one. The workflow needs no dependency install (the script imports only `node:child_process` and `node:url`) and checks out PR head with full history, because the default depth of 1 would find zero merges and pass every time.
- Tooling and CI only. No API, schema, migration or wire change, and no existing merge on `main` is rewritten.


### Fixed — Three pages skipped `h1 -> h3`, but only once they had content (2026-09-01)

`/projects`, `/resumes` and `/projects/:projectId` each rendered the page `<h1>` and then went straight to `<h3>` for every row title, with no `<h2>` between them — a WCAG SC 1.3.1 level skip that leaves the row titles with no parent heading to belong to (WIC-1827).

- **The skip was on the populated branch only, which is why it outlived the card that was supposed to fix it.** `EmptyState` gained a `headingLevel` prop defaulting to `2` under WIC-1417, so from 2026-08-26 all three pages rendered a clean `h1 -> h2` when the list was empty. WIC-1483 was then closed `done` with its AC-2 ("the 6 unambiguous `h1 -> h3` skips are fixed") half-satisfied: the visible half of the fix looked like the whole fix.
- **Fix is `h3 -> h2` on the three row titles** — each row is a sibling section of the page heading. This matches the resolution already under review on PR #299 (WIC-1675) character for character, so the two merge as a no-op on each other in either order rather than colliding.
- **Each page gains a rendered outline assertion per branch** (`*.outline.test.tsx`, 6 tests), using the existing `getOutline` / `findOutlineSkips` from `src/test/headingOutline.ts`. Asserting both branches is the load-bearing part, not boilerplate: a check that renders one branch — realistically the empty one, since it needs no fixture — reports all three pages clean while the defect is live.
- **That claim is measured, not argued.** Reintroducing the `h3` on each page reds *only* that page's populated test; its empty test stays green (3 of 3). Deleting the page `<h1>` reds both of that page's tests (3 of 3), and deleting a row heading outright reds only the populated one (3 of 3) — the latter is why each test pins the outline as an exact sequence rather than asserting `findOutlineSkips` is empty, since a page with fewer headings also has no skips.
- **The queries carry an explicit 5s budget.** Testing Library's `asyncUtilTimeout` defaults to 1000ms and this repo configures it nowhere; under load on a cold cache the first query in each file failed at ~2.3s. That is a different knob from vitest's `testTimeout`, which WIC-1889 (PR #322) raises to 15s — so this neither duplicates nor depends on that change.
- **AC-3, re-measured on `main` rather than inherited:** the other three of WIC-1483's six (`ReportsNeedsAction`, `ReportsStale`, `ReportsClosedLoop`) are **not** closed — all three are still live. No card is filed for them because PR #299 already fixes all three. `ReportsClosedLoop` is the mirror of this entry: its *empty* branch skips to `h3` while its *populated* branch is a legitimate `h1 -> h2 -> h3`, because its card renders inside a section `<h2>`. Per-branch coverage is required in both directions.
- Web only. No API, schema or wire change.

### Docs — Ruling 2 of the a11y ruling stands; the argument that WIC-1675 should have *been* the axe adoption is refuted, not merely overtaken (2026-09-01)

`A11Y_ENFORCEMENT_RULING.md` §4.2 argued that WIC-1675 ("rendered heading-outline enforcement per route") should be implemented *as* an axe-core adoption **rather than** as a second bespoke utility, and §5 concluded on that basis that "nothing here needs a new card". WIC-1675 shipped as the second bespoke utility (`586712c2`, #299) and shipped well, which left three defensible readings of Ruling 2 — satisfied, superseded, or outstanding — and no disposition. §4.2 and §4.3 now carry one, measured on `main` @ `78e97903` against `axe-core@4.13.0`.

- **§4.2 is superseded: it conflated a _host_ with a _checker_.** The blind spot it names is real — a source sweep cannot see the 26% of headings built from expressions — and it is closed. But the ingredient that closes it is **rendering the component**, not axe's rule corpus. `routeOutlineHarness.tsx` exposes `forEachBranch(factory, options, visit)`, a generic visitor over a mounted `root: HTMLElement`; `collectOutlines` is one visitor over it and PR #339's `routeAxe.render.test.tsx` is a second, on the same harness. "Axe **rather than** a bespoke utility" was a false dichotomy — the answer is both corpora on one host, which is what the tree now has.
- **Building WIC-1675 as axe would have covered strictly less, and this is measurable rather than arguable.** `page-has-heading-one` carries the selector `html:not(html *)`, so it matches only the `<html>` element — and this harness must read from `document.body`, because `/applications/new` portals its entire body into a Radix dialog. The rule is therefore **structurally inapplicable on all 120 (route, branch) pairs**, and the whole `MISSING_H1` inventory of **25 pairs** would have been invisible. Both it and `heading-order` are tagged `best-practice`, not `wcag2a`/`wcag2aa`, so a WCAG-scoped axe config drops them — while Ruling 2's actual target, `aria-prohibited-attr`, _is_ `wcag2a`. The tags run opposite to §4.2's argument.
- **Narrowed, not withdrawn.** `heading-order` does apply and does overlap on the skip half; PR #339 runs axe's full default corpus over the same 120 pairs and reports **zero** `heading-order` findings, independently corroborating the sweep's unconditional no-skip assertion from a second implementation. The h1-presence half has no axe equivalent that can run here at all.
- **§4.3 stands and has now been executed in its stated order, but its precondition was the wrong predicate.** "Only after axe is green" would have been satisfied by a *false* green: axe reports the WIC-1185 shape as **`incomplete`, not `violation`**, so `toHaveNoViolations()` passes on the exact defect that motivated Ruling 2. The precondition to cite hereafter is **green under a helper that fails on `incomplete` too, with a mutant proving that read is load-bearing** — which ADR-011 §4.1 made binding and PR #339 (green, in review) implements. Retirement is also partial by design: the hand-rolled *detector* is deleted, the AT *simulation* (`dropProhibitedNames`) survives inside `axe.ts`, because axe reports that a prohibited name may be ignored and only the simulation shows what the user is left with.
- **The cost of the bad premise was ownership, not code.** §5's "nothing here needs a new card" meant Ruling 2 shipped nowhere and was owned by nobody until WIC-1926 picked it up. Ownership is now explicit in the doc: **WIC-1926** the adoption, **WIC-1942** the 26 frozen axe findings, **WIC-1864** the 25 missing-`<h1>` pairs.
- **The §4.2 Outcome note from #341 is replaced, not left beside the answer.** That note recorded what shipped and explicitly routed the ruling call to WIC-1945; leaving it in place would keep the doc pointing at a question that now has an answer two paragraphs below it. Its facts are carried forward into the disposition. Its one claim with a shelf life — "`axe-core` is still not a dependency" — is deliberately **not** carried forward, because #339 makes it false the day it lands and a frozen decision record should not contain a fact scheduled to rot.

### Docs — `GET /dashboard` returns three top-level keys and the API contract documented two (2026-09-02)

`getDashboardStats` has returned `{ stats, recentActivity, attention }` since `a3d81a7b` (2026-08-26, WIC-1478). `docs/architecture/API_CONTRACTS.md` declared `interface DashboardResponse` with `stats` and `recentActivity` only, its **Example Response** JSON showed the same two keys, and `DashboardApi.getStats()` in the TypeScript SDK section repeated the omission a third time. An entire top-level response key — two thresholds, four counts and four sample lists — was absent from the document the API's own source cites as the contract of record: `DashboardStats.responseRate`'s docstring points a reader at "`docs/architecture/API_CONTRACTS.md`, `GET /dashboard`" for the authoritative shape.

- **Nothing in CI could have gone red.** The code was correct and the contract was merely silent, so no test, type or lint had anything to fail on. It was found by diffing this merge burst's file lists against the docs that describe those files — the same method that found the SC 2.4.2 gap, and again not by any string search. A grep for the retired identifiers (`staleActive`, `staleSaved`, `savedThresholdDays`) returned nothing anywhere under `docs/` at `4957738d`, which reads like a clean bill of health and is really just the absence of any documentation to be stale. That grep stops being empty with this entry, and deliberately so: the five hits it now finds are all in the rename note added below, which is the first time any of those names has been written down where a reader of the contract would meet them.
- **The window is worse than seven days of silence, because WIC-1479 reshaped the block on the way in.** A reader arriving now would have had to reconstruct the payload from source twice over. The new section states the rename field by field, and singles out the one a consumer cannot detect by reading `undefined`: `counts.stale` kept its name and changed its meaning, from every non-terminal status over a hardcoded 7 days to `applied`/`phone_screen` over `staleThresholdDays`.
- **The shape is declared once.** `DashboardAttention` and `AttentionApplication` are written out under `GET /dashboard` → "Attention block"; the SDK section names the type and points at that heading rather than repeating it. This document already carries the reason, under "Cover Letters (Read-Only Reference)": a duplicated declaration is worse than a missing one, because both copies look authoritative and the reader who finds the stale one first has no signal to keep looking.
- **`counts` are full-table aggregates and `samples` are capped at 5 and 2**, so a sample list shorter than its count is expected rather than a truncated count — recorded because it is the reading error the shape invites. Each sample's population and sort order is tabulated by field name, not by position, and the sample caps are attributed to the constants that set them rather than pinned to line numbers.
- **`unsubmittedSaved` is documented as explicitly not staleness.** It is keyed off `createdAt`, and a `saved` application was never submitted, so there is nobody to follow up with. That distinction is the whole point of WIC-1479's rename and it is now stated on the wire contract, not only in the changelog entry that made it.
- **Written against the regions no open PR is editing.** PR #247 is revising the `stats` block of this same interface for WIC-1515; its changed lines and this entry's insertion are separated by unchanged context, and a real three-way merge against its head was run to confirm no conflict rather than inferred from the hunk headers.
- **Documentation only.** No source, schema, wire or test change — the wire already looked like this.


### Added — `axe-core` runs over every rendered route, completing the ruled a11y mechanism (2026-09-01)

Ruling 2 of `docs/design/A11Y_ENFORCEMENT_RULING.md` §4 (WIC-1926). Ruling 1 (`jsx-a11y`, WIC-1483/PR #226) merged 2026-09-01; Ruling 2 had never been implemented and no card owned it, because §5 said "nothing here needs a new card" on the premise that WIC-1675 would be built _as_ the axe adoption. It was built as a second bespoke utility instead, so the premise did not hold. This closes it.

- **The two layers are disjoint, and it is measured rather than argued.** `jsx-a11y` at `strict` — all 40 rules, with a 4-error positive control in the same invocation — returns **zero** findings for `aria-label` on a role-less element, because `role-supports-aria-props` only fires once an element _has_ a role. That is exactly WIC-1185 and WIC-1191. Restoring either defect now fails the suite on axe's `aria-prohibited-attr`.
- **Both restored defects report as `incomplete`, not `violation`** — an element carrying text leaves axe unable to decide whether the author name or the text content wins, which is precisely the ambiguity that made it a bug. **A helper reading `violations.length` alone reports both real defects as clean.** `src/test/axe.test.ts` pins that three-way result (no text → violation; text → incomplete; `role="img"` → pass) against literal fixtures, because the degradation is a one-word edit away and is otherwise invisible: deleting the `incomplete` read reds **exactly one test in the package** — that one. Both component tests stay green, since the components they cover are currently fixed.
- **`axe-core@^4.13.0` is now a declared devDependency, and that is load-bearing rather than bookkeeping.** It was already resolvable on disk as a transitive dependency of `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` (which declares `^4.10.0`), so an undeclared import would have worked locally and in CI today, then vanished silently the day jsx-a11y moved off it.
- **It reuses the WIC-1675 harness rather than building a third one** — all **120 (route, branch) pairs**, plus the two component tests. Two rules are excluded, both because _jsdom cannot answer them_ and neither because the app is exempt: `region` (354 findings, entirely artifact — the app's `<main>` is in `App.tsx` chrome the route harness deliberately does not mount) and `color-contrast` (108 needs-review, 0 violations — no layout, no canvas). Each carries its reason as data, and an id axe stops defining fails loudly instead of excluding nothing.
- **The remaining 26 findings across 22 keys are frozen shrink-only in both directions**, like the lint baseline: a new finding fails, and a _fixed_ one fails until its line is deleted and the two pinned totals are edited down. They sit on four routes — unlabelled `<select>` filters on `/resume-variants`, an unlabelled file input on `/resumes/upload`, an unnamed `role="progressbar"` on `/projects/new/dialogue`, and needs-review on Radix's own focus-guard sentinels. Retiring them is **WIC-1942**. `aria-prohibited-attr` itself finds **nothing** across all 120 pairs, which is a clean result rather than an idle rule — the mutation controls above are what prove it is live.
- **Every assertion is guarded against passing vacuously.** All of them report a defect by returning a non-empty list, so all of them pass over a sweep that collected nothing. The helper throws rather than returning `[]` when axe evaluated no rules; the sweep pins the pair count (120), the thinnest ruleset any pair saw (≥50 rules), and the number of pairs whose tree was non-trivial (≥90).
- **`src/test/prohibitedName.ts` is deleted**, in the ruling's stated order and not before it: land axe → confirm it flags both components the helper was written for → then delete. Its `dropProhibitedNames` survives inside `src/test/axe.ts` because axe has no equivalent for it — axe reports that a prohibited name _may_ be ignored, and only this shows what the user is left with when it is. WIC-1191 is why that distinction matters, and the WIC-1191 mutant reds on both assertions.
- **A now-false claim in `docs/design/ACCESSIBILITY.md` is corrected rather than left standing.** It asserted that "`axe-core` is still not a dependency … the only mention of it anywhere in the tree is a comment in `src/test/prohibitedName.ts:10`" — both halves false as of this change. Its adjacent "until it lands" clause about WIC-1675 was already false on `main`, and is corrected too. The WCAG caveat is **strengthened, not relaxed**: heading order plus a lint rule set _plus axe_ is still not AA, per the ruling's own §7.
- **A second false claim in the same document is corrected: the 21 loading/error pairs are not "nameless" (WIC-1959).** That clause predated PR #336 (`7f8646d2`, WIC-1089) and denied shipped behaviour, which is the worse direction of rot — an overclaim invites the reader to check, a denial tells them not to look. Measured pair by pair at `ca776dda`, with the shell's `RouteTitle` mounted where `App.tsx` mounts it: **all 21 carry a real `document.title`** — 15 from `RouteTitle`, which sits outside every page's render branch so an early return cannot suppress it, and 6 from pages that call `useDocumentTitle` above their own early return (4 reading `DYNAMIC_TITLE_FALLBACKS` while the record loads, 2 titling from a URL param known before any fetch). The complementary control: re-run with `RouteTitle` unmounted and **15 of the 21 fall back to the _previous_ route's title**, so the effect is load-bearing rather than incidental; a one-route mutant (`RouteTitle` skipping `/reports/stale`) reds **exactly that route's two pairs** and no others. **SC 2.4.2 (Page Titled, Level A) therefore holds on all 21.** The `<h1>` defect is untouched and still real — a `document.title` is not a heading, so SC 1.3.1 / 2.4.6 are unaffected and `MISSING_H1` keeps all 25 entries.

### Fixed — a bare `COMPONENT_SPECS` was mangled by an emphasis reformat (2026-09-01)

One CHANGELOG line rendered as `COMPONENT*SPECS ... left the \_decision* open`. It should read `COMPONENT_SPECS ... left the *decision* open`. The wholesale `*x*` -> `_x_` emphasis reformat in #299 (WIC-1675) re-paired the underscore in the bare identifier `COMPONENT_SPECS` with the `_` it was inserting to close `*decision*`, splitting one emphasis span across two unrelated tokens. Net effect on the rendered page: the identifier lost its underscore and displayed as italic `SPECS`, and `decision` displayed a literal backslash.

- **This is why the identifier is now in backticks, not merely un-mangled.** Immediately before #299 the file held 23 occurrences of `COMPONENT_SPECS`: 21 inside a code span and 2 bare. All 21 code-span occurrences came through the reformat untouched — an underscore inside a code span is inert to the emphasis parser. So a code span is what actually confers immunity, and backticking matches the file's own dominant convention; un-mangling alone would leave the line exposed.
- **Being bare is not sufficient to be corrupted — the line must also gain an emphasis delimiter.** Only one of the two bare occurrences was mangled. The other, the `### Docs — COMPONENT_SPECS wireframe casing is now marked per line instead of derived (2026-08-26)` heading, is still bare and came through #299 intact, because its line carries no emphasis for the stray underscore to re-pair with. The salary line was hit only because the reformat was rewriting `*decision*` -> `_decision_` on that same line, supplying the partner delimiter. That heading is left exactly as it is on purpose: it is a landed entry, a cosmetic edit to a pre-existing line is itself the `merge=union` collision vector this class is about, and its exposure is conditional on some future edit adding emphasis to that one line.
- **Blast radius was exactly one line, and that was measured, not assumed.** Pairing every line of the reformat by its emphasis-stripped text, 88 of the 89 rewritten lines round-trip cleanly; this was the 89th. The `\_` escape count across the whole file went 0 -> 1 at #299 and is back to 0.
- **It reinforces the standing rule rather than qualifying it:** do not run a formatter over `CHANGELOG.md` (WIC-1732). This is the first observed instance of that class actually corrupting content rather than only re-arming a `merge=union` seam.

### Fixed — The repo's own formatter was hiding the loudest headings from the caps lint rule (2026-09-01)

`CAPS_PATTERN` admitted a space but not a newline, so a JSX text node spanning more than one line could never match and `local/no-literal-caps-jsx-text` silently reported nothing on it. The formatter this repo mandates is what puts the newline there, which made the blind spot systematic rather than incidental (WIC-1922).

- **The rule was blind to exactly the headings most worth catching.** `.prettierrc` sets `printWidth: 100` and `format:check` globs `packages/**/*.{ts,tsx,css,md}`, so `src/**` is formatter-enforced and the wrapped form is the one that survives CI. A shouted heading was therefore caught while short and dropped out of the rule entirely once it grew past the wrap — the longest, loudest sentences being the ones that escape.
- **`node.value.trim()` → `node.value.trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ')`.** Collapsing internal whitespace is also the accurate reading rather than merely the convenient one: JSX folds a whitespace run containing a newline down to a single space, so the collapsed string is what actually reaches the DOM and therefore the accessibility tree. It is likewise the string quoted in the report and matched against `allow`, so both now key off the rendered name instead of the source layout — without this, an `allow` entry could never have matched a wrapped site.
- **WIC-1922's own worked example does not reproduce, and the tests say so.** That ticket presents `<h3>NOTE: … THE ATTACHED RESUME FIRST!</h3>` as prettier's input and a wrapped form as "prettier's OWN output". Run at the configured width, prettier leaves that line alone: it is **92 columns**, inside the 100 limit. The defect is real and the mechanism is exactly as described — it just needs a heading past the wrap, so the cases here are longer, and each is prettier's verified real output. Components in `src/**` indent deeper than the test probe, so the blind spot opens at a shorter heading there than these cases need.
- **`eslint .` is unchanged at 47 problems / 0 errors**, with zero findings from this rule. The widening closes the gap without surfacing a single new violation or false positive in the tree.
- **The three unpinned KNOWN GAPS are now pinned, each with a differential control.** The rule's doc comment claimed every statement in it about what the rule does and does not catch was pinned by `caps-rule.test.ts`; only the `$` gap actually was. Runtime `.toUpperCase()`, caps in attribute values and caps reaching JSX through a variable binding were unchecked prose. Each now asserts no finding **and** that the same shouted string in a plain text node does flag — because "0 findings" is satisfied just as well by a rule that reports nothing at all, which is the precise failure mode this file exists to catch.
- **Eight mutants, each killed by the cases named for it.** Whitespace collapse reverted → **exactly the 5 WIC-1922 cases**, and `caps-baseline.test.ts` stays green, so that file could not have caught this defect either; reporting path no-op'd → 19 (was 11 before these cases, and it now takes the 3 gap cases with it, which is the controls doing their job); `CAPS_PATTERN` reverted → 10, the 8 punctuation cases plus the 2 wrapped cases that carry punctuation, still sparing the colon-only control; `hasUppercaseClass` forced true → 19, forced false → 5, the 4 `className` cases plus the wrapped R1 heading; acronym check dropped → 3; ancestor walk cut → 1; `HAS_CAPS_WORD` dropped → 1. Fix committed before the controls ran; unmodified re-run green, working tree clean.
- No production code changed. Lint rule and tests only.

### Fixed — Ordinary punctuation walked through the caps lint rule, and nothing could tell the rule was alive (2026-09-01)

`local/no-literal-caps-jsx-text` shipped in WIC-1209 to end the seven-ticket hand-enumeration chain by supplying a completion criterion. Two defects meant it supplied a weaker one than claimed, and that its being alive at all was unobservable. Both were reproduced on merged `main` at `ca97445` before anything was changed.

- **A single trailing period defeated the rule (WIC-1262).** `CAPS_PATTERN` admitted only space, `&`, `:`, `'` and `-`, so any other punctuation dropped the string out of the rule entirely rather than merely narrowing the match. Measured over WIC-1262's nine realistic shouted headings, **eight escaped** — `NOTE: DO NOT SUBMIT.`, `WARNING, READ THIS`, `ARE YOU SURE?`, `SAVE AND EXIT!`, `PROS/CONS SUMMARY`, `KEY POINTS (DRAFT)`, `STEP 1 — GET READY` and the en-dash form. The class now also admits `?`, `!`, `.`, `,`, `(`, `)`, `/` and both dashes, which flags all eight. `eslint .` over the real tree is **unchanged** (0 new problems from this rule), so the widening buys the coverage without a single new false positive. The absolute count this was measured against — 47 problems on this branch — has since dropped to 27 on `main` via WIC-1589's unrelated `jsx-a11y` fixes; this rule's own contribution to it did not move.
- **`$` is deliberately still excluded**, because it risks matching currency-and-caps fragments and `SALARY: $120K RANGE` is rarer than the punctuation cases. The gap is now pinned as its own test case rather than left implicit, so closing it later is a deliberate act with a test to update instead of an accident nobody notices in either direction.
- **The rule's reporting path was unpinned, and a dead rule looked exactly like a working one (WIC-1903).** Once WIC-1440 emptied the shrinking baseline and dropped the `allow` option, `caps-baseline.test.ts` degenerated: one assertion filters an empty list and is vacuous, the other reduces to "the tree has no violations" — which a rule that reports *nothing at all* satisfies just as well. Measured: no-op the single `context.report(...)` call and that file is still `2 passed`, with `npm run lint` green. The rule was the only thing enforcing the class, and nothing in the repo could observe whether it still worked.
- **`packages/web/src/test/caps-rule.test.ts` (new, 22 cases) closes both.** It lints synthetic snippets through the real resolved config rather than over the repo, so it is tree-state-independent and stays valid now that `src/**` is legitimately clean — and it exercises the config wiring (file scope, plugin registration, `error` severity) rather than re-declaring it. It also pins the coupling `caps-baseline.test.ts` depends on but cannot see: that the message text names the offending string in the shape that file parses out.
- **Every negative case is load-bearing only because the positive control shares its run.** A "must not flag" assertion passes identically when the probe path is not linted at all, so the helper additionally fails loudly on zero results and on a fatal parse error, and the file header forbids moving the negative cases away from the positive control.
- **Seven mutants, each killed by the cases named for it.** Reporting path no-op'd → 11 red including the positive control (and `caps-baseline.test.ts` stays green, which is the WIC-1903 claim); `CAPS_PATTERN` reverted → **exactly the 8 punctuation cases**, and *not* the colon-only control that flagged before the widening too; `hasUppercaseClass` forced true (fail-open) → 11; forced false (exemption broken) → exactly the 4 `className` cases; acronym check dropped → **3**, the 2 acronym cases here plus `caps-baseline.test.ts`'s `suppresses every violation it declares` (this entry first said 2; re-measured at this branch's own head under WIC-1922 and corrected); ancestor walk cut to the immediate element → exactly 1; `HAS_CAPS_WORD` dropped → exactly 1. Fix committed before the controls ran; unmodified re-run green, working tree clean.
- No production code changed. Lint rule and tests only.

### Fixed — `packages/web` unit tests get real timeout headroom, so a contended runner stops reading as a code failure (2026-09-01)

`packages/web/vitest.config.ts` set `environment`, `globals`, `setupFiles`, `include`, `exclude` and `restoreMocks`, and no timeout at all — so every test ran against vitest's default 5000 ms. That is not a lot of room for this suite: these are jsdom component tests driven by `@testing-library/user-event`, and their cost is **event-loop turnaround, not CPU work**. User-event's default is `delay: 0`, and `wait()` skips its timer only when `typeof delay !== 'number'` — so `0` schedules a real macrotask on every one of the suite's 89 call sites. The tests are latency-sensitive rather than slow, which is exactly the shape that degrades when the box is busy (WIC-1889).

- **`testTimeout` and `hookTimeout` are now 15 s.** On a quiet box the slowest test here takes ~3.0 s, so the default left about **1.6x** headroom; 15 s restores roughly 5x. Vitest sizes its fork pool from the host, so a 2-core CI runner is already oversubscribed relative to the 4-core box this was measured on — the margin was thin everywhere, not just under a noisy neighbour.
- **Measured, at `--maxWorkers=8` on 4 cores (2x oversubscription), interleaved to control for ambient load:** 10/10 full-suite runs green with the change, against **3 of 4 red** on the unmodified config in the same window. Every failure in the negative control is a timeout clustered at **5116–6357 ms** against the 5000 ms default. The fixed runs still contain 1–3 tests over 5000 ms each — the same slow tests, no longer failing.
- **`userEvent.setup({ delay: null })` was measured and rejected**, rather than assumed. Aliasing user-event to a shim that forces `delay: null` at all 89 call sites cut the five heaviest files from **39.79 s to 33.29 s of test time — about 16%**, which does not cover the 3-5x slowdown contention causes. It also removes a flush these tests currently depend on. Real effect, wrong size, and 89 sites of churn for it.
- **Not a retry.** Retries would hide both this and the next genuine race, which is how the suite carried WIC-1795's router race for weeks.
- **The failing set is not a fixed list of files.** WIC-1889 was filed against `FilterPanel` / `ProjectsList` / `CommandPalette`; those three files are byte-identical since, yet re-measuring moved the failures almost entirely onto `OnboardingModal.step-actions.test.tsx`. What fails is whichever test has least headroom on the day, so the file names in a flake report are a symptom and not an address.

### Fixed — settled by measurement: GitHub's server does not apply `merge=union`, and `.gitattributes` now carries the evidence (2026-09-02)

`.gitattributes` is the first thing anyone reads when a PR flips red, so the question it has answered three different ways actually matters. It originally asserted that "GitHub computes PR mergeability server-side with the default text driver **and does not apply this rule**." That claim was true but unevidenced; the evidence behind it (WIC-1363) counted stale flags. Its mirror image was withdrawn too — WIC-1859 retracted "38 of 38 proves GitHub *does* apply it" as a base-coordinate artifact. The lineage has cost a run of cards: WIC-1291, WIC-1323, WIC-1543, WIC-1699, WIC-1710, WIC-1859 (WIC-1904).

**It is now measured, at the base GitHub actually used, by two designs that agree.** The file states the finding and shows its working.

- **Cross-section — the flag matches the no-union replay 50 of 50.** All 50 open `main`-targeting PRs at `main` `8ab4618`, each force-polled for a *fresh* `mergeable` and replayed at that same commit both with and without the driver: 32 MERGEABLE/clean and 18 CONFLICTING/conflict, no exceptions. The with-union replay disagrees on exactly 15 — the union-dependent set — and GitHub sides with no-union on all 15. Of the 18 genuine conflicts, 15 are `CHANGELOG.md`-only and 3 are real source conflicts (#316, #292, #234).
- **Paired transition — same PR, same head, only the base moved.** Five PRs (#227, #318, #335, #337, #342) held their heads across `main` `7f8646d` → `8ab4618`. At the old base all five were clean without union and all five read MERGEABLE; at the new base exactly three conflict without union, and exactly those three flipped to CONFLICTING. This controls for everything PR-specific, which is what the earlier cross-sections could not do.
- **Why the previous answer was "no evidence" — a selection artifact, not a shortage of data.** The prior revision required the discriminating case to have a *fresh* `refs/pull/N/merge`. That test can never return anything: GitHub only writes the merge ref when the merge **succeeds**, so a conflicting PR always has a stale or absent ref. Measured today, 18 of 18 CONFLICTING PRs have a stale (17) or missing (1) ref, while 26 of 32 MERGEABLE PRs read stale as well. **Ref freshness is one-sided** — FRESH certifies a clean merge, STALE certifies nothing — so demanding a fresh ref on a conflicting PR demands a contradiction. The case looked structurally empty while it in fact had 15 members.
- **The other failure was stale reads, and it has a cheap fix.** `mergeable` is not recomputed on demand, and `gh pr list --json mergeable` returns `UNKNOWN` or a stale value — on this sweep it returned `UNKNOWN` for most of the queue while GitHub recomputed. Poll each PR individually and **retry until it is not `UNKNOWN`**; every "flag says CONFLICTING but it merges clean" result here came from a read taken at a base GitHub had already moved off. Freshly resolved, the flag was exact on all 50.
- **The driver stays, and is load-bearing precisely *because* GitHub ignores it.** With union disabled at `main` `8ab4618`, 15 of 50 flip clean → conflict, and in all 15 the only conflicting file is `CHANGELOG.md`. The local pre-merge sync is what clears the flag, and the driver is what makes that sync free.
- **The operational guidance is unchanged, byte for byte** — "merge main in and push", "do not rebase a PR that others are stacked on", "keep BOTH entries, newest date first". It was correct throughout and is exactly the procedure used to clear #190 and #209. `--attr-source` remains a **global** option that must precede `merge-tree`: placed after it git exits 129, and omitted it silently reads attributes from the working tree and prints a confident wrong answer.

### Fixed — A Quick Wins row no longer states an age the bucket that selected it excludes (2026-09-01)

The Dashboard aggregates select an attention row with `updatedAt < now - staleThresholdDays` — a **fractional** age strictly greater than the threshold — while `QuickWins` reported that age with `differenceInDays`, which **floors**. So a row the server picked at 7.5 days rendered "Company — No update for **7** days" immediately beside an "Attention Required" card advertising the same rows as "**N applications need follow-up (>7 days)**". The user was told a 7-day-old row sat in a strictly-greater-than-7-day bucket. Same shape on the saved rows: "Saved 3 days ago" for a row selected because `createdAt < now - 3 days` (WIC-1575, from the review of WIC-1478).

- **Copy only — no count, threshold, or selection changed.** The numbers were already right; only the sentence rendered next to them was not.
- **The exact count is stated only once the floor clears the threshold.** Below that the row states the bound the selection actually proves — "No update in over 7 days", "Saved over 3 days ago" — so precision is kept for the genuinely older rows (a 31-day row still reads "31 days") and surrendered only in the one window where flooring makes it false.
- **The bound is read off the wire** (`staleThresholdDays` / `savedThresholdDays`), not from a constant in the component, so the copy tracks whatever threshold the server picks rather than re-introducing the same disagreement at a different number. A payload with no threshold degrades to the plain count rather than to an invented one.
- **Regression coverage** pins both directions and both fields: the `(threshold, threshold+1)` window states the bound, ages past it keep their own number, a stale bound of 14 proves the component is not reading a hardcoded 7, and the saved row is bounded against `savedThresholdDays` rather than the stale one. A final case renders `AttentionCard` and `QuickWins` together and asserts the row may not state the bucket's own bound as an exact age. Four mutants were run against the suite — reverting the component, always stating the bound, bounding the saved row on the wrong wire field, and `>=` for `>` — killing 8, 6, 4 and 8 cases respectively.


### Added — `applications.interviewDate` is backed by a real column, so every interview-date render site can finally light up (2026-09-04)

`interviewDate` was consumed by the web app and backed by nothing. There was no column on `applications`, no migration adding one, and no endpoint sending the field — while `packages/web/src/types/interviewPrep.ts` declared it on `ApplicationSummary` and four render sites gated on it (`InterviewPrepCard.tsx:138`, `QuickReferenceExport.tsx:111`, `InterviewPrepPage.tsx:287,368`). Every one of them took the empty branch unconditionally, and TypeScript could not see it: reading a declared-optional property the server never populates is exactly as legal as reading one it does. This is the root blocker under WIC-1823, WIC-1821 and WIC-1798 (WIC-2023).

- **Migration `0026_application_interview_date.sql`** adds `interview_date TIMESTAMPTZ`, nullable, no default, no backfill. **`TIMESTAMPTZ` and not `DATE`**, which is the one real design choice here: the consumers already do `new Date(application.interviewDate)` and format a time from it, so a date-only column would round-trip as `YYYY-MM-DD` and render as UTC midnight — the previous evening for any user west of Greenwich. `nextActionDue` is `DATE` and is the wrong sibling to copy.
- **Threaded through the read and write paths** following `nextActionDue`'s shape but not its type handling: the column is `TIMESTAMPTZ`, so drizzle hands back a `Date` and the DTO needs `.toISOString()` (as `appliedAt` does), while the route validators take `z.string().datetime({ offset: true })` rather than the date-only regex. The `'interviewDate' in input` keying is what lets an explicit `null` clear a scheduled date.
- **RLS was checked, not assumed.** All four `applications` policies are row-level predicates over `user_id` with no column lists, and grants are table-level, so a new column inherits the existing protection. No policy change.
- **The drift-test baseline is now empty**, which is the acceptance criterion: `KNOWN_UNBACKED_FIELDS` no longer carries `interviewDate`, so the guard demands that *every* field the web type declares be backed.
- **Three gates, because the named criterion does not reach the migration.** Measured by reverting each piece alone: reverting `interviewPrep.service.ts` turns the drift test red; reverting `db/schema.ts` leaves it **green** and turns `tsc` red; reverting the migration leaves **both** green. The drift test parses source text and never opens a database, so the column could have been absent from the real schema with every named gate passing. `test/application-interview-date.test.ts` closes that gap against PGlite with the real migrations replayed in journal order — it fails if the `.sql` is unregistered, which is the WIC-1955 silent-skip shape.
- **One over-tight existing assertion relaxed.** `job-fit-analysis-fk.test.ts` asserted migration 0025 held the file-wide maximum `idx` and `when` — i.e. pinned it as permanently last, so it failed on the arrival of any later migration for reasons unrelated to itself. It now asserts 0025 sorts after every entry that *precedes* it, which is what the silent-skip trap actually requires; the file-wide invariant remains covered by the next test.

### Added — The interview-prep `application` payload has a drift guard, so a client type cannot outrun the wire contract unnoticed (2026-09-01)

`InterviewPrepPage` passes `interviewDate` down to two consumers that gate on it — `InterviewPrepCard.tsx:138` renders a days-until-interview countdown, and `QuickReferenceExport.tsx:111` prints the date into the exported quick reference. Neither has ever rendered. The interview-prep endpoint does not send the field, and nothing in the toolchain says so (WIC-1821).

- **The read is legal, which is why nothing caught it.** `application` at `InterviewPrepPage.tsx:287`/`:368` is an `ApplicationSummary` (via `GetInterviewPrepResponse`), not an `Application`, and `ApplicationSummary` declares `interviewDate?: string`. Reading a declared-optional property the server never populates type-checks exactly as cleanly as reading one it does — the optional marker absorbs the absence. The originating report diagnosed this as a read of a *non-existent* property on `Application`; it is not, and the distinction changes the remedy.
- **The client type is wider than the wire contract.** `getInterviewPrep` declares and builds `application` as exactly `{ id, jobTitle, company, status }` — the projection at `interviewPrep.service.ts:634`, the return-type annotation at `:610`, and the object literal at `:647` all agree on four fields, and `getInterviewPrepByApplication:660` repeats the same four. `interviewDate` appears **zero** times anywhere in `packages/api`.
- **Adding the database column alone would not light these sites up.** That is the follow-on feature (WIC-1823), and because the four-field shape is hardcoded in three independent places in the read path, an `applications.interview_date` column plus an `Application` DTO field would leave this endpoint — and therefore both render sites — exactly as dark as they are now. The guard's failure message says so, at the moment someone tries it.
- **`interviewPrep.drift.test.ts` pins the divergence in both directions.** It reads the API service and the web types as text through Vite `?raw` (the packages cannot import each other — the API builds under `rootDir: ./src`), and asserts that every `ApplicationSummary` field is API-backed except an explicit `KNOWN_UNBACKED_FIELDS` baseline, *and* that nothing on that baseline has quietly become backed. One direction alone would rot: absence-only would fail correct work with no guidance, and allowlist-only would let the entry outlive the defect. Two scope-pin cases assert the exact parsed field lists, so a regex that stops matching fails loudly instead of turning the "for each field" assertions green over an empty set.
- **No behaviour change.** The dark branches are left in place deliberately — whether they should light up or be deleted is WIC-1821's open product decision, and this guard is correct under either outcome.

### Fixed — `export_viewed` could never fire, so dashboard tile B1 was pinned at 0% (2026-08-30)

`ResumeExports.tsx` hardcoded `const exports: ResumeExport[] = []` behind a "replace with actual data from API" TODO. `ResumeExportList` invokes `onPreview` only from inside `exports.map(...)`, so with zero rows there was no Preview control to click, `handlePreview` never ran, and `handlePreview` is the **only** `export_viewed` callsite in the bundle. The event was not rare, it was unreachable (WIC-1707, found by the Data Analyst while validating the PostHog build pack).

- **The tile it broke reads as a product failure rather than an unwired page.** Dashboard B tile **B1 — Export View Rate** (`docs/analytics/dashboard-spec.md:75`) is `export_viewed` unique sessions over `resume_upload_completed` unique sessions, target ≥50%, warn <30%. Its numerator was zero by construction, so B1 rendered a red `0%` no matter how many real users arrived. No analytics change was needed to fix it: the event name, its properties and B1's HogQL were already correct and already validated against the live project. B1 begins reporting the moment rows render.
- **The endpoint already existed.** `GET /resumes/:id/exports` has been live in `packages/api/src/routes/resumes.ts` the whole time; this was purely a frontend wiring gap. `resumeService` gains `listExports(resumeId)` and, for the flat `/resumes/exports` route, `listAllExports()` — which fans out over `GET /resumes` because the API exposes no all-resumes export collection.
- **The same stub was pinning a second surface nobody had connected to it.** `useExports()` returned `[]` from a mock service, and `App.tsx` derives `exportCount` from it for the nav badge in `TopNavigation`, `MobileNavigation` and `BottomTabBar`. All three read 0 for every user. Replacing the mock unpins the badge and the page together.
- **Two rendered fields have no data source, and are now absent rather than zero.** `resume_exports` records no file size and no experience ids — its `metadata` is `{ sections, charCount }`, and `charCount` counts characters of the *source* resume text, not bytes of the export. `fileSize` and `experienceIds` are therefore optional on `ResumeExport` and their chips render only when present. This is the load-bearing half of the change: defaulting them would render a confident, wrong "0 B" and "0 experiences", and `formatFileSize(undefined)` renders "NaN MB". Both failure modes are silent, so the tests assert on rendered text.
- **The empty-string `resume_id` is gone without touching the analytics contract.** The page sent `resume_id: resumeId ?? ''` — and `''` is a real value that lands in PostHog as its own breakdown bucket. The flat route has no `:resumeId` param, but every export row carries its own `resumeId`, so `handlePreview` now reads the id off the clicked row and always sends a real one.
- **Reachability is what the tests pin, because a component test cannot see this defect.** Rendering `ResumeExportList` with fixture rows passes just as happily against the hardcoded empty array — it certifies the component, not the fix. The new specs drive the real page with a stubbed API and click the Preview that results. Five mutants were run against them: restoring the empty literal reds 7, restoring `resumeId ?? ''` reds 2, rendering either optional chip unconditionally reds 1 each, and ignoring the route param reds 4.

Still open, and deliberately not in scope: `handleDownload` and `handleDelete` remain `console.log` TODOs. Neither has a backend route to call — there is no export download-url endpoint and no export `DELETE` — so wiring them is API work first.

### Fixed — the outline check named after `/applications` was not rendering `/applications` (2026-08-30)

`KanbanBoard.test.tsx` is one of only two component tests wired to the rendered-outline helper, and its fixture was documented as *"the `ApplicationsList` shape"*. It was not. The fixture is a hand-written `<h1>Applications</h1>` + `<KanbanBoard>`; the real page mounts `SavedFilterShortcuts` between those two, and that panel rendered an `<h3>`. So the live route read `h1 -> h3 -> h2` — a skip, on **every** render branch, not just a populated one — while the check named after the page stayed green (WIC-1834, stacked on WIC-1675).

- **A rendered-outline assertion certifies the composition it renders, not the route it is named after.** The assertions in that file were never the problem; they are good ones, run against a composition the router never produces. Nothing tied the fixture to the page, so it drifted silently — and a green check on a page that skips is worse than no check, because it stops anyone looking. `CoverLetterPreview.test.tsx` is the control showing this is a fixture problem and not a method problem: it is built the same way and its real page genuinely agrees.
- **`/applications` now asserts its own outline through the real composition**, in `src/pages/ApplicationsList.headingOutline.test.tsx`. It mounts the actual page with its actual children, so the drift that caused this is no longer possible by construction rather than by review. The fixture in `KanbanBoard.test.tsx` is kept and re-described as what it is — a minimal host for the board, whose subject is the board's *internal* depth (a column one level below the page, a card one level below its column) — a question genuinely answered at that layer.
- **Two grades the 30-route sweep deliberately does not give.** It pins the **exact** outline rather than the absence of a skip: `h1 -> h2 -> h2` has no skip and is still wrong here, being the shape you get when a card stops nesting under its column. And it covers the page's **interaction** branches — the collapsible filter panel and the save-shortcut dialog are *user* state, so no value of the sweep's `loading`/`error`/`empty`/`loaded` dial reaches them. Both render the same outline as the closed page today, and that identity is the thing pinned: an `<h3>Filters</h3>` on the panel is the obvious next edit to that component and would reopen this exact defect.
- **Six mutants, each with a distinct signature, and the two that matter are invisible everywhere else.** Restoring the `<h3>` reds all 4 new cases and the route sweep's skip assertion, while `KanbanBoard.test.tsx` stays 5/5 green — the measurement that says the check named after the page never graded the page. Moving the shortcuts panel *below* the board, and dropping it from the page entirely, each introduce **no skip**, so the route sweep (10/10) and the fixture (5/5) both miss them and only the new file reds. Giving `FilterPanel` an `<h3>`, and the save dialog an `<h4>`, each red exactly **one** case — the interaction branch named for it — with those components' own 21 and 8 tests green. The `<h3>` -> `<h2>` production fix is WIC-1675's, in the entry below; it is not duplicated here.


### Tests — the catalog-diffs migration chain is built from the journal, not a directory listing (2026-09-03)

`catalog-diffs-userid-not-null.test.ts` said its migrations were "the real files read off disk in journal order". They were a `readdirSync` of the migrations directory, sorted by filename; `meta/_journal.json` was never opened. `db:migrate` is journal-driven — drizzle reads the journal and applies each entry in array order — so the suite and production agreed only by convention, and the WIC-1955 defect class (a renumbered migration inheriting a `when`, permanently skipped) was invisible to it (WIC-1978, split out of WIC-1955).

- **The chain is now `meta/_journal.json`, applied in `entries` order.** The two-phase split is positioned by journal index rather than by `filter((f) => f < THIS_MIGRATION)`, which was a second, quieter copy of the same filename-order assumption.
- **The `*_rls` skip moved from the listing to the tag.** `0016_personal_info_rls` and `0019_onboarding_status_rls` are journaled migrations, so filtering them out of a *directory listing* read as "drizzle does not run these", which is false. They are dropped by tag after the journal is read, because PGlite has no `auth.users` to GRANT against — a harness limitation, now stated as one.
- **The divergences the old builder could not see are three assertions rather than assumptions**: the applied chain equals the journal minus the RLS grants, order preserved; every `.sql` on disk is journaled and every journaled tag has a file; and journal order still matches a filename sort, so a renumber that breaks that convention reds the suite instead of silently applying a different chain than `db:migrate` does.
- **Graded by the mutation the card names.** Deleting a journal entry while leaving its `.sql` on disk: the old builder is **7/7 green** on both `0023` (the migration under test) and `0006` (an entry nothing in the file touches); the new one exits non-zero on both. The `0023` case is reported as a failed assertion rather than a throw in the `describe` body on purpose — a collection throw yields `no tests`, which tallies as "not failing" in exactly the sweeps meant to catch it.
- **Defence in depth, and no production code changes.** The broader journal guard is `scripts/audit-migration-journal.mjs` from WIC-1939, still unmerged in PR #338; this file no longer depends on it being there. 10/10 green, with the original 7 assertions unaltered.

### Hardened — api test mocks no longer hand-enumerate service exports (2026-08-30)

A `vi.mock` factory that lists a module's exports by hand is an **allowlist**: anything it does not name comes back `undefined`. That is harmless until a *different branch* adds an export to that module, at which point the merge breaks with **zero textual conflict** — the two sides touched different files, so neither branch's own CI can see it. WIC-1499 / PR #143 is the instance that already happened: `onboarding.routes.test.ts` went 26 passed to 6 failed / 20 passed on merge, because the factory named five exports of `onboarding.service.js` and the PR added a sixth, read inside a `.superRefine` that runs while the Zod schema is built — so `for...of undefined` threw at *router construction* and every request 500'd, with no missing-mock error to read (WIC-1701).

- **62 of 86 service-module factories now spread the real module** — 60 converted here, 2 that already did — via `async (importOriginal) => ({ ...(await importOriginal<...>()), fn: vi.fn() })`, so a newly added export arrives on its own instead of as `undefined`.
- **24 sites keep total replacement on purpose and now say so**, one line each. `auth.test.ts`, `security-headers.test.ts` and `spa-fallback.test.ts` mock whole services to `() => ({})` only so routes register; those suites never invoke a handler, and spreading the real module would pull DB imports in for no assertion. `db/client.js` is out of scope for the same reason.
- **Two sites were already safe and were left alone** — `interview-prep.routes.test.ts` (`importOriginal`) and `dialogue.routes.test.ts` (`vi.importActual`, which keeps the real Zod schemas). Recognising only the first idiom would have flagged correct code and rewritten a working mock.
- **A guard fails on any newly added hand-enumerated service mock**, so the class cannot regress the way the instance did. Per WIC-1483 it asserts how much was *read*, not just what was *found*: the walk is cross-checked against an independent directory listing, file and call-site counts carry floors, and an inline positive control proves the classifier still detects the defect on a corpus that is now clean. A staleness test in the opposite direction fails an orphaned justification comment, so an allowlist entry cannot outlive the mock it excused.
- **The guard caught 8 live sites the moment `main` was merged in** — exactly the WIC-1499 class one bullet up, self-demonstrated: `application.change-owner.test.ts`, `project.touch.tenancy.test.ts` and four in `resume-upload-correlation.test.ts` hand-enumerated a service's exports in test files that landed on `main` after this branch forked, and are now converted to spread. `project.guards.test.ts`'s `storage.service.js` mock is a real in-memory fake keyed on an `OBJECTS` map, not a spy stub — spreading the real module there would pull in R2/filesystem I/O the suite has no way to satisfy, so it takes the `// deliberate-total-mock:` exemption instead. As a side effect, spreading `project.service.js` in `resume-upload-correlation.test.ts` also silences a benign `[vitest] No "projectFileKey" export is defined on the mock` warning that fixture was throwing on every run.

### Fixed — 20 of the 47 baselined `jsx-a11y` findings; two rules are back at `error` (2026-08-30)

WIC-1483 adopted `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` and pinned 47 pre-existing findings behind a both-directions ratchet rather than fixing them in the adoption PR. This is the first slice of WIC-1589, which owns them. **All 19 `label-has-associated-control` findings and the 1 `no-redundant-roles` finding are fixed**; both rules are deleted from `BASELINED_RULES` and are `error` again, the enforcement surface goes **24 → 26** rules at `error`, and `--max-warnings` goes **47 → 27** on both `lint` and `lint:fix`. The ratchet asserts equality in both directions, so the 27 remaining entries in `A11Y_BASELINE` and the two ceilings could not have been lowered without the fixes actually landing.

- **19 unlabelled controls were two different defects wearing one rule name.** 15 were `A form label must be associated with a control` — a `<label>` sitting as a *sibling* of its input with no `htmlFor`, so clicking the label did nothing and a screen reader announced the field unnamed. Those took `htmlFor` + a matching `id`. The other 4 were `A form label must have accessible text`, which is a different failure and would have been mis-fixed by the same edit: the `<label>` *does* wrap its control correctly, but its visible text sits three levels deep, past the rule's `depth: 2` traversal.
- **Three `<label>`s were not labels at all, and `htmlFor` would have been a lie.** `OutreachComposer`'s "Platform" names a radio **group**, not any one radio; it is now a native `<fieldset>` + `<legend>` (merged against WIC-1583, landed independently on `main` in the interim — a `role="radiogroup"` + `aria-labelledby` `<span>` fix was reconciled away in favour of it during this branch's merge; both close the same finding). `OutreachNew` no longer has a platform picker to label at all: WIC-1583 deleted its duplicate control as a live bug — the page and `OutreachComposer` disagreeing about which platform was selected — and the finding went with it. `WizardContainer`'s "Technologies used" names `TechStackPicker`, a multi-control composite with no single control to point at — now `role="group"` + `aria-labelledby`. `ProjectFileEditor`'s "Preview" captioned the rendered-markdown pane, which is not a form control in any sense; it is now a `<span>` naming a `role="region"`. Pointing `htmlFor` at any of these would have satisfied the linter while promising an association the DOM cannot honour.
- **The 4 depth failures were fixed two different ways, and neither is an `eslint-disable`.** `AmbiguityResolver`'s "Skip" option had two nested wrappers where one would do; collapsing them puts the text where both the rule and a terse screen-reader summary can reach it, with no visual change. `CoverLetterGenerator`'s three radio-card groups (tone, length, emphasis) keep their layout and take an explicit `aria-label={option.label}` — which also *improves* the announced name, from the run-on of title + "Recommended" badge + description that the subtree yields, down to "Enthusiastic". Verified against a live negative control: the pre-fix markup still reports the finding under the same probe that reports the fixed markup clean.
- **`no-redundant-roles` was the one genuinely free finding; the other two "free wins" were not free.** `ApplicationCard`'s `role="article"` on an `<article>` is deleted. But the card's suggested slice-1 also listed `no-noninteractive-tabindex` (`ApplicationCard:120`) and `no-noninteractive-element-to-interactive-role` (`ResumeVariantCard:39`), and neither is mechanical: both are the *same* "clickable card" defect as the `no-noninteractive-element-interactions` finding sitting beside them, `ApplicationCard` is `draggable` with nested Edit/Delete `<button>`s, and both cards contain an `<h3>`. So a `<button>` is invalid content-model, and a stretched-overlay button would swallow the kanban drag. Left for the interaction slice with the rest of its defect rather than split across two PRs by rule name.
- **Every count in the config and the suite was re-derived, not decremented.** `24 error / 8 warn / 2 off` becomes `26 / 6 / 2`, asserted against the resolved config; the `label-has-for` note now says its successor is at zero rather than "baselined at 19"; the "a new instance lands as a 48th warning" prose is now 28th against a ceiling of 27. The `A11Y_ENFORCEMENT_RULING.md` §6 table is **deliberately not edited** — it is the frozen `743cfeb` record the ruling was decided on, and §7 already warns that its counts drift; a dated progress note above it points at `A11Y_BASELINE` as the live source of record instead.
- **27 remain, and they are the ones with real user impact.** 9 `click-events-have-key-events` + 6 `no-static-element-interactions` + 5 `no-noninteractive-element-interactions` are 20 findings over the same handful of call sites — `onClick` on a `<div>`/`<tr>` with no keyboard path, on all four Reports pages among others, which keyboard users cannot reach at all. Plus 5 `no-autofocus` (per-site judgement; a command palette is a legitimate use), 1 `no-noninteractive-tabindex` and 1 `no-noninteractive-element-to-interactive-role`.


### Fixed — the STAR picker's "Recommended" section has data at last, so `fitAnalysisId` stops being a phantom (2026-09-03)

`listStarEntries` hardcoded `relevanceScore: undefined`, and it is the field's only producer. `StarEntryPicker` filters that section on `relevanceScore != null && >= 0.8`, so the filter had no possible input and the section could never fill. It was **dead rather than wrong** — the heading is guarded by `recommendedEntries.length > 0`, so nothing empty ever rendered and no user saw a fault, while `showRecommended={!!fitAnalysisId}` read like a live gate and was not one (WIC-1820, spun off from the WIC-1519 / WIC-1813 ruling).

- **The join, not a new scorer.** `GET /star-entries` now takes an optional `jobFitAnalysisId` and merges the stored analysis's `recommendedStarEntries[].relevanceScore` by entry id. No score is recomputed here: `analyzeJobFit` already scores the `quantified_bullets` rows it read and stores their ids verbatim, and `listStarEntries` lists that same table, so the two id spaces are **identical** and the join needs no mapping. That correspondence is the one load-bearing claim a type checker cannot see — both sides are `string` — so it is pinned against a real Postgres with the real migrations replayed, not a stub.
- **The card's premise was half stale, and only half.** It was filed reading "no job-fit analyses table exists"; WIC-1652 / #283 has since shipped the table, the `id` on `AnalyzeJobFitResponse` and the owner-scoped read, and #167 fixed the picker's threshold from `80` to `0.8`. What survived re-measurement is the clause this entry closes: the field still had no producer. The "delete the feature" branch the card offered is therefore moot.
- **An unresolvable id is refused, not ignored.** A stale or foreign `jobFitAnalysisId` is a 422, because degrading to "no scores" would make it indistinguishable from an analysis that recommended nothing — the phantom-identifier behaviour under a new name. Presence is `!== undefined`, so `''` is a supplied id that does not resolve rather than an absent one (the WIC-1818 trap), and the route's `z.string().min(1)` turns `?jobFitAnalysisId=` into a 400 rather than a silent no-op.
- **Scoped fail-closed, and the read takes an owner *term*.** The analysis lookup conjoins `ownerScope`, whose absent-owner branch is `IS NULL` rather than the whole table, and "not yours" and "no such analysis" are the same answer so it cannot be used to enumerate other users' analyses. `relevanceByStarEntryId` takes the owner scope rather than an optional owner of its own — the `[SIG]` shape `audit-owner-predicates.mjs` exists to stop spreading, which it duly caught on the first draft.
- **Graded by mutation, with the pre-fix code as one of the mutants.** Five mutants, each confirmed to still compile by holding the collected test total at 8: reverting the join kills 2, making an unresolvable id lenient kills 4, dropping the owner term kills 2, emitting `0-100` instead of a ratio kills 2, and dropping the id from the page's fetch kills both web assertions. The unit mutant is why the suite asserts a below-threshold entry is *excluded* — "Recommended is non-empty" alone is satisfied by any `0-100` producer, since every such value clears `0.8` trivially.
- **`relevanceReasoning` stays dark, deliberately.** `RecommendedStarEntryDTO` carries no reasoning to join, and re-deriving one here would be a second, silently divergent copy of the scorer. The picker already guards that render on truthiness, so it costs nothing to leave unset and say so.
- **`CatalogEntryDTO` was documentation and is now checked.** Nothing referenced it, so `listStarEntries` is annotated with it and its `relevanceScore` is branded `Ratio` per ADR-008 §1, matching the web mirror.

### Added — `relevanceScore` has a ruling, and the `fitAnalysisId` behind it turns out to be a phantom (2026-08-30)

WIC-1519 asked whether `relevanceScore` — one name over a `[0,1]` population and a `[0,100]` one — is two concepts with two names or one concept with one unit. `docs/architecture/RELEVANCE_SCORE_TERM_RULING.md` answers it, ratifies ADR-008 rather than competing with it, and records the one clause the answer does not close. Documentation only; no code changes (WIC-1813 / WIC-1519).

- **The ruling already existed, unmerged, and checking first was the whole job.** ADR-008 answers WIC-1519 directly and a four-PR stack (#166 → #167 → #168 → #249) implements it end to end. None of it is on `main`: at `a46c63a` there is no `packages/api/src/types/units.ts`, no `packages/web/src/types/units.ts` and no ADR-008, so WIC-1519's premise — "WIC-1514's brand would make the mismatch a compile error" — is not true of `main` today. All four PRs are open and `MERGEABLE`; the gate is merge, not authorship. Writing a fifth opinion would have been the exact defect the card was filed about — a second source of record for one term.
- **The answer is one concept, one unit, with the deviant carrying its unit in its name.** `relevanceScore` is a `Ratio` in `[0,1]` — the fraction of a job's requirements a bullet matches, with a real denominator at `job-fit.service.ts:882-883` and `resume-variant.service.ts:155`, never persisted. `relevanceScorePct` is a `Percent` integer in `[0,100]` — an LLM's holistic judgement of a STAR story, prompted at `interviewPrep.service.ts:315`, clamped at `:548`, stored in an `integer` column (`schema.ts:708`). **The deviation is legitimate, not sloppy:** a `[0,1]` ratio cannot survive that column (`0.85` rounds to `1`), so unifying downward buys a migration and an LLM contract change for nothing, and unifying upward overstates a genuine fraction's precision. That is precisely why ADR-008 §2 puts the unit in the name rather than in a comment.
- **`CatalogEntry.relevanceScore` stays, typed `Ratio` — deleting it would revert tested work to save two lines.** #249 leaves it "correctly untouched" and `catalog.service.ts:512` still hardcodes `relevanceScore: undefined`, so this is the one WIC-1519 clause the stack does not close.
- **"Just populate it" is a feature, not a fix, because there is nothing to populate it from.** No job-fit analyses table exists among the 21 in `schema.ts`; `AnalyzeJobFitResponse` (`types/index.ts:260`) has no `id` field; and `POST /catalog/job-fit/analyze` persists nothing. `jobFitAnalysisId` is never dereferenced anywhere in the API — its only substantive uses interpolate it into an LLM prompt as the literal string `` `Job Fit Analysis ID: ${id}` `` (`cover-letter.service.ts:217`, `resume-variant.service.ts:355`). So the `fitAnalysisId` that `CoverLetterNew.tsx:65` reads off the query string is a **phantom identifier**: no endpoint can have produced it and none can resolve it. Populating the field first requires persisting analyses — a table, a `GET` by id, tenancy and retention.
- **Consequence: `StarEntryPicker`'s "Recommended" section is structurally unreachable, and it is dead rather than wrong.** `recommendedEntries` needs `relevanceScore != null`, which its sole producer never sets; the heading is guarded by `recommendedEntries.length > 0`, so no empty section renders and no user sees a fault. `showRecommended={!!fitAnalysisId}` (`CoverLetterGenerator.tsx:333`) reads like a live gate and is not one. This is the *delivered-but-unreachable* class, not the undefined-term class the card was filed under, and it survives the entire unit ruling untouched.

### Added — ADR-012 rules that job fit analyses are persisted, and finds the "dead" column is doing harm (2026-08-30)

WIC-1652 found three `WorkflowChecklist` props no caller can supply truthfully — `hasFitAnalysis`, `fitScore`, and the `recommended` badges derived from them — because a job fit analysis is never stored, and asked for a ruling: persist it, or delete the props and the four `job_fit_analysis_id` columns. `docs/architecture/adr/ADR-012-job-fit-analysis-persistence.md` rules **persist**. Decision only; no behaviour changes here (WIC-1809, routed from WIC-1652).

- **The table is already specified — it was never built.** `DATA_MODEL.md:981` gives `interview_preps`' DDL as `job_fit_analysis_id TEXT REFERENCES job_fit_analyses(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`, and `:1128` lists the `interview_preps → job_fit_analyses` relationship as `N:1 (optional)`. So this was not an open choice between two designs: the four bare `text('job_fit_analysis_id')` columns (`schema.ts:411`, `:431`, `:531`, `:683`) are a documented foreign key that regressed to `text` when its referent was skipped. The doc is itself half-finished — it references the table in a FK and in the relationship index but never defines it — which is why the gap survived review.
- **The columns are not vestigial, and the status quo is worse than the card knew.** `jobFitAnalysisId` is an accepted *request* field on three generation endpoints, typed `z.string().optional()` with no format or existence check, and because it can never be dereferenced it currently satisfies `JOB_CONTEXT_REQUIRED` (`cover-letter.service.ts:144`, `resume-variant.service.ts:211`), **waives `TARGET_INFO_REQUIRED`** (`:164`, `:225`), and becomes the entire job-description context handed to the LLM — literally ``jdContext = `Job Fit Analysis ID: ${input.jobFitAnalysisId}` `` at `cover-letter.service.ts:217` and the same at `resume-variant.service.ts:355`. In `interviewPrep.service.ts:494` any non-empty string silently suppresses the `NO_FIT_ANALYSIS` warning. `generateSchema` is `.strict()` with no `.refine`, so `POST /cover-letters/generate` with `{"jobFitAnalysisId":"x","selectedStarEntryIds":[...]}` is accepted today, skips both guards, and generates against the context string `Job Fit Analysis ID: x`. That is a live output-quality defect, which is why "leave it" was never available.
- **Removal is not the cheap option it looks like.** Because the field waives `TARGET_INFO_REQUIRED`, deleting it is a breaking change to two public endpoints — the guards must be restored unconditionally, rejecting requests that are valid today — on top of editing four tables, three request schemas, `API_CONTRACTS.md`, `UC-6_RESUME_VARIANT_API.md` and both DTO layers. Neither option is a pure deletion, so cost was not the tiebreaker; contradicting the documented data model was.
- **The frontend already carries the association and the API drops it.** `WorkflowChecklist` links to `/job-fit-analysis?appId={id}` and `JobFitAnalysis.tsx:23-24` reads `appId` and loads the application, but `analyzeJobFitSchema` (`catalog.routes.ts:127-131`) accepts only `jobDescriptionText | jobDescriptionUrl`, and `analyzeJobFit` receives no `userId` — only a `clientId` for rate limiting. The owning application is known in the browser and discarded at the API boundary.
- **Persistence is a product requirement independent of the checklist.** `analyzeJobFit` is LLM-backed and returns `X-RateLimit-Remaining`/`X-RateLimit-Reset`, while `JobFitAnalysis.tsx:26` holds the result in `useState` alone — so a page refresh destroys the analysis and costs the user rate-limit budget to reproduce.
- **A fifth acceptance criterion is added, and it is severable.** AC-5 (validate the id, feed the stored analysis to the LLM, make `NO_FIT_ANALYSIS` depend on a resolvable row) is the only user-visible harm on `main` and does not depend on the table — it can land first as a boundary rejection. AC-1..AC-4 then unblock WIC-1652 and the `hasFitAnalysis` half of WIC-1536 / PR #217. Measured at `main` @ `a46c63a`.

### Fixed — the Dashboard's applied-volume metric named a calendar week and measured a rolling seven days (2026-08-30)

`appliedThisWeek` is computed as `new Date()` minus seven days — a window that ends now and slides forward with every request. It was rendered under two labels that both denote the current calendar week: `Applied This Week` on the Dashboard's Recent Activity card and `This Week` on the `DashboardStats` tile. A user who submitted two applications on Thursday and nothing afterwards opened the Dashboard the following **Monday** and read `Applied This Week: 2`, having submitted nothing that week. Deterministic — no threshold, no volume of data, no race. Both labels now name the rolling window (WIC-1743, under AC-N12 of the UC-5 spec).

- **Relabelled rather than re-windowed, and the choice is enforced rather than noted.** Making the count calendar-week-to-date would contradict AC-N10, which defines the metric as the last seven days regardless of status.
