That reason stands on its own and deliberately does not appeal to the `appliedThisMonth` sibling, which cannot carry the argument: it is `setMonth(getMonth() - 1)`, so it measures 28 to 31 days rather than a flat 30 (2026-03-31 looks back 28, 2026-02-28 looks back 31), and it has no label to be consistent with, since it reaches no surface. `appliedWindow.test.ts` asserts the API service contains no `getDay()` call — the only way to find the start of the current week with a JS `Date` — so a silent re-windowing reds the suite and forces the AC-N10 amendment the card asks for, instead of it being made by accident.
- **The day count is single-sourced and pinned to the arithmetic it describes.** Both labels are built from `APPLIED_WINDOW_DAYS` in `packages/web/src/constants/appliedWindow.ts`, so they cannot drift from each other; a `?raw` source audit reads `oneWeekAgo = new Date(now - 7 * DAY_MS)` out of `packages/api/src/services/dashboard.service.ts` and asserts the captured number equals it, so they cannot drift from the window either. The regex is anchored on both identifiers and its match count is asserted to be exactly 1 **before** the number is read off it — a renamed variable would otherwise turn every assertion in the file into a vacuous pass. (Resynced against WIC-1515, which had already moved this arithmetic off `setDate`/`getDate` onto a `DAY_MS` multiply by the time this branch merged main.)
- **The render assertions deliberately do not import the label constants.** Comparing the rendered text against the same constant the component renders is a tautology: it would stay green if someone set `APPLIED_WINDOW_LABEL = 'This Week'`. They match on the shape AC-N12 requires instead — the window is named, and no calendar period is — and the "no calendar period" case counts over the whole rendered tree rather than the two known nodes, because the defect being closed was one label copied to a second surface.
- **The value control caught its own vacuity.** Asserting the count immediately after locating the label read `0`, not the fixture's `2`: the labels are static and resolve against `Dashboard`'s zeroed pre-fetch fallback, so a `findByText` on a label proves nothing about whether the query settled. It is now a `waitFor`. The fixture's first draft also had `appliedThisWeek` and `inReview` both equal to 2, which would have let the assertion pass by matching a neighbouring stat; every figure the screen renders is now distinct.
- **The two design docs that draw this tile were corrected in the same change.** `WIREFRAMES.md` (two blocks) and `COMPONENT_SPECS.md` both rendered the cell as `This Week`; the ASCII cells were widened to fit `Last 7 Days` with the surrounding box widths preserved exactly. `COMPONENT_SPECS.md` §5 gains a `Window semantics` note recording that the `appliedThisWeek` **prop name** is a legacy of the original calendar-week reading and is not a statement about the window — nothing in CI checks prose, so leaving the drawings saying `This Week` would have shipped a document the code falsifies.
- **Not fixed here, and filed separately:** `CommandPalette.tsx` and `SavedFilterShortcuts.tsx` both offer an `Interviews This Week` shortcut whose filter is status-only and carries no time window at all. Same phrase, worse mismatch, but a different defect — those surfaces render no window metric, so AC-N12 does not reach them.


### Docs — the applied-window rationale no longer cites a sibling defect that was fixed underneath it (2026-09-04)

`packages/web/src/constants/appliedWindow.ts` argued that the `appliedThisWeek` relabel does not rest on its `appliedThisMonth` sibling, on the grounds that the sibling "is `oneMonthAgo.setMonth(getMonth() - 1)`, so it measures 28 to 31 days rather than a flat 30". That premise is dead: WIC-1777 replaced the computation with `new Date(now - 30 * DAY_MS)`, and `dashboard.service.ts` now carries a comment documenting exactly the `setMonth` overflow it removed. The file was describing a defect that no longer exists, in the present tense, as the reason for a decision (WIC-1777).

- **The conclusion is unchanged and the argument still holds** — it just rests on the half that is still true. `appliedThisMonth` remains unusable as support because it has no label to be consistent with: **nothing in `packages/web/src` reads it.** All five occurrences are inert — the DTO declaration, the `appliedWindow.ts` prose itself, two test fixtures supplying it inside a whole `DashboardResponse`, and the `Dashboard.tsx` pre-fetch fallback, which sets it to `0` for DTO shape and then drops it (the `displayStats` object built directly below omits the field, and `DashboardStats.tsx` never names it). So AC-N12 does not reach it.
- **Records what is still owed.** The computation is an honest rolling 30 days; the *name* is not. Any surface that ever renders the field has to label it "last 30 days", which is the AC-N12 obligation the original card raised and the reason this is worth stating rather than deleting.
- **Docs only.** No behaviour, no exported value, no test expectation changes.

### Fixed — an apostrophe in JSX copy silently disabled the navigation audit's comment stripper (2026-09-04)

`stripComments` in `packages/web/src/test/route-integrity.test.ts` is a character scanner that treats `'`, `"` and `` ` `` as string delimiters, because `App.tsx` declares `path="/*"` — a string literal containing a block-comment opener — and a stripper that opens a comment there deletes the routes after it. But the scanner is not JSX-aware, and **a lone `'` in JSX prose is not a delimiter**. `Don't` was read as an opening quote, so comment detection stayed suspended and the rest of the file passed through verbatim: the stripper became a no-op, and every route commented out below it re-entered the route table (WIC-1724).

- **One character of ordinary English was the whole difference.** Measured at `1463eccc`: adding `<p>Don't forget to review</p>` to `App.tsx` and changing nothing else takes the file from 18 passing to **1 failed**, on `strips every JSX comment opener out of the real App.tsx`. That canary is why this was loud rather than silent — WIC-1551's defect could not return unnoticed — but the only remedy it left was to reword the copy. An apostrophe in `App.tsx` red CI.
- **`'` is now exempt when it is welded to the end of a word**, which is prose, and still a delimiter everywhere else. The test is the **immediately** preceding character, not the preceding non-whitespace one, and that is load-bearing in the dangerous direction: `return 'x'` and `case 'x':` are real string literals whose nearest non-whitespace neighbour is a letter, so the whitespace-skipping form — the one originally suggested — stops suspending on them and opens a comment at any `/*` inside. That is the over-strip class, which WIC-1551 established is the worse of the two. A quote welded directly to an identifier is not valid JS/JSX, so the narrow test has no matching false positive; `keeps a single-quoted string that follows a keyword intact` pins it, and is the single test the whitespace-skipping variant kills.
- **A second finding, unasked for: the over-strip control against real source had already gone vacuous.** The route-table floor assertions were documented as catching it, on the reasoning that `path="/*"` is the only in-string comment opener and `/` the only route between it and the next closer. That reasoning was true when written and `App.tsx` moved underneath it — WIC-1089 inserted a one-line JSX comment at line 91, between the hazard at line 87 and the first `<Route path="/">`, and its closer now ends the over-strip window before any route. **Measured with quote suspension removed outright: the route table is identical — 31 entries, `/` and `/settings` both present — so both floor assertions stay green against a scanner with no string handling at all.** The comment that armed them still claimed otherwise; it is retracted in place.
- **Replaced with a control keyed on the hazard rather than on a consequence of it.** `keeps the path="/*" string literal intact in the real App.tsx` asserts the literal survives stripping, which is a direct statement that quote suspension works and cannot be disarmed by an edit that merely moves what follows the hazard.
- **Graded by mutation, with a compile gate.** Six variants, each required to collect all 23 tests so a variant that fails to parse cannot read as green: reverting the fix kills exactly the two new prose tests and nothing else; dropping the quote branch and a naive-regex stripper each kill 6, now including the new real-`App.tsx` control; the whitespace-skipping heuristic kills exactly the keyword test; a no-op stripper kills 7. Full `packages/web` suite 632 passed, lint 0 errors, `tsc -b --force` clean under the locked 6.0.3.

### Added — the dialogue wizard confirms before discarding unsaved answers (2026-08-30)

WIC-1621 ruled draft persistence out of the dialogue wizard, and WIC-1495 removed the write, the "Save Draft" button, the 30-second autosave and the Ctrl+S handler that fed it. That is the right call — all four promised a restore no code could perform — but it leaves closing the wizard as total, silent loss. `Escape`, the header close button and in-app navigation away from `/projects/new/dialogue` now each raise a confirmation first, reusing `ConfirmationModal` with `variant="danger"` (WIC-1765).

- **Dirtiness is measured against the seeded initial state, and that is the whole point.** `data` is seeded with `{accomplishments: [], jobFit: [], techStack: []}`, so the obvious predicate `Object.keys(data).length > 0` is true before the user types anything — the exact bug that made the removed autosave fire unconditionally on an untouched wizard. The load-bearing tests here are therefore the _untouched wizard never prompts_ ones, not the happy-path ones: every "does prompt" test passes under that bug, so on its own none of them says anything about it.
- **One dismissal funnel, because the wizard is a Radix dialog.** WIC-1181 made `WizardContainer` a modal `Dialog.Root`, so `Escape`, the header × (a `Dialog.Close`) and an overlay click all arrive at a single `onOpenChange`; routing that into the guard covers all three, and picks up the overlay click the card did not list. `ConfirmationModal` renders _inside_ `Dialog.Content` so Radix stacks the layers and only the topmost answers `Escape` — which is what makes `Escape` mean "keep editing" while the confirm is up, rather than a second discard request.
- **The in-app navigation path the card describes no longer exists, and the one that does was unguarded.** Nav links are the obvious answer, and the first cut of this change intercepted capture-phase clicks on in-app `<a href="/…">`, justified by the wizard having no focus trap. WIC-1181 inverted both halves of that: the modal marks the whole nav `aria-hidden` and inert, so no user can click it, while the ⌘/Ctrl+K palette's shortcut listener is on `window` and is unaffected. Measured with the wizard open — the palette's search box renders with **no `aria-hidden` ancestor**, two dialogs on screen. So the click interceptor had become a guard on a path users cannot take, and the one live way to navigate out of a dirty wizard had none.
- **Fixed with a single-slot navigation guard on `CommandPaletteContext`**, consulted by the palette immediately before it navigates (it closes first, so a confirmation does not render underneath it). `useInAppNavigationGuard` registers into it, so the click half and the programmatic half land in the same `pendingHref` and one confirmation renders either way. With nothing registered the palette behaves exactly as before, and `useNavigationGuardControls` deliberately does not throw without a provider — unlike `useCommandPalette` — so standalone tests of either component still stand up. **Still not total: browser back/forward, and any future `navigate()` caller that does not consult `requestNavigation`, are not covered and cannot be generically without a data router (WIC-1924).** `useBlocker` is the right tool and throws `useBlocker must be used within a data router`; `App.tsx` mounts a plain `<BrowserRouter>` and migrating it is a whole-app change, not a wizard change. The hook says all of this at its definition rather than reading as a complete guard.
- **The fixture change is pinned by its own control.** The three navigation tests now drive ⌘/Ctrl+K instead of the nav link. Quietly swapping what a test drives is how a real failure gets dodged, so a separate test asserts the nav link is present in the DOM and _unreachable_ through the accessibility tree; making the wizard non-modal reds it.
- **There is no "has completed" latch, and adding one would be a bug.** Completion leaves through `onComplete`, which never routes into the discard request, so AC-4 needs no special case. A latch would also disarm the guard exactly when it matters most: `DialogueCapture.handleComplete` catches a failed create and only `alert()`s, leaving the wizard mounted with every answer still typed in and still saved nowhere. A test pins that failure shape.
- **No `beforeunload`**, per the ruling: browsers substitute their own generic string, so the copy cannot survive, and it fires on tab close where the user has no recourse. A test asserts its absence.
- **The card's AC-5 asked for something that would have reintroduced the previous bug.** It required `git grep dialogue-wizard-draft` to return zero hits. It does not, and must not — WIC-1495 deliberately keeps the `dialogue-wizard-draft-` prefix registered in `appStorage.ts` so copies already on users' disks are cleared at their next sign-out; deleting the name strands that data permanently. The invariant asserted instead is the one that matters: no write path, checked against the wizard's own source.
- **Focus management is inherited, not claimed.** The card said not to describe this guard as focus-managed, because at the time `ConfirmationModal` declared no `role="dialog"`, no `aria-modal` and no focus trap. **That premise expired: WIC-1181 has since landed**, and `ConfirmationModal` is now a Radix `Dialog` with `useDialogFocusRestore`. This change adds nothing on that axis and asserts nothing about it — it reuses the shared component, which was the right call before the fix and still is. This is a nested dialog, so focus restores to the wizard control rather than the page.

### Added — `listCoverLetters`' owner conjunction is now measured, not assumed (2026-08-30)

`cover-letter.service.ts:389` builds `and(...conditions)` with the caller's `eq(coverLetters.userId, userId)` inside it. The predicate is **correct as shipped** — this is a coverage gap, not a live defect. But nothing in the repo could tell: flipping that single `and` to `or` left the entire API suite green, because `listCoverLetters` was reachable only through a *mocked service* in `cover-letter.routes.test.ts`, so no test ever rendered its `where` clause. It was the ninth owner-bearing conjunction in that file and the only one the `and`→`or` matrix did not kill. New `packages/api/test/cover-letter-list.tenancy.test.ts` closes it (WIC-1614, found while re-reviewing PR #159 at `9f44eaa`).

- **The mutation is conditional, so the test's shape is load-bearing.** With an owner and no other filter, `conditions.length === 1` short-circuits to `conditions[0]`; there is no `and()` to flip and the owner-only list stays scoped under the mutant. Widening requires `userId` **plus** at least one of `status` / `company` / `search`. A negative case that lists with no filters therefore passes under the mutant and proves nothing — so all three guards pair the owner with a second filter, and the owner-only case is kept at the bottom explicitly labelled a non-guard, pinning the short-circuit branch rather than the conjunction.
- **The victim fixture is separated from the caller's rows by the owner term alone.** It is a `draft` at `Acme` exactly like the attacker's. Had the second filter done any of the excluding, the mutant would have been caught by the status term and the file would have been measuring the wrong thing.
- **Two independent oracles per guard.** The fake `getDb()` filters fixtures through `applyTenancyPredicate`, so the returned DTO list is honest — a stub that resolves a canned row set whatever predicate it is handed reports green against the leak and the fix alike. On top of that, `expectScopedTo` re-evaluates the captured clause against probe rows, so a wrong-table term or a missing `where` fails too (WIC-1491 / WIC-1502).
- **`ilike` stays unmodelled and is still decisive.** The `company` and `search` guards constrain a column the evaluator deliberately reads as UNKNOWN. Under `and` the foreign row is excluded by the owner term (`false ∧ unknown = false`); under `or` it becomes `unknown` and is admitted. The mutation is caught without the harness pretending to understand pattern matching.
- **Reaching the function at all required the full builder chain.** `listCoverLetters` chains `.orderBy().limit().offset()`, and takes the `.orderBy()` hop *without* a `.where()` when no condition applies, so both the pre- and post-`where` builders carry the whole chain. A `limit()` resolving straight to a promise is what made this service function unreachable from a fake db, and is much of why its owner term went unpinned.
- **Verified as a mutation, not asserted.** Anchor matched exactly 1 site; the mutant typechecks (`tsc` clean) and runs, so `passed + failed == 4 == baseline` rather than reading green by failing to compile. Predicted kill count stated before the run and met exactly: **3 killed, 1 survivor** (the labelled non-guard). Across the full suite the mutant's only failures are those 3 — 3 failed / 736 passed, reproducing the original all-green finding and showing this file is the sole detector. Service restored byte-identical (`cmp`); the diff is purely additive. Pristine: **739/739 API tests pass**, `tsc` clean.


### Docs — `Job Application Manager` is retired from the repo front doors, `docs/architecture/` and `docs/analytics/` (2026-09-04)

The product name is `Careerpin` (ruled under WIC-1102). Two earlier passes were deliberately narrow — WIC-1950 closed the user-facing strings, WIC-1954 the `packages/web/src` comments and `docs/design/` titles. This is the remainder outside those two boundaries: 21 occurrences across 17 files, all of them prose except two.

- **`Careerpin` is a proper noun, so it drops the definite article.** "The backend for Careerpin", not "the backend for the Careerpin". Where the article attaches to a following common noun it stays — "the Careerpin backend", "the Careerpin API", "the Careerpin codebase".
- **The two non-prose sites are metadata, not identifiers.** `packages/api/package.json` `description` (the `name` is `@wic/api`, untouched, and the package is `private: true` so nothing is published) and the header *comment* on `packages/api/wrangler.toml` (the Worker `name = "jobapp-api"` on line 4 is untouched). Neither is read by any code, CI step or deploy script — checked before editing, because a Worker rename is a production incident and a package rename breaks workspace resolution.
- **The five ADRs were a judgment call, and they moved.** An ADR records a decision as it was made, and all five predate the rename, so renaming them is arguably the falsification-of-evidence problem that keeps `ROUTE_TITLE_CONVENTION.md` frozen. They moved because every one of the five *describes the system* — "requires persistent storage", "codebase has evolved", "was originally designed" — rather than quoting the old name as a string. The distinction is quotation, not date.
- **`ARCHITECTURE.md` also carried the only wrong-cased `CareerPin` outside `CHANGELOG.md`**, in a line reading "CareerPin (the Job Application Manager) is…". The parenthetical was the rename's own scaffolding and is now redundant, so the line is simply "Careerpin is…".
- **Four classes are deliberately left alone**, which is why this was a listed sweep and not a `sed`: historical quotations that are evidence of the pre-rename state (`ROUTE_TITLE_CONVENTION.md`, `NOTFOUND_PAGE_DESIGN_SPEC.md`), the ruling's own argument (`CONTENT_STYLE.md`), the "this used to say" markers and the negative assertion in `title.test.ts` (inverting `expect(title).not.toContain('Job Application Manager')` silently guts the test), and the generated `.gitleaks-baseline.json` plus `CHANGELOG.md` as a historical record.
- **`docs/AUTHENTICATION.md` is in scope but deliberately not in this change** — PR #349 already edits it, and taking it here would have manufactured a conflict with a stack that is open now.
- Verified by re-running all four `docs/design/*.py` audits: `doc-reference-audit.py` resolves **322** references, and the modal-focus, route-title and wireframe-casing audits are clean. Prose plus one JSON metadata field, so nothing compiles differently.

### Tests — the project `updated_at` re-stamp is now graded on its slug half, not just its owner half (2026-09-02)

`touchProject` has been owner-scoped since WIC-1433 (`fd7e1d40`) and has required the owner outright since WIC-1554 (`54460cc2`), so the cross-tenant write WIC-1676 reported is not live on `main`. `test/project.touch.tenancy.test.ts` pins it against regression and closes a coverage gap the existing suites left open (WIC-1676, verified under WIC-1970).

- **Test-only.** No production file is modified. An earlier revision of this change also added `if (!userId) return;` to `updateProjectFile`, `createProjectFile` and `deleteProjectFile`; that was dropped as unreachable — `assertProjectOwned(slug, userId)` is the first statement of all three and already throws `userId is required to access a project` via `requireOwner`, so the guard could never be reached with a falsy owner.
- **The gap was real and measured, not hypothetical.** Mutating `touchProject` alone against `main` @ `4957738d` and running `project.tenancy.test.ts` + `project.sibling-owner-required.test.ts` (35 tests): dropping the owner term reds 2 tests, `and`→`or` reds 2, but **dropping the *slug* term while keeping the owner is fully green at 35/35**. That mutant leaks nothing across tenants — which is exactly why every existing cross-tenant assertion accepts it — yet it re-stamps *all* of the caller's own projects on every file save, reshuffling their `listProjects` ordering, which sorts on `updatedAt DESC`. This file reds it.
- **Structural, not a substring match.** `expectScopedTo` (WIC-1491) renders the real drizzle clause and evaluates it against probe rows; `idKey: 'slug'` grades the slug half by *column*, so an owner term that replaced the slug term rather than joining it is caught. A `toContain('"user_id" = $')` check passes for all three mutants above.
- **Each mutant held the suite at its baseline count**, so none of them merely failed to compile and read as a kill. Note that `or` is not imported by `project.service.ts`: an `and`→`or` mutant needs the import added first, or it reports a false GREEN.
- **Not a clean bill of health for these functions.** This grades the database predicate only.

### Fixed — the navigation audit read a commented-out `<Route>` as a live route (2026-08-29)

`route-integrity.test.ts` builds its route table by splitting `App.tsx` on the literal `<Route` and reading each chunk's `path=`. A commented-out route still contains that literal, so it entered the table as if it were mounted. Found while reviewing PR #173 (WIC-1531); pre-existing on `main` and not introduced by that PR (WIC-1551).

- **It failed green in both directions at once.** A commented-out route on its own is reported as an orphan — loud, and survivable. But a commented-out route _plus_ a link pointing at it is fully green: the phantom route absorbs the dead link, and the link in turn credits the phantom route as reachable. Commenting out a route while leaving a button pointing at it is an ordinary way to disable a feature, and it produced a dead button neither direction of the audit could see.
- **Sanitised once at the import, not inside each scraper.** `stripComments` runs on the raw `App.tsx` source and every scraper consumes the result. WIC-1531 adds a second scraper that mirrors this same split to read each route's element; because it reads the same binding, it inherits the fix on merge rather than needing the patch applied twice. A `StrippedSource` branded type makes that structural: passing the raw import to a scraper is a compile error (`TS2345`), so the sanitisation cannot be routed around later.
- **The stripper is a character scanner, and that is load-bearing.** `App.tsx` declares `path="/*"` for its catch-all layout route — a _string literal_ containing a block-comment opener. The obvious regex stripper opens a comment there and swallows everything through to the closer on the `/dashboard` note below it, deleting the `/` (Dashboard) route from the audit's own table. That over-tightened failure is the more dangerous of the two: the bug being fixed here is noisy, whereas an audit whose route table is quietly missing live routes passes while guarding nothing. A quote suspends comment detection, so a mis-read quote _usually_ under-strips — but not always, and the exception is reachable from ordinary English. A desync that closes _inside a double-quoted string_ swallows that string's opening quote and shifts double-quote parity from there on; `path="/*"` is then read as a bare comment opener after all. Measured against the real `App.tsx`: `<p>Sarah's applications</p>` above `<div title="Don't panic" />` — a possessive and a contraction, no regex literal required — takes the route table from **30 entries to 29**, dropping `/`, and reds three cells. The floor assertions over the real file are what catch that, and they name `/` because `path="/*"` is the only in-string comment opener in the file and `/` is the only route between it and the next closer, so an over-strip starting at that hazard cannot avoid dropping a route they name.
- **Under-stripping is the safe direction for route loss, but it is not harmless — and it has a live trigger.** The scanner is not JSX-aware, and a lone `'` in ordinary JSX copy is not a string delimiter. `Don't` reads as an opening quote and suspends comment detection until the _next_ `'` — a bounded window, not the rest of the file. Everything inside that window passes through verbatim, so over that span the stripper is silently a no-op, reopening this exact bug. Measured on this branch: `<p>Don't forget to review</p>` above a commented-out `<Route path="/legacy">`, plus a live link to `/legacy`, is **10 passed/10, fully green**; changing only `Don't` to `Do not` reports the dead link. A canary over the real `App.tsx` asserts that no JSX comment opener survives stripping, which makes that desync loud instead of green, with a staleness control asserting the raw source still contains an opener so the canary cannot go vacuously true. Found in review of PR #223. What makes the canary sound is structural rather than incidental: a route commented out in `{/*` form carries its own opener into the window with it, so the opener survives stripping exactly when the route does — the commented route is its own tripwire, whatever the rest of the file looks like. Known limit: it catches a desync that swallows a `{/*` opener — the shape that can carry a `<Route>` into the table — not one that swallows a bare `//` line comment.
- **Pinned in both directions, per the WIC-143 technique.** A commented-out route (JSX, block and line forms) must not enter the table, _and_ a live route must still be found — either cell alone is satisfied by a broken stripper, since returning the source untouched passes the second and returning an empty string passes the first. A fixture reproducing `App.tsx`'s exact `path="/*"` hazard pins the over-tightening direction, and a floor assertion over the real `App.tsx` names the two routes that bracket that hazard, so an over-strip against live source cannot pass.
- **Test-only.** No production file is modified and no route, link or component behaviour changes.

### Docs — ADR-003 still offered a null owner as a legitimate local-dev state, which ADR-010 retired (2026-09-02)

ADR-003 lists the local auth bypass as a feature in three places, and its Migration Path step 4 ends *"or left as null for local-only"*. ADR-010 §D3 ("Local development gets an owner, not an absence") superseded that: the bypass now supplies a `LOCAL_DEV_USER_ID` defaulting to the `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` sentinel that migration `0017` backfills to. Nothing pointed from ADR-003 to that supersession, so the older and more discoverable document still told readers a null owner was fine (WIC-1962).

- **The error direction is what makes this worth fixing.** `user_id IS NULL` in a multi-tenant table is precisely the shape the `packages/api` owner-predicate guard exists to police. An ADR that overclaims invites someone to check it; one carrying a retired affordance says *don't look*. Addendum A now states the supersession, and all three affected claims are annotated in place rather than silently edited.
- **Neither ADR's Status changes.** ADR-003 is still `Accepted` — Supabase Auth, `jose` verification and per-user `user_id` isolation all still bind; only the null-owner affordance is retired. Per the Status-line convention (WIC-1932), a Status line records whether a decision **binds**, not whether its cleanup has landed.
- **The addendum reports the implementation gap instead of hiding it.** At `main` `8ab4618` D3 is *not* implemented: `LOCAL_DEV_USER_ID` appears only in comments and tests, and `plugins/auth.ts:31-33` still returns with `request.userId` unset. ADR-010 sequences D1 before D2, but D2 landed first (WIC-1554), so `projects`, `catalog`, `resume-variants` and `interview-preps` all answer 400 in bypass mode today. That is a sequencing artifact, not a reversal, and it closes when WIC-1964 lands D3.
- **It also settles PR #316.** That PR proposed per-caller `if (!userId)` short-circuits to keep project routes working in dev mode — the one design D1 commits us to deleting. Ruled against and recommended closed as superseded; its three dev-mode tests are carried onto WIC-1964 as acceptance criteria rather than deleted.

### Docs — the site-wide SC 2.4.2 build gate was missing from the accessibility enforcement table (2026-09-01)

PR #336 (`7f8646d2`, WIC-1089) gave every route its own `document.title` and shipped four test files to hold it there, one of them a site-wide completeness sweep. `docs/design/ACCESSIBILITY.md` — the document whose whole purpose is to inventory which accessibility guarantees are enforced and which are still a reviewer's eye — did not mention it: no `document.title`, no SC 2.4.2, no `ROUTE_TITLE_CONVENTION.md`, nothing. A shipped WCAG Level A build gate was invisible in the one place a reader goes to find out what the build gates are.

- **This is the failure mode CI cannot see.** No test, type or lint can go red when only the contract dissents; the code was right and the doc was silent. It was found by diffing the merge burst's file lists against the docs that describe those files, not by any check in the repository.
- **The row states what the sweep proves and what it does not.** `route-title-coverage.test.ts` parses `App.tsx` as raw source and reconciles it against `constants/title.ts` in *both* directions, so a `<Route>` added without a title fails CI and a deleted route cannot leave a dangling title. It does **not** check that a title *describes* its screen, and it sweeps the seven hook-titled routes only for *calling* the hook, never for the string they pass.
- **Inserting the row re-parented three sentences elsewhere in the file, and all three were repaired in the same commit.** Two read "the last row of the table" and meant the WIC-1675 route sweep, which the insert displaced; both now name `routeOutline.render.test.tsx` explicitly, because a positional pointer rots every time the table grows. A third read "the six checks in the table above" and is now seven. A table row is a counted list item: check the lead-in and every downstream ordinal before adding one.
- **Not fixed here, because the lines are contended by open PRs.** The "What remains unverified" paragraph still says the loading and error branches leave the page "nameless", which #336 made false; PR #339 is rewriting that exact paragraph from a pre-WIC-1902 copy. `constants/title.ts` opens by saying the old shared title covered "all 31 routes", which is neither the 30 routes that render nor the 32 the title table accounts for; PR #346 carries that line verbatim as an addition. Both are routed to the PR owners rather than fixed on `main`, where the fix would land as a conflict against work already in flight.


### Security — There is no anonymous authenticated caller: a `sub`-less JWT is rejected, and every project lookup requires an owner (2026-08-27)

WIC-1434 (above) required an owner in `getOrCreateProjectBySlug` and described the fallback left in its siblings as "the deliberate local auth-bypass dev mode". Measured, it was broader than that, and it was destructive. `middleware/auth.ts` set `c.set('userId', (payload.sub as string) ?? null)` and called `next()`, so a **validly signed, non-expired JWT carrying no `sub` claim** was authenticated with `userId: null` — with Supabase fully configured, on a path that is not in `PUBLIC_PATHS`. Every route launders that to `undefined` (`c.get('userId') ?? undefined`), and the services read `undefined` as "no owner filter". Reproduced at PR #163 head `4622934` on PGlite plus a real object store: `getProjectBySlug(SLUG, undefined)` returned another user's project id, name, description and true file count, and the `DELETE /api/projects/:projectId` flow composed exactly as `routes/projects.ts` composes it left **0 rows for the victim and emptied their object-store namespace** — `deleteProject` builds its delete prefix from `project.userId`, the victim's. Found reviewing PR #163 (WIC-1554).

- **The decision, written down, because the recurrence is that each fix scoped itself to one function and left the shared helper's fallback intact.** Both halves of the card's suggested shape are implemented rather than one: the boundary now rejects an identity-less token, *and* every predicate requires an owner. Neither is load-bearing alone — the service guards still hold if the middleware regresses, and the middleware still holds for the routes this card did not touch.
- **Five predicates degraded, in three distinct shapes, all keyed on `projects.user_id`** — enumerating by the owner *column* rather than by call shape is what found the last two. `getProjectBySlug` and `touchProject` degraded to `slug = $1` (and `touchProject` is an `UPDATE` with **no `LIMIT`**, so an owner-less file save re-stamped every tenant's row holding that slug); `getProject` and `deleteProject` to `id = $1`, with `deleteProject` reusing the same predicate for the `DELETE`; and `listProjects` to `where(undefined)`, which is not a permissive predicate but *no* predicate — it returned every tenant's projects, not one slug's worth. `assertProjectOwned` was an explicit `if (!userId) return;`, so the one guard positioned to backstop the others was a no-op for exactly the caller that needed backstopping.
- **Requiring the owner is a total fix here, not a trade**, on WIC-1434's premise re-checked against the tree: `createProject` is the only `insert(projects)` in `src/` and it rejects a missing `userId`, and `projects.user_id` is `NOT NULL` (migration `0017_enforce_userid_not_null.sql:29`). Every row has a real owner, so an owner-less predicate could not match "the anonymous user's project" — only somebody else's. There was no correct outcome to preserve.
- **The cost is stated rather than discovered later.** In the local auth-bypass dev mode — `SUPABASE_URL` *and* `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` both absent, per ADR-003 — the project routes now answer `400` instead of operating on an implicit shared user. That mode has been unable to *create* a project since WIC-1434, so this makes an existing dead end honest instead of letting reads and deletes wander into a real user's rows. The bypass branch itself is untouched and pinned by a test.
- **The `sub` check is not `?? null`.** That admits an empty-string `sub`, which is falsy and degrades identically at every call site downstream, and the old `as string` was a compile-time assertion with no runtime check at all — a numeric `sub` passed straight through. Both branches needed the fix, HS256 and the ES256/JWKS path production actually uses; a matrix covering only HS256 would have left the live one open.
- **Verified by reverting each fix alone against a kill count predicted first — 13 of 13 cells matched, including two controls that correctly killed nothing.** Predicting the count rather than counting sites is what caught the two tests that were passing for the wrong reason. The disclosure case used `.catch((e) => e)`, so when the reverted code *resolved* it captured the leaked `ProjectMeta`, read `undefined` off `.message`, and passed its own no-secret scan — the assertion passed precisely when the disclosure it was written to detect occurred. The end-to-end delete case asserted only that the flow rejected *somewhere*, and `deleteProject`'s guard caught it at step two, so no single mutation could kill it while half the fix was missing; it now grades *where* the flow stops. Both cells were under-kills against the prediction, which is the only reason they were found.
- **Guards refuse before `getDb()`**, and the tests grade that with a call spy: several guards here answer the same `BAD_REQUEST`/400, so a code-and-status assertion alone is satisfied by the wrong one. Each carries a distinct message and each mutation cell names which test it expects to kill.

### Added — the rendered heading outline of every route is now a build gate (2026-08-30)

WCAG 2.1 AA (SC 1.3.1) has been an accepted NFR with nothing enforcing heading order. Layer 1 (WIC-1483/PR #226) added `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` and **cannot** close this: the plugin has no `heading-order` rule, and heading order is not a property of any single element, so a per-file lint is structurally blind to it. This is layer 2 (WIC-1675) — it renders all **30 routes × 4 branches = 120** (route, branch) pairs under jsdom and reads the outline a screen reader would build.

- **The defect class is compositional, so the check has to be too.** `/cover-letters/new` (WIC-1571) was the proof: the page file had no heading, the child component had the `<h2>`, and _neither file was defective on its own_. A source-order scan of either one reports clean. The sweep mounts the real page, its real children, its real hooks and React Query, stubbing only the `services/api` barrel — a chokepoint, so a thirteenth service reaches the harness by construction rather than by someone remembering to add it.
- **Every heading-level skip is fixed, and that rule now has no allowlist.** Nine files had headings moved from `h3` to `h2` — eleven headings in all, since `/reports/stale` and `/reports/needs-action` each moved two. They are the row cards on `/projects`, `/projects/:id`, `/resumes`, `/resume-variants` and `/catalog` (5); the report row _and_ the empty-state message on `/reports/stale` and on `/reports/needs-action` (4), plus the empty-state message alone on `/reports/closed-loop`, whose card heading is correctly an `<h3>` under a section `<h2>` (1); and `/applications`' Filter Shortcuts panel (1). `/login`'s `<h2>` became the `<h1>` it always should have been; it is the one route `ProtectedRoute` does not wrap, so nothing above it could supply a heading. Measured on the merge-base: **43** defective pairs — 14 carrying a skip and 29 without a clean `<h1>`, two disjoint sets. After: **25**, none of them a skip. The 18 pairs fixed are those 14 skips plus `/login`'s four branches.
- **The 25 remaining pairs are an inventory, not an exemption**, and it is a one-way ratchet. Almost all are the same shape — the page renders its `<h1>` only on the happy path, so the `isLoading`/`isError` early returns come back with no heading at all. `MISSING_H1` lists them with a staleness guard in _both_ directions: fixing a pair without deleting its line **fails**, and the list's size is pinned so entries cannot be added quietly to make a new defect pass.
- **Three harness defects were found and fixed before any finding was trusted, and each one failed silently.** Reading the outline from `container` rather than the document body scored `/applications/new` — a Radix dialog that portals out — as _zero headings on all four branches_, indistinguishable from a page that renders none. Flushing a fixed number of ticks instead of waiting on the query cache made two consecutive sweeps of the same tree disagree on three routes. And a bare `Proxy` mock reported only `__esModule` as an own key, so every named import threw _inside_ the query function, React Query caught it, and all four branches rendered the **error** state while the sweep stayed green and claimed four branches of coverage.
- **The gate caught a regression on `main` the moment the two were merged, which is the whole point of the card.** WIC-1141 (#97) replaced `WizardContainer`'s `<h1 id="wizard-title">` with a bare `<Dialog.Title>`. Radix renders that as an `<h2>` — correct for a dialog nested inside a page, but this dialog _is_ the page: `DialogueCapture` is its only call site and emits no heading of its own, so `/projects/new/dialogue` was left with **no `<h1>` on any of its four branches**. Neither file is defective read alone, and the merge is textually clean, so nothing but a rendered per-branch sweep could see it. Restored with `<Dialog.Title asChild>` around the `<h1>`, which keeps Radix's accessible-name wiring — asserted here, not assumed: the child receives the generated id and the dialog's `aria-labelledby` still points at it. The same merge renamed `ProjectsList`'s "Create New Project" `<h2>` to a `Dialog.Title`; that one is a rename rather than a deletion, so the source guard now counts both spellings, and counts an `asChild` title as contributing nothing of its own so the child is not double-counted.
- **All eleven changed files are paired with a source guard naming the file that owns the heading.** An outline assertion alone cannot tell the correct fix from promoting a shared component's `<h2>` to `<h1>` — both make the outline start at 1, and a mechanism that certifies the wrong fix is not enforcement. The guards also close the one direction the render sweep is blind to: _deleting_ a heading rather than demoting it leaves an outline that still opens at one `<h1>` with no skip, so it reads as clean. The per-file heading counts are therefore pinned exactly, in one table that drives both the guards and the coverage check: each guard records its own name as it runs, and the coverage check compares _what ran_ against the table, so a guard cannot be deleted while its name stays on the list. An earlier revision kept those two as separate literals and was anti-correlated with its own claim — deleting a guard passed, deleting a name failed. The AC-3 premise is measured rather than assumed: `App.tsx`, `ProtectedRoute`, `TopNavigation`, `MobileNavigation` and `BottomTabBar` are asserted to emit no heading of any level, so "the page owns its `<h1>`" stays a fact.
- **Base drift broke the sweep three ways before it landed, and two of them failed quietly.** `main` advanced ~390 commits between this branch's head and its merge. `NotFound` gained a `useCommandPalette()` call, which throws with no provider above it — and because that throw happened during collection it failed the whole suite and **skipped 7 of its 10 tests**, so the headline "no route skips a heading level" assertion did not execute at all. Merged as-is the layer would have shipped **inert**, which is the failure mode this card exists to prevent. The harness now mirrors `AppShellProviders` from `App.tsx`. `main` also added `/cover-letters`, which the route table's own completeness meta-assertion caught — working exactly as designed — and it passes unexempted (`h1` on `loading`, `h1>h2` on the other three). Third, the new `coverLettersForApplication` runs during `ApplicationDetail`'s render and calls `.trim()` on each letter's `targetCompany`/`targetRole`, so the shared fixture row had to carry them.
- **`route-integrity.test.ts` was scanning its own directory as application source.** Its `/test/` exclusion cannot match a sibling: Vite normalises `../test/name.tsx` to `./name.tsx`, leaving no `/test/` segment. Harmless while `src/test/` held only `headingOutline.ts` and `prohibitedName.ts`; the new route table carries concrete URLs and surfaced it.

### Changed — Web reads the interview-prep relevance score as `relevanceScorePct` (2026-08-26)

The interview-prep population is the one that deviates from ADR-008 §1: it is a `0-100` integer, persisted as an `integer` column and produced by an LLM prompt that asks for one. Per §2 it therefore carries its unit **in its name**. This is the frontend half of that rename; the wire change is WIC-1520.

- **Six consumers renamed** — `types/interviewPrep.ts`, `STARStoryBank` (sort, badge, render), `QuestionsList`, `GapMitigationPanel`, `QuickReferenceExport`, `InterviewPrepPage`. All six were already *correct* as percent renders; they are renamed so the name carries the unit, not because they were wrong. `InterviewPrepPage`'s `>= 80` is right here — this population really is `0-100`.
- **`PrepStory.relevanceScorePct` is typed `Percent`**, so it cannot be crossed with a job-fit `relevanceScore: Ratio`.
- **Completeness is compiler-enforced, not grepped** — because the property no longer exists on `PrepStory`, any missed or reintroduced site is a `TS2551`. Measured by reverting one consumer: two errors, naming the replacement. No source-scanning drift test was added; it would restate what `tsc` already proves.
- ⚠️ **Breaking wire change — do not merge before WIC-1520.** Until the API emits `relevanceScorePct`, these six sites read `undefined` and render `undefined%`.

### Fixed — Cover letters are reachable after they are generated (2026-08-26)

`CoverLetterDetail` (`/cover-letters/:id`) was fully built and had no standing entry point. The only inbound navigation was the redirect `CoverLetterNew` fires on completion, and it sits on one branch of a conditional: with an application id it returns to `/applications/:id` instead. Two of the three routes into the generator set that id, so on those paths the detail page was never shown at all — and on the third it was available only in the seconds after generation. Navigate away and `.docx` export, delete, variant switching and the full preview became unreachable for the life of the letter (WIC-1533).

- **The card's stated scope did not survive measurement, and the fix is shaped around what it found.** The suggested fix was to list "that application's letters" via `GET /api/cover-letters`, "no API change" required. There is no such query: `cover_letters` has **no `application_id` column**, `POST /cover-letters/generate` validates with a `.strict()` schema that has no `applicationId` key, and the list endpoint filters on `status`/`company`/`search` only. `CoverLetterGenerator` receives an `applicationId` prop and puts it solely into the in-memory result object it hands to `onComplete` — it is never sent anywhere. The association does not exist to be looked up; it has to be reconstructed.
- **`/cover-letters` (new) is the sound half.** A standing index of every letter, regardless of which path created it, deliberately shaped as a sibling of the already-shipped `/resume-variants` list — same entity shape, same draft/finalized filter, same generate affordance. It is also the first UI consumer of `GET /api/cover-letters`, which UC-4 AC-22 has flagged as consumer-less since rev 1. Rows are real `<Link>`s rather than the precedent's `role="button"` `<article>`, so they can be middle-clicked and are read as links by assistive tech. Reachable from all three navigation components.
- **`ApplicationDetail` gains a Cover Letters section**, the placement the card asked for, so the letter is where the user was returned to. It reconstructs the association from `(targetCompany, targetRole)` — both `NOT NULL`, both prefilled from the application by `CoverLetterNew`, and the same pair `resume_variants` already uses for the same purpose. `packages/web/src/constants/coverLetterMatch.ts` (new) owns that predicate so the section and the checklist row cannot disagree about which letters count.
- **Not the endpoint's own `company` filter.** That is `ilike '%company%'`, under which an application at "Meta" claims every letter written for "Metabase". The filter is still sent, to narrow server-side; the client-side predicate is exact.
- **The reconstruction has two limits, not one, and they fail in opposite directions.** *Over-inclusion, visible:* two applications for the same role at the same company are indistinguishable, and each shows both letters — pinned as an explicit test rather than left to be discovered. *Under-inclusion, silent:* the endpoint pages at 20 rows by default, and because the server filter is a substring match, every letter for every other role at that company competes for that page in `created_at desc` order. The exact predicate runs **after** the page is chosen, so it can only remove rows — it cannot recover one the server never sent. An application with 20 newer sibling letters would render "No cover letters yet for this role" with an unticked checklist: this entry's own defect, reappearing at the tail. `ApplicationDetail` therefore requests `COVER_LETTER_PAGE_MAX` (100, the endpoint's `.max(100)` ceiling), asserted at both ends — the page passes the limit, and the limit reaches the query string. **Residual, unfixed:** above 100 substring-matching letters the silent case returns. Raising the cap cannot close it and pagination UI would treat the symptom; only WIC-1544's real `applicationId` association can, which is where both limits end.
- **The checklist row is repointed, not merely ticked.** A completed step drops its link, so passing `hasCoverLetter={true}` alone would have converted a wrong-but-clickable row ("Cover Letter" → write *another* one) into a correct-but-inert one: the checklist would read "done" and the letter would still be unreachable. `WorkflowChecklist` takes a `coverLetterId` and a completed step now links `/cover-letters/:id`, falling back to the old inert row if no id is available.
- **A stale duplicate in `API_CONTRACTS.md` was the root of the type drift, and is removed.** The doc declared `GET /cover-letters` **twice** — once accurately under UC-4, once under "Cover Letters (Read-Only Reference)" with a `keywords: string[]` the API has never sent and without `status`/`targetCompany`/`targetRole`. The web `CoverLetterSummary` had been written from the stale copy, which is why the fields this fix needs appeared not to exist. The web type now mirrors the API's `CoverLetterSummaryDTO` (the phantom `keywords` had zero consumers), and the duplicate section is replaced by a pointer so there is one declaration to maintain.
- **Tested at three levels, with the controls measured.** `coverLetterMatch.test.ts` (10 cases) and `WorkflowChecklist.test.tsx` (5) unit the predicate and the row; `ApplicationDetail.coverLetters.test.tsx` (7) asserts the entry point on a **cold render** of the route — no generation flow completed — which is the distinction between a control and a post-action redirect; `coverLetters.list.test.ts` (3) and `ApplicationDetail.pageCap.test.tsx` (2) cover the page cap, the second by running the real hook and service against a `fetch` that replays the endpoint's substring filter, `created_at desc` order and 20-row default. Reverting `ApplicationDetail` to its pre-fix state reds 5 of those 7; reverting the checklist link logic reds 2 of 5; substituting the endpoint's substring semantics for the exact match reds exactly the Metabase case; dropping `limit` from the page reds the cap tests at both levels, the replay one showing the literal "No cover letters yet for this role" the user would have seen.
- **No API, schema or wire change.** Web only.
- Known residue, recorded rather than folded in: `ApplicationDetail` is `WorkflowChecklist`'s only render site and still passes none of `hasFitAnalysis`, `hasResumeVariant` or `fitScore`, so those two rows remain permanently incomplete on the same mechanism this entry fixes for the third — tracked as WIC-1536.

### Added — failing coverage for the three artefact steps' in-flight false negative (2026-08-30)

`ApplicationDetail.artefactLoading.test.tsx` (new, 12 cases) reproduces WIC-1630 as it exists after the entry below widened it from one row to three. **10 of the 12 are RED on this tree by design** — they are the acceptance signal for the fix, not a regression, and they go green together when it lands (WIC-1811, QA).

- **Reproduced exactly, not paraphrased.** With the application resolved and all three artefact queries in flight, the rendered page gives `0 of 4 steps completed`, **0%**, `Cover Letter → /cover-letters/new?appId=app_1`, `Tailored Resume → /resume-variants/new?appId=app_1`, `Interview Prep` unticked, and the section copy `No cover letters yet for this role.` — the state WIC-1630's amendment block predicted, confirmed against the running component rather than read off the source.
- **The header count has the same defect, and this answers that question explicitly.** `completedCount` counts only `item.completed === true` while `totalCount` is the literal row count, so three *unknown* steps are counted as three known failures **and** the denominator claims all four answers are in hand. The count is not a separate bug to be fixed after the rows — it is the same one, and AC-3 is what closes it.
- **The tests assert distinguishability, not a chosen affordance.** WIC-1630 offers a `'unknown' | 'absent' | 'present'` prop as "rationale, not a mandate", so pinning a skeleton, an `aria-busy` attribute or a prop name here would test the fix rather than the defect. Each row is instead rendered twice — in flight, and settled-and-genuinely-empty — and the two markups must differ. Any honest affordance satisfies that; a rename that changes nothing the user sees does not.
- **Job Fit Analysis is the negative control and must stay identical across both phases.** It is driven by no query at all (nothing persists a fit analysis — WIC-1652), so a fix that makes *it* differ too is keying off a page-wide "something is loading" flag and would blank a row whose answer was never in doubt. That case is one of the 2 that are green here.
- **Both directions were measured before the file was committed.** Unpatched: 10 fail, and all 10 are genuine `AssertionError`s — no crash, no missing element, no vacuous pass. Against a reference fix: 12/12, with the full web suite at **141/141** and `tsc -b` clean, so the contract is satisfiable and does not regress the 13 cases in `ApplicationDetail.workflowChecklist.test.tsx`. That reference fix is deliberately **not** included here; the remedy is WIC-1630's and touches `WorkflowChecklist`'s public shape, which is worth its own review.
- **Tests only** — no source, API, schema or wire change.


### Fixed — the workflow checklist and the cover-letters section no longer state a false negative while their queries load (2026-08-30)

`ApplicationDetail` read all three artefact queries by `data` alone and never by `isLoading`, so `[]`, `[]` and `undefined` meant both "we looked and there is none" and "the request has not come back". On the first render after the application resolves, the page therefore asserted that no cover letter, tailored resume or interview prep existed, offered to create all three, and summarised it as `0 of 4 steps completed` / **0%** — the same figures it shows an application that genuinely has nothing. `enabled: !!application` means those queries cannot even start until the application query settles, so this is one full round-trip of the page confidently stating the wrong thing, and longer on a slow connection (WIC-1630).

- **The three steps are tri-state now, and that is the whole fix.** `WorkflowChecklist` takes `coverLetterStatus`, `resumeVariantStatus` and `interviewPrepStatus` as `'unknown' | 'absent' | 'present'`, replacing the three `hasX` booleans. One prop rather than a boolean paired with an `xUnknown` flag, so "present *and* unknown" is unrepresentable — a pair would oblige every consumer of one to remember the other, which is the same mistake in a new place. Each defaults to `'absent'`, so a caller that does not wire a step keeps the old behaviour instead of showing a row that loads forever.
- **An unknown step renders inert**: a pulsing marker instead of a tick or an empty circle, a "Checking…" label, `aria-busy` on the row, no link and no "Recommended" badge. The two generator links are the user-visible harm — inviting you to write a letter you may already have — but Interview Prep drops its link too, even though `/applications/:id/prep` is its destination either way, because what the link *means* ("go read your prep" versus "go make one") is exactly what is not yet known.
- **The count reports known steps only, and the percentage is withheld.** The denominator is now the settled steps rather than the row count, so an unknown step is not counted as a known failure and the summary does not claim all four answers are in hand. The percentage is replaced by `—` and the progress bar by an indeterminate one while anything is unknown: a percentage over a partial denominator is itself a settled-looking figure, which is the defect being fixed. The transient `0 of 1 steps completed` reads oddly on its own, so a second line names what is still outstanding ("Checking 3 more steps…"); "steps" stays literal at a denominator of 1 because the acceptance suite reads that line by a `/steps completed/` matcher.
- **The section and the checklist move together.** Both read the same `coverLettersLoading`, so the section cannot say "checking" while the row beside it says "none yet" — the half-fix this card was split out of WIC-1533 to avoid.
- **Job Fit Analysis is untouched and stays identical throughout.** It is backed by no query (WIC-1652), so it is never unknown; the acceptance suite pins that as its negative control, and a fix keyed off a page-wide loading flag would red it.
- **Turns the 10 RED cases in the entry above green** — 12/12 in `ApplicationDetail.artefactLoading.test.tsx`, **141 passed** across the web suite, `tsc -b --force` and lint clean, with no regression to the 13 cases in `ApplicationDetail.workflowChecklist.test.tsx`. Controls run against the committed fix: restoring the row-count denominator reds exactly the two AC-3 cases; restoring the cover-letter generator link during the unknown window reds the AC-1 link case and the AC-2 agreement case; the unmodified tree is green again after both.
- **Web only** — no API, schema or wire change.
- **Resynced against the Job Fit Analysis entry below, which merged to `main` after this file was written.** `ApplicationDetail` now also calls `useJobFitAnalyses`, and `ApplicationDetail.artefactLoading.test.tsx` mocked every other hook the page calls but not that one, so every case in the file threw `No QueryClient set` rather than exercising the tri-state fix. Mocked it the same way `ApplicationDetail.workflowChecklist.test.tsx` does — settled and empty in both phases, consistent with Job Fit Analysis being this file's negative control.

### Fixed — the Job Fit Analysis step ticks, and unlocks the two steps after it (2026-08-30)

The fourth checklist row is wired, so the ceiling stops being 3 of 4 / 75%. Until now `hasFitAnalysis` and `fitScore` were props no caller could supply truthfully: nothing persisted an analysis, so the step stayed unticked however many analyses the user had run, and it kept linking "go create one" at an analysis they already had. Two further badges rode on the same flag — `recommended` on **Cover Letter** and on **Tailored Resume** are both `hasFitAnalysis && !hasX` — so those were dead branches in the markup with no state that could reach them, and the checklist's only recommendation for an applied application was the analysis row itself. WIC-1652 AC-2 and AC-3, split out as WIC-1835 once its API half shipped separately.

- **This is the web half of WIC-1652 and it needs the other half first.** PR #283 adds the `job_fit_analyses` table, `GET /api/catalog/job-fit/analyses`, and `id`/`applicationId`/`fitScore` on the analyze response. Merge order is **#283 before this**. Without the endpoint the query 404s, `data` stays `undefined`, and the step degrades to exactly the unticked state described above rather than breaking the page — but nothing here is _true_ until #283 lands.
- **`hasFitAnalysis` means an analysis exists, not that one scored something.** It is `analyses.length > 0`. `fitScore` is `null` exactly when `recommendation` is — the catalog was empty, or the job description named no required skills — and that analysis is still one the user has run. Ticking off the score instead would keep offering to create an analysis they already have, which is the user-visible complaint WIC-1652 was filed on, reappearing one layer in.
- **The badge tests `fitScore != null`, and the `?` it replaces was a real defect, not a style.** `badge: fitScore ? …` is a truthiness test, so a genuine **0% match** — a catalog matching none of the required stack, which is precisely when a user most needs to be told — rendered no badge at all and was indistinguishable from having run no analysis. The three states are kept three all the way from the endpoint to the pill: `undefined` no analysis, `null` unscored, `0` a real zero. A null score renders no badge on purpose; there is no percentage to show and "0% match" would be a false one, so the tick is what tells that user their analysis exists.
- **The `appId` the browser already had stops being dropped at the API boundary.** `WorkflowChecklist` has always linked `/job-fit-analysis?appId={id}` and `JobFitAnalysis` has always read that param — but only to pre-fill the description. The analyze call carried the job description and nothing else, so the stored analysis belonged to no application and could never satisfy the query that ticks the step. It now rides along, absent rather than empty when the page was reached without one: `application_id` is nullable by design, analysing a bare job description is a supported flow, and the endpoint validates the field as `.min(1)` so a `''` would turn that flow into a 400.
- **The filter is the server's, and that is load-bearing rather than tidy.** Because `application_id` is nullable, an unfiltered page can consist entirely of rows that belong to no application and could never tick anything; a client-side narrowing applied after the server has chosen a page can only remove rows, never recover one it never sent. This is the same page-cap trap the two entries above live with for cover letters and resume variants — with the difference that here there is a real foreign key to filter on, so `limit: 1` is safe and none of the company-substring machinery applies.
- **Asserted where the defect lives, which for two of the four changes is the request.** Nothing on `JobFitAnalysis` renders differently with or without `applicationId`, and a page that dropped the filter from the analyses query would tick this application's step off someone else's analysis while every render assertion still passed — the fixture is whatever the test hands over. `ApplicationDetail.workflowChecklist.test.tsx` goes 13 → 20 cases and `JobFitAnalysis.applicationId.test.tsx` (new, 2) covers the call site; the application record is left deliberately unloaded there, so the id can only have come from the URL. `useJobFitAnalyses.request.test.tsx` (new, 2) closes the two layers below that: the page assertion is made on the mocked hook, so it stops at the hook boundary, and both `listAnalyses` dropping `applicationId` and a `queryFn` calling `listAnalyses()` with no params compile cleanly and leave the suite at baseline. Those are asserted on the request URL, the one representation in the chain that cannot be satisfied by an object nobody serialises — hook-level rather than service-level, because a service-only test does not reach the `queryFn`.
- **WIC-1536's tripwire is inverted, not deleted.** That file carried a case asserting the step **could not** tick and pinning 3 of 4 as the honest ceiling, and `WorkflowChecklist`'s JSDoc explained at length why the prop was kept rather than removed. Both were correct on that tree and are the regression on this one. The negative control survives unchanged as its own case — no analysis still means unticked, still linking `/job-fit-analysis?appId=…`, still no badge.
- **Eleven mutants, each killed by the case named for it, and each built as well as run** — an uncompilable mutant reports baseline and proves nothing. Restoring `fitScore ?` reds exactly the zero-score case (1) — every other assertion passes under truthiness, since 72 is truthy and `null` falsy either way. Ticking off the score rather than existence reds 2, both unscored cases. Dropping `applicationId` from the page's query reds only that request assertion (1); dropping it from the analyze request reds 1, and substituting the loaded record's id for the URL's reds the same one. Reverting the call site to its pre-fix props reds 6. Below the hook: `listAnalyses` dropping `applicationId` reds 1 and a `queryFn` calling `listAnalyses()` with no params reds the same 1 — both compile — while pinning `applicationId` to a constant reds only the negative case, which is what makes that half load-bearing rather than decorative, and an endpoint path typo reds both. Ticking the step unconditionally is two different mutants and they do not measure the same: at the call site (`hasFitAnalysis = true`) it reds **10 across three files**, inside the component (`completed: true`) it reds **11 across four**, the extra being `WorkflowChecklist.test.tsx`'s own progress-readout case, which no call-site edit can reach.
- **Residual, recorded not fixed.** The badge reflects the **newest** analysis only, so re-running an analysis against a job description that now names no required skills replaces a score with no badge; that is the honest reading of "the current analysis" but it is a choice, not a law. And this widens WIC-1630's transient false negative from three rows to four — the page reads each query's `data` and never its loading flag, so mid-flight the checklist states as fact that the analysis does not exist. Still WIC-1630's to answer: what an *unknown* step should render is a design question.
- **Web only** — no API, schema or wire change, and no new dependency. The endpoint and the two response fields this consumes are #283's.

### Fixed — the application workflow checklist could never report progress (2026-08-29)

`ApplicationDetail` is `WorkflowChecklist`'s only render site in the package, and it did not supply the props the checklist needs to count anything. On the base this entry lands on, the entry above had already wired the Cover Letter step; `hasResumeVariant` and `hasFitAnalysis` were left on their `= false` defaults, `fitScore` on `undefined`, and the Interview Prep step was hardcoded `completed: false` inside the component, with no prop to override it. So a user who had written a tailored resume and generated an interview prep read *"1 of 4 steps completed"* and **25%** with neither step ticked — the same literal string the entry above already pins in `ApplicationDetail.pageCap.test.tsx` — and because each link is `completed ? undefined : <create one>`, "Tailored Resume" kept inviting a duplicate forever. On `main`, where the Cover Letter step is unwired too, that same user reads *"0 of 4"* and **0%**. The component was always correct — this was a wiring defect at the single call site (WIC-1536, found while placing the outreach entry point for WIC-1530).

- **Three of the four steps are now wired; the fourth cannot be, and that is stated rather than faked.** Cover Letter and Tailored Resume resolve from the artefact lists, Interview Prep from a real lookup. Job Fit Analysis stays permanently unticked because **no job fit analysis is ever persisted** — there is no `job_fit_analyses` table, `POST /catalog/job-fit/analyze` computes and returns without writing a row, and `AnalyzeJobFitResponse` carries no id to remember it by. The `job_fit_analysis_id` columns on four tables are bare `text` referencing nothing. So the ceiling is 3 of 4 / 75%, and a test asserts exactly that rather than leaving the gap to be rediscovered. Filed as WIC-1652, which is a *different* gap from WIC-1544: there the row exists and only its `application_id` link is missing, here there is no row at all, so WIC-1544 landing does not make this reachable.
- **Interview Prep needed no reconstruction, and it is the one step that did not.** `interview_preps.application_id` is a real `notNull`, `unique` foreign key and `GET /applications/:applicationId/interview-prep` resolves it directly, with the service mapping the endpoint's 404 to `null`. Before this change the step was hardcoded `completed: false`, so a user who had generated a prep still saw it empty.
- **Its link is deliberately kept in both states.** Dropping the link on completion is right for the two "go generate one" rows, but `/applications/:id/prep` is where an existing prep is *read* — dropping it would take the finished artefact away. Pinned as its own test so the asymmetry is not tidied up later.
- **The Tailored Resume row is repointed, not merely ticked** — the same correction the entry above made for cover letters, for the same reason: `hasResumeVariant={true}` alone would convert a wrong-but-clickable row into a correct-but-inert one. A completed step now links `/resume-variants/:id`.
- **`coverLetterMatch.ts` becomes `applicationMatch.ts`, generalised rather than copied.** `resume_variants` has no `application_id` either and carries the same `NOT NULL` `target_company` / `target_role` pair, so it needs the identical predicate. Copying it is how the type drift that module exists to work around got started in the first place; one predicate means the Cover Letters section, the Cover Letter row and the Tailored Resume row cannot disagree about which artefacts count. `COVER_LETTER_PAGE_MAX` → `TARGETED_LIST_PAGE_MAX`, `coverLettersForApplication` → `itemsForApplication`, which stays generic in its element type so callers keep their concrete summary types.
- **Both lists ask for the endpoint maximum, and `useResumeVariants` gained the `enabled` option to do it.** The page cap reasoning in the entry above applies unchanged to resume variants: `resume-variant.service.ts` pages at `Math.min(params.limit ?? 20, 100)`, the only server-side narrowing is an over-matching `ilike '%company%'`, and the exact predicate runs after the page is chosen, so it can only remove rows. Asserted on the **request** rather than the render — no render-output assertion can see a row the server never sent. **Residual, unchanged:** above 100 substring-matching artefacts the silent under-inclusion returns, and only WIC-1544 closes it.
- **This widens WIC-1630's transient false negative from one row to three, and does not fix it.** The page reads each artefact query's `data` and never its loading flag, so while a query is in flight the checklist states as fact that the artefact does not exist. Before this change that hit the Cover Letter row alone; it now hits all three, which during that window read *"0 of 4 steps completed"* with every row simultaneously offering to create a duplicate of something the user already has. The `enabled: !!application` gate above lengthens the window rather than shortening it: the two list queries cannot start until the application query resolves, so they are guaranteed a second round-trip after the page is already rendering. Left to WIC-1630 deliberately — deciding what an *unknown* step should render is a design question, not a wiring one, and answering it inside this entry would be guessing.
- **Tested at the call site, not on the component.** `WorkflowChecklist` passed on the defective tree — give it the props and it has always worked — so a test over the component in isolation is structurally blind to this defect. `ApplicationDetail.workflowChecklist.test.tsx` (13 cases) renders the real page over the real component and mocks only the data hooks. Every list fixture carries an artefact for a *different role at the same company*, which is what the server actually returns; without it a page that stopped filtering and merely asked "is the array non-empty" would still pass.
- **Repairs a union-driver weld inherited from the entry above.** The `### ` heading below that entry was welded to its last bullet with no separating blank line — present on this branch, absent from `main`, so introduced by a merge rather than by either author. Found by the two-check script in `CLAUDE.md`. Repaired here rather than by force-pushing the entry above, whose head is under review.
- **Web only** — no API, schema or wire change, and no new dependency.

`packages/web/src/test/upload-limit-drift.test.ts` carried two `it.fails` trip-wires — one for the onboarding upload zone's 5MB-vs-10MB drift (WIC-1382, PR #143), one for `ONBOARDING_FLOW.md` quoting 5MB (WIC-1436, PR #150) — each documented "when it merges, delete `.fails`".
