### Fixed — `require-owner.routes.test.ts`'s sub-less-caller test was exercising a path WIC-1554 closed (2026-09-01)

WIC-1638's negative control drove the app with a JWT that verifies but carries no `sub`, asserting `requireOwner` answers `401 OWNER_REQUIRED`. WIC-1554 landed independently and closed that exact input one layer up: `middleware/auth.ts` now rejects a sub-less token itself, `401 UNAUTHORIZED`, before any route or `requireOwner` runs. Both fixes are correct on their own; merged together, the test's `OWNER_REQUIRED` assertion failed on all 11 cases, and `requireOwner`'s own owner-absent branch went untested by this file since the token shape it dispatched never reached it.

- **Repointed at the path `requireOwner.ts` itself still names as reachable: the local-dev bypass.** With neither `SUPABASE_URL` nor `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` set, `middleware/auth.ts` skips auth entirely and resolves `userId: null`, which is exactly what `requireOwner` guards. The sub-less-but-signed-token scenario is deleted rather than adjusted — it is no longer reachable through a real request now that WIC-1554 rejects it earlier.
- **`getConfig()` is a module-level singleton**, so the bypass env has to be in effect for the whole request, not merely while `buildApp()` runs; the fix builds and calls the bypass app inside each case with the Supabase vars deleted from `process.env`, rather than in a shared `beforeEach`, which is what the positive-sub `valid` case there still needs configured.
- **No production code changed.** Test-only; both `require-owner.ts` and `middleware/auth.ts` are unchanged.

### Fixed — `staleCutoff` shifted by an hour across a DST boundary; `dashboard.service.test.ts` didn't know about WIC-1479's rename (2026-09-01)

Two independent defects surfaced merging WIC-1479 ("one definition of stale") into `main`.

- **`staleCutoff` used `Date.setDate`/`getDate`, which read and write the host's local calendar.** Subtracting `days` across a spring-forward DST transition shifts the result by the zone's offset delta (an hour, in every zone that observes it) even though `days` itself never changes — `stale.drift.test.ts`'s own boundary case (`now` after the transition, cutoff before it) failed on this machine's `America/Chicago` clock, and reproduces on the PR's own unmerged branch, so it predates this merge. Both `packages/api/src/services/stale.ts` and its web mirror now use `setUTCDate`/`getUTCDate`, which have no local offset to shift.
- **`packages/api/test/dashboard.service.test.ts` (added by WIC-1574, not touched by this PR) asserted the pre-WIC-1479 shape** — `STALE_THRESHOLD_DAYS`/`SAVED_THRESHOLD_DAYS` exports, a separate `staleActive` bucket alongside `stale`, `staleSaved`. `packages/api/tsconfig.json` excludes `test/`, so the now-renamed imports resolved to `undefined` at runtime rather than failing `tsc`. Updated to the merged shape (`stale`/`unsubmittedSaved`, `DEFAULT_STALE_THRESHOLD_DAYS`/`UNSUBMITTED_THRESHOLD_DAYS`), and to the fixture consequences of `stale` narrowing to `applied`/`phone_screen` at 14 days: `interview` and `saved` rows that used to count no longer do, by status rather than by age, so the fixture gained an `applied-stale-fresher` row to keep the sample-ordering mutations (asc→desc, sort column) discriminating now that `interview-newer` no longer competes for the two sample slots. Reverting `asc(updatedAt)` to `desc` or to `asc(createdAt)` still reds the ordering case — verified directly, not assumed.


### Tests — the owner-less caller is now asserted on all four project paths that reject one (2026-09-03)

WIC-1962 ruled (ADR-010) that project routes must **not** function under the ADR-003 auth-bypass dev mode, refusing PR #316's design. `main` was already correct; what it lacked was coverage. PR #316's test file carried 21 cases against `main`'s 16 — 18 of the 21 pass here, and the 3 that fail are exactly the 3 asserting the refused design. This ports the part worth keeping and adds the half nobody had.

- **Ported the two `main`-passing cases from #316** (`packages/api/test/project.tenancy.test.ts`), keeping their original identifiers so the ADR-010 / WIC-1952 references still resolve. `AC-T0-4` is the load-bearing one: it pins the *ordering* of `createProject`'s two checks. With the existence check first, an owner-less caller gets `409 Project with this slug already exists` and the endpoint becomes an existence oracle over other tenants' project names — so "it throws" is a vacuous assertion and *which* error it throws is the whole finding. #316's `AC-T0-1`, `AC-T0-2` and `AC-T0-5` are deliberately absent, which is why the numbering has a gap.
- **Added `AC-T0-6` and `AC-T0-7`, the two paths no branch had ever asserted.** `listProjects(undefined)` and `getProject(<another tenant's id>, undefined)` both throw `AppError` 400 on `main` — correctly, and until now untested. That gap is why the two designs looked equivalent and why the question reached a decision card at all: #316's own AC-T0 block covers the re-stamp, `getProjectBySlug`, `getOrCreateProjectBySlug` and `createProject`, and neither of these.
- **Every case pins `statusCode` *and* `message`.** `NotFoundError` and `ConflictError` both extend `AppError`, so `toBeInstanceOf(AppError)` is satisfied by a 404 and a 409 alike; `AC-T0-7` additionally asserts that the *same* id yields a 404 for a different real tenant, which is what makes its 400 a statement about the absent owner rather than about the id failing to match.
- **Graded by mutation, not by passing.** Each of the four was re-run against a service mutated to reintroduce the defect it describes — `listProjects` fail-open to no predicate, `getProject` to an id-only predicate, `getOrCreateProjectBySlug` to a slug-only match, and `createProject`'s checks reordered. Each mutation fails exactly its own case and no other; `AC-T0-4` fails on the 409 specifically. Uses the file's existing PGlite harness, not `stubDb`, whose `where` spy resolves whatever it was primed with regardless of the predicate and would pass with every one of those mutations in place (the WIC-1373 lesson the file's header records).
- **Test-only.** `project.service.ts` is unchanged, and deliberately so: relaxing an owner requirement to make dev mode work is the exact recurrence ADR-010 exists to stop. ADR-010 **D3** (resolving a real `LOCAL_DEV_USER_ID` in local dev) remains open with the board and is not implemented here.

### Fixed — `route-integrity.test.ts` declared `stripComments` twice (2026-09-02)

Merging WIC-1551 (a hand-rolled, string-literal-aware comment scanner for the route table) with the already-landed WIC-1560 (a regex-based stripper for `collectLinkSites`, guarding against a commented-out link crediting its route) produced two functions of the same name in one file — a duplicate declaration `tsc` catches, but only because both PRs happened to touch the same file; a duplicate in two files would not have been.

- **Unified on WIC-1551's scanner.** It is the strictly more correct of the two: the regex stripper had the identical string-literal hazard WIC-1551 was written to close for the route table (a `/*`-shaped substring inside a string, e.g. `path="/*"`, opens a comment a regex closes at the next real `*/`, silently deleting everything between). `collectLinkSites` now calls the character scanner instead; `StrippedSource extends string`, so no caller-side type change was needed.
- **No baseline change.** WIC-1560's own measurement — 0 of 152 link sites sat inside a comment — is a property of the source tree, not of which stripper reads it; the commented-out-link and orphan-route tests both still pass against the unified function.
- **Test-only.** No application code changes.


### Security — the local-dev auth bypass supplies an owner instead of an absence (2026-09-02)

ADR-010 §D3 (WIC-1964). With neither `SUPABASE_URL` nor `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` set, `middleware/auth.ts` bypassed auth and left `userId` null. §D2 had already landed ahead of it — `requireOwner` rejects an absent owner — so in that dev mode every route behind the guard answered 401, across projects, catalog, resume-variants and interview-preps alike. That was the predicted, temporary cost of the sequencing inversion, and it resolves here.

- **The bypass now resolves a real tenant.** It sets `userId` to `LOCAL_DEV_USER_ID`, defaulting to the sentinel migration `0017` backfills every pre-tenancy row to. Local dev is one specific tenant rather than no tenant, so the tenancy predicates run their owner branch exactly as they do in production instead of being skipped. ADR-003's "left as null for local-only" affordance is retired.
- **The default cannot drift from the migration.** The test parses the sentinel back out of `0017_enforce_userid_not_null.sql` and asserts equality, rather than comparing against a second copy of the literal — a copied constant would only prove someone typed the same string twice.
- **The bypass condition is unchanged.** §D3 changes what the bypass supplies, never when it fires. A deployment with either variable set still takes the JWT path and still 401s on a missing or invalid token; that half is pinned by its own tests, because widening the condition would serve unauthenticated traffic as the sentinel — strictly worse than the 401 it replaces.
- **No new owner-absent branch.** `scripts/audit-owner-predicates.mjs` still exits 0 with its 122 baselined sites unchanged. `requireOwner` keeps rejecting the `sub`-less JWT caller (WIC-1554), which is now the only owner-less caller left.
- **Supersedes PR #316**, which short-circuited each caller with `if (!userId)` ahead of the scope predicate. That is an owner-absent code path, the category §D1 commits to deleting; its 3 dev-mode tests are carried over here re-pointed from "200 via a null-owner filesystem fallback" to "200 as the sentinel tenant".

### Fixed — WIC-1099's `/login` h1 fix landed after the WIC-1089/WIC-1675 rebrand it needed to reconcile with (2026-09-02)

WIC-1099 (h1 fixes for `/applications/new`, `/login`, `/job-fit-analysis`) was branched before three since-merged changes it directly overlaps: WIC-1089's product rebrand to `PRODUCT_NAME` ("Careerpin"), WIC-1675 AC-3's partial `/login` heading fix, and WIC-1560's `/cover-letters` route-table row. Merging surfaced five conflicts and three stale main-only test files.

- **`/login`'s wordmark is now `{PRODUCT_NAME}`, not the hardcoded "Job Application Manager" string.** WIC-1099's branch predates the rebrand entirely; its fix (demote the wordmark to a `<p>`, add a real `<h1>` naming the screen below it) is unaffected by which string the wordmark renders, so the two compose directly. `Login.test.tsx` and `auth.spec.ts` (WIC-1099's own) updated to assert "Careerpin"; `title.ts`'s `LOGIN_TITLE` (a single string) became `LOGIN_TITLES` (keyed by mode), since the tab title now mirrors the mode-dependent `<h1>` per the usual rule instead of the constant wordmark it used to name.
- **`/job-fit-analysis`'s tab title is now the same constant string as its new h1**, replacing the four-way `STAGE_TITLES` lookup keyed on a heading shape (two wrong headings, two right ones) that WIC-1099's persistent-`<h1>` fix retires.
- **Two main-only test files (`dashboard`-class drift, not this PR's own) asserted the pre-fix shape and needed updating, not this PR's code:** `routeOutline.render.test.tsx`'s `MISSING_H1` registry listed all four `/applications/new` branches, which now render a correct h1 — deleted, per the test's own "delete a fixed pair" instruction. `routeOutline.source.test.ts` pinned `Login.tsx` at exactly one literal `<h1`; it now has two (the session-bootstrap branch's `sr-only` one and the mode-dependent one), mutually exclusive at render time, which is correct and now asserted as 2.
- **`ApplicationForm.test.tsx` (WIC-1854, unrelated) asserted the pre-WIC-1099 dialog copy** ("Add New Application" / "Edit Application"); updated to the copy this PR ships ("New application" / "Edit application"), matching `ROUTE_TITLE_CONVENTION.md` §5's own table entry for the route.
- **The `/login` heading question is now ruled and written down, not settled by whoever merged last (WIC-1968).** `ROUTE_TITLE_CONVENTION.md` gains a §10 recording the decision — the `<h1>` names the *screen*, the wordmark keeps `{PRODUCT_NAME}` as a `<p>` — and the reasoning, which is that `ROUTE_HEADING_OUTLINE.md` §0 already governs this ("the page `<h1>` names the route") and §0.3 of this document declares itself a *consumer* of it, "not a peer". So the product-name `<h1>` was this document overruling its own stated parent. WCAG 2.4.6 says the same thing independently: `Careerpin` is the identical string on every unauthenticated view, so heading navigation lands somewhere that cannot name the screen. **Two people resolved this conflict independently and reached the same answer**, which is the strongest available evidence the reading belongs to the documents rather than to either author.
- **§9's standing exception is withdrawn, and it had already gone stale in this very commit.** §9 said `/login` was "the one route where the title mirrors the `<h1>` is deliberately not applied", ending on an escape clause: *if the heading is ever reworded to describe the screen, `LOGIN_TITLE` should be deleted and the route moved onto the ordinary rule.* That is exactly what this change does — yet the paragraph still asserted, in the present tense, that the heading names the product, that `Sign In` survives, and that a future reader should delete a constant this commit had already deleted. A reader trusting it over the code would have reverted the fix. Struck rather than removed, because it is the reason the reversal is legitimate rather than a branch overruling `main`. Neither doc audit reads that prose, which is why nothing caught it; the check is a read.
- **The mirroring rule paid for itself immediately.** §0.3 justifies "the title is the `<h1>` verbatim" as making titles immune to the casing decision in `CONTENT_STYLE.md`. `LOGIN_TITLE` was `Sign In` — title case, which that document's closed exception list does not permit — and restoring mirroring corrects it to `Sign in` for free, with no separate copy pass.
- **Neither deferral in the conflicting comments was still live.** Both sides deferred `Job Application Manager` to the Copywriter; the Copywriter/Editor had already ruled the product name `Careerpin` on 2026-08-19 under WIC-1102, and that ruling names `Login.tsx` as a site `PRODUCT_NAME` fixes. The dialog copy was closed the same way, by a sentence-case rule that does not exempt modal titles. The two genuinely outstanding copy sites remain `OnboardingModal.tsx` and `QuickReferenceExport.tsx`. **A code comment reading "pending X" is evidence about the day it was written, not about today** — check before paying for another round.
- **No behaviour change beyond WIC-1099's own scope.** Every reconciliation above makes an already-merged fact (the rebrand, WIC-1675's partial fix, WIC-1560's new route) consistent with WIC-1099's fix, rather than changing what either side already shipped.

### Fixed — `extraction.tenancy.test.ts` still expected the pre-WIC-1414 failure shape for a cross-tenant `generateDiff` call (2026-09-02)

### Fixed — The STAR entry picker read a `[0, 1]` relevance score as `0-100` (2026-08-26)

`StarEntryPicker` split its "Recommended (from fit analysis)" section on `relevanceScore >= 80` and rendered the badge as `{relevanceScore}%`. Both are the `0-100` reading. `CatalogEntry.relevanceScore` is the **job-fit population**, a ratio in `[0, 1]` (ADR-008 §1, `packages/api/src/types/index.ts` → `CatalogEntryDTO`). The defect never fired only because the field's sole producer, `catalog.service.ts`, still hardcodes `relevanceScore: undefined`. On the day the job-fit path populates it, no entry could clear `0.85 >= 80`, so the Recommended section would have been **structurally always empty**, and any badge that did render would have read `0.85%` (WIC-1521, the latent instance recorded in ADR-008 §Context).

- **The threshold is `0.8` and the render goes through `formatRatioAsPercent`** — the one blessed ratio → percent conversion, rather than a second hand-written `* 100`. The threshold is declared through the checked `ratio()` constructor, so it is range-validated once at module load and carries the brand instead of being a bare number that means nothing on its own.
- **`CatalogEntry.relevanceScore` is typed `Ratio`** — the brand makes a `Percent`, or a bare `number` from a wire parse, a compile error at the assignment.
- **Correcting the entry above: the brand does not, on its own, catch either half of this bug.** `Ratio` is `number & {…}`, so `score >= 80` is a well-typed comparison and `{score}%` is a well-typed render — arithmetic and JSX both erase the brand. Routing the render through `formatRatioAsPercent(r: Ratio)` *does* make it a compile error (measured: deleting the brand yields `TS2345` at that call), but nothing makes the threshold one. The threshold is held by a test, and only by a test.
- **`packages/web/src/components/StarEntryPicker.test.tsx`** (6 tests) pins `0.85` → Recommended → `85%`, the `0.8`/`0.79` boundary, and a total partition over `{high, low, zero, unscored}` — an entry must appear in exactly one section, which is not implied by two independently written predicates. Plus a control that cannot expire, in the shape WIC-1514 needed: six distinct ratios must produce six **distinct** badges, so a conversion that compiles and runs but collapses its input range cannot pass. Mutation-checked in four cells — threshold reverted (4 red), render reverted (2 red), the full pre-fix component (4 red), and the brand deleted (`TS2578` on both `@ts-expect-error` lines, so the type-level assertions are genuinely checked; `packages/web/tsconfig.app.json` includes `src`, unlike the api package).

### Fixed — The Dashboard's "Response" stat could only ever read 0% or 1% (2026-08-26)

`responseRate` crossed the API/web boundary with **two different units and no adapter between them**. The API ships a ratio in `[0, 1]` — `docs/architecture/API_CONTRACTS.md` says `// 0-1` and gives `0.75` in its own example response — while `DashboardStats` documented the prop as `// 0-100` and rendered `Math.round(val)`. Both sides were `number`, so TypeScript saw nothing. `Math.round(v)` over `v` in `[0, 1]` has a **two-element range**, so the "Response" card could only ever print "0%" or "1%": every true rate below 50% read as 0%, everything at or above 50% read as 1%. A user with 1 applied, 1 phone screen, 1 interview and 1 rejected — a true 75% response rate — saw **1%**. The card was correct in exactly one case, a true rate of 0%, and correct there by coincidence (WIC-1514).

- **The ratio is the unit of record, and the presentation layer converts** — that is what API_CONTRACTS specifies, what the API already ships, and the convention UC-3 uses for `relevanceScore`. `DashboardStats` now renders `Math.round(toPercent(stats.responseRate))`, so `0.75` reads "75%". The API is unchanged; nothing was rescaled server-side.
- **The unit is branded into the type, because a comment was the load-bearing artifact in every place this value passed through** — `packages/web/src/types/units.ts` (new) defines `Ratio` and `Percent` as `number` intersected with a `unique symbol` brand, plus `asRatio` and a single sanctioned `toPercent`. A bare `number` can no longer be assigned into a `responseRate` slot: reverting the transport type in `services/api/types.ts` to plain `number` now fails `tsc` at `Dashboard.tsx`, which is the exact passthrough that let the wrong unit reach the screen. The `// 0-100` and un-commented declarations across `DashboardStats.tsx`, `types/application.ts`, `services/api/types.ts` and `packages/api/src/types/index.ts` are corrected to say ratio.
- **What the brand guards is the boundary, not the render site — and the module comment now says so** — a brand only bites where a *declaration* names the type. `Ratio` is an intersection, so it is still a `number` and arithmetic erases the brand: `Math.round(r)`, `r * 100`, `r >= 0.8`, `r.toFixed(0)` and `` `${r}%` `` all compile, verified against `units.ts`. `toPercent` therefore owns the only `* 100` **applied to a `Ratio`**, not the only one in the package — there are nine others, two of them this same ratio-to-percent render on fields not branded yet (`JobFitAnalysis.tsx`, `CatalogDiff/AmbiguityResolver.tsx`). Nothing in the type system would stop `Math.round(stats.responseRate)` being written again; the test below is what stops it. Recording this because the first draft of this entry claimed the stronger property, and a reader who believed it would reasonably skip the test.
- **The component's `value` + `formatValue` pair is gone** — each stat now carries its finished display string. That split existed so four differently-united numbers could share one `(val: number) => string` shape, which is precisely how a ratio came to be handed to a percentage formatter.
- **`DashboardStats.test.tsx` (new) pins it, including a control that cannot expire** — beyond the 75% acceptance case, one test asserts that six distinct ratios render as six *distinct* readings. A single-point assertion would still pass if a later change re-collapsed the output range somewhere else; a cardinality assertion cannot. Restoring the old `Math.round(val)` reproduces the reported defect exactly: `['0%', '0%', '0%', '1%', '1%', '1%']`.
- **Docs corrected at the two places that disagreed** — `docs/design/COMPONENT_SPECS.md` said `0-100` and now says `0-1`, citing API_CONTRACTS as the source of record for the unit; `docs/architecture/DATA_MODEL.md` declared `responseRate` with no unit at all, directly above a code sample that computes a ratio.



### Docs — the product name is `Careerpin`, and that ruling now exists in the repository

### Added — a merge that drops a migration from the journal is now a red build, not a silent data-loss (2026-09-01)

Drizzle's `migrate()` is **journal-driven**: `packages/api/src/db/migrate.ts` hands it `meta/_journal.json`, and a `.sql` file that is not in the journal never runs. Nothing checked that the journal and the migrations directory agree, and the way they come to disagree is a routine merge. Merge-base `bb701190` had no `0020`; `main` claimed idx 20 for `0020_prep_relevance_score_pct` (WIC-1520) while PR #238 independently claimed idx 20 for `0020_backfill_catalog_diffs_user_id`. Re-verified at `main` `586712c2`: merging #238 conflicts on `_journal.json` and **on nothing else**, and the conflict region is a single `tag` line inside the idx-20 object — so resolving it the natural way, keeping both migrations because both are wanted, produces one entry object with two `"tag"` keys. That is valid JSON. Every parser keeps the last key, so WIC-1520's migration vanishes from the journal while its `.sql` stays on disk, and on a fresh database it would never run (WIC-1939).

- **`packages/api/scripts/audit-migration-journal.mjs` (new) is now a `Lint & Test` step** — it fails the build when the journal and the directory disagree in either direction: a journal `tag` with no `.sql` on disk, or a `.sql` on disk in no journal entry. It runs unconditionally rather than filtered to `packages/api/src/db/migrations/**`, because the damage is done by a *merge*: the PR that breaks the journal need not have touched a migration in its own diff.
- **It parses the raw text with a duplicate-key-detecting parser, not `JSON.parse`** — `JSON.parse` cannot represent the defect. It sees only the surviving key, so a `JSON.parse`-based guard reports the orphaned file and cannot say why it was orphaned, which is exactly how this class survives review. Run against the real merged tree the guard reports both halves: `duplicate-key` names the cause, `orphan-sql` names the damage.
- **`idx` must be dense, strictly increasing, and agree with its own tag's numeric prefix** — a number claimed twice by parallel branches cannot merge quietly, and a half-finished renumber that renames `0020_x` → `0021_x` but leaves `idx` at 20 is caught too. The density check is anchored to the first entry's `idx` rather than a hard-coded 0: this journal starts at 1, not at drizzle's usual 0.
- **`when` must strictly increase in journal order — the one field drizzle actually gates on (WIC-1955)** — every other check here is hygiene on human-facing numbering. `readMigrationFiles` iterates `entries` in **array order and never reads `idx` at all**; `PgDialect.migrate()` reads the newest applied `created_at` once, before the loop, and applies an entry only when that value is strictly less than the entry's `when`. So two entries sharing a `when` are indistinguishable to the migrator: once one has been applied in an earlier deploy the other is skipped **permanently and silently**, with `db:migrate` exiting 0. A hand renumber is how it happens — renaming `0021_x.sql` → `0022_x.sql` and editing `idx`/`tag` does not regenerate the timestamp, so every check that looks at the fields the renumber updated still passes. Measured on the exact tree from PR #261: the guard as first written reported **0 violations**, and reports **1** with this check. CI cannot catch it either, because a **fresh** database has a null `lastDbMigration`, never runs the strict `<`, and applies both entries fine.
- **`test/migration-journal.guard.test.ts` (new) proves every check fires** — thirteen synthetic mutants, each asserting the **exact set** of checks it trips, so a check that over-fires is caught as well as one that has gone dead. Asserted in the other direction too: disabling a check reds the suite, with `passed + failed` equal to the baseline test count in each run, so no mutant was merely failing to load.
- **…and one oracle that does not consult `CHECKS` at all** — the "every check is exercised by a mutant" meta-assertion iterates `CHECKS`, so it measures self-consistency: it is satisfied whether or not a *needed* check exists, and it stayed green for the whole life of this PR with the `when` gap present. The added block instead models `PgDialect.migrate()` directly and asserts the guard rejects any journal that loses a migration under **some** two-deploy split — phrased in terms of the mechanism, so deleting or renaming `when-sequence` fails there rather than silently disarming the guard. It carries its own positive control: the same broken journal applies all four migrations on a single fresh-database pass, which is precisely why no from-scratch test in the suite can see the defect.
- **AC-1's `*_rls.sql` exemption is deliberately not implemented** — the only two `_rls.sql` files in that directory, `0016_personal_info_rls.sql` and `0019_onboarding_status_rls.sql`, are genuine drizzle migrations journaled at idx 16 and 19. A suffix carve-out would exempt exactly the files the guard exists to protect. The unjournaled RLS SQL lives under `supabase/migrations/`, outside this directory, and is applied by `scripts/apply-rls.mjs`. The orphan check instead takes an explicit allowlist, empty today.
- **The audit derives the journal when it is absent, instead of crashing on it (WIC-1981)** — the read above was a bare `readFileSync`, correct only while `_journal.json` is committed. PR #351 (WIC-1963) makes it a *generated, git-ignored* artifact, so it is simply not in a fresh checkout, and that read throws `ENOENT`. Because this step is unconditional the breakage was total rather than scoped: **every** PR build, in either merge order, plus the vitest suite independently, which read the same path at module-evaluation time and so took the whole file down before a test could register. `readRealJournalText` now resolves three cases — file present, read it; file absent but `src/db/generate-journal.ts` present, run `npm run db:journal` and audit what it wrote; neither, report a `journal-unavailable` violation. The middle case is the stronger check, not a workaround: it audits what `db:migrate` will actually apply, since `db:migrate` regenerates the journal in-process immediately before migrating, rather than a committed copy that may be stale. A generator that *fails* — its own same-number-collision throw included — is the third case, and its stderr is carried into the violation so the cause is on screen. Verified on the real both-merged tree: the pre-fix script exits non-zero on `ENOENT` where this one exits 0, the generated journal is byte-identical to the one the tree used to commit, and the api suite is 1174/1174 green with the file deleted.
- **`journal-unavailable` is deliberately not a member of `CHECKS`** — every value in that object must be provable by a synthetic mutant handed to `auditMigrationJournal`, and the suite asserts exactly that. This one is raised by the CLI wrapper *before* there is any text to audit, so it has no mutant and putting it there would only weaken the invariant. Its own five cases are covered against throwaway package fixtures with real `npm run` subprocesses rather than a stubbed spawn, including the one that proves the generator is never invoked when the file is already on disk.

### Docs — ADR-008's own "percentage is not a ratio" rule was violated on `main` for six days, and every live citation in the ADR had rotted (2026-09-01)

The unit convention landed in `38b4cc8e` (2026-08-26 17:26:59Z) carrying a rule — do not write "percentage" about a `[0, 1]` field — and deleted the single annotation that broke it, in the same commit. Thirty-one minutes later `8433ff2f`, whose subject reads *"say what the brand actually guards, and unit the second declaration"*, annotated the **second** `responseRate` declaration by reaching for the wording the ADR had just retracted: `// 0-1, percentage of applications with response`, byte-identical to the string removed upstream. That second declaration is `DashboardStats` — the field whose mis-unit *is* WIC-1514, a 75% response rate rendering as `1%`. The contract re-asserted the wrong unit on the one field the ADR exists because of, and it stood on `main` until now.

- **The live defect is fixed.** `DashboardStats.responseRate` in `docs/architecture/API_CONTRACTS.md` now carries the same corrected annotation as its sibling: a ratio in `[0, 1]`, not a percentage, multiplied at render. Shipped code was never wrong and never disagreed — `dashboard.service.ts` emits `Math.round(responseRate * 100) / 100`, and the web side declares the field `Ratio` in four files and renders it through `toPercent`. The contract was the only dissenter, which is why nothing failed.
- **ADR-008 §5 and its Implementation table both claimed the corpus was swept, one site.** There were two, and the sweep's own remedy had been reverted into the second half an hour later. Both now record what actually happened. The generalisable half: a retraction only protects the copy it is written next to, and the reverting commit was not careless — it was deliberately propagating an annotation to a second declaration and reached for what that field had always said.
- **Every `file:line` citation in the ADR's Decision and Consequences sections had rotted, and is now addressed by symbol.** `schema.ts:708` still resolved to the right line but to the *renamed* column, contradicting the sentence citing it; `interviewPrep.service.ts:278` and `:506`, three producer citations in §1, and all six `COMPONENT_SPECS.md` numbers landed on unrelated text — box-drawing characters, blank lines, a `### Performance Considerations` heading. `doc-reference-audit.py` resolves the filename and cannot see the number, so nothing in CI catches this class.
- **The Context section is pinned whole to `45d70f6`, the SHA it was traced against.** Its numbers had rotted too, but re-pointing them would misreport what was measured — the faults it describes have since been fixed and the field renamed. The pin previously covered only the "Two live populations" table, leaving the rest reading as live pointers.
- **The delegated code work is recorded as landed** — PR #249 (`b64c743c`, WIC-1520) for the `relevance_score_pct` rename and migration `0020`, PR #168 (`2c3b1ba3`, WIC-1521) for the frontend consumers. The Implementation table had read "Delegated" and the costs section "it needs a coordinated landing", both of which now deny shipped work.

Documentation and contract annotations only. No source, schema, or test change; the ADR's decision is untouched and its status is left to its owner.

### Docs — ADR-008 is `Accepted`; a `Status` line records whether a decision binds, not whether its cleanup has finished (2026-09-01)

ADR-008 sat at `Status: Proposed` for six days while its decision governed the tree: the branded `Ratio` / `Percent` types shipped in both packages, the interview-prep field was renamed end to end behind a migration, and the convention was cited as normative from `API_CONTRACTS.md` and `COMPONENT_SPECS.md`. `Proposed` told a reader deciding how to unit a new score field that none of that was binding yet. It is now **Accepted (2026-09-01)**, with the implementing SHAs named — PR #166 (`bc0bd8b1`) for the convention and the brands, PR #249 (`b64c743c`, WIC-1520) for the backend rename and migration `0020`, PR #168 (`2c3b1ba3`, WIC-1521) for the frontend consumers (WIC-1932, closing WIC-1516).

- **The status was decoupled from the acceptance criteria, deliberately, and the ADR now says why.** Waiting for the last residual to close is the reflex, and it is what kept this line stale: AC-T3d's own final violation stood on `main` until the PR this one is stacked on, six days after the rule that forbade it landed. A rule and its last known violation are not the same artifact and do not share a clock. Residual conformance work belongs in the Implementation table, which tracks it.
- **The error direction is what makes it worth a card.** An overclaimed `Accepted` invites a reader to go check; a `Proposed` on a binding convention tells them not to look. The denial is the more expensive failure, and it is the one that was live.
- **`Accepted` is not claimed wider than the tree supports.** `responseRate` is declared `Ratio` at all four of its `packages/web` declarations and rendered through `toPercent`, so the assignment that produced WIC-1514 no longer type-checks — but adoption on the API-side DTOs is still incremental, which §3 provides for explicitly, and the one standing deviation (`completeness`) stays recorded as a decision rather than being quietly folded in.

Documentation only — one ADR's `## Status` section. No source, schema, test, or contract change.

### Security — Resolving a project by slug now requires an owner rather than defaulting to one (2026-08-26)

`getOrCreateProjectBySlug` is the entry point for resume upload and dialogue capture, and it took `userId` as **optional**. WIC-1433 scoped its lookup, but through the shared `projectScope(slug, userId)` helper, which by design degrades to a slug-only predicate when `userId` is falsy — and both call sites above thread through a `userId?: string` of their own. The scoping was therefore only ever as good as the identity the entry point happened to carry: with no `sub` claim the predicate widened back to the whole table and handed the caller whichever user already held that company slug (WIC-1434).

- **Requiring the owner is a total fix here, not a trade.** `createProject` is the only `insert(projects)` in the codebase and it already rejects a missing `userId`, so every row has a real owner. An owner-less call therefore had exactly two possible outcomes — return some *other* authenticated user's project id, name and file count, which the request then treated as the caller's, or fall through to a create that always throws. There is no input for which the owner-less path was correct, so the parameter is now required and the predicate is spelled out inline rather than delegated to the conditional helper.
- **`createProject` checked existence before ownership**, so an owner-less create matched an existing row on the degraded predicate and answered `409 Project with this slug already exists` — disclosing that *somebody* holds that slug, to a caller who was going to be rejected either way. The two checks are now ordered so the `400` comes first, which is both the honest answer and the one that leaks nothing.
- **`uploadResume` and `captureProjectFile` reject early**, at the layer that knows what the caller was doing. Capture previously resolved another user's project and then had `createProjectFile`'s own ownership guard reject the write — a `404` for a project the service had just told itself existed. The resume path's project write stays best-effort inside its existing `try/catch`, so an upload with no owner still succeeds with the project write skipped and logged.
- **Verified by reverting each change alone and counting failures against a prediction made first** — 0 / 2 / 2 / 1 / 1 / 0, matching on both count and identity in all six. The two zeroes are reported rather than hidden: the inline predicate is equivalent to the helper once the owner is guaranteed, and the resume guards are invisible at runtime because the inner guard throws identically — both are load-bearing for the compiler instead, which is where they were checked. The first pass of this matrix is what exposed that **four of the tests were passing for the wrong reason**: an absent owner renders `user_id = $n` bound to `null` against a `NOT NULL` column, so the query matches zero rows and falls through to `createProject`'s own `400` — same code, same status. Those cases now grade *which* guard fired, and one asserts the lookup refuses before a connection is even opened.

### Fixed — Dashboard attention counts are server-side aggregates, so they stop going blind as the account grows (2026-08-26)

The Dashboard's "Attention Required" and "Quick Wins" cards derived every number from `useApplications()`, which returns **a page** of applications — `GET /api/applications` defaults to `limit=50` and orders by `desc(updatedAt)`. The detectors then filtered that page for the rows with the *oldest* `updatedAt`. The two are in direct opposition: the server hands back the 50 most-recently-updated rows, and the client asks which of them have not been touched in a week. Past 50 applications the answer is structurally always "none", so the "N applications need follow-up" warning silently stopped rendering — and the card next to it said **"All applications are up to date!"** instead. Worst when the user is most active, and worse the larger the account gets (WIC-1478).

- **The aggregates moved to `GET /api/dashboard`**, next to the `GROUP BY status` count that was already correct — which is why the "Total" tile read 137 while the card beside it read zero. `getDashboardStats` now also returns an `attention` block: full-table counts (`interviewing`, `stale`, `staleActive`, `missingJobDescription`, `staleSaved`) plus short top-N `samples` for rendering individual action rows. Counts and samples are separate on purpose — a bounded sample must never bound the count printed beside it.
- **The Dashboard no longer lists applications at all.** `AttentionCard` and `QuickWins` take `attention` instead of `Application[]`, so there is no truncated array on the page for a future detector to reach for. The count cannot have come from a page because the page is never fetched, and the regression test asserts exactly that.
- **`staleThresholdDays` / `savedThresholdDays` come down the wire**, so the "> 7 days" copy on the *card* can no longer disagree with the SQL that produced the number. The *row* copy beside it still could, and did — corrected under WIC-1575 above.
- **Raising the cap was explicitly not the fix** — `limit` is capped at 100 server-side, which still fails a 137-application account, and the governing NFR says "100+".
- **`getAll()` follows `nextPage` to exhaustion** rather than dropping it (`ApplicationService.getAllPaged`, page size 100, bounded at 50 pages). It reports `totalCount` and a `truncated` flag; `ApplicationsList` — which previously showed at most 50 rows with no next-page control — renders a notice when the view is a prefix instead of presenting it as the whole account. `CommandPalette` and the global application list get the full set for free.
- **Neither card claims good news it cannot support.** With the aggregates still in flight, "All applications are up to date!" / "All caught up!" are withheld — an absent answer is not a clean bill of health.
- **Three behaviour changes worth noting:** the Quick Wins badge now counts every actionable application rather than the (≤5) rows on screen; the sampled follow-up rows are ordered oldest-first, so the two most-stale applications surface rather than the two least-stale ones that happened to head the page; and **the follow-up counts step up on deploy**, because moving the filter into SQL also silently changed the predicate. The client's `differenceInDays(now, updatedAt) > 7` floors, so it really meant *age ≥ 8 days* while the copy beside it said "> 7 days"; the SQL `updatedAt < now - 7 days` is stale at *age > 7 days*, which is what the copy always claimed. The whole `(7, 8)`-day window is newly counted — an off-by-one being fixed, not introduced, but an account whose applications were last touched 7–8 days ago sees a follow-up warning that was not there before. Recorded here rather than left as a surprise (noted in the review of this work, WIC-1575).
- **Regression coverage** — `Dashboard.attention.test.tsx` seeds 150 applications with 40 stale past the page boundary and asserts the card reports 40 (AC-N1c); it is red on the pre-fix tree, and its first case pins that the seed's first page contains zero stale rows, so the suite cannot pass for the wrong reason. Plus `applicationService.pagination.test.ts` (exhaustion, filter forwarding, visible truncation), `AttentionCard.test.tsx`, `QuickWins.test.tsx`, and `dashboard.routes.test.ts` for the wire contract. `dashboard.routes.test.ts` mocks the service module wholesale, though, so none of those execute the aggregation itself — inverting `lt` to `gte` on both thresholds compiles, would ship, and passed the entire gate while reporting the freshly-touched rows as the ones needing follow-up, which is this card's own defect one layer down. `dashboard.attention-conditions.test.ts` closes that: it lifts the predicates into an exported `buildAttentionConditions(now)` and pins them in two independent halves — the SQL each renders (the direction of every threshold comparison and the status set each count covers, via drizzle's own dialect, no database and no new dependency) and the wiring from predicate to reported field (a fake `db` that answers with a distinct count per predicate, so swapping two `countMatching` calls moves a number into the wrong field).

### Tests — The Dashboard attention aggregates are now executed, not just described (2026-08-27)

The `attention` block above is ~167 lines of aggregate SQL, and nothing in CI ran a line of it. `dashboard.routes.test.ts` opens with `vi.mock('../src/services/dashboard.service.js', ...)`, so it pins the route's JSON pass-through and stops there; `Dashboard.attention.test.tsx` computes its own expected counts in `seedDashboardResponse()` and hands them to a `fetch` stub, which tests the client beautifully and never reaches the server. The `40` that satisfies AC-N1c was a literal in a fixture at both layers. Measured: six independent mutations to `dashboard.service.ts`, each applied alone, left the whole suite green (WIC-1574).

- **`packages/api/test/dashboard.service.test.ts` drives the real `getDashboardStats` against a real Postgres** — PGlite, added as a devDependency, with `getDb()` mocked at it and the `applications` / `status_history` DDL mirrored from `schema.ts`. A stub database was not an option: every defect here is a *predicate* defect, and a hand-rolled stub resolves whatever rows it was primed with regardless of the predicate it was handed, so it certifies all six mutations as passing. Only a real planner distinguishes `updated_at < $1` from `updated_at > $1`.
- **The grading bar was the mutation matrix, not the line count.** All six now fail, each on correctly-named cells: the stale comparison flipped, the stale scope narrowed to active-only, the sample ordering reversed, the interviewing set losing `phone_screen`, and the two that matter — **bounding the counts by the sample limit**, which is WIC-1478's own defect re-implemented server-side, and **dropping the owner term from `countMatching`**, which leaks another user's counts.
- **Four more cells came out of review, all on one axis: pairs the typechecker cannot separate.** `staleThreshold` (7d) and `savedThreshold` (3d) are both `Date`s declared four lines apart, and `createdAt`/`updatedAt` are interchangeable columns — but no fixture row made either pair disagree, so swapping one for the other moved no row across any boundary and shipped green. Two rows close all four: one aged into the (3, 7)-day gap that nothing previously occupied, and one stale by `updatedAt` yet created yesterday. Both are inert under correct code, and the original six still fail on precisely the same cells, so the rows add discrimination without blurring.
- **Three more on that same axis, this time in `staleSaved`, which the two rows above could not reach.** Both are `status = 'applied'` and `staleSavedCondition` requires `status = 'saved'`, so neither ever enters that bucket — the threshold pair and the column pair were still interchangeable there, and only the column swap was tested. One `saved` row closes it: created into the (3, 7)-day gap, and last by `createdAt` but second by `updatedAt`, so the threshold choice and the ordering choice each move it. Reading `staleThreshold` for `savedThreshold` and ordering the sample by `updatedAt` both now fail, and the ordering assertion is split into its own case so the predicate and the ordering fail independently rather than pinning three properties under one name. That row takes `staleSaved` to 3, above the sample limit, so the count-clamping mutation reds seven cells rather than six — it was already a blanket failure, so no discrimination is lost (WIC-1588).
- **Counts and samples are asserted separately**, because `countMatching` and `sampleMatching` carry their own owner predicate; asserting only "no foreign rows in the samples" would have left the count's tenancy untested, which is precisely the leaking mutation.
- **AC-N1c is now reproduced server-side** — 150 seeded applications, 40 stale, asserting `counts.stale === 40` *and* `samples.staleActive.length === 2` together, since either number alone is satisfied by some mutation.
- One test documents rather than endorses: `getDashboardStats()` with no `userId` builds no owner filter and so reads every tenant (the WIC-1554 `sub`-less-JWT class; `applications.user_id` is nullable, as migration 0017 does not cover this table). When that is fixed the expectation should invert — failing there is the signal the fix landed.


### Tests — Focus E2E now covers all six dialogs, and the fourth one does not pass (2026-09-01)

`MODAL_FOCUS_MANAGEMENT_SPEC.md` §10 had one open follow-up: four of the six dialogs that consume `useDialogFocusRestore` had zero E2E focus coverage — `QuickReferenceExport`, `OnboardingModal`, `WizardContainer`, `DiffReviewModal`. It also predicted the outcome: *"all four consume the same hook, so the expected result is that they already pass."* Three do. One does not (WIC-1925).

- **47 new tests** across `modal-focus-onboarding.spec.ts` (19), `modal-focus-wizard.spec.ts` (10), `modal-focus-quick-reference.spec.ts` (9) and `modal-focus-diff-review.spec.ts` (9), at parity with `modal-focus.spec.ts`: dialog role and accessible name, focus moves in on open, Tab is trapped, Escape and Cancel restore the trigger, background scroll locked, page behind hidden from the SR virtual cursor.
- **`WizardContainer`'s focus restore is inert** — closing the dialogue wizard strands focus on `<body>`. It is entered by `navigate()` from `ProjectsList`, so the captured trigger unmounts on the way in and is detached by close time, and there is no `fallbackRef`. Third instance of the WIC-1181 / WIC-1222 class. Pinned `test.fail()` and filed as WIC-1931.
- **The deletion control is what distinguished the two cases.** Removing `{...focusRestore}` from each component costs exactly 4 tests on `QuickReferenceExport`, `DiffReviewModal` and `OnboardingModal`, and **0** on `WizardContainer` — nothing observes the hook's removal there because it does nothing. A spec that stays green when the code under test is deleted is not coverage.
- **`OnboardingModal`'s nested-confirm pins fired, and were collected on the merge.** The two nested confirms used to expose the panel behind them (two `role="dialog"`, neither `aria-hidden`); reproduced in Chromium, asserted honestly and pinned `test.fail()` rather than weakened to pass, on the stated basis that the pins turn RED when the behaviour is fixed. WIC-1868 then shipped that fix on `main` (`aria-hidden={confirmationOpen}`, `OnboardingModal.tsx:309`), so both pins were deleted when this branch merged `main` in and the two assertion bodies now pass unchanged, on their merits. Worth noting how it presented: the four spec files do not textually conflict with `main`, so the branch was green, `main` was green, and only the *merge* was red — a `test.fail()` is a dependency on another card's state, and the merge is where that dependency settles.

### Tests — `extraction.write-tenancy.test.ts` no longer names its cases for the defect they disprove (2026-09-01)

The catalog write-tenancy regression guard asserted correctness and was *named* for the leak. Its `describe` read `extraction.service catalog writes are not owner-scoped`, and each of its four generated cases read `<table> UPDATE admits a foreign tenant's row`, while every assertion inside demanded the opposite — `expect(admits(foreign)).toBe(false)`. On the fixed tree the suite is green, so `vitest` printed a tick beside the statement that the cross-tenant write is live, to anyone auditing tenancy from test output — which is the audit this file exists to serve. Names and comments only: no assertion, fixture or clause changed, and `extraction.service.ts` is byte-identical (WIC-1928).

- **The cases now state the property held** — `<table> UPDATE is owner-scoped: rejects a foreign tenant's row (not WHERE <column> alone)`, under `extraction.service catalog writes are owner-scoped`. A header banner states that green means the write is closed rather than live, since the sections below it describe the defect in the present tense of the tree it was found on.
- **The provenance citation was a one-digit typo.** The header and `describe` cited **WIC-1613**, a real but unrelated card ("US-6.3 filter by date"), so a reader chasing provenance landed somewhere plausible and wrong rather than on a 404. Corrected to **WIC-1623** — the card whose four UPDATE clauses this file pins, and the one commit `e58322fe` itself cites — with **WIC-1404** / **WIC-1406** named as the tenancy family. The typo came in from QA's branch name, `test/wic1613-extraction-write-tenancy`.
- **Detection power was re-measured rather than assumed.** Baseline 1042 passed across 49 files. Dropping `eq(techStackTags.userId, userId)` from the `techStackTags` UPDATE still reds exactly two cells — this file's *renamed* `tech_stack_tags` case and `extraction.tenancy.test.ts`'s co-resident-row case — at 2 failed / 1040 passed, so `passed + failed` reconciles against the baseline and the mutant is known to have compiled (`tsc --noEmit` clean) rather than to have failed to build.

### Fixed — Closing the dialogue wizard returns focus to the button that opened it (2026-09-01)

Dismissing the wizard at `/projects/new/dialogue` left `document.activeElement === document.body`, dropping a keyboard user to the top of `/projects` with the whole page to re-traverse. Scroll lock and `#root[aria-hidden]` were both released correctly; this was the only residue, and the only one a sighted mouse user never notices. Third instance of the WIC-1181 / WIC-1222 class, found by the WIC-1925 sweep (WIC-1931).

- **The prescribed remedy could not be applied, and that is the finding.** `MODAL_FOCUS_MANAGEMENT_SPEC.md` §5.3 makes a fallback obligatory for exactly this shape, but a `fallbackRef` cannot discharge it here: the wizard **is a route**, so at the moment `onCloseAutoFocus` runs *nothing on either page is mounted* — the trigger unmounted on the way in, and every fallback candidate lives on the destination route, which has not mounted yet. `fallbackRef.current` would be `null`. Both halves of `useDialogFocusRestore` are refs, and a ref cannot name a node that does not exist yet.
- **`useRouteFocusHandoff` (new) carries the target in `location.state` instead.** `DialogueCapture`'s `onCancel` names the destination control on the way out; `ProjectsList`'s "Add New Project (Guided)" button claims it on arrival. The button the user lands on is a **new instance** of the one they pressed. §5.3.1 of the spec records this as an extension to the rule rather than an exception to it.
- **It hands back a callback ref, not a `useRef`, and that is load-bearing.** `/projects` renders a loading skeleton until `useProjects()` resolves, so the control is absent on the destination's first commit — a mount effect reading `ref.current` would read `null` and focus nothing, reintroducing the same bug one layer up. Pinned by a test that holds `listProjects` open across the navigation and asserts the button is genuinely absent before it resolves.
- **The handoff is consumed once.** History state outlives the navigation that carried it, so an uncleared handoff would yank focus again on every Back into that entry and after a reload. Asserted as behaviour — navigate away, come Back, focus is not stolen — not as an implementation detail.
- **`{...focusRestore}` is deleted from `WizardContainer.tsx`**, replaced by a `focus-restore-exempt` comment naming the real mechanism. WIC-1925 measured its removal as costing **0** tests there against 4 on each of the other three dialogs; leaving an inert call is what made this dialog look covered in the first place.
- **The `test.fail()` pin in `modal-focus-wizard.spec.ts` is deleted and its assertion is unchanged** — byte-for-byte the one that was failing. 18 new vitest cases cover the mechanism and the wiring.
- No API, schema or wire change. Web only.

### Tests — The partial-view notice, and the collection metadata behind it, are now pinned (2026-08-27)

Two invariants that the entries around this one depend on were carried correctly by the code and asserted by nothing. Both turned out to be the same fixture problem wearing two hats, and both were found by re-measuring those changes rather than by reading them (WIC-1570, off the PR #180 and PR #160 reviews).

- **`ApplicationsList` *showing* a truncated view was unpinned, while `getAllPaged` *computing* it was not.** Replacing `{isPartialView && (` with `{false && (` — deleting the notice outright — leaves the web suite **fully green at 67 passed / 2 todo**, re-measured on this branch with the new file held out. (That reconciles against this PR's own base `9293b0e`, which measures **64 passed / 2 todo**: the three hook cases added here bring it to 67, and with the new file held out the mutation kills nothing. An earlier report of 62 for the same mutation was taken on a PR #160 tree that this branch is not stacked on — the merge-base it actually descends from measures 59 — so that figure reconciles with nothing here and is not the baseline.) So the AC-N1b promise "either it paginates to exhaustion or it renders that the view is partial" had five red cells behind its first limb and none behind its second. `ApplicationsList.test.tsx` (new, 5 cases) drives the real page over a stubbed server through the real `apiClient`, `getAllPaged` and `useApplicationCollection`; it reds that mutation on 3 of its cases.
- **The fixture is the load-bearing half, not the assertion.** Every existing web fixture set `totalCount` to `applications.length`, and against that seed a notice printing the row count where the account total belongs is *indistinguishable* from a correct one. The new stub serves one row per page and never runs out of cursor, so the page holds 50 rows out of a reported 137 — the only shape in which "Showing the first 50 of 137" can fail. A dedicated first case asserts the two numbers differ, so the suite cannot quietly regress to passing for the wrong reason.
- **The optimistic patch's `...collection` spread is now asserted, not merely present.** `useUpdateApplicationStatus().onMutate` preserves `totalCount` and `truncated` correctly; the drift `totalCount: collection.applications.length` inside the updater was **5 passed / 0 failed** and `tsc`-clean, because it is a well-typed `number`. Since `ApplicationsList` reads exactly that pair, the drift would have made the notice read "the first 100 of 100" for the width of every in-flight status change — silently converting a partial view into a complete-looking one at the moment the user is interacting with it. The two seeded collections now differ in their metadata (one truncated prefix, one complete), so neither field can be satisfied by a hardcoded literal either.
- **`updatedAt` on the optimistic row is asserted.** Dropping `updatedAt: new Date()` was also 5 passed / 0 failed — `...app` supplies the stale value, so it is type-clean. `calculatePipelineStats` derives its "Stale (14+ days)" count from that field, so without it a card the user has just moved keeps counting as stale until `onSettled` refetches.
- `useApplications.optimistic.test.tsx` grows from 5 cases to 8. The "(5 cases)" figure in the entry below was accurate for what that change shipped and is left as written.
- **Six negative controls, all measured, all discriminating**, on the two files together (13 cases green unmodified): deleting the notice reds 3; printing `rawApplications.length` where `totalCount` belongs reds 1; the `totalCount` drift reds 1; hardcoding `truncated: false` in the updater reds 1; dropping `updatedAt` reds 1; and weakening the seed back to `totalCount: applications.length, truncated: false` reds 2 — the last of those is the control on the fixture itself, so the property that makes the other five capable of failing cannot be removed silently.
- **Test-only — no production file is modified by this change.**


### Added — every route now sets its own `document.title` (2026-09-01)

`docs/design/ROUTE_TITLE_CONVENTION.md` has specified this since 2026-08-19 and was ported into
the repo on 2026-08-27, but **nothing had ever implemented it**: `grep -rn "document.title"
packages/web/src/` returned nothing at all, and all 31 in-app routes plus `/login` shared the one
static `<title>` in `index.html`. Every browser tab, history entry, bookmark and window-switcher
row named every screen identically — the textbook WCAG **2.4.2 Page Titled (Level A)** failure for
a single-page app, and the reason `Ctrl/Cmd+H` could not be used to get back to an application.

- **The title mirrors the route's `<h1>` verbatim** (§0.3), so titles inherit whatever the casing
  standard lands on and cannot drift from the heading independently. The strings were re-measured
  against the tree rather than copied from the doc: every one is stable, but **every line number in
  §5 had moved** in the five days since the port.
- `PRODUCT_NAME`/`formatTitle` live in one module, so the brand is a one-line change. `index.html`
  and `Login.tsx`'s `<h2>` now read **Careerpin**, which is what the marketing site and the
  production host say. Those are the two places §2 named; they are **not** the last two in the
  product. `OnboardingModal.tsx:330` ("Welcome to Your Job Application Manager") and
  `QuickReferenceExport.tsx:201` ("Generated with Job Application Manager", printed on the exported
  interview sheet) still carry the old name. Both are prose headlines rather than titles, neither
  is mechanical to rename — "Welcome to Your Careerpin" does not read — and the wording is the
  Copywriter's to set, so they are flagged here rather than guessed at.
- **The 404's title is read from its copy block, never retyped.** `NotFound.copy.ts` is a new module
  for exactly that: the separator is a typographic em dash and the apostrophe in "couldn't" is a
  straight `'`, so a title retyped from the design doc's prose disagrees with the heading in a way
  that is invisible on the page and fails only in an exact-match assertion.
- **A `<Route>` added with no title fails the build.** The convention's AC8 asked only that this be
  "visible in review", on the strength of co-locating a `title` field with the path. That was not
  available: `route-integrity.test.ts` parses `App.tsx` as raw source, so converting the route table
  to a data array would have left that audit matching nothing and passing vacuously — trading a live
  guard for a stylistic one. `route-title-coverage.test.ts` pairs the declared paths against the
  title table in both directions instead, which is stricter than review, not weaker.
- 47 unit cases across four files, each negative-controlled: writing the title during render instead
  of in an effect, dropping the restore-on-unmount, adding an untitled `<Route>`, and unmounting
  `RouteTitle` from the shell each fail the suite. The last of those is the one that matters — the
  other three files all pass with the mechanism deleted from `App.tsx`.

### Fixed — Moving a Kanban card between columns shows the move immediately (2026-08-26)

`useUpdateApplicationStatus` has carried an optimistic-update block since it was written, and none of it ever ran. `onMutate` snapshotted with `queryClient.getQueryData(applicationKeys.lists())`, but `lists()` is the *prefix* `['applications', 'list']` — a list query registers under `list(filters)` = `[...lists(), filters]`, one entry per filter combination the app has rendered. `getQueryData` and `setQueryData` are exact-match; prefix matching is `getQueriesData` / `setQueriesData`. So the snapshot was always `undefined`, the `if` guarding the patch never fired, and the paired `setQueryData(lists(), …)` would have written to a key nothing reads. Dragging a card between columns had no optimistic feedback at all: the board only moved once the request round-tripped and `onSettled` refetched. The `onError` rollback was dead for the same reason (WIC-1497).

- **This is a latency-masking defect, not a correctness one, which is exactly why it survived.** `onSettled` invalidates and refetches, so the final state was always right. Any test that awaits the mutation passes on the broken code — the bug is only observable *during* the in-flight window, so every assertion in the new suite is taken there.
- **The patch now reaches every cached list, and the rollback reaches every list the patch touched.** `previousLists` is the full `[queryKey, data][]` from `getQueriesData`, restored pair by pair in `onError`. Restoring a single key would leave every other filter showing a status the server had rejected. The single-application path (`detail(id)`) was always exact-match and always worked; it is unchanged.
- **Regression coverage** — `useApplications.optimistic.test.tsx` (5 cases) drives the real hook against a hand-held deferred, so nothing it asserts can be satisfied by the post-settle refetch. All 5 are red on the pre-fix implementation. Four further negative controls were measured on top of that pre-fix tree: reverting the rollback to the bare `lists()` key, and restoring only the first list, each red exactly the rollback case; patching only the first matching list reds the multi-list case; and writing to `['applications', 'list']` itself reds the guard asserting nothing is ever stored under that key — which is the shape the original defect had.
- **No wire change, and no change to the settled state.** Only the window between the drag and the response.


### Security — the dev server's filesystem allow-list is ratified and pinned, and it narrows rather than widens (2026-09-02)

`packages/web/vite.config.ts` carries `server.fs.allow: ['..']`, which bounds what `vite dev` will serve off disk. It reached `main` inside merge commit `d59c74bf` (PR #143, WIC-1382) as conflict-resolution content, and is present in **neither parent**: the board-approved head `75aaf1e`, the branch parent `f8b046d4` and the `main` parent `fb57518f` all lack it. Content that exists only in a merge resolution appears in no commit's own diff, so `git log -p` over the branch never rendered it and it was never in a reviewed diff — `git show --cc` is the only view that shows it. Found while re-deriving the post-approval delta for WIC-1499 (WIC-1971) and filed as WIC-1980.

- **The reflex reading of `allow: ['..']` is backwards here, and the reflex fix would have made things worse.** In a single-package repo that idiom widens a boundary, so the instinct is that a security setting was loosened without review and the remedy is to delete it. The opposite is true. `server.fs.allow` **replaces** Vite's default rather than extending it (`allow: raw?.fs?.allow ?? [searchForWorkspaceRoot(root)]`), and the default is the **repo root**, because the root `package.json` declares `workspaces: ["packages/*"]` and `searchForWorkspaceRoot` stops at the nearest ancestor carrying that field. Resolved against this config's root of `packages/web`, `'..'` is `packages/` — a strict subset. The line **tightens** the dev server, and deleting it would hand it the whole repository, `.dev.vars` and `supabase/` included.
- **Measured against a running dev server, in both directions.** Same tree, same branch, booted with and without the line, probing `/@fs/<abs>`: the repo-root `package.json` is served with real file content without it and returns `403 Restricted` with it, while `packages/api/package.json` is served either way. Vite's own 403 body prints the resolved allow-list, and it is the single entry `<repo>/packages`.
- **Status codes alone are not a valid signal on this surface — read the body.** A probe of `/@fs/etc/shadow` returns **200** with the key unset, which reads as the dev server serving the shadow file. It is not: `checkLoadingAccess` returns `fallback` for a path that is neither allowed nor readable, so the response is Vite's SPA-fallback `index.html`. Only a probe whose body can be recognised as the file's real content discriminates, which is why the repo-root `package.json` is the one used above.
- **Ratified rather than reverted, and the config now says why.** Reverting was the card's other option and is the strictly worse posture. The three lines stay, with a comment naming what they resolve to and warning against "restoring the default". Nothing measured requires `packages/` specifically over the tighter `['.']`; tightening further is a real option and a separate change.
- **Pinned behaviourally, not textually.** `src/test/viteFsAllow.test.ts` resolves the real config through Vite's own `resolveConfig` and asserts file-by-file access with `isFileServingAllowed`, so it measures what the value resolves to rather than that the literal `['..']` is present. It carries a control that resolves the config a second time with `configFile: false` and asserts the default **is** the repo root — the assertion that makes "this narrows" falsifiable instead of a claim in a comment, and that goes red if Vite ever changes how the default is derived.
- **No functional change, and nothing shipped is affected.** `server.*` is absent from `vite build` output. With the optimizer cache cleared, the dev module graph crawls identically with and without the line — 146 modules, zero non-200, zero `/@fs` escapes — because `react` and friends, though hoisted to the repo root, are pre-bundled into `packages/web/node_modules/.vite/deps`, inside the boundary. The line also does not gate vitest: narrowing it to `['.']` leaves the cross-package `?raw` audit in `upload-limit-drift.test.ts` green at 17/17.

### Security — Cover letter generation no longer trusts caller-supplied STAR and cover-letter ids (2026-08-26)

UC-4's eight row-addressed handlers all scoped their lookup by `user_id`, so AC-20 read as satisfied. But AC-20 only ever described the id in the **route path** — it was silent about ids carried **inside the request body**, and those were unchecked. Two reads acted on them without an owner predicate, both returning another user's content to the caller rather than merely consuming it internally (WIC-1437; pre-existing, not introduced by any open PR).

- **STAR entries are scoped to the caller** — `fetchStarEntries` selected `quantified_bullets` by id alone. `selectedStarEntryIds` is caller-controlled and required on the generate route, so supplying another user's bullet ids returned that user's `rawText` — the user-authored accomplishment sentence — in the `201`'s `usedStarEntries`, interpolated it into the LLM prompt, and persisted it as the caller's cover letter. The existence check made this worse rather than better: `invalidIds` was computed against whatever came back, so another user's ids counted as valid and no error fired; only ids belonging to *nobody* were rejected. The helper now takes `userId` as a **positionally required** parameter — so no call site can silently omit it — and adds `eq(quantifiedBullets.userId, userId)`. All four call sites thread it, including `getCoverLetter`: a cover letter row written by the old path can already carry a foreign STAR id, so the ids stored on a row are not trustworthy merely because the row is owned. Another user's ids now report as not found, keeping the 404-not-403 posture AC-20 already chose.
- **Outreach cover-letter context is scoped to the caller** — `generateOutreach` loaded a cover letter by caller-supplied `coverLetterId` with no owner predicate, putting the first 500 characters of another user's letter into `contextText` for the LLM and into the outreach message returned to, and stored for, the caller. It already received `userId` and applied it correctly on its insert; it just never applied it to this read. Now matches the five sibling lookups.
- **When no identity is present, the STAR read fails closed** — routes pass `c.get('userId') ?? undefined`, and auth is bypassed only when both `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` are absent (ADR-003). An earlier revision of this fix made the whole conjunction conditional — `userId ? and(ids, owner) : inArray(ids)` — which scoped the authenticated branch and left the anonymous one selecting purely by caller-supplied ids. That is the same IDOR, narrowed rather than closed, and it was argued for here on the grounds that `quantified_bullets.user_id` is `NOT NULL` so an `IS NULL` predicate "would match zero rows and break local dev". Matching zero rows is the point: WIC-1465 ruled against that idiom, and the owner term is now unconditional — only its value varies, `IS NULL` when there is no caller. An anonymous caller gets the `STAR_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND` empty state rather than a global read (WIC-1482). The outreach cover-letter read is a genuinely different case and is unchanged: `cover_letters.user_id` **is** nullable, so it has a real legacy-null cohort and degrades unscoped to stay consistent with its five sibling lookups.
- **Regression cover** — `packages/api/test/cover-letter.tenancy.test.ts`. The fake `getDb()` renders each `where` clause with `PgDialect.sqlToQuery` and filters the fixtures by the predicate actually built, because a stub that resolves rows regardless of the predicate passes just as happily with the bug present. Each of the six changed sites — two predicates and four call sites — was reverted individually and confirmed to fail the suite on its own.
- **The guard evaluates boolean structure, not the presence of an owner term** — the first version of this suite decided "is this scoped?" with a regex per constraint and then applied the constraints *conjunctively itself*, so the conjunction was the test's assumption rather than the query's. Flipping `and(id, owner)` to `or(id, owner)` reintroduces this very defect and left the suite green. It now delegates to the shared tenancy evaluator (`packages/api/test/helpers/tenancy.ts`, WIC-1491), which parses the rendered SQL into a real boolean tree and throws on shapes it cannot model rather than assuming they pass. Pinned by a per-site mutation matrix over the eight **id-addressed** owner-bearing conjunctions — the seven `and(id, owner)` reads plus `updateCoverLetter`'s `and(id, version, owner)` UPDATE — each flipped to `or` **alone**: `:130` 7 failures, `:342` 1, `:435` 1, `:446` 1, `:461` 1, `:481` 1, `:610` 3, `:715` 1. Zero survivors *among those eight*. This is **not** a file-scoped completeness claim, and an earlier revision of this bullet wrongly read as one ("each of the eight owner-bearing conjunctions in `cover-letter.service.ts`"). Enumerating that file by the `and(id, owner)` call *shape* misses a ninth owner-bearing site, `listCoverLetters`, which hoists its owner term into an array. It was raised as coverage residue on WIC-1614 and is closed by the next bullet.
- **The absent-caller branch is pinned in both directions** — restoring `userId ? and(ids, owner) : inArray(ids)` turns exactly the three new `IS NULL` tests red and leaves every other test in the file green, so the control proves the assertions bite on this predicate alone rather than on the fix as a whole. Measured at head `6cc366a`, where the file holds 28 tests: 3 red, 25 green.
- **`listCoverLetters` was the ninth owner-bearing site, and nothing reached it** — the mutation matrix above enumerated this file by the `and(id, owner)` call *shape*. `listCoverLetters` hoists its owner term into an array — `conditions.push(eq(coverLetters.userId, userId))`, applied later as `and(...conditions)` — so it matched no such grep and was never counted. Re-enumerating by the owner **column** finds it, and it survived a lone `and(...conditions)` -> `or(...conditions)` flip with the full suite green: with `?status=draft`, a caller would have received every user's draft letters. The service was already correct; nothing exercised it. `cover-letter.routes.test.ts` mocks the service wholesale, `pagination.test.ts` calls it with a cursor and no `userId` (so `conditions` is empty and the `and` is never built), and this suite's fake `db` could not reach it either, because the list path is `.orderBy().limit().offset()` and `limit` resolved straight to a promise. The stub now returns a chainable from `limit`, and four cases drive the real list path. Note the mutation only bites with a *second* condition present — `conditions.length === 1` short-circuits past the `and` — so a case that passes identity alone re-pins nothing; one case supplies a filter alongside it and another covers the single-condition branch.
- **Re-measured at head `0f3dcde`, all ten mutants killed** — flipping each owner-bearing site **alone**: `:141` 9 failures, `:355` 1, `:411` 3, `:388` (owner term deleted) 4, `:446` 1, `:457` 1, `:472` 1, `:492` 1, `:621` 3, `:726` 1. Zero survivors. Two controls bound the matrix from both sides: a comment-only edit to the service kills 0 (so the suite is not merely failing on any edit), and the two `id + version` optimistic-locking predicates at `:451` and `:566` stay green (so the assertions target tenancy rather than over-fitting to every conjunction in the file). Line numbers here supersede the `:130`/`:342`/`:435`… tally in the bullet above, which predates the WIC-1482 commit that shifted the file.



### Docs — the a11y enforcement note denied the check that had just landed (WIC-1675 / PR #299)

`586712c2` landed the rendered route sweep, and `ACCESSIBILITY.md` went on saying it had not. Six passages in the top status block were false against `main` @ `22e60707`, all in the direction that tells a reader not to bother looking: the "What remains unverified" note said outline coverage was pending "until it lands"; a paragraph asserted **four `h1` → `h3` skips are live on `main`** when `586712c2` fixed all four; and the spec-coverage figure still said the check reaches "two of the seven specs, and for UC-5 a fixture rather than the route" — the exact case the sweep now covers as a route.

- **A denial is the expensive direction of a stale pointer.** An overclaim invites a reader to check; a denial tells them not to. This block denied a build-gating accessibility check for as long as it stood, and no test, type or lint could ever have failed — the code was right and the contract was the sole dissenter.
- **The four skips are fixed, not merely visible.** `ProjectsList.tsx:145`, `ResumeManager.tsx:189`, `ProjectDetail.tsx:66` and `SavedFilterShortcuts.tsx:127` are `<h2>`; `Login.tsx:63` went `<h2>` → `<h1>`. The paragraph is kept in the past tense on purpose — the shape of the defect is the argument for rendering four branches per route rather than one, and deleting it leaves the check's design unexplained.
- **The table gains a sixth row and the lead-in count moves five → six.** The sweep renders **30 routes × 4 branches = 120 pairs**, pinned in the test itself. Heading-level skips are enforced with **no allowlist**; the weaker missing-`h1` half allows **25** pairs via `MISSING_H1`, shrink-only and guarded both ways. **21 of the 25 are `loading`/`error` branches** — the page is nameless exactly while it is slowest and while it is reporting a failure — and the other 4 are the two routes with no route-level `<h1>` in any branch. An allowlisted defect is still a defect, and that list is now the honest residual.
- **PR #299's own description says "29 routes x 4 branches (116 pairs)"; the merged test pins 30 and 120.** A route was added during review. Re-derived from `expect(ROUTES).toHaveLength(30)` rather than restated from the commit message, which is the only reason the figure published here is right.
- **`SC 1.3.1` is split rather than flipped.** Its heading-order component is now covered site-wide; labels, list and table semantics, and visual-only relationships still have no site-wide check. Claiming the whole criterion either way would have been wrong.
- **A stale enumeration predating this merge, found while re-deriving it.** The `headingOutline.ts` row claimed assertions against "exactly **two** application components". `b4b87c66` added a third on 2026-08-27 — `pages/CoverLetterNew.test.tsx`, which mounts the real page — under WIC-1571, *the same card the row cites*. Wrong for five days, and not caused by #299.
- **The `KanbanBoard.test.tsx` fixture is deliberately left alone.** It still does not match the page; that was never the fix. What stopped being true is "nothing checks that it does" — `routeOutlineRoutes.tsx` mounts the real `<ApplicationsList />`, so the route is judged as a route. WIC-1834 closed on that basis.
- **One divergence recorded but not decided.** `A11Y_ENFORCEMENT_RULING.md` §4.2 argued WIC-1675 should ship *as* an axe-core adoption "rather than as a second bespoke utility"; it shipped on the bespoke `headingOutline.ts`, and `axe-core` is still in no `package.json`. §4.2 now carries a dated outcome note stating that fact and explicitly declining to rule on it — whether Ruling 2 is satisfied, superseded or outstanding is an architectural call, routed as **WIC-1945**.

Docs and one routed decision; no source, schema, wire or test behaviour is touched by this entry.
