- **`/applications/new` could not be fixed the way the ticket, and `ROUTE_HEADING_OUTLINE.md` §5.1, both prescribe.** The suggestion is an `<h1>` on the page; the route mounts `ApplicationForm` with `open={true}` and never closes it, and a Radix modal marks every node outside its portal `aria-hidden`. A page-level `<h1>` there is present in the DOM and absent from the accessibility tree — it reads as fixed, and no screen reader can reach it. §5.1 assumes a page whose body a user can reach; this route has none, so the dialog's own title carries the `<h1>` via a new `titleLevel` prop. **That prescribed fix is now a negative control in the suite**: `ApplicationNew.test.tsx` renders it and asserts the heading is unreachable, so the arrangement cannot come back as a "simplification". Measured — applying it fails 3 tests, the first with `Unable to find an accessible element with the role "heading"`.
- **Every assertion goes through `getByRole`, never `querySelector`.** That is the whole design of these files rather than a style preference: Testing Library's role queries read the accessibility tree and skip `aria-hidden` subtrees, so they can tell the two arrangements above apart. A `querySelector('h1')` check passes on the broken one, which is how a heading no screen reader can reach ships with a green test.
- **The section heading moves with the dialog title.** "Extended Tracking" sits directly beneath it, so promoting the title alone would run the outline `h1 → h3` — the level skip `ROUTE_HEADING_OUTLINE.md` §1.3 forbids, introduced by the fix for a missing heading. Both tags derive from `titleLevel` together, and the test asserts the whole sequence rather than the presence of an `<h1>`; pinning `SectionTag` back to `h3` fails exactly that one case.
- **`/login` keeps its wordmark, at the same size and position, as a `<p>`.** The product-name string is deliberately unchanged: `ROUTE_TITLE_CONVENTION.md` §2 has it and `index.html:13` as the last two places saying `Job Application Manager` while the marketing site says Careerpin, pending a Copywriter call. That is a copy decision and this is a markup one, and they are separable now that the element is not carrying the outline. The new `<h1>` names the task (`Sign in` / `Create an account`), and the session-bootstrap branch carries an `sr-only` copy so that state is not a hole in the outline either.
- **Two doc claims that no diff of this PR touches were falsified by it, and are corrected here.** `COMPONENT_SPECS.md` §10 listed `ApplicationForm` among the components "already correct at both of their depths" — WIC-1563 measured the two depths for a level *skip*, and at both sites there wasn't one. What a comparison of depths cannot see is that on `/applications/new` there is no host `<h1>` and cannot be one: the outline is not too deep there, it is missing its root, and a check for skips is satisfied by an outline that never starts. `ACCESSIBILITY.md`'s form snippet named the old string at a fixed `<h2>`.
- **Both `/applications/new` and `/login` were marked `new copy` in the §5 title table, and `route-title-table-audit.py` skips any row whose title cell contains that phrase.** So for as long as the copy was aspirational, CI verified *nothing* about those two rows. Dropping the marker is what puts them under the check — the audit is what caught this PR's own change to the `/job-fit-analysis` row, failing with "the copy changed, or the heading moved" before it was updated.
- **Titles re-cased to sentence case** (`New application`, `Edit application`) per `CONTENT_STYLE.md`, which governs heading copy — these strings became headings rather than decoration. `Add` is dropped because the title now names the screen rather than instructing the user, and §5's tab label is a verbatim copy of it. §5's hook-driven count stays at 6 while its composition changes: `/job-fit-analysis` left the set and `/login` joined it, since naming the screen made that heading `mode`-dependent.
- **Eleven Playwright assertions encoded the old outline, and `npm run test` cannot see them.** The vitest suite went fully green while 10 gates in `job-fit-analysis.spec.ts` waited on `heading "Job Fit Analysis Results"` — a heading this change removes — and `auth.spec.ts:19` asserted `getByRole('heading', { name: /job application manager/i })`, which *is* the `/login` defect, written as an expectation. A copy change to a heading is therefore also an e2e change, and the unit suite is structurally blind to it: vitest does not collect `e2e/`, so the only signal was CI's separate E2E job.
- **The obvious retarget for those 10 gates is the one that breaks them silently.** Pointing them at the new persistent `<h1>` compiles, reads natural, and makes every gate **vacuous** — the `<h1>` is on screen at the input stage, so the wait resolves before anything has been submitted. Measured by deleting TC-1's submit click: with the `<h1>` gate the wait still resolved and the test failed five lines later on `getByText('Possible fit')`, reporting missing *content* for a submit that never happened; with the `<h2>Results</h2>` gate the same deletion fails **at the gate**. They key on the `<h2>`, which is now the only heading whose appearance marks the input → results transition.
- **Six mutation controls, all discriminating**, with the fix committed first and the tree verified clean afterwards: frame `<h1>` removed 6 · `titleLevel` dropped 3 · the ticket's literal page-`<h1>` fix 3 · section tag pinned to `h3` 1 · `/login` reverted 5 · the ticket's *first* option for `/job-fit-analysis` (promote both stage `<h2>`s) 6. That last one fails `holds the route's name still across the input → results transition`, which is the assertion the option-2 choice rests on. Web suite 114 passed / 2 todo across 18 files.

### Fixed — three of ONBOARDING_FLOW.md's eight Must-Have acceptance boxes were checked and untrue (2026-08-29)

`docs/design/ONBOARDING_FLOW.md` §Acceptance Criteria → Must-Have carried eight `- [x]` boxes. WIC-1656 was filed about the last two (`Keyboard accessible`, `Screen reader compatible`); re-measuring all eight against `main` @ `4681803` found a third. Five hold and stay checked, with their evidence now stated; three are unchecked with what is actually true restated underneath, in the shape WIC-1655 established for `ACCESSIBILITY.md`. Documentation correction only — no component behaviour changes here (WIC-1656).

- **The third box was found because the card said to check its neighbours.** `Feature tour highlighting 4 key UI elements` is wrong on both counts and is not a tour: step 4 renders **three** static description cards, and there are zero `getBoundingClientRect` / `anchorEl` / `spotlight` / `popover` / `data-tour` occurrences anywhere under `components/onboarding/`, so nothing is anchored to any live UI element. This is the same result WIC-1655 got — one authoring pass wrote the whole list, so one bad box is evidence about the rest, not an isolated slip.
- **`aria-modal` without a focus trap is worse than neither.** Both dialogs in `OnboardingModal.tsx` (`:139-140`, `:174-175`) set `aria-modal="true"` while the file handles zero `Escape` keypresses, installs no focus trap, and contains zero `.focus()` calls. Assistive tech is told to hide everything outside the dialog while keyboard focus can still walk out into it — so focus lands on controls the AT has been told do not exist, and nothing is announced.
- **`Keyboard accessible` is unchecked as _partial_, not as false.** The steps genuinely are operable — 17 native `<button>` controls, plus a `ResumeUploadZone` drop zone that is a correctly-built pseudo-widget (`role="button"` + `tabIndex={0}` + an `onKeyDown` handling `Enter`/`Space` + an `aria-label`). Collapsing that to a bare `- [ ]` would have thrown away a true fact and sent the next reader to re-audit working code; the failure is the dialog container, and the box now says so.
- **Re-check requires a measurement and the commit it was taken at — not a PR number**, per WIC-1628. The behaviour fixes are explicitly _not_ claimed here: they belong to `MODAL_FOCUS_MANAGEMENT_SPEC.md` §4 (migrate the hand-rolled dialogs to Radix `Dialog`). Unchecking records the gap; it does not schedule it. `doc-reference-audit.py` cannot catch this class at all — it proves a cited document exists, not that a claim inside one is true, so a false `[x]` passes it cleanly.

### Added — `restoreFocusTo` now has a stated obligation, and a check that will enforce it (2026-08-29)

`MODAL_FOCUS_MANAGEMENT_SPEC.md` §5.1 and §5.2 both answer _which_ element to pass to `ConfirmationModal`'s `restoreFocusTo` — but only once you have already decided you need to pass one. Nothing stated _when_ a fallback is obligatory, and the prop is optional (correctly: a cancel-only dialog whose trigger survives must not be forced to name one). So a future call site whose confirm action destroys its own trigger reintroduces WIC-1181 with no type error, no lint error and no failing test. New §5.3 states the obligation, and `docs/design/confirmation-modal-focus-audit.py` makes it a red check rather than a hope (WIC-1670, from the Code Reviewer's non-blocking note on PR #115).

- **The obligation is written as a structural test on the render tree, not a judgement about the trigger.** The natural question — "is the trigger detached when the dialog closes?" — is the wrong one and has already misled two reviews: it usually is _not_ detached, because the failure is an ordering race in which the restore succeeds and is undone a macrotask later (§4.2). §5.3 asks instead **"does the trigger render inside anything the action's refetch re-renders?"**, which an author can answer by reading their own JSX. A per-row control inside a `.map()` over the mutated collection always answers yes; so does a control inside any arm of a branch whose predicate the action can flip.
- **The three non-remedies are named**, because all three were tried: an `isConnected` guard (passes, because the node is still connected when it runs), declining to `preventDefault()` (Radix's own handler prevents anyway and focuses an always-`null` ref), and a manual pass that looked fine (the damage lands after the decision point).
- **Enforcement is a declaration, not an inference.** A lint rule would have to decide whether a dialog's `onConfirm` unmounts its own trigger — data flow across a mutation, a query invalidation and a conditional render, not statically decidable. And making the prop _required_ would be worse than the status quo: authors would satisfy the type with a throwaway ref, converting a visible omission into an invisible dead ref, which is §5.1 rule 2's failure mode on purpose. So every `<ConfirmationModal>` call site must instead either pass the prop or carry a `focus-restore-exempt` comment saying why its trigger survives. Reasons under 40 characters are rejected — "cancel only" is a shrug, not a declaration.
- **The audit is dormant at this commit, and says so on every run.** `restoreFocusTo` does not exist on `main` yet; it lands with PR #115. Rather than fail the build on a compliant-by-absence tree or pass silently, the script prints a `NOTICE` naming every unenforced call site (one today, `ResumeManager.tsx:176` — the one whose trigger the action destroys) and exits 0. It arms itself automatically on the commit that declares the prop. This deliberately avoids touching `ResumeManager.tsx`, which PR #115 is currently editing.
- **What the green check does not cover is stated in the script and in the spec.** It cannot tell whether the ref you passed is any good — that the fallback renders on both arms of the branch, and is non-`null` at close time, are §5.1 rules no grep can check. It covers `ConfirmationModal` call sites only, while the rule itself is normative for all six dialogs. Verified end-to-end against PR #115's head, where it goes green on the real compliant call site, and against synthetic call sites for each failure path: bare, short-reason, well-reasoned exemption, and an unparseable tag.
- **The UI/UX workspace copy of the spec is now marked superseded.** Two copies of a normative document is how §5.3 would have ended up in the one nobody can open.

### Security — `POST /api/catalog/generate-diff` decides ownership at its own boundary (2026-08-30)

The route validated only the *shape* of `sourceId`, so an authenticated caller could name any user's resume or application ULID. Nothing downstream re-checked it on the way in: `getTextContent` (`extraction.service.ts`) reads the source row by id alone, and the extraction that follows auto-applies whatever it finds into the **caller's** catalog — so the owner's résumé prose was both read and written into a stranger's catalog before the scoped diff lookup at the end of `generateDiff` ever ran. `generateDiff` now resolves the source row scoped by `userId` *before* calling `processCatalogChange`, and raises the same `404` an absent document yields (WIC-1414).

- **This is a boundary decision, not a second copy of the reader's predicate.** The card was filed as defence-in-depth on the premise that PR #141 had already closed the leak. That premise does not hold on `main`: #141 is still open, so neither `resolveOwnerUserId` nor the owner-scoped `getTextContent` it adds exists here, and the pre-existing scoped lookup cannot help because the damaging write happens strictly before it. Checking at the entry point means the `404` survives whether or not #141 lands, and whether or not the reader beneath is later widened.
- **A foreign id and an absent one are deliberately indistinguishable** — both yield `NotFoundError`, so the endpoint does not become an existence oracle for other users' document ids.
- **Single-user mode is unchanged.** `authMiddleware` sets `userId` to `null` when Supabase is unconfigured and the route forwards that as `undefined`; requiring ownership there would `404` every local-dev call, so the probe is skipped when no identity exists to compare against. A mutant that runs the probe unconditionally is caught by two tests.
- **Covered by a four-mutant matrix, each gated on the suite still collecting 70 tests** so a mutant that fails to compile cannot read as a pass. Removing the guard (the original defect) kills 4 tests; dropping the owner term from the resume probe kills 2; from the application probe, 1; forcing the probe to run in single-user mode kills 2. The fixtures drive `scopedReadStub`, which evaluates the real Drizzle clause against each row, so an id-only predicate admits the foreign row and the guard genuinely goes quiet rather than a canned row set masking it.

### Fixed — the changelog duplicate check could not see the failure mode it was written for (2026-08-29)

Root `CLAUDE.md`'s "Check what the driver did" detector counted **byte-identical** stripped lines. The first failure mode named two paragraphs above it is _"both sides revised the same existing entry — union keeps both revisions"_, and two revisions of one bullet are by definition not byte-identical, so the check was blind to the class it was partly written for. It also never looked at `### ` headings at all, which is where a whole-entry double-ship shows up (WIC-1687, found by the Frontend Developer while fixing WIC-1684).

- **It now compares a normalised 70-character prefix, and checks headings as well as bullets.** The tradeoff is stated in place: a prefix match also flags genuine pairs that merely open the same way, so the discriminator is the tail, not the prefix. The two known-benign pairs currently on `main` are named so the check has a meaningful pass condition, and a duplicate `### ` heading is called out as having no benign case.
- **A third failure mode is documented: one side moves a block, the other edits inside it.** The two do not align as one diff3 region, so union keeps the relocated copy _and_ the edited copy. The sting is that **moving a block is the documented remedy for the ordering defect**, so fixing one failure mode arms another for the next branch to touch that entry. Caught on PR #212 before merge (WIC-1692): its base branch had relocated an entry while #212 added a bullet inside it, and the union result carried the whole `### Security — Resume-variant and interview-prep reads…` entry twice, with the surviving second copy silently missing the hijack disclosure that entry exists to record.
- **The check is now runnable before you push, not only after you merge.** A clean `main` says nothing about what is queued to land on it — the corruption exists only in the merge _result_, and both parents can be individually spotless. The section carries a `git merge-file --union` simulation, with the warning to run it against the PR's **true base** rather than `main`, since simulating a stacked PR against `main` manufactures duplicates that will never ship.
- **Verified by extracting the embedded block from `CLAUDE.md` and running it verbatim**, rather than by eye: it returns `duplicate headings: none` and exactly the two documented benign bullet pairs on `main` @ `e0897df`, and as a positive control it fires on the reconstructed #212 union with `duplicate headings: {'security  resumevariant and interviewprep reads are sco': [11, 32]}` — which the previous byte-identical check reports as no headings at all.

Documentation and tooling only. No code, no tests, no behaviour change.

### Fixed — "Applied This Week" fell when an application progressed (2026-08-30)

`dashboard.service.ts` counted applications where **`status = 'applied'`** AND `appliedAt` was inside the window. The filter was on *current status*, not on the act of applying. `appliedAt` survives a status transition, so the timestamp was there the whole time — the row simply stopped matching the moment the application advanced. A user who applied to three jobs on Monday and moved one to `phone_screen` on Tuesday saw "Applied This Week" read **2**. The metric decremented on exactly the outcome the product exists to produce, under a label — "Applied This Week" — that every user reads as *submissions* (WIC-1515, filed by the Business Analyst from an undefined-term audit of WIC-15 US-6.3).

- **This was not implementation drift.** `docs/architecture/DATA_MODEL.md` carried the same `status = 'applied'` predicate, so the reference design and the implementation agreed with each other and both were wrong. The definition itself was the defect, and it went unexamined because US-6.3 named the metric without ever writing one down for it to be checked against. Both are corrected together, and `DATA_MODEL.md` now carries a "Window metric definitions" section stating the two rules that were violated, so the next reader inherits a definition rather than a query to copy.
- **Both window metrics now count submissions, blind to status** — the predicate is `applied_at` inside the window and nothing else. Terminal states are deliberately included: an application that was submitted and then rejected was still submitted. Rows that were never submitted need no special handling, because their `applied_at` is NULL and `NULL >= $1` is UNKNOWN, which `WHERE` does not treat as a match.
- **`appliedThisMonth` is now a fixed rolling 30 days, and its window no longer depends on the day it is read.** It used `setMonth(getMonth() - 1)`, which overflows short months in *both* directions — read on March 31 it produced Feb 31 → March 3, a **28-day** window; read on January 31 it produced December 31, a **31-day** window. The card predicted 28–31 days and both ends are now pinned by tests. It is a rolling 30 days rather than calendar month-to-date; the AC left the choice open, and the rolling window is what matches the sibling 7-day metric. Nothing renders this field yet, so the defect was latent — the API contract and both `DashboardStats` declarations now say "last 30 days" so that whoever binds it labels it truthfully.
- **`packages/api/test/` had no dashboard test at all**, which is why this and its sibling shipped. `GET /dashboard` now has one, asserting `appliedThisWeek`, `appliedThisMonth`, `byStatus`, `recentActivity` and `responseRate` against a fixed fixture on a frozen clock. `responseRate` is asserted, not changed — the web-side defect in it belongs to the sibling card.
- **Reverse-checked rather than assumed.** Restoring the original service verbatim from `origin/main` fails 5 of the 12 new tests with the exact predicted values — the card's own scenario reports `2` where it should report `3`, six post-submission statuses collapse to `1`, March 31 yields `0` and January 31 yields `2`. The other 7 pass under both versions by design: they are controls covering the never-submitted rows, the 7-day boundary, the two dates on which `setMonth` happens to be correct, and the owner term. The test count is identical across both runs (12), so no failure is a mutant that merely failed to compile. 747 API tests pass; baseline on `origin/main` is 735.
- **The counts needed a fake `db` that the existing one could not provide.** `scopedReadStub` resolves `.where()` honestly but always to *rows*: `.groupBy()` is a no-op and a `count(*)` projection is ignored. It also evaluates predicates with the tenancy parser, whose operator set stops at `= <> is null in` — and `>=`, the operator that *is* the window, degrades there to UNKNOWN and therefore admits everything. A test built on it would have reported the same number for a 7-day window, a 30-day window and no window at all. The new `aggregate-db-stub.ts` models the aggregation and is **fail-loud** where the tenancy helper is fail-open: a `WHERE`, `ORDER BY` or projection it cannot parse raises instead of resolving. That is the opposite posture from its neighbour, deliberately — for a leak assertion the permissive value is safe, but for a metric definition a query that quietly resolves unfiltered is the whole bug.

### Fixed — the changelog check reported ten branches as damaged when nine of them repair themselves (2026-08-30)

Root `CLAUDE.md` told readers that when a duplicate is already committed on a branch rather than introduced by the union merge, "re-merging `main` will not help." That is false, and false in the direction that turns a detector into an accusation generator. Ten open PRs still carry the WIC-1319 retracted fit-tier claim that PR #204 deleted from `main`; **nine of the ten lose it automatically the next time `main` is merged in.** The previous revision would have had someone file cards on all ten (WIC-1677).

- **The discriminator is one question, and the section now leads with it: is the offending text in `git merge-base origin/main <branch>`?** If it is, `main`'s correction is a deletion relative to a shared ancestor — a one-sided change that the three-way merge applies cleanly, without ever consulting the union driver. The branch is a passenger and owes nothing. If it is not, the branch introduced the text itself, `main`'s deletion has nothing to attach to, and no amount of merging forward will remove it. Measured across the ten: mergebase=1 on #123, #146, #180, #183, #188, #191, #215, #222 and #239; mergebase=0 on #117 alone.
- **What an owner looks like is a committed union result.** PR #117 took its copy inside merge commit `508289b`, which merged `fix/wic1309-fit-tier-blurbs` into `copy/wic1318-fit-tier-blurbs` while the source branch still held the retracted wording. That source branch has since been corrected and measures clean today, but #117 committed the driver's output and thereby converted a transient merge artifact into a branch-side addition. The generalisation is now stated in the file: the union driver's damage becomes permanent at the instant it is committed, which is the concrete reason to simulate before pushing rather than trust a clean `git merge`.
- **The self-heal test runs against `origin/main`; the union simulation runs against the PR's true base.** They disagree deliberately, because they ask different questions — the simulation asks what a merge will produce and needs the base that merge uses, while the self-heal test asks where the correction lives, and it lives on `main`. A stacked PR whose immediate base still carries the stale text is not thereby an owner: #191 and #123 both show the duplicate in a union against their own bases and are passengers against `main`.
- **The previously filed set was measured again and neither member survives.** The 2026-08-29 entry named PRs #146 and #160. #146 is a passenger; #160's branch is at `494d49d` and now contains zero occurrences, its author having repaired it. This is the second consecutive tick in which an accusation about a peer's branch decayed before it could be acted on, so the file now carries the round-trip confirmation as well as the count comparison.
- **Verified by extracting the new `bash` block from `CLAUDE.md` and executing it verbatim**, which reproduces the `pr/146 mergebase=1 branch=1` / `pr/117 mergebase=0 branch=1` split the prose quotes. Round trip on both, merging `main` into the branch and that result back into `main`: #146 ends at zero occurrences with the detector clean, #117 retains the retracted claim and both `SAME-ENTRY` bullet pairs. `main` itself is clean — the sweep returns `duplicate headings: none` and only the two documented benign `distinct entries` pairs at 0.40 and 0.50.

Repository guidance and its embedded checks. Application code, tests and runtime behaviour are untouched.


### Added — Cover letters and resume variants record the application they were written for (2026-08-30)

`cover_letters` and `resume_variants` each carried `target_company` and `target_role` and nothing else tying them to the application that prompted them. The web app collected the association and threw it away: `CoverLetterGenerator` takes an `applicationId` prop and wrote it only into the in-memory result handed to `onComplete`, and the generate route's Zod object is `.strict()` with no such key, so sending the id was a `400` rather than a no-op. WIC-1533 shipped the entry point by reconstructing the link client-side from `(targetCompany, targetRole)`, which works and has a ceiling that pair cannot pass — two applications for the same role at the same company are indistinguishable, pinned as an explicit test in `packages/web/src/constants/coverLetterMatch.test.ts`. That ceiling is not liftable from the web side (WIC-1544).

- **Migration `0024` adds a nullable `application_id` to both tables, `REFERENCES applications(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`, and deliberately does not backfill.** (Renumbered from this branch's original `0021`/`0022` — three sibling PRs independently claimed 0021 through 0023 before this branch merged `main`.) The only way to guess an id for an existing row is the same `(company, role)` heuristic, which by construction writes a *wrong* id wherever it is ambiguous — replacing an honest "best match" with a false record of fact. `NULL` means "we do not know", which is true. `SET NULL` rather than `CASCADE` because a cover letter is the user's writing and outlives the application it was aimed at.
- **`POST /cover-letters/generate` and `POST /resume-variants/generate` accept an optional `applicationId`, and both resolve it through the caller's own owner scope before persisting it.** The field is a client-supplied foreign key, so an unscoped lookup would both confirm the existence of another user's application id and staple it onto this user's row. A mismatch is a `404 APPLICATION_NOT_FOUND`, not a silent drop — a letter that quietly forgets the application it was asked to record is the defect being fixed.
- **`GET /cover-letters?applicationId=` and `GET /resume-variants?applicationId=` filter on exact equality, not the substring `ilike` the neighbouring `company` filter uses.** An id is an identity, not a search term: one ULID's prefix is a legitimate prefix of another, so `ilike` would silently widen the filter.
- **Verified against a real Postgres rather than a query stub.** Three of the five acceptance criteria are properties of the database — exact-versus-substring matching is a claim about compiled SQL, "existing rows keep working" is a claim about nullability, and "deleting an application does not delete its letters" is a claim about a foreign key's `ON DELETE` action that no amount of TypeScript can demonstrate. The new suite replays the project's real migration files under PGlite **in `meta/_journal.json` order, by tag**, which is what drizzle's migrator does at deploy time, so a `.sql` file added without its journal entry fails loudly instead of passing as a stub would.
- **Each oracle was shown to be load-bearing by a seven-mutant matrix with predicted kill counts**, every mutant gated on `passed + failed == 11` so a non-compiling mutant cannot read as a clean sweep. Dropping `applicationId` from the cover-letter insert kills 2; swapping the list filter's `eq` for `ilike` kills exactly the prefix test and nothing else; flipping the foreign key to `CASCADE` kills both `AC-5` tests; removing the journal entry kills 8 of 11, the three survivors being precisely the tests that throw in the ownership lookup before ever reaching the new column. Six of the seven matched the prediction exactly.

API-side only. `packages/web` is untouched by design — once this lands, `packages/web/src/constants/coverLetterMatch.ts` should be deleted in favour of the filter, and its same-role/same-company test will start failing, which is the intended signal. That follow-up belongs to the Frontend Developer.

### Fixed — `catalog_diffs.user_id` is NOT NULL, closing the one table 0017 backfilled and forgot to constrain (2026-08-30)

Migration `0017_enforce_userid_not_null.sql` backfills NULL `user_id` to the `00000000-…-0` placeholder on **seven** tables (step 1) and applies `SET NOT NULL` to **six** of them (step 2). `catalog_diffs` is in the first list and absent from the second — the only one of the seven omitted — and `schema.ts` agreed, declaring the column nullable. The table therefore _looked_ migrated: its historical NULLs were gone, but nothing stopped new ones, and `processCatalogChange` wrote `userId ?? null` on every ownerless event, undoing the cleanup at runtime. New migration `0023_enforce_catalog_diffs_userid_not_null.sql` sweeps whatever NULLs remain to the same placeholder and adds the constraint (WIC-1604).

- **An ownerless diff row was never "kept for later" — it had no reader at all.** `listDiffs`, `getDiff` and `applyDiff` all scope with `eq(catalog_diffs.user_id, caller)`, and NULL equals nothing, so the user whose upload produced the diff could never see it. The only caller that could is one passing no `userId`, which applies no owner predicate whatsoever — the fail-open path WIC-1638 is closing, not a feature. So `processCatalogChange` now declines the write and logs why, rather than persisting a row that the new constraint would reject anyway.
- **Ordering against 0021 is load-bearing, which is why this is stacked and not standalone.** `0021_backfill_catalog_diffs_user_id.sql` (WIC-1408) recovers the _real_ owner of these rows by joining `trigger_id` back to `resumes` / `applications`. Sweeping to the placeholder is irreversible — once a row reads `00000000-…-0` its true owner can no longer be inferred — so running this migration first would destroy recoverable ownership. 0023 runs after 0021 (and after 0022, an unrelated `catalog_diffs` column added by a sibling PR that landed on `main` first and claimed this migration's original number), deliberately.
- **One cohort is knowingly given up, and the migration prints the number rather than leaving it to inference.** 0021 leaves NULL those rows whose source was deleted or is itself unowned, so they stay countable; the second becomes recoverable if that resume or application ever gets an owner. `SET NOT NULL` ends that option. A `RAISE NOTICE` reports NULLs before, rows swept, and NULLs after — the same trick that made 0021's own count legible in CI — and the migration raises rather than constrains if anything is still NULL.
- **The tests apply the real migration files off disk, in journal order, under PGlite.** Everything under test is SQL semantics, and hand-written DDL that merely mirrors `schema.ts` is how a sibling card got a clean false negative. The chain is applied in two phases — through 0022, then 0023 alone — because "confirm the count before and after" is only observable by seeding rows into the pre-0023 world. Blanking the migration body turns exactly 4 of the 7 red; the other 3 assert what it must _not_ do, which an absent migration also satisfies. Reverting the service guard turns exactly 2 of its 3 red, the third being the owned positive control that proves the fixture reaches the write.
- **The other 13 nullable `user_id` columns were audited and none is the same bug.** Of 21 `user_id` columns the tree now has 8 NOT NULL and 13 nullable, and all 13 are mentioned **zero** times in 0017 — none was ever backfilled, so none is "backfilled but not constrained". Constraining any of them is a separate decision needing its own backfill, not a sweep. `personal_info` explicitly stays nullable: single-user local rows genuinely carry NULL and `personal-info.service.ts` depends on it.

### Fixed — the changelog check's most-trusted signal missed a real double-ship by one character (2026-08-29)

Root `CLAUDE.md` told readers that a duplicate `### ` heading "has no benign case — that one is always a bug". True, and it quietly invited the inverse, which is false. The heading check matches a fixed normalised 55-character prefix, and a correction normally rewords the heading along with the body, so its silence carries no information at all. Open PRs #146 and #160 carry the WIC-1309 fit-tier entry twice — once in the wording WIC-1319 retracted, once in the correction — and the check reports `none` on both (WIC-1677, generalised from the PR #117 report).

- **The near-miss is a single character wide, and widening the window is the wrong instinct.** The two headings normalise to `…no longer contradict the c` and `…no longer contradict the t`, diverging at index **54** of a 55-character comparison. A longer prefix makes the check stricter, not more sensitive; a shorter one collapses every `Fixed — ` entry together. The fixed-prefix framing has no setting that catches this, so the heading check is kept exactly as it is — high precision, low recall, a hit is still always a bug — and the prose now says outright that `duplicate headings: none` is not a clean bill of health.
- **The sensitive check is the bullet check, and it now names the entry each hit sits under.** Reporting a bare line number pair asked the reader to re-derive the context that decides the fix. The enclosing `### ` headings separate three genuinely different bugs: `SAME-ENTRY` (union interleaved two revisions _inside_ one entry, so a claim and its own retraction sit a few lines apart — delete the superseded bullets, keep the heading), `REVISION-PAIR` (union kept a whole entry _and_ its rewrite under near-identical headings — delete the superseded entry outright, then re-check the seam), and `distinct entries` (two real entries that merely open alike).
- **Heading similarity is a classifier on bullet hits, never a standalone sweep.** Anchored to a shared bullet it drew zero false positives across `main`. Run over all `### ` pairs instead, a 0.75 threshold flags two innocent pairs on `main` at `eb40da8`: the WIC-1373 and WIC-1365 catalog-scoping entries at 0.81 (different services, different endpoints, read in full to confirm) and `UC-6: Resume Variant Generation` against `UC-4: Cover Letter Generation` at 0.75. The distinction between the two framings is the whole reason the classifier is usable.
- **Every figure in the section was produced by extracting the block from `CLAUDE.md` and executing it, not by reading it.** Negative control on `main` @ `eb40da8`: `duplicate headings: none`, and the two known-benign pairs classified `distinct entries` at exactly the 0.40 and 0.50 the text quotes. Positive control on the affected branch files: `REVISION-PAIR` at 0.83 on #146 (`1a4b992`) and #160 (`c0d9089`), `SAME-ENTRY` at 1.00 on #117 (`508289b`) — each alongside `duplicate headings: none`, which is the claim the section rests on.
- **The affected set is quoted at a measured head because it moves.** PR #150 was in it and is not any more: its author repaired the branch while this change was being written, and a re-measure immediately before merge found `374a52b` clean. Naming three PRs would have shipped a false accusation with a green check on it — the same failure the anchor figures elsewhere in this file carry a "re-run it, never quote it" warning about.
- **The three-input control from the previous revision is what kept this honest.** Every hit is already committed on its branch, not introduced by the union, so the merge is innocent and the fix belongs to the branch author. Baselining on `main` would have reported them as merge damage and sent the repair to the wrong place.

Repository guidance and its embedded checks. Application code, tests and runtime behaviour are untouched.


### Tests — the storage backfill's `main()` wiring is covered; five reinstatable defects are not (2026-08-30)

- `packages/api/scripts/migrate-project-storage-keys.mjs` exported four pure helpers and the suite
  pinned them well — but only where they were *defined*, never where `main()` consumed them, and
  `main()` is where both WIC-1433 round-2 defects actually lived. Five mutants inside `main()`
  survived the full green suite. The worst is silent: hand the local walk the **slug** set instead
  of the userId set and it enumerates nothing, prints `Legacy files: 0`, prints "All legacy project
  artefacts are attributable" and exits **0**, leaving every project file on the shared cross-tenant
  prefix. An operator reads that as done.
- Fixed structurally rather than with more assertions. `ownerIdsOf` is now the single place the
  userId set is derived, and it **throws** on a pre-derived set rather than honouring it — a `Set`
  answers `.values()` too, so the wrong argument would otherwise reproduce the original bug exactly.
  Both enumerators take the slug map itself, and the backend branch moved out of `main()` into an
  exported `enumerate`: making the wrong argument unpassable does not make the call site *testable*,
  and both round-2 defects were call-site defects.
- The unresolved tally no longer adds two slug counts to a file count and labels the total
  "N slug(s)". `unresolvedCounts` reports slugs, occupied destinations and files separately, and an
  occupied destination alone still blocks. The exit code was already right; the number was not.
- The local walk's `.catch(() => [])` swallowed `EACCES` identically to `ENOENT`, so an unreadable
  legacy directory produced that same false "all attributable / exit 0". Only a missing directory is
  tolerated now. This deliberately reverses `c1b50f9` — aborting loudly is the safe direction for a
  script whose entire product is a trustworthy answer to "is the move complete?".
- 41 tests, up from 22. Verified by mutation: all five reported survivors now red, plus five further
  mutants covering the new seams — 10/10 red, 0 survivors, each gated on the mutant parsing and on
  `passed + failed` matching the baseline, so a non-compiling mutant cannot read green.

### Added — a shared outcome announcer, and the create-success announcement `ProjectsList` never had (2026-08-30)

`MODAL_FOCUS_MANAGEMENT_SPEC.md` has required two things of the destroyed-trigger class since 2026-08-19: send focus somewhere sensible when the control the user activated is unmounted by its own action, **and** announce the outcome in a polite live region. Only the focus half was implemented for `ProjectsList`'s create-success path. A screen-reader user who created their first project therefore heard `"Create Project, button"` — the header control focus had been redirected to — and was never told the project existed, or why focus was on a button they did not press (WIC-1304, split out of the WIC-1295 review of PR #97 as explicitly non-blocking for it).

- **The helper exists because four hand-rolled regions were four different answers.** `useAnnouncer` + `<Announcer>` (`hooks/useAnnouncer.ts`, `components/Announcer.tsx`) encapsulate the three rules a live region has to satisfy, each already rediscovered the hard way here: portal out of `#root` or `#root[aria-hidden]` silently stops being set behind _every_ dialog app-wide (the PR #115 / `ResumeManager` failure); wrap nothing focusable or the `aria-hidden` exemption leaks a live control behind every dialog (WIC-1155, `EmptyState`); and stay permanently mounted, because assistive tech announces _updates_ to a region already in the accessibility tree.
- **Announcing the same outcome twice is otherwise silent.** Two projects may legitimately share a name, and re-setting an identical string is not a DOM change, so the second create would announce nothing at all. `useAnnouncer` alternates an unspoken zero-width space so consecutive identical outcomes still read as two distinct updates, without the text growing without bound.
- **The regions that were _not_ consolidated are named, with the discriminator.** `wizard/ProgressIndicator`, `OnboardingProgressIndicator` and `KanbanBoard`'s drag announcer derive their text from render state — they are content, not outcome reporting, and `ACCESSIBILITY.md`'s component-local carve-out already blesses them in place. Migrating them would have been churn against the documented rule, so the scope note says so rather than leaving the next reader to wonder why a "shared helper" has one caller.
- **The portal assertion was rewritten after it was caught passing against a deleted portal.** Testing Library's default container is a fresh `<div>` on `<body>`, so a component rendered the normal way is already a body-level sibling of `#root` whether it portals or not — the `#root[aria-hidden]` test could not fail. It now renders _inside_ a synthetic `#root`, which is what makes the portal the thing under test. Both portal tests and both repeat-announcement tests were then confirmed to fail against a deliberately broken implementation; the `ProjectsList` test fails with the `announce()` call removed.
- **Cover is unit-level as well as end-to-end.** `Announcer.test.tsx` drives the real `aria-hidden` package rather than asserting on attributes, since the point is the interaction between the attribute and the hiding library. `ProjectsList.test.tsx` pins the wiring, including that a _failed_ create announces nothing. `e2e/modal-focus-projects.spec.ts` gains the browser-level assertion the card asked for, next to the focus half it already covered.

### Fixed — a malformed JSON body was reported as a server fault on every write endpoint that takes one (2026-08-30)

Every route read its body as `schema.safeParse(await c.req.json())`, with the `await` outside any `try`. `c.req.json()` throws a `SyntaxError` on unparseable input, `app.onError` has no branch for one, so it took the generic arm and returned `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` — and `console.error`'d the client's typo into the logs as a server fault. **34 call sites across 10 route files, none of them guarded.** All 34 now go through a shared `readJsonBody` helper (`packages/api/src/lib/request.ts`) that raises `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` / `Request body is not valid JSON` (WIC-1524, reported by the Technical Writer while documenting the onboarding endpoints on WIC-1359).

- **Zod was never the problem, which is why the test carries a wrong-shape control.** Valid JSON of the wrong shape already returned a correct `400` — the defect was strictly upstream of Zod. A test asserting only "400" therefore cannot tell the new guard from the pre-existing one and would pass with the helper deleted, so every case in `test/json-body.test.ts` is paired with a `[]` control and the discriminator is the message, not the status.
- **The fix is verified by reverting it, not by watching it pass.** Restoring the bare `c.req.json()` at all 34 sites turns the suite `19 failed / 9 passed` against a predicted `19 / 9`, and the 9 survivors are exactly the 9 wrong-shape controls. A single-site revert on `personal-info.ts` kills exactly the 3 tests that touch that route and leaves its control green.
- **An empty body was the same defect and is fixed with it.** `Content-Length: 0` is not valid JSON, so it took the same `500`; it is now the same `400` rather than a `200` treating the body as `{}`.
- **A missing `Content-Type` is not a separate code path.** Measured, because the card asked: Hono does not gate `c.req.json()` on the header, so a body parses with or without it. That is the one thing checked here that needed no change.
- **The helper is the shape that stays fixed.** A per-route `try`/`catch` would work and reopen at every new endpoint — the same reasoning `lib/pagination.ts` records for cursors.
- **`API_CONTRACTS.md` documented the `500` as a known rough edge; that paragraph is now the plain `400` contract**, moved out of the onboarding section since it was never onboarding-specific. Both `/api/auth` routes still return `503 NOT_CONFIGURED` for a malformed body in an unconfigured environment — a config gate short-circuits ahead of the parse. That is a different code path and is unchanged. (The card named only `login`; `register` measures the same, so the two guarded sites in `auth.ts` are the ones this suite cannot reach and are covered by the count, not by a case.)
- **The contract is scoped to write endpoints that take a JSON body, and the qualifier is load-bearing** (WIC-1843, reported by the Technical Writer against this PR's own diff). `POST /resumes/upload` reads `multipart/form-data` via `c.req.parseBody()`, so a malformed body there is a `400` carrying `BAD_REQUEST` / `No file provided` — the status matches but the discriminator the section invites clients to branch on does not. Every `DELETE`, plus writes like `POST /auth/logout`, read no body at all and ignore a malformed one outright (`/auth/logout` measures `204`). The unqualified claim was wrong about more endpoints than the report caught, so the section states the rule rather than a grep tally, per the "counts in prose rot" note in root `CLAUDE.md`.

### Fixed — the onboarding navigation tests raced the navigation they assert, and one of them could not fail (2026-08-30)

`OnboardingModal.test.tsx` failed on roughly **1 run in 4**, measured locally at 1/4 and reproduced on CI against PR #252's head (`Received: "/"` at the `/applications` assertion). It is a test defect, not a product one: the step-6 shortcuts and step 5's CTA all route through `handleFinishAndGo()`, which is `await completeOnboarding(); navigate(to)` fired from `onClick` as a floating promise. `userEvent.click()` resolves while the navigation is still a microtask away, so sampling the location probe once immediately after the click is a race. The three navigation assertions now poll through a `waitFor` helper. 20 consecutive runs pass.

- **One of those three could never have failed, which is why the flake looked narrower than it was.** The harness started the router at `initialEntries={['/']}`, and "Go to Dashboard" navigates to `/` — the assertion's expected value was the _initial_ value, so it read identically whether the click navigated or did nothing. Verified rather than asserted: with `navigate(to)` commented out of the component, `main`'s suite reports **2** failures and this one stays green; after the fix it reports **3**. The start path is now a sentinel (`/onboarding`) that no shortcut targets, so `/` is a destination the test can actually distinguish.
- **The fourth location assertion is deliberately left synchronous.** "Advances without creating anything when the footer is used to decline" asserts that navigation did _not_ happen; wrapping a negative in `waitFor` passes on the first poll regardless, so it stays a single sample — now against the sentinel rather than against `/`.
- Closes WIC-1795. The flake sat on an untouched base and was blocking unrelated PRs, which is why it is fixed on its own branch rather than inside the PR that surfaced it.

### Fixed — a decorative ✓ could land in a STAR field's accessible name (2026-08-29)

`STARInput` marked a valid field with `<span aria-label="Field valid">✓</span>`. The span has no `role`, so it maps to the ARIA `generic` role, whose name-from-author is **prohibited** in ARIA 1.2 — assistive tech may honour that `aria-label` or ignore it, and both readings are conformant. Because the span sits inside the `<label>` that names the textarea, the two readings produced two different accessible names for the form control: `"Situation: … Field valid"` when honoured, `"Situation: … ✓"` when dropped. Closes WIC-1191, the second and last member of the class opened by WIC-1185 (`ChangeActionBadge`, PR #101).

- **The glyph is now decorative and the status is real text.** `<span aria-hidden="true">✓</span>` plus a `sr-only` "Field valid" — no ARIA naming on a `generic` element, so the field's accessible name is stable at `"Situation: … Field valid"` under either reading. This is the worse variant of the class and needed the opposite remedy to WIC-1185: there the fallback text was the meaningful label `Create`, so dropping the attribute was sufficient; here the fallback was a bare tick that polluted a form control's name, so the status had to be re-expressed as text rather than merely unlabelled.
- **The class is closed, and the scan that says so is multi-line aware.** A tag-aware sweep of every `.tsx` in `packages/web/src` — matching opening tags across line breaks, not `aria-label` lines in isolation — finds zero remaining `generic` elements carrying an author name. The single-line grep the original ticket used would have missed any site whose attributes wrap, so the count is re-derived rather than inherited.
- **Both halves are now pinned by tests, asserted on behaviour rather than markup.** `src/test/prohibitedName.ts` strips prohibited names to model the AT that ignores them, and the tests assert the accessible name both before and after: it must name the field valid and must never contain the glyph, under either reading. Asserting `not.toHaveAttribute('aria-label')` would instead go green again the moment the attribute returns in another shape. Reversal-checked — restoring the old markup fails 2 of the 4 `STARInput` tests, with the pre-fix name reported as `"Situation: What was the context or challenge you faced?✓"`, reproducing the ticket's measurement in-repo.
- **Accessible names are read through jest-dom's `toHaveAccessibleName`, not `dom-accessibility-api` directly.** The latter is only a transitive dependency here, and its `package.json` `exports` block hides its own `.d.ts` from `tsc` — a direct import resolves to `any` and fails `tsc -b` under `noImplicitAny`, while passing an incremental local typecheck whose `.tsbuildinfo` predates the new file. Caught by CI on the first push of this branch; `tsc -b --force` is the check that reproduces it locally.
- **`ChangeActionBadge` gets its regression cover retroactively.** PR #101 shipped with none available: `packages/web` had no unit-test harness on `main` at the time and the evidence was an out-of-tree axe-core run. The harness has since landed, so the assertions are backfilled here alongside the sibling fix rather than left as prose in a merged PR body.
- **This class is invisible to `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`.** `role-supports-aria-props` only fires once an element _has_ a role, so a role-less element passes clean — confirmed in the WIC-1185 review against the strict ruleset, all 40 rules, zero findings. The lint rule tracked by WIC-1192 would not have caught either instance; these tests are the enforcement.

### Fixed — `/outreach/new` had two platform pickers and the visible one was a lie (2026-08-29)

The route rendered **four radios, two of them "Email"**: one picker owned by `OutreachNew`, a second owned by `OutreachComposer` directly below it. The composer copied the page's `platform` prop into a `useState` initialiser, which runs on first mount only, and nothing keyed the composer — so every later write from the page's picker was discarded (WIC-1583).

- **The harm was not a dead control, it was a lying one.** Clicking the page's "Email" radio showed Email selected while the composer stayed on LinkedIn, with no error state. The composer's value is what feeds the generation request, `PLATFORM_LIMITS` (a 1900/300-char InMail budget instead of email's unlimited/500), and `limits.hasSubject` — so a user who picked Email at the top and never noticed the second picker got a LinkedIn InMail, silently, with a subject line they were never offered.
- **The page's picker is deleted and the `platform` prop with it.** Removing only the picker would have left a vestigial prop still copied into state. Dropping the prop means the composer's `platform` reads nothing external, so the drift is structurally impossible rather than merely unreachable — and the control now sits with the fields whose limits it decides. That is one of the five `OutreachComposer` sites blocking the lint rule in WIC-1618.
- **The remaining seed props are reset by a `key`, not by an effect.** `company`, `jobTitle` and `contact` are editable fields that must stay local, so the composer is keyed on every seed prop *this page passes* — not on `hiringManager`, which it never passes. `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` rejects the textbook resync effect in this repo (WIC-1612), and remounting cannot go stale by construction. `prefillContext` is renamed `initialContext` so the prop name states the mount-only contract it always had. The key is defence-in-depth and no test pins it: reaching the stale-seed case needs a link to `/outreach/new` from within `/outreach/new`, which does not exist.
- **The surviving picker was also not a radio group.** Its two radios shared no `name`, so each took its own tab stop and arrow keys did not move between them; the bare `<label>` above them named nothing. Now a `<fieldset>`/`<legend>` with `name="outreach-platform"`. The three Context inputs were likewise unassociated with their labels and are now wired by `htmlFor`/`id` — four unlabelled controls removed, no visual change.
- **Seven regression tests, red before the fix.** They drive the real route rather than the component in isolation, which is the only way this class is observable (WIC-1612): a component-only test is green on the defect. The load-bearing one asserts `getAllByRole('radio')` returns 2, not 4. Three of them stub `coverLetterService.generateOutreach` and generate, because everything `PLATFORM_LIMITS` decides — the Subject field, the `Body`/`Message` label, the character budget — is inside `{body && (…)}` and is therefore unobservable until a message exists. Each is a killed mutant: giving email LinkedIn's limits, giving LinkedIn email's, and pinning the picker to `linkedin` each turn a test red.

### Changed — the interview-prep relevance score is `relevanceScorePct` on the wire and in the column (2026-08-30)

`relevanceScore` named two populations at once: the job-fit / resume-variant one is a ratio in `[0, 1]` (the accepted UC-3 definition), and the interview-prep one is a 0-100 integer with no spec backing. ADR-008 §4 puts ratios at the API boundary and requires a deviating field to carry the unit **in its name**, so the interview-prep population is now `relevanceScorePct` end to end — `interview_prep_stories.relevance_score_pct` (migration `0020`), `PrepStoryDTO.relevanceScorePct`, the LLM prompt's JSON key, and the markdown export (WIC-1520, backend half of WIC-1516 AC-T3c).

- **Renamed, not converted, and the migration is gated to prove it.** The column is `INTEGER` and the value is produced by a prompt asking for a `<0-100 integer>`, so converting would mean a column type change plus a value backfill — failure modes strictly worse than the naming problem. `ALTER TABLE ... RENAME COLUMN` moves no data and carries `NOT NULL` with it. The statement is wrapped in an `information_schema` guard so a re-run is a strict no-op rather than `column "relevance_score" does not exist`, and a test asserts the migration contains no `UPDATE` and no `ALTER COLUMN`.
- **The rename passed the entire 753-test suite with no test edits at all — that was the finding, not the result.** Nothing in the suite observed this field. The one assertion naming it (`interview-prep.routes.test.ts:440`) sits behind a `vi.mock` of the whole service and reads back the test file's own fixture, so it stays green whichever name the service uses; it is structurally incapable of failing on this change. The new gates in `interview-prep-relevance-pct.test.ts` drive the **real** service through the WIC-1449 stub harness instead.
- **Typed `Percent` *and* tested, because the brand does not reach any of these sites.** Per ADR-008 §3 the brand is checked on assignment only — arithmetic, template interpolation and `JSON.stringify` all erase it — so `relevanceScorePct: Percent` cannot defend the `[0, 100]` clamp or the `/100` export string. Both are pinned by test, along with a negative control that sends the **old** key and asserts the value does *not* arrive: without that direction, a service reading either name looks identical.
- **Verified by an 11-mutant matrix, each gated on a predicted kill count.** Two predictions were wrong and the gate caught both. One is worth recording: mutating the clamp to `clampRatio(...)` — an identifier this module does not import — crashed at runtime rather than mutating semantics, killing 9 tests instead of 4 and *reading as stronger coverage*. A `passed+failed == baseline` gate does not see that, because all 16 tests still collect. Only the predicted-count gate does.
- **`drizzle-kit generate` could not produce this migration**, so `0020` is hand-authored in the repo's house style and its `meta/_journal.json` entry (idx 20) is hand-maintained, per the WIC-930 convention. `meta/0001_snapshot.json` is an empty stub (`"tables": {}`) declaring version `"7"`, which the pinned drizzle-kit v0.21.4 rejects as unsupported, and none of the 19 preceding migrations carry drizzle's `--> statement-breakpoint` marker — this repo has never used the generator.
- **`completeness` (0-100) is deliberately left alone**, as ADR-008 records under "Not addressed", and WIC-1514's files are untouched — that card owns them.

### Docs — onboarding step 5 is ruled back to an inline quick-add; the entry directly below is superseded in part (2026-08-29)

`main` @ `eb40da8` (WIC-1689, the entry below) and open PR #146 (WIC-1383) are two mutually exclusive answers to the same step, and their test files auto-merge into a suite no component can satisfy: one asserts the "I'll Do This Later" button is absent, the other clicks it. That is a product disagreement, not a merge conflict, so it was ruled rather than resolved. **The inline quick-add wins, under WIC-1689's own single-body-control rule** — build #146's form, do not re-add its second button. Design ruling only; no component behaviour changes here, and `docs/design/ONBOARDING_FLOW.md` §Step 4 carries the reasoning (WIC-1715, routed from WIC-1711).

- **The route-out fails accepted AC-7 in all three clauses.** _"application is created with status 'Saved' / And user proceeds to completion step"_ — `handleFinishAndGo('/applications/new')` takes no fields, creates nothing, and **leaves** onboarding rather than proceeding. Confirmed downstream: `applicationStepCompleted` and `applicationStepSkipped` appear in `packages/web/src` only as type declarations in `onboardingService.ts`, with zero assignments anywhere in the client, so both schema columns are still permanently `false` and the two metrics that read them ("Skip Rate by Step", "First Application Time") still report a step nobody has reached. WIC-1689 fixed the visible no-op and delivered neither AC.
- **Three UX costs are independent of the AC.** It inverts the reward — step 6's "You're All Set! 🎉" is the payoff, and the user who _declines_ sees it while the user who does the most engaged thing available never does. It is a one-way door: `handleFinishAndGo` calls `completeOnboarding()` _before_ navigating, so anyone who opens `/applications/new` and thinks better of it has silently finished onboarding with no application and no way back in. And it hands over the full application form at the terminal step of a first-run flow, where AC-7 asks for two fields.
- **The document already contradicted itself.** WIC-1689 amended §Step 4's prose but left the flowchart in the same file describing `Create Now → fill form → Submit Success → Completion`. `main` has disagreed with its own design doc since `eb40da8`. The ruling makes them agree again instead of degrading the diagram to match the code.
- **The objection that expired is why this was open at all.** WIC-1689 declined to render inline because this dialog has no focus trap (`MODAL_FOCUS_MANAGEMENT_SPEC.md` §2) — true when written. PR #97 (WIC-1141) migrates `OnboardingModal` to a Radix `Dialog`. So this is a **sequencing requirement, not a caveat**: #97 lands first, then #146 rebased on it. An inline form in an untrapped dialog is precisely the §2 case.
- **Cost measured, not estimated.** One of the four step-5 tests `eb40da8` shipped needs rewriting (`sends the primary CTA to the real create form`); the other three pass unchanged, including `offers exactly one body control`, because the deleted button stays deleted. On #146's side exactly one test changes — its "I'll Do This Later" case folds into the footer test beside it, which already covers that path. The reported cost of "delete/rewrite 4 tests" applied to option A, not to what was ruled.

### Fixed — a SQL comment could silently unfilter a dashboard tile, and the synthetic exclusion had no offline test (2026-08-30)

`build_dashboards.py`'s `_sql_tokens` skipped string literals but not comments, so a `)`
inside a `/* ... */` decremented the scope depth. The injected `AND NOT (<predicate>)`
then landed **inside the comment**, where it is discarded — while `inject_hogql` still
reported one filtered site, `apply_exclusion` (which only aborts on _zero_ sites) passed
it, and the tile executed green against unfiltered probe residue. A trailing `-- ...`
comment produced the milder version: the closing paren was commented out, leaving the
SQL unbalanced. Both are now masked whole, and the wrap puts its closing paren on its own
line so a trailing line comment cannot swallow it.

- **Latent, not shipped.** None of the 18 committed payloads contains a SQL comment, so
  no tile ever built wrong. This closes the gap before a hand-authored query — Route 3's
  are meant to be read by humans — walks into it.
- **The fail-closed guarantee was the thing that broke.** `apply_exclusion` treats a
  nonzero site count as success, so a rewrite that filters nothing but _reports_ a site
  defeats it. **Both** comment syntaxes reach that outcome, not just `/* */`: an unmasked
  `-- GROUP BY x` ends the WHERE body early and promotes the commented text into
  _executable_ SQL, silently regrouping the tile while the site count, the paren balance
  and a live `AND NOT (` all still read correct. The line-comment case has a loud form
  (`-- note )` emits unbalanced SQL) and this silent one; only the loud form was obvious.
- New `docs/analytics/build_dashboards_selftest.py` — 22 offline cases, wired into
  `Lint & Test`. It needs no PostHog credential, so it runs on every PR; the live half
  (`build_dashboards.py --dry-run`) still needs a key. Verified against the pre-fix file:
  exactly the four comment cases fail there and the other 18 pass both ways.
- **Each masking branch is pinned by a mutant, because three tests were not enough.** The
  `--` branch of `_sql_tokens` could originally be deleted outright without reddening a
  single case (WIC-1664 review); the two `--` twins of the `/* */` tests close that. Each
  mutation now reds exactly its own pair and nothing else: dropping the `/*` branch reds 2,
  dropping the `--` branch reds 2, reverting the wrap reds 1. Note the pre-fix file alone
  could never have found this — against it, `line_comment_parens_do_not_desync` _passes_,
  because the missing mask adds a stray `)` while the old wrap swallows the real one and
  the two errors cancel. Only a targeted mutant separates them.
- Its helpers deliberately re-implement comment and literal masking instead of calling
  `_sql_tokens`. Borrowing the module's own tokenizer made the line-comment case pass
  spuriously, because the helper mis-parsed the output exactly as the injector did.
- All 17 enabled payloads produce injected SQL that is unchanged modulo whitespace.

### Fixed — the synthetic-exclusion rewriter now fails closed on an unterminated `/*` and on a comment-only WHERE body (2026-08-30)

Two latent edge cases left by the WIC-1664 review of `build_dashboards.py`, both reachable only by a hand-authored Route 3 query and neither present in any committed payload. An unterminated `/* ...` reproduced the real silent-unfilter signature: `_sql_tokens` masked it to end-of-string, so `WHERE event = 'a' /* oops` swallowed the injected predicate inside the never-closed comment while `inject_hogql` still reported one filtered site — it was bounded only because the emitted SQL was unbalanced and died loudly at PostHog rather than shipping a wrong-but-plausible tile. A WHERE body that is only a comment (`WHERE -- all`) wrapped to `WHERE ()`, empty parens, because the `if not condition` guard saw the non-empty substring `"-- all"` and passed it. Both now `fail()` (WIC-1844).

- **`_sql_tokens` refuses an unterminated block comment** instead of swallowing it to EOF. An unterminated `/*` is never valid input, so no legitimate query is rejected.
- **The empty-WHERE guard counts tokens after comment masking** rather than trusting the raw substring's truthiness, so a comment-only body is caught exactly as an all-whitespace one already was.
- Each refusal is pinned by a mutant, matching the branches WIC-1664 pinned: dropping the `close == -1` guard reds only the unterminated-comment test, reverting the guard to `if not condition` reds only the comment-only-WHERE test, and neither touches the other 22 cases. `build_dashboards_selftest.py` is now 24 cases; injected SQL for all 18 payloads is byte-identical, since this only adds refusals on input that is already invalid.

### Fixed — two filter shortcuts named a week they never measured, and the command palette's filter was never read (2026-08-30)

Both the command palette and the applications-list shortcut row offered a saved filter called `Interviews This Week`. Neither carried a time predicate of any kind — both were status-only — so the result set was identical in every week of the year: an application that reached `interview` four months ago, with nothing scheduled, appeared under a label promising this week's interviews. `Recently Applied` had the same defect one entry away in the same two arrays. Ruled and fixed under WIC-1775 (routed via WIC-1812); `docs/design/SAVED_FILTER_SHORTCUT_NAMING.md` is the governing document.

- **The reported defect was the smaller half. `/applications?status=…` was read by nothing.** `ApplicationsList` imported `useNavigate` only — no `useSearchParams`, no `location.search` — and seeded `useState<FilterOptions>({})`. So the palette entry did not filter by status either: it was not "status-only, no window", it was **no filter at all**, landing the user on the complete list with `rejected` and `withdrawn` rows included. Three of the palette's four shortcuts were inert this way; only `Needs Follow-up` had a real destination (`/reports/stale`). That is why a rename alone could not fix it — renaming to `Interviewing` over a destination that still ignored the filter swaps one false label for another — so the label and the wiring land together here.
- **Option 2 was measured, not assumed, and rejected.** WIC-1775 offered "give the filter the window its label promises", conditional on an interview-date field existing. None exists at any layer: not in the `applications` table (`schema.ts` has only `appliedAt`, `nextActionDue`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`), not in the API DTO, not in the web `Application` type. The sole `interviewDate` is on `ApplicationSummary` in `types/interviewPrep.ts`, a view model. So that option is a feature — schema migration, API field, a control to populate it — and is split out rather than smuggled in as a fix.
- **The scope is four sites because the defect was four sites.** Fixing only the two that were reported would have repeated, one level up, the mistake WIC-1775 itself warned against ("do not relabel one surface without the other"). The unit that must stay consistent is the shortcut row.
- **The rule is enforced, not just written down.** Labels now come from one constant (`constants/filterShortcuts.ts`), so the two surfaces cannot drift apart again, and `filterShortcuts.test.ts` fails on any shortcut label containing a time word. Tests assert the label _and_ the filter behind it together — each is defensible alone, only the pair is wrong — and all seven new cases were confirmed to fail against the pre-fix tree before the fix was applied. Unknown `?status=` tokens are dropped rather than forwarded to the API.
- **Two dead-code findings are recorded but deliberately not fixed here.** `InterviewPrepPage.tsx:287,368` read `application.interviewDate` off a type with no such property, so it is always `undefined` and both downstream render sites are permanently dark — invisible to TypeScript because the target property is optional. And `FilterOptions.dateRange` has zero consumers: the one window field the filter contract already has is wired to nothing.
- **The precedent this card was told to follow is not on `main`.** WIC-1775 cites `constants/appliedWindow.ts` as "added by WIC-1743"; PR #260 was still open at `a46c63a`, so that file exists only on its branch. This change follows the _shape_ of that pattern — shared constant plus tests — without importing from it.
- **A pre-existing full-suite flake was measured and left alone.** `OnboardingModal.test.tsx` fails intermittently under parallel load: 2 of 4 runs on unmodified `main`, versus 1 of 3 with this branch applied. It renders no route this change touches. Filed separately rather than folded in.



### Added — `upload_id` correlates all three `resume_upload` legs, so the gap-derived failure metric joins per upload

The failure KPI of record (`docs/analytics/dashboard-spec.md` §6) is gap-derived: a
`resume_upload_submitted` with no matching terminal event is a failure. That join had no key.
`session_id` is one-to-many over uploads, and `resume_id` / `export_id` are generated *by* the work
that may fail, so neither can ever appear on `_submitted` or `_failed`.

`uploadResume()` now generates one ULID per call and emits it as `upload_id` at all four emit sites
— `resume_upload_submitted`, **both** `resume_upload_completed` callsites (the duplicate
short-circuit and the full pipeline), and `resume_upload_failed`. This retires the two limitations
recorded in dashboard-spec.md §6.5: the metric was valid only in aggregate (a session that uploaded
twice and failed once netted out to "fine"), and an upload spanning a window boundary was
miscounted. §6.6 Query 2 now resolves per upload.

- **Purely additive.** No existing count, funnel or breakdown changes, the §6 gap metric reads the
  same before and after, and no dashboard rebuild is required.
- **This does not make `_failed` reliable, and does not retire the gap metric.** Delivery is
  deliberately unchanged: `ctx.waitUntil()` would defer the `fetch` into the *same* exhausted
  per-invocation subrequest budget and be dropped identically, so it would look like a fix and
  change nothing (dashboard-spec.md §6.3). Only a Tail Worker / Logpush is genuinely out-of-band.
- **The `ResumeUpload*Props` interfaces are documentation, not enforcement.** `track()` takes
  `Record<string, unknown>`, so `tsc` does not check emit callsites against them and a dropped or
  misspelled `upload_id` compiles clean. `packages/api/test/resume-upload-correlation.test.ts` is
  the enforcement — it drives the real `uploadResume()` across all three legs and asserts the shared
  *value*, not mere presence. A five-mutant matrix pins it: deleting `upload_id` from each of the
  four emit sites reds only the tests covering that site, and replacing the ULID with a constant
  reds only the distinctness test — the one case a presence-only assertion would wave through, and
  which would otherwise join every upload in the account to every other.
- Verification against production still needs a deliberate probe: analytics has no organic traffic
  (6 lifetime events, all synthetic). Register any probe in `docs/analytics/probe-registry.json` —
  an end-to-end probe that submits without completing is byte-identical in shape to a real outage.


### Fixed — the changelog classifier files a real double-ship under a label that reads as benign (2026-08-30)

Root `CLAUDE.md` sorted every duplicate-bullet hit into three classes and described the third, `distinct entries`, as "almost always two real entries that merely open the same way". There is a fourth class that lands in it: union keeps both copies but files one under a **different `### ` entry**, so the superseded text stays where it belongs and the correction lands somewhere it does not. Two entries end up wrong instead of one. Found on PR #129 at head `97989e6`, filed as WIC-1768, and fixed by its owner in `a7a13fb` before this entry merged (WIC-1567 follow-up).

- **Similarity is anti-correlated here, in both places you would reach for it.** By heading similarity #129's real hit scores **0.47** — between the two known-benign exemplars on `main` (0.40 and 0.50), so it is bracketed and no threshold can separate it. Switching to bullet-body similarity inverts the ranking instead of fixing it: the genuine revision pair scores **0.24**, _below_ both benign pairs (0.64 and 0.68), because a thorough correction rewrites the body it corrects while the benign pairs share long boilerplate openers. Either metric, tuned either direction, ranks the one real bug below both false ones.
- **The replacement discriminator is structural and threshold-free.** A bullet belongs under exactly one heading, so a copy filed under a heading **neither parent** filed it under is misfiled by construction, with no benign reading. It keys on heading text rather than position, so it is merge-base independent — the same property that fixed the weld control and the anchor tally.
- **One hit, no false positives, and it stays silent on the known-benign pairs.** Run across all 78 open PRs — 66 with a `CHANGELOG.md` differing from their true base — it returned exactly #129. Re-run afterwards over 81 open PRs (69 with a delta) it returns **zero**: the single hit was the real one, and it is now fixed.
- **What #129 would have shipped.** Its 2026-08-26 onboarding entry kept `main`'s superseded description of the WIC-1354 tests (query-counts, three reversal directions, "488 API tests pass") while the corrected version (read-sequences, five directions, "18 tests in this file") was filed under the unrelated 2026-08-29 "Create Application Now" entry. The branch file itself was clean: both parents carried two duplicate pairs and the union carried three, so exactly one was merge-introduced.
- **The loop closed, and the fix verified.** The owner merged `main` in and resolved the hunk per bullet rather than take-ours/take-theirs; the PR moved `CONFLICTING / DIRTY` → `MERGEABLE`. Re-measured at `a7a13fb`: the union introduces zero duplicate headings, welds and duplicate bullets, the bullet appears once in its corrected form under the entry it belongs to, and the seam left by the deletion is un-welded.
- **Re-measure an accusation immediately before acting on it.** This entry was written against `97989e6` and was stale before it could merge — under an hour. The pre-merge re-measure is the only reason it says "fixed" instead of asserting a live defect against a branch that had already complied. A claim about another branch is as perishable as a board ask.
- **The label was the defect, not the check.** The bullet check found this pair on every run; the prose told the reader it was almost certainly benign. Naming a class is a claim about what to do next, and "distinct entries" was read as a verdict rather than as a description of the headings.

### Fixed — the weld count was measured with a line-number subtraction and on a `main`-only population; both are corrected (2026-08-30)

The entry below reported **9** PRs welding a `### ` heading, "all `main`-based", over "74 open PRs". Re-measuring puts it at **10** across **65** divergent PRs of **78** open, and one of the ten is stacked. Two independent method defects produced that, and the second is the same coordinate-system error this file already documents for the anchor tally (WIC-1567 follow-up).

- **Subtract by content, never by line number — `ours`, `theirs` and `union` are three different coordinate systems.** The three-input control exists to report only what the merge _adds_, but subtracting raw line numbers reports **17** PRs welding where the truth is **10**. All 7 extra are false: the weld already sat on the branch and the merge merely shifted it down the file. PR #95's weld is line 511 in `theirs.md` and 600 in `union.md`; PR #117's sits on **both** parents (169 and 78) and lands at 172; PR #168 carries the same **7** welds in `ours.md` and `union.md`, offset by nine lines, so a line-number control blames the merge for all seven. The detector now keys on normalised heading text and prints the line number only as a locator.
- **The check's own output shape was the trap.** It printed `headings missing a preceding blank line (line nos)` — a bare list of integers, which is precisely what invites the subtraction that over-reports by 70%. A diagnostic that emits coordinates will be differenced in coordinates; emitting the content key is what makes the correct control the easy one.
- **Do not restrict the sweep to `main`-based PRs.** The tenth welder is #123, stacked on `fix/wic1312-shared-cursor-guard`. Its three simulation inputs are commits dated 2026-08-26 and have not moved since, so the result is a deterministic function of unchanged data — it was welding when the entry below was written and was simply outside the population measured. A stacked PR welds against its own base branch exactly as readily.
- **Neither correction touches the remedy, which was re-tested against all ten including #123:** as-is **10** welds, extra **leading** blank **0**, extra **trailing** blank **10** — no effect, both **0**. Unanimous, as before.
- **The shared-anchor heuristic would also have missed #123.** Resolved to content anchors the ten sit on four seams, and #123 welds onto `### Security — App-host transport hardening` entirely alone — so "all welders share a seam" was an artifact of the truncated population, not a property of the defect.

### Fixed — the blank-line weld remedy is stated as a single edge, and for sibling PRs no single edge works (2026-08-30)

Root `CLAUDE.md` presented the blank-line discipline as a prevention an author applies to their own branch, with a tie-break — "if you only add one, add the trailing one" — for the case where you pick just one edge. Both halves are wrong outside the one merge they were measured on. The eaten blank sits at the _join between the two competing insertions_, so it is the trailing edge of the block union emits first and the leading edge of the block it emits second: one physical line, named from two sides.
