- **`docs/design/README.md` was itself part of the problem** and now indexes `ROUTE_HEADING_OUTLINE.md`, `ROUTE_TITLE_CONVENTION.md` and `COVER_LETTER_PANE_LABELLING.md`, none of which the index listed.
- **No behaviour changed.** This is documentation only; every route still ships the same static title, and nothing in CI checks otherwise.

### Docs — the dialogue wizard's draft persistence is ruled out, and the ✅ that said it shipped was false (2026-08-30)

`DIALOGUE_CAPTURE_WIZARD.md` specified `.draft` files in `data/projects/`, autosave every 30 seconds, a recovery prompt on re-open and a clear-on-cancel path — and its "Requirements Decisions" item 3 marked draft persistence **✅**, i.e. delivered. None of it was ever built. WIC-1621 rules the feature out rather than building it, and strikes the passages in place so old links still land on something that explains itself.

- **What actually ships is one `localStorage.setItem`** in `DialogueCapture.tsx:47`, with **no read path** — `git grep dialogue-wizard-draft` returns exactly one hit tree-wide, the write. There is no `removeItem` either, so the store survives logout and accumulates per variant. "Save Draft" is a control that lies: it promises restoration, returns no feedback, and restores nothing.
- **The 30-second autosave fires unconditionally.** Its guard is `Object.keys(data).length > 0` and `data` is seeded with three keys, so the condition is vacuous. Measured by rendering the real route in jsdom and advancing 30s with zero user input: it writes `{"data":{"accomplishments":[],"jobFit":[],"techStack":[]},...}`. Project content goes to disk on a timer the user never started.
- **The replacement was already specified and also unbuilt.** This document's own keyboard section reads _"Escape: Cancel wizard (with confirmation)"_; there is no `Escape` handler and no `confirm()` in `WizardContainer.tsx`. The ruling extends that one line to all three discard paths — `Escape`, the header close button, and in-app navigation away — with confirm copy that says plainly that nothing was saved.
- **It reuses `ConfirmationModal`,** whose existing props take the copy directly, rather than a new dialog or `window.confirm`. Noted rather than glossed: that component currently declares no `role="dialog"`, no focus trap and no `restoreFocusTo`, and the repo's own `confirmation-modal-focus-audit.py` reports §5.3 unenforced pending WIC-1181 — so the guard must not be described as focus-managed until that lands.
- **Ordering constraint, called out because getting it wrong is worse than today.** Removing the write and the button without the guard takes the user from "a button that lies" to "silent total loss". The guard must land with or after the removal.
- **Documentation only. No code, no tests, no behaviour change** — the ruling is stated, the implementation is tracked separately.


### Fixed — catalog extraction wrote a null owner into five NOT NULL columns, and silently ingested nothing (2026-08-30)

`extraction.service.ts` inserted `userId: userId ?? null` into `company_catalog`, `tech_stack_tags`, `job_fit_tags`, `quantified_bullets` and `recurring_themes` — the five tables migration `0017_enforce_userid_not_null.sql` (`:29`–`:34`) had made `user_id NOT NULL`. `processCatalogChange` resolves `userId` to `undefined` whenever `event.metadata.userId` is not a string, so the auto-apply transaction aborted on a `23502`, and `flush()` swallowed it into a `console.error` (WIC-1617).

- **Executed, not reasoned about.** The five inserts were run against the real migration set under PGlite: all five die on `null value in column "user_id" … violates not-null constraint`. The `catalog_diffs` write in the same function succeeded, because 0017 backfills that column but deliberately leaves it nullable — so the failure is specific to the constrained columns, not to the harness.
- **The owner was being dropped one line after it was used.** `application.service.ts` called `enqueueChange('application', id, …)` with no metadata at all, while writing that same `userId` into `status_history` directly above. Both call sites now pass `{ userId }`, the shape `resume.service.ts` and `catalog.service.ts` already used. This ran ownerless for authenticated callers too, so application-triggered catalog ingest had stopped entirely — silently, since `flush()` logs and moves on.
- **`applyChangeToDb` now requires `userId: string`** rather than accepting `string | null | undefined`. That makes it a compile-time gate: removing the caller's guard fails `tsc` with `TS2345` at the call site, which was verified by removing it.
- **An ownerless event declines to auto-apply instead of writing rows nobody could read.** An anonymous caller scopes to `user_id IS NULL`, which 0017 also made select the empty set, so those rows were unreachable even when the insert was legal. The diff is still recorded, as `pending` rather than `approved`, so the changes survive for an owned caller to apply, and a warning names the missing field.
- **Tests are paired against a positive control.** "No insert happened" passes vacuously when the fixture produces no changes, so every ownerless assertion has an owned counterpart on the same fixture proving all five tables are really reached. 4 of the 6 new `extraction.owner` tests fail against the previous code, and both `application.change-owner` tests do; the 2 that stay green are the controls, by design.

### Fixed — the merge-tenancy test helper asserted the SQL shape this branch had just removed (2026-08-27)

This branch declared `fix/wic1373-catalog-tag-patch-tenancy` as its base but did not contain it (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` fails), so its CI never compiled the two changes together. Merging the real base in surfaced 6 failures that neither PR could see alone, and that GitHub reported as `mergeable: true / clean` throughout — a textual merge, not a semantic one (WIC-1605).

- **The collision.** WIC-1373 added `expectIds()`, asserting the prefix `` `"t"."id" = ` `` on every merge predicate, and documented the source read as rendering `"t"."id" = ANY(($1))`. That is the exact row-constructor spelling the entry above removed: WIC-1377 replaced the raw `= ANY` template with `inArray`, which renders `"t"."id" in ($1, $2)`. The helper therefore encoded the _defect_ as its expectation — it matches the broken form and fails against the fix.
- **The helper now accepts both legal renderings**, because the target and the sources are built by different operators: `eq(t.id, targetId)` → `= $1`, `inArray(t.id, sourceIds)` → `in ($1, $2)`. Both stay table-qualified, so the wrong-column check that stops `eq(t.normalizedName, targetId)` from passing is unchanged.
- **Widening the match did not cost detection power**, which was measured rather than assumed: dropping the id term from the source predicate (the tenancy-only mutation the helper exists to catch) still fails 5 tests, and re-keying the target read on `normalizedName` still fails 1, against a green unmutated baseline.


### Security — an unresolvable `jobFitAnalysisId` is rejected instead of becoming the job context (2026-08-30)

`jobFitAnalysisId` was accepted on five generation entry points as `z.string().optional()`, with no format check and no existence check. No job fit analysis is ever persisted — there is no `job_fit_analyses` table and `AnalyzeJobFitResponse` carries no `id` — so the field could never be dereferenced. It was not inert, though: it satisfied `JOB_CONTEXT_REQUIRED`, waived `TARGET_INFO_REQUIRED`, was interpolated into the model prompt as the entire job description (`` `Job Fit Analysis ID: ${input.jobFitAnalysisId}` ``), and was written to the generated row's `job_fit_analysis_id` column.

- **Every value is now rejected `422 JOB_FIT_ANALYSIS_NOT_FOUND`, before the model spend and before the write.** Until the table lands (WIC-1652 AC-1) nothing can resolve, so rejecting outright is the honest interim answer — which is what makes ADR-012 AC-5a severable from the table. Resolution is confined to one function, `resolveJobFitAnalysis`, so AC-5b changes that function alone.
- **Five sites, not the three the card enumerated.** `POST /cover-letters/outreach` and `POST /resume-variants/suggest-bullets` also let the id satisfy `JOB_CONTEXT_REQUIRED`; found by grepping the operation rather than the cited files. Before the fix all five *resolved successfully* on a junk id — the reproduction returned a cover letter addressed to "the company" for "this role".
- **`NO_FIT_ANALYSIS` is keyed on a resolved row, not a non-empty string.** Any junk id used to silence the "gaps may be incomplete" warning while nothing ever read an analysis.
- **An empty string is a supplied id that does not resolve, not an absent one.** Every shipped site tested the field with `!!` / `!`, so `''` read as "not supplied" and fell through to the other guards.
- **Non-breaking in practice, and that was measured rather than assumed.** No id can exist: the analyze response has no `id`, and nothing in the SPA ever sets the `fitAnalysisId` / `jobFitAnalysisId` query parameter that the two components read — `JobFitAnalysis.tsx` navigates to `/cover-letters/new` carrying `jobDescriptionText`, not an id. The field was reachable only by a hand-crafted request.
- **The interpolation sites fail closed rather than being left unreachable-but-live**, so a future AC-5b that forgets one prompts with no job context instead of with an id.


The same authorization miss as the merge fix below, on three more services in the same file, found while fixing it and held back to keep that diff at its filed scope. `updateJobFitTag` and `updateTechStackTag` both declared `userId?: string` and never referenced it, and `generateDiff` took it and dropped it twice over (WIC-1373).

- **`PATCH /api/catalog/tags/job-fit/:id` and `.../tech-stack/:id` were cross-tenant writes.** Any authenticated caller holding a tag's ULID could rename it, move it between categories, or flip `needsReview` on another user's tag. The optimistic-lock `version` was the only obstacle and it is `1` for any tag never edited, so the guard was effectively absent — reverting the fix does not merely produce a misleading `version conflict` error, it lets the rename **succeed**. Both the read and the update now carry the tenancy predicate; a foreign tag reports `NotFoundError` rather than confirming the id exists.
- **`POST /api/catalog/generate-diff` was orphaning the diffs it wrote, and failing outright on the rest.** `processCatalogChange` reads the owner off `event.metadata.userId` (the shape `resume.service.ts` uses when it enqueues), and `generateDiff` passed no metadata at all, so the owner resolved to `undefined` for every call. The `catalog_diffs` row then landed with `user_id` null — that column is still nullable, unlike the catalog tables — and was invisible ever after to `listDiffs`, `getDiff` and `applyDiff`, all of which are scoped. Where the call also auto-applied a _new_ catalog entry it did not orphan that row but lost the whole request: `company_catalog`, `job_fit_tags`, `tech_stack_tags`, `quantified_bullets` and `recurring_themes` have had `user_id NOT NULL` since migration `0017`, so the insert raised `23502` inside an untrapped transaction and 500'd before any diff row was written. Only `update` changes, which never touch `user_id`, got through. The caller is now threaded into the event metadata.
- **Its lookup was also unscoped.** The trailing `SELECT` matched on `trigger_source` + `trigger_id` only. `processCatalogChange` returns early when the source yields no text, so the row this call would otherwise have inserted need not exist, and the query then falls through to whatever diff is newest for that trigger id — another user's, for a foreign `sourceId`.
- **Single-user/local mode is unchanged**, on the same conditional-predicate pattern as the merge fix; three tests pin the emitted SQL as unscoped when `userId` is absent.
- **Tests reuse the `PgDialect` rendering harness from the merge fix**, extended two ways: `stubDb` gained the top-level `update().set().where().returning()` chain, and a new `stubOwnedRow` double honours the where-clause instead of resolving its canned rows regardless — without that, the "another user's tag" cases pass with the bug still present, since the shared `where` spy cannot express "the row exists but the caller may not see it". Reverting the service fix fails 7 of the 8 new service tests; the eighth is the single-user regression guard, which is meant to pass either way.

### Fixed — "Stale" is one definition now, so the dashboard count and the report it links to cannot contradict each other (2026-08-29)

The product shipped **seven** definitions of stale across four screens that link to each other. The card named three; review of the first fix found two more; the tree-wide scan written to answer that review found the last two. The Dashboard attention card counted every non-terminal status (`saved`, `applied`, `phone_screen`, `interview`) over a hardcoded **7** days; Quick Wins counted `applied`/`phone_screen`/`interview` over the same 7; the applications list's "Stale (14+ days)" tile counted every *active* status at 14; `ApplicationCard`'s "Stale" badge counted every non-terminal status at 14; `/reports/pipeline` carried **two** of its own — a local `isStale` helper behind a "⏱️ Stale" badge and an inline duplicate in its stats memo, both at 14 days with **no status check at all**; and `/reports/stale` counted `applied`/`phone_screen` over **14**.

The attention card rendered "N applications need follow-up (>7 days)" and linked straight to the report, which promises the report is the detailed view of that count. It was not. One application in `interview` status updated 9 days ago — on an account holding **three** applications, so no paging is involved — gave a card reading "1 application needs follow-up" and a report reading "No stale applications found — All your applications have been updated within 14 days." Deterministic, and reachable on a nearly-empty account (WIC-1479).

Four of the seven agreed with the specified definition on the **threshold** and differed only on the **status set**, which is why they outlived the first pass: a guard aimed at the number 7, or at the shared module's own text, walks straight past them. At 20 days an `interview` row was badged "Stale" in four places and absent from the report the word links to.

- **The report was the conformant surface and the dashboard was the drifted one**, because the dashboard was never specified: UC-5 US-5.7 (WIC-143) defines stale as `applied` or `phone_screen` with no status change in 14+ days, selectable across 7/14/21/30, and `/reports/stale` implemented exactly that. UC-5 contains zero occurrences of "dashboard", "attention" or "quick win" — the two most prominent components on the landing page had no requirement behind them, so nothing tied their definition to the one the board accepted. The specified definition wins.
- **One predicate, `packages/api/src/services/stale.ts` (new)** — `STALE_STATUSES`, `DEFAULT_STALE_THRESHOLD_DAYS`, `resolveStaleThresholdDays`, `staleCutoff`, and `staleWhere()`, the single drizzle condition. `getDashboardStats` and `getStaleReport` both build their queries from that one call, so the count and the report's row count are equal **by construction** rather than by assertion (AC-N2b). The report's `?status=` filter can still subset the definition; it can no longer widen it.
- **The threshold travels down the wire and the card renders it.** `AttentionCard` no longer holds a number at all — not even as a fallback, since a fallback literal is a second definition of stale living on the client, and with no aggregates in hand there is no count to label anyway. `ReportsStale` opens on the shared default rather than `useState(14)`, and builds its selector from `STALE_THRESHOLD_OPTIONS`.
- **`staleSaved` is renamed `unsubmittedSaved`, and `savedThresholdDays` to `unsubmittedThresholdDays` (wire contract change).** A `saved` application was never sent to anyone, so there is nobody to follow up with; it is keyed off `createdAt`, not `updatedAt`. Calling it stale put a second meaning on the word, which is what AC-N2a forbids. `staleActive` is deleted outright — with one definition there is no second population to name.
- **Quick Wins draws from the same population**, `samples.stale`, instead of applying its own inline threshold over its own status set.
- **`?status=` no longer widens the definition.** The report's filter was applied against the full status enum rather than `STALE_STATUSES`, so `/reports/stale?status=saved,applied,phone_screen,interview` was honoured verbatim and served the exact pre-WIC-1479 definition — from the one surface the card calls conformant. It now filters against `STALE_STATUSES`, and a filter that leaves nothing returns an **empty report** rather than the 500 that narrowing would otherwise cause (`inArray` throws on an empty list, so `staleWhere` renders the empty set as a predicate matching no row).
- **The four client surfaces read one predicate.** `constants/stale.ts` now carries `STALE_STATUSES`, `staleCutoff` and `isStale`, mirroring the API's function shape; `ApplicationsList`, `ApplicationCard` and both copies in `ReportsPipeline` call it instead of computing their own. The predicate is an instant comparison, not `differenceInDays(startOfDay(now), …) >= days` — rounding to whole calendar days disagreed with the server part-way through the boundary day, which is this defect again, one day wide. Both "Stale (14+ days)" tiles now interpolate the shared constant instead of stating a literal.
- **Behaviour change:** `saved` and `interview` rows are no longer badged or counted as stale anywhere. They were never stale under the specified definition — a `saved` application was never sent to anyone, and an `interview` is an active conversation rather than a silence.
- **The dashboard is tested for adding *nothing* to the shared predicate.** `dashboard.attention-conditions.test.ts` arrived from WIC-1478 asserting that the dashboard's own stale predicate was spelled correctly; under one definition that question no longer exists, so the assertion was retargeted rather than deleted: the clause `buildAttentionConditions` returns must render byte-identically to `staleWhere()`'s. That is AC-N2b as a test. It matters because a local `and(...)` wrapped around the shared call — an extra status, a second day count — restores exactly the drift this entry removes and leaves `stale.definition.test.ts` completely green, since the drift would not be in `stale.ts`. Its `staleActive` cases went with the field.
- **The client mirror is tested, not trusted** — `packages/web` and `packages/api` share no compiled module, so `constants/stale.ts` is a hand-mirror. `stale.drift.test.ts` reads the API source through Vite's `?raw` loader and fails if the values, the status list, or the selector's bounds stop matching; it also reads `ReportsStale.tsx` and requires the threshold to arrive by **identifier**, since a literal `14` would agree today and drift silently tomorrow. A hand-mirror with no test is how this defect was born.
- **The guard is at the point of introduction, not the point of effect.** `stale.definition.test.ts` serializes both services' real WHERE clauses through drizzle's `QueryBuilder` with no connection and asserts they are the same SQL — equal SQL means equal counts on *every* dataset — and asserts the statuses `?status=` actually binds into the query rather than the rows a fixture happens to hold. It then scans for a re-inlined status pair, a rebuilt upper-bound comparison on `updatedAt`, or a hardcoded `days:` argument, with negative controls for each regex plus a check that a legitimate `gte(applications.updatedAt, …)` in the closed-loop report does not trip it. AC-N2c is reproduced verbatim, with a control asserting the same fixture *would* have counted one under the old dashboard rules.
- **Both scans are tree-wide, and their scope is pinned.** The previous revision had a test titled "stale.ts is the only file that names the definition" that read only `stale.ts` — it asserted nothing about any other file, and four definitions were live while it was green. Both halves now enumerate their package (`readdirSync` for `packages/api/src`, `import.meta.glob` for `packages/web/src`) and assert the enumeration reached the files under guard, because an empty walk is a vacuous pass that looks identical to a clean one. Adding the positive control immediately found a hole in the original regex: it did not tolerate the trailing comma prettier adds once an array reflows, which is how `STALE_STATUSES` is formatted — so it would not have matched the very declaration it exists to detect duplicates of. The four copies of that regex are now one binding.
- **The web scan tracks the binding, not the identifier name.** It flags a value derived transitively from a row's `updatedAt` and then compared against a numeric literal, which is the shape of a client-side staleness predicate. Following the taint to a fixpoint rather than one hop is what catches `ReportsPipeline`'s helper, where the compared binding never mentions `updatedAt` — a single-hop version ran green on that file while the definition was live in it. It deliberately does not fire on deriving elapsed days for *display*, which is what Quick Wins does over a server-selected population, nor on the due-date thresholds sitting beside it; both are pinned as controls.

### Fixed — Every match and gap row states whether the skill is required (2026-08-26)

The three per-skill sections on the Job Fit Analysis screen disclosed the same `isRequired` flag three different ways at row level: gap rows named both branches, strong-match rows carried a red `Required` badge **or nothing**, and partial-match rows said nothing at all. This is the residue of the WIC-1528 entry below, not a regression from it — that change fixed the section _headings_, and this is what was left one level down (WIC-1534).

- **An absence was doing the work of a statement.** On a strong-match row, no badge meant "nice-to-have" — indistinguishable from a row where the flag simply was not rendered. No fixture can catch that: a mock that renders nothing and a component that renders nothing agree. Both branches are now named on every row, in all three sections.
- **Partial-match rows had no signal at all.** The heading states the split, so the counts were known, but with more than one row of each kind _which_ row was which could not be recovered. Rows now read `Partially matches: postgresql (alias) — Nice-to-have skill`.
- **The red badge is removed, not propagated.** It was `bg-red-100 text-red-800` — red, on a green-bordered card meaning good news, to say "important" rather than "bad". Gap severity owns red on this screen, so the badge was already a cross-axis colour reuse; extending it to two more sections would have spent the colour three times over and added a chip per row for one boolean. A text qualifier instead reuses the one pattern gap rows already proved.
- **One formatter, so the sections cannot drift again.** `packages/web/src/constants/requirementLabel.ts` (new) exports the labels and the shared `REQUIREMENT_SEPARATOR`; all three sections read it, and gap rows moved from a hyphen onto the same spaced em dash. The row formatter carries the noun ("Required skill") that the heading formatter elides ("2 required") because the heading supplies it — same vocabulary at two altitudes, neither reaching for "fit" or a reserved severity word.
- **Tested at both levels.** `requirementLabel.test.ts` (7 cases, `npm run test`) asserts neither branch is ever empty, that the two are not substrings of each other, and that the row and heading formatters agree on which word names which branch — so a re-wording of either fails rather than letting a section quietly contradict its own heading. The e2e spec pins the rendered row copy in all three sections and asserts the red badge is gone from the strong-match cards.
- **No wire values change.** Presentation only.
- Specified in `docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` → "Per-row required-ness", which replaces the "Known residue" note left by the entry below.

### Fixed — Signing out clears every app-owned `localStorage` key, and the dialogue wizard stops writing drafts nothing can read (2026-08-27)

Five `localStorage` keys held user data on the user's own disk in plaintext and `signOut` cleared one of them. On a shared or borrowed machine the next person to open the app was offered the previous user's recent searches — company names, role titles, contact names — plus their saved filters and their onboarding progress, with no session required. A sixth surface, `dialogue-wizard-draft-*`, was written and never read by anything (WIC-1495).

- **The threat model was already written down in the function that missed it.** `signOut`'s own comment reasons about "a next user on a shared browser" — for the *analytics identity*, which it rotates correctly. The four keys sitting beside the token were not swept. Nothing about this was unknown; the sweep just stopped at `auth_token`.
- **The draft store was write-only, permanent, and automatic.** `dialogue-wizard-draft-${variant}` had exactly one reference in the whole package — the `setItem`. No read path, no clear path, and it fired on a **30-second interval** and on **Ctrl+S**, not only on the "Save Draft" button, so project dialogue content was persisted without the user asking and could never be restored. The write is removed, and with it the button, the interval and the key handler that existed only to feed it: every one of them promised a restore that no code could perform. Rebuilding drafts properly is WIC-1621.
- **One registry, not four `removeItem` calls.** `packages/web/src/services/appStorage.ts` (new) owns the key names and `clearAppStorage()`. It enumerates what is actually in the store and removes what matches, so key *families* like `dialogue-wizard-draft-*` are covered — an exact-match list structurally cannot reach a key whose suffix is generated at runtime. It is deliberately not `localStorage.clear()`: keys the app does not own are not ours to delete, and a test asserts a foreign key survives.
- **The legacy prefix stays in the registry on purpose.** Deleting the writer does not delete the copies already on users' disks. `dialogue-wizard-draft-` remains registered so those are cleared on that user's next sign-out; the module says so, because it otherwise reads as dead weight.
- **`sessionStorage` is out of scope and that is a finding, not an omission.** Its one key is already rotated on logout by the analytics `reset()`, and it does not outlive the tab. The exposure is specific to `localStorage`.
- **What keeps this true is the second test, not the first.** `AuthContext.test.tsx` (6 cases) signs in through the real `AuthProvider`, populates the keys, signs out, and asserts nothing app-owned survives — but it is fully green against a *sixth* key added next month. `appStorageRegistry.test.ts` (4 cases) closes that: outside the registry module, a `localStorage` key must be an identifier imported from it, never a literal, so the only way to add a key is to register it. Both files assert they found something to check before checking it.
- **The fixture key strings are written out by hand rather than imported.** Importing them from the registry would make the test a restatement of the thing under test, and a key dropped from the registry would take the fixture with it and stay green. A separate assertion pins the two lists against each other, so drift in either direction fails.
- **Eight negative controls, all measured** (see the PR). The two worth naming: reverting `signOut` to `removeItem(AUTH_TOKEN_KEY)` reds 2 cases, and a sweep that removes keys *during* the index walk instead of collecting them first reds 4 — `localStorage.key(i)` renumbers on removal, so a live-removal sweep silently leaves half of any run of adjacent keys behind.
- **`auth_token` stays in `localStorage`.** Moving it to an `HttpOnly` cookie is real hardening and is explicitly out of this card's scope: it is an auth-architecture change with CSRF consequences and belongs in its own ticket.
- Three `'auth_token'` string literals outside `AuthContext` (`services/api/index.ts`, `contexts/OnboardingContext.tsx` ×2) now import the registry constant. No behaviour change; they are what the registry test would otherwise flag.
- **An expired session sweeps too, not only an explicit sign-out.** `handleUnauthorized` cleared just the token, so a session that lapsed underneath the user left the same data on disk that a logout now removes — the shared-browser threat does not distinguish "chose to log out" from "was logged out". This is safe only because the listener is strictly 401-driven: `auth:unauthorized` has exactly one dispatch site, inside `!response.ok` behind `status === 401`, so an offline or parse failure throws `NETWORK_ERROR` without ever reaching it. That precondition is now pinned by a test asserting **both** directions — dispatch on a 401, silence on a network failure — because a "does not dispatch" assertion alone is green against a client that never dispatches at all. The sweep deliberately stays out of any request `catch` block, where a network blip would wipe a still-valid session.
- **The AC-3 test was invisible in the pull request.** `AuthContext.test.tsx` carried a raw NUL byte in a `join()` separator, so git classified the file as binary and GitHub rendered it as `additions: 0` with no patch — all 198 lines of the sweep test were unreviewable. The separator is now `'|'`, which no fixture value contains. Caught in review; worth naming because a binary-classified source file defeats diff review silently and nothing in CI flags it.

### Docs — ADR-010 settles what an authenticated request with no owner may do, and a CI guard now enforces it (2026-08-27)

Every tenancy fix so far scoped itself to one function, and the count still grew, because the tree-wide question was never written down — WIC-1554 asked for it and could not answer from inside one function, and WIC-1596 and WIC-1549 each re-derived it within a day. `docs/architecture/adr/ADR-010-absent-owner-posture.md` is the answer (WIC-1600).

- **The affordance was deliberate and was never retired.** ADR-003 specified `user_id` as "nullable initially for migration from single-user data", ending "or left as null for local-only". "Owner absent" was a migration state; the migration finished and the state became permanent, because nothing said it should end. ADR-010 supersedes that clause.
- **The predicate is at least three shapes, not one.** Alongside the known `userId ? and(...) : eq(t.id, id)` ternary there is an `if (userId) conditions.push(...)` form (4 sites) and a `...(userId ? [eq(...)] : [])` spread (3 sites), plus a write-side class the audit did not count — `userId: userId ?? null` in `.values({...})` (11 sites), which creates the ownerless rows the read predicates then match. Any mechanism written for the ternary alone misses a quarter of them.
- **ESLint could not have been the mechanism.** Not because a rule cannot see a ternary's false branch, but because `packages/api` has no ESLint config and no `lint` script — root `lint` is `--workspaces --if-present`, so the API package is skipped entirely and zero of the 48 sites are lintable today.
- **`tsc` makes the fail-open branch unreachable, not rejected.** `tsc -b packages/api` does cover `src/services` and does fail CI (confirmed with a negative control), but even with `userId: string` the expression `userId ? A : B` still typechecks, because the empty string is falsy. So the posture change needs a guard alongside it.
- **The guard is AST-based and ships on a frozen baseline.** `packages/api/scripts/audit-owner-predicates.mjs` uses the TypeScript parser, so it sees all three shapes; it catches **48 of 48** sites in the WIC-1600 table and finds 14 more the table missed, plus the 76 optional-owner signatures underneath them. It fails only on **new** sites, keyed on file and content rather than line number — verified to reject a newly added ternary, `if`-guard and optional signature, and verified _not_ to fire on a pure line shift. `main` has a population to burn down, so a guard that failed on all of it could never have landed.
- **The guard caught 19 real new sites on its own branch, one day after the baseline was frozen.** Merging `main` `5e2956b` into this branch failed the guard: `catalog.service.ts` +14, `resume-variant.service.ts` +3, `interviewPrep.service.ts` +2, total **138 → 157**, across the same 30 shape-keys — **no key went down**. Every commit responsible is itself a tenancy fix (WIC-1365, WIC-1373, WIC-1377, WIC-1395, WIC-1360, WIC-1449, WIC-1465), and the new sites are newly exported functions written in the prohibited shape — `mergeCompanies(…, userId?: string)` branching to a bare `eq(companyCatalog.id, targetId)`, with `mergeJobFitTags` and `mergeTechStackTags` identical. The burndown is adding fail-open predicates faster than it retires them, which is the recurrence the ADR exists to stop; a criterion nothing executes did not survive a single day. The baseline is therefore re-frozen at the landing commit and the delta recorded rather than absorbed — a guard pinned behind the commit it merges into fails on debt it did not create and can never land.
- **Local dev gets an owner rather than an absence.** The no-Supabase bypass will set a real `LOCAL_DEV_USER_ID` (defaulting to the sentinel `0017` already backfills to) instead of `null`, so single-user local dev becomes one tenant rather than no tenant — and local dev and E2E start exercising the isolation logic instead of bypassing it.
- **Two corrections to the audit.** The nullable-`user_id` tables where `isNull` would match real rows number **14 of 21**, not the 7 listed; and `catalog_diffs` is backfilled by `0017` STEP 1 but is the one table STEP 2 forgot to constrain, so new NULLs can still be written there. The latter needs its own card.
- **Decision only, plus the guard.** No service or middleware behaviour changes in this entry; the per-site burndown stays with WIC-1549, WIC-1554, WIC-1596 and WIC-1435.
- **AC-T0 is deliberately not widened to the owner-present case, and the guard measures AC-T0 only (2026-08-30, WIC-1756).** Ten service-layer predicates carry no owner term at all and so satisfy AC-T0 vacuously; re-derived independently at `614ad91`, all ten are already **not met** under AC-T2/AC-T3 with owning cards (WIC-1404, WIC-1406, WIC-1433, WIC-1434). Coverage is 10/10, so widening AC-T0 would restate what AC-T1..AC-T3 assert and split one requirement across two clauses whose enforcement points differ — AC-T0 at the entry point, AC-T1..AC-T3 at the predicate. PR #141 is the worked example: it needed a non-optional `applyChangeToDb(… userId: string)` **and**, separately, an owner term on six predicates. **The measured consequence is a false green:** changing only that signature on `614ad91` and touching no predicate takes `extraction.service.ts` from 1 finding to **0** — the file leaves the burndown table and the guard reports "1 fixed since baseline", exit 0 — while all six ownerless predicates remain byte-unchanged. A branchless violation matches neither `[SIG]` nor `[COND]`, so it enters neither numerator nor denominator. Any burndown quoted against these specs must therefore name the clause it measures; the predicate-level counterpart is the `[NOWNER]` check (WIC-1672).
- **Correction — the site count has now gone down, and "never once gone down" is withdrawn.** The guard scores **144** at `origin/main` `614ad91`, not 157: `resume-variant.service.ts` 17 → 10 and `interviewPrep.service.ts` 15 → 9, every other file unchanged. WIC-1601 scoped those two services' reads and replaced `bulletOwnerScope` with a generic `ownerScope(table, userId?)` that is **fail-closed** (`isNull`) and now serves 27 call sites. So the drop is part genuine posture improvement and part metric artifact of consolidating two helpers into one — the step-function-keyed-to-exports mechanism still holds, only the monotonicity is falsified. This also supersedes the "4 `isNull` branches in total" figure: the fail-closed shape is now the majority shape in those two files. The number counts owner-absent branches, which is all it ever literally claimed; it is not a safety score.
- **Fixed — the guard rejected its own recommended remediation (2026-08-30, WIC-1853).** Appending WIC-1601's verbatim fail-closed `ownerScope(table, userId?)` helper — the fix this ADR points people at — to any service lacking one **failed CI**, reproduced at head `00036f1`. Two independent causes, both in the guard: `[COND]` read only the ternary's `condition` and never `whenFalse`, so fail-**closed** `: isNull(t.userId)` and fail-**open** `: idTerm` produced an identical finding; and `[SIG]` flagged the `userId?` parameter the helper must have, since representing absence is its whole job. `[SIG]` headroom was **0 in all 14 baselined service files**, so there was nowhere the remediation could land for free — a guard that blocks the burndown it exists to drive. Both checks now exempt the fail-closed scope helper **by shape**, which also subsumes the `ALLOWLIST` entry for `personal-info.service.ts:34` (keyed by *line*, while the baseline is deliberately line-agnostic, so it would have stopped matching the moment the file shifted); that entry is deleted. Exempts exactly three helpers, 144 → 139, baseline file byte-unchanged so the `#209 → #220 → #227` merge order is undisturbed. **Narrowed beyond the reported patch:** testing only that the false branch *calls* `isNull` would exempt `userId ? eq(t.userId, userId) : isNull(t.archivedAt)`, which drops the owner term for an unrelated column and is fail-**open** — measured exit `0` under the callee-only form, `1` under the shipped one, which also requires the `isNull` **argument** to be an owner column. **The exemption is an AC-3-bounded concession:** `isNull` is zero-rows only on the 7 backfilled NOT NULL tables and matches real rows on the other 14, so on a nullable table it narrows rather than matching zero rows. The AST cannot see column nullability, so this is a syntactic proxy — justified because the admitted shape is always strictly safer than the defect it replaces (dropping the owner term selects every tenant; `isNull` selects at most the unowned one), but a green guard is not proof of AC-T0 on a nullable table.
- **Fixed — the regression report over-counted.** A tripped key printed *every* site sharing it, because the key is deliberately line-agnostic and cannot say which physical site is new; the repro's **2** new sites rendered as **13**. The message now separates them (`N NEW site(s) … across M candidate site(s)`, and `N of M in this key are new` per line). This is the third measured imprecision in this guard and they bracket it on both sides — it counts safe branches, it is blind to branchless violations, and it over-reported regressions.

### Fixed — The `/cover-letters/new` outline tests could not see a heading skip (2026-08-27)

`CoverLetterNew.test.tsx` shipped its own `getOutline` / `findOutlineSkips` / `describeOutline` rather than importing `src/test/headingOutline.ts`, which already exports all three — and which `CoverLetterPreview.test.tsx`, edited in the same PR, does import. The local copy resolved a heading's level as `Number(ariaLevel ?? tagLevel ?? NaN)`, reintroducing the exact `NaN` blinding the shared helper's own docstring is written to rule out (WIC-1571).

- **The failure mode was silence, not a wrong answer.** `findOutlineSkips` reports a problem by returning a *non-empty* array, and `NaN` compares false in both directions, so one uncomparable entry suppressed the check for the headings on **either** side of it. Measured on the merged tree with the file's own functions: `h1` → `div[role="heading"]` (no `aria-level`) → `h4` gives levels `[1, NaN, 4]` and **`[]` skips**; the shared helper gives `[1, 2, 4]` and reports the `h2 -> h4`. Same for `aria-level="abc"` on a real `<h2>`.
- **The two tests that exist to catch skips were the two that went blind.** Under that injected `h1 → ? → h4`, `starts the outline at h1 and skips no level on the way down` and `leaves no branch with a heading-level skip` both stayed **green**; after the swap both go **red**. The one test that did fail pre-swap failed for the wrong reason — it asserts the generator's first heading sits at level 2, and `NaN ≠ 2` is true by accident, since ARIA defines a bare `role="heading"` as level 2 exactly as the shared helper resolves it.
- **`role="heading"` is not a hypothetical walk-around.** It is what the surrounding tests already claim to defend against: the deleted docstring said an outline check means "a heading re-expressed as `<div role="heading" aria-level="1">` is still caught". It was not.
- **Whitespace collapsing moved into the shared helper rather than being dropped.** The local copy normalised internal runs of whitespace and the shared one only trimmed, and that difference is load-bearing for the `has no heading below the h1 repeat the route name` check, which compares heading text for *equality* — JSX wraps a long heading across source lines, so `textContent` carries the indentation and the comparison would silently never match. `headingOutline.ts` now collapses, which fixes the same latent gap for `KanbanBoard.test.tsx` and `CoverLetterPreview.test.tsx`.
- **Tests only; no source or behaviour change.** Full `packages/web` suite is 83 passed / 2 todo before and after, `tsc -b --force` clean, lint and `format:check` clean. The remaining API deltas are inert: `findOutlineSkips` returns objects where the local copy returned strings, but every call site asserts `.toEqual([])`, and `describeOutline` joins with ` -> ` instead of a newline, which only reaches failure messages.

### Fixed — The route audit is no longer blind to a commented-out entry point (2026-08-26)

The `route → link` direction added below credited a route from any inbound link site found in source — but `collectLinkSites` regexes over **raw** source, so a link that had been *commented out* still counted. Deleting the sole `<Link>` to a page turned the suite red; **commenting the same link out did not**, even though the user-visible outcome is identical (button gone, page unreachable). Commenting the entry point out is the single most common way a page actually becomes orphaned, so this was a fail-open on the exact class the audit exists to catch — JSX-commenting `CoverLetterDetail`'s `<Link to={\`/outreach/new…\`}>` would have silently reverted WIC-1530's fix and kept this guard green (WIC-1560).

- **`stripComments` runs before the link patterns**, dropping `{/* … */}` JSX comments, `/* … */` block comments, and `// …` line comments. The line-comment rule carries a `[^:'"\`\\]` guard so `https://` and `to="//x"` are not mistaken for comments.
- **Latent, not live.** Measured at introduction: **0 of 152** link sites sat inside a comment and all 28 non-`<Navigate>` routes keep a live credit, so the baseline is unchanged (`packages/web` suite `45 passed / 2 todo`). Eight of the 28 routes hang on exactly one credit, where a single commented-out line is the whole difference between guarded and unguarded.
- **Three negative controls, all now red.** Deleting the `/reports/needs-action` nav entry (was already red), **line-commenting** it (was green → now red), and **JSX-commenting** the sole `/outreach/new` `<Link>` (was green → now red, naming `/outreach/new`). A new in-file capability test (`does not credit a route from a commented-out link`) pins all three comment forms plus the `https://` guard, so this cannot regress.
- **Test-only.** No application code changes.

### Docs — ADR-009 proposes per-PR changelog fragments, because the insertion collision is a category and not an incident (2026-08-27)

Eleven board cards have been opened, worked and closed by performing the same manual re-merge of `CHANGELOG.md`. `docs/architecture/adr/ADR-009-changelog-fragments.md` (new, **Proposed**) prices that aggregate for the first time and proposes one file per change instead of one line per change.

- **The diagnosis is measured three times, not asserted, and it has been corrected twice.** At `main @13cb1e3`: 40 of 58 open PRs (69%) touch `CHANGELOG.md`, 6 `CONFLICTING`. Three hours later at `3396925`: 47 of 62 (76%), **13** conflicting. At `bf0b18e`: 48 of 67 (71%), **10** conflicting — **21% of the exposed population at both re-measurements, either side of a day's merges, which is what a steady state looks like rather than a spike seen twice.** The surviving claim is a *near*-necessary condition: **`CHANGELOG.md` is in the conflict set of 9 of 10 conflicting open PRs, and removing the shared line would take the count from 10 to 2.** Both stronger forms are now falsified and corrected in place — the *sole-cause* form ("the file set is exactly `CHANGELOG.md`") died at the second census, and the strict *necessary-condition* form ("no open PR here conflicts without it") dies at the third, on **PR #93**.
- **The counterexample is the most useful finding, and it argues _for_ the proposal.** #93 touches `CHANGELOG.md`, `main` has changed `CHANGELOG.md` since its merge base, and the two merge **cleanly**; its only real conflict is `NotFound.test.tsx`. It escaped because it inserts at **line 11** — the *pre-WIC-1543* top anchor — while everything landing on `main` now inserts at **line 23**, the below-top anchor WIC-1543 introduced (5 of the last 8 changelog commits on `main` hit line 23 exactly; this PR's own entry collided with `bf0b18e` there, which is what prompted the third census). **The one PR that did not collide is the one that ignored the convention.** WIC-1543 relocated the collision point rather than removing it, and made it just as deterministic for everyone who complies — so there is no third line that works better. What causes the collision is not *which* line is shared but *that* one is.
- PR #141 still settles the diagnosis: it touches two API service files that `main` also changed since the merge base, *those merge cleanly at all three censuses*, and it remains `CONFLICTING` on exactly `CHANGELOG.md` with no change to its code. This repository does not have a merge-conflict problem; it has a changelog problem that presents as one.
- **Both prior fixes were right, and neither removes the shared line.** WIC-1157's `merge=union` is invisible to GitHub, which computes mergeability without `.gitattributes`. WIC-1543's below-top anchor took the collision from *guaranteed by construction* to roughly 15% of the changelog-touching open-PR population standing conflicted at any instant — a real win, credited as such, and still a steady-state occupancy against ~11 changelog-touching merges per day.
- **The cheap alternative was checked first, and it is available.** A repository ruleset carrying a `merge_queue` rule was accepted on this public repo in a Free org (probe created `enforcement: disabled` against a non-existent branch, then deleted). It is rejected on **mechanism**: a merge queue serialises merges and resolves *semantic* conflicts, but a textually conflicting PR is ejected from the queue for the author to fix by hand. It relocates the same manual repair to a later moment. Auto-"Update branch" fails one step earlier for the same reason.
- **The cutover is the risky part, so the rollout is phased.** Removing the union driver on day one would make things worse — 40 open PRs still edit the file and would lose their local auto-resolution. Open PRs are grandfathered, the driver is removed only once none of them touches `CHANGELOG.md`, and the fragment-required CI gate is deliberately deferred rather than failing 58 open PRs at once.
- **Assembly opens a PR rather than pushing to `main`.** That keeps the change reviewable, needs no branch-protection bypass, and avoids the pending force-push governance question entirely. It is scheduled rather than deferred to release because this repo has zero tags and its `[Unreleased]` has never been cut — "assemble at release" would mean "never assemble".
- **A falsifiable success metric.** Zero changelog conflicts across the next 50 merges for PRs authored under the convention, plus a liveness check that no fragment sits in `changelog.d/` for more than 7 days — the failure mode the proposal itself introduces.
- **A fourth union failure is now documented: a weld propagates down a stack and multiplies at each stack merge.** Measured across the stacked PRs #209 → #220 → #227. Merge `bfd1dc0` welded a `### ` heading onto the previous entry's last bullet with **both parents provably clean** (`3d23b91` and `bf0b18e` each score zero) — the WIC-1567 class reproduced a second time, on a different branch, five days after #185 repaired it. It then survived **six** first-parent commits on #209's branch, four of them merges of `main`, and propagated into both stacked children. At `ee7c08f` the two contaminated parents carried the same original weld at drifted offsets (130 and 174); union did not recognise them as one seam and kept both, so **one defect became two** (75 and 184). The three modes in `CLAUDE.md` describe what the driver does to a file; this one describes what a stack does to a defect, and it makes the blast radius of a single bad resolution the whole dependent subtree. Repaired in `1305b2b` and `cc5386c`; all six open PRs on the stack now verify clean under the union simulation.
- Documentation only. No source, schema, wire, or test change. Adopting the ADR is a follow-up.

### Tests — The by-fit-tier empty state is guarded by a test instead of a comment (2026-08-26)

Nothing in `packages/web/src` or `packages/web/e2e` referenced `ReportsByFitTier` or any of its copy, so the WIC-1297 §4 ruling — the dependency notice must not enumerate the fit tiers, because the notice and the tier cards render in one `return` block and every label named in the notice is a label rendered twice on one page — was held up by a source comment alone. That ruling was already on the record when PR #111 rewrote the exact line it governs and grew the parenthetical from three labels to four; review caught it, CI had no opinion (WIC-1557).

- **`packages/web/src/pages/ReportsByFitTier.test.tsx` (new, 7 cases on `main`).** Mocks `useReportsByFitTier`, renders the empty state, and asserts every `FIT_TIER_LABELS` value occurs exactly once in the page text, plus that the notice block itself enumerates none of them.
- **The obvious version of this test passes on the broken page, so it is not the version here.** `expect(screen.getAllByText(label)).toHaveLength(1)` matches an element's whole normalised text, and the enumeration sat mid-sentence inside a `<p>`, so only the tier-card `<h3>` ever matched and the count was 1 in both directions — **measured: 6 passed against the page carrying the defect.** The assertion is an occurrence count over `container.textContent` instead.
- **The two assertions are not redundant, and that was measured too.** Deleting a tier card while *keeping* it named in the notice leaves every count at exactly one and still violates §4; only the notice-scoped assertion goes red on it.
- **Written over the label table, not over hardcoded copy**, so it keeps its meaning across the `FitTier` change in flight on PR #111 — it reads 4 labels on `main` and 6 on `main` + #111, green on both with no edit.
- **Guards on the guard.** A table-driven test can go vacuous without going red, so the table is separately pinned as non-empty with distinct labels (an emptied table would contribute zero cases), and no label may be a substring of another (which is the precondition the occurrence count depends on).
- **Negative controls, all four run.** Pre-fix page at `93e8847` on `main` + #111 → **5 failed / 4 passed**, red on exactly `strong_fit` / `moderate_fit` / `stretch` / `low_fit` and correctly green on `unscored` / `not_analyzed`, which were never enumerated. The same defect rebuilt on `main`'s own three-tier shape → **4 failed / 3 passed**. Enumeration-in / tier-card-out → **1 failed**, the notice assertion alone. Unmodified trees → 7 green on `main`, 9 green merged with #111.
- Test-only. No component, route, endpoint, schema, or wire value changes; `ReportsByFitTier.tsx` is untouched.

### Added — The route audit now runs in both directions, so an orphan page turns the suite red (2026-08-26)

`route-integrity.test.ts` asserted **link → route**: every internal path the UI can send a user to must be matched by a concrete route in `App.tsx`. It structurally could not assert the converse, **route → link** — a page that is built and mounted with no button anywhere pointing at it produces no link site, so there was nothing for the assertion to look at and orphans accumulated green. That class had produced four cards on this project (WIC-109 `CatalogPage`, WIC-110 the Diff Review modal, WIC-1428 catalog `pending_review`, WIC-1530 the outreach composer) and had **never once produced a guard**. This is the guard (WIC-1531).

- **The new assertion:** every route declared in `App.tsx` must have at least one inbound link site, **except** routes whose element is `<Navigate>`. Measured on this branch: 30 declared paths (`*` and `/*` excluded as before), 2 of them `<Navigate>`, and all **28** others carry at least one inbound site — min 1, mean 5.4, across 152 link sites in 132 source files. **No allowlist and no baseline**, in either direction of the exemption.
- **The `<Navigate>` exemption is principled, not a list.** A redirect-only route exists precisely to absorb traffic the app does *not* generate — bookmarks, stale external links, renamed paths — so requiring it to have an inbound link would be backwards. It is read out of the `<Route>`'s own `element` in the source, so rewriting `/dashboard` to render a page makes it stop being exempt automatically, with nothing here to maintain.
- **A link is credited to the route `matchRoutes` actually picks for it**, not to every route it could conceivably match — the same matcher and the same ranking the forward assertion already relies on, so the two directions cannot disagree about what a link means. `/resumes/exports` is credited to the static route, `/resumes/x/exports` to the parameterized one, and a link to a list page is *not* credited to the detail route underneath it.
- **`KNOWN_DEAD_LINKS` is not consulted and cannot weaken this.** An entry there either still matches no route, in which case it credits nothing, or the route has since been added, in which case the link is live and crediting it is correct.
- **Four negative controls measured**, plus two capability tests in the file. Reverting `CoverLetterDetail`'s entry point → red, naming `/outreach/new`. A synthetic unlinked `<Route>` added to `App.tsx` → red, naming `/nowhere`. The identical route with `element={<Navigate to="/" replace />}` → green. Breaking the element-extraction regex → **3** tests red, so the exemption cannot silently become universal. Against `origin/main` (both `45d70f6`, the sha the audit was written against, and `485c6f5`) the new assertion reports **exactly one** orphan, `/outreach/new`, and the other eight tests stay green — no false positives.
- **Deliberately not oversold, and the docstring says so.** It is static, so a target computed at run time (`navigate(returnTo)`) is invisible to it — the same limitation the forward direction already documents and accepts. And it proves a link exists *in source*, not that a user can ever reach it: a link inside a permanently false conditional, or on a page that is itself unreachable, satisfies it. This reduces the orphan class; it does not eliminate it.
- **Test-only.** No application code changes.

### Fixed — The outreach composer is reachable (2026-08-26)

US-4.4 shipped complete in UC-4 (`f70af52`, PR #12) and spent its entire life unreachable. `/outreach/new` was routed, `OutreachNew` and `OutreachComposer` were finished, and `POST /api/cover-letters/outreach` was live — but **nothing in the app linked to it**. Applying `route-integrity.test.ts`'s own five link patterns across every non-test source, `/outreach/new` had **0** inbound link sites against `origin/main`; the neighbouring `/cover-letters/new` had 2 and the app's 31 routes averaged 5. The only way in was to type the URL. Found by the Business Analyst's entry-point audit (WIC-1530).

- **The entry point is "Write Outreach Message" on `CoverLetterDetail`**, in the header actions beside Delete. That page is where the strongest content source already exists — a finished letter — and it is a `<Link>`, so the target is a real anchor and is visible to the static audit (measured: 0 → 1 inbound link site).
- **The composer had no way to receive a cover letter, which is the part that made this more than a missing button.** `OutreachNew` read only `applicationId` / `jobFitAnalysisId` / `company` / `jobTitle` from the query string, and `OutreachComposer` had no `coverLetterId` prop and never sent one. `generateOutreach` rejects with `JOB_CONTEXT_REQUIRED` unless one of `coverLetterId` / `jobFitAnalysisId` / `selectedStarEntryIds` reaches it — so a link added *without* this wiring would have 400'd on the first click of Generate. `coverLetterId` is now read from the query string, passed down, and sent. The field was already declared in `GenerateOutreachRequest`, accepted by the route's Zod schema, and implemented in the service; only the client path was missing.
- **`targetCompany` / `targetRole` are now carried on the web's cover-letter types.** The API has always mapped both unconditionally through `toDTO` and both are `NOT NULL` on `cover_letters`, but the web response type omitted them and `transformCoverLetter` dropped them — so the letter's own job context was unreadable client-side. They prefill the composer's Company and Role fields, which are what enable its Generate button.
- **`ReviseCoverLetterResponse` now references the generate response's shape instead of re-declaring it.** It was a hand-copied duplicate of the same server DTO, which is exactly how it came to be missing the two fields while its twin was corrected.
- **No API change.** The endpoint, its schema and its contract are untouched; this was a wiring defect.
- New `packages/web/src/pages/OutreachEntryPoint.test.tsx` drives the real pages through a router: click the link, land on the composer, assert the outgoing request carries `coverLetterId`. Five negative controls measured — removing the link (5 red), dropping `coverLetterId` from the handover (2 red), from the page's prop pass-through (1 red), from the composer's request (1 red), and dropping `company`/`jobTitle` (2 red). The static-detectability test carries a mutation control so it cannot pass vacuously.
- `route-integrity.test.ts` asserts link → route and structurally **cannot** catch an orphan route, which produces no link site to inspect. The converse audit is owned by a separate card; this one is the user-facing fix.

### Fixed — secret-scan now actually reads the `.env` family (2026-08-27)

The ADR-0001 Pillar 3 secret lint is a required step in `deploy.yml`, and its comment there says it scans "any tracked file". It did not. `SCANNABLE_EXT` lists `'.env'`, but `path.extname('.env')` is `''` and `path.extname('.env.production')` is `'.production'` — so that entry only ever matched a file literally named `foo.env`, and no real env-family file has ever reached the scanner.

- **A tracked `.env.production` carrying a live-shaped Anthropic key passed CI clean.** Reproduced end-to-end against the real command (`npm run scan:secrets`) on `775c288`: `.env.production`, `.env.staging`, `.envrc`, `.npmrc` and `packages/web/.env.production` each exit 0, and the scanned-file count stays at **333** — the file is never read, not merely un-flagged. `.gitignore` covers only `.env`, `.env.local` and `.env.*.local`, so every one of those is committable with a plain `git add`.
- **The discriminator is the dotfile-ness alone.** Byte-identical content in `foo.env` exits 1. Same extension-set entry, same patterns — only the leading dot differs.
- **Root cause is a coverage boundary, not a typo.** `test/secret-scan.test.ts` covers the pure core in `src/lib/` exhaustively; the file-*discovery* layer in `src/secret-scan.ts` had no tests at all. Deleting the new discovery test leaves the api suite green at 512 passing, which is what let a dead entry sit in `SCANNABLE_EXT` unnoticed.
- **Fixed by matching dotfiles on basename** (`.env*`, `.envrc`, `.npmrc`, `.netrc`, `.secrets`, `.pgpass`) alongside the existing extension rule, and by giving those files generic high-entropy scanning the way `.dev.vars` already gets it — an env file is a secret-bearing manifest by definition. The clean tree stays at 333 files and exit 0: no new false positives.
- **Two Supabase patterns added.** `sb_secret_…` is the WIC-902 leak shape and had no named pattern, so it rode through any source file (entropy is deliberately off outside config files). `sb_publishable_…` alongside it.
- **Pinned by `test/secret-scan-discovery.test.ts`.** Six mutations, each run against the whole api suite: reverting the `shouldScan` rule, reverting the entropy rule, dropping either Supabase pattern, and over-widening the basename rule to every dotfile all go red with correct attribution; removing the test file goes green.
- **Known residual, unchanged and deliberate:** a password inside a connection string (`postgres://user:pw@host/db`) is still not detected anywhere — the entropy heuristic needs a ≥32-char base64url run and a URL breaks on `:@/.`. Source files still get named patterns only, so an opaque token with no recognised prefix in a `.ts` is out of scope by design.



### Fixed — a Radix warning fired against `ApplicationForm`'s correct dialog markup (2026-08-30)

`ApplicationForm` put `aria-describedby="application-form-description"` on `Dialog.Content` and the matching `id` on `Dialog.Description`. That markup is correct — the dialog had a real accessible name, a real accessible description, and the attribute pointed at a node that existed — and Radix printed `` Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby={undefined}` `` on every mount regardless (WIC-1854).

- **Why it warned.** `DescriptionWarning` (`@radix-ui/react-dialog` 1.1.15, `dist/index.mjs:302-311`) never reads the `aria-describedby` attribute. It resolves Radix's _own_ generated `context.descriptionId` with `getElementById`, so overriding the id moves the node off that id and the lookup returns null. Only the description warning fired here; `Dialog.Title` did not override its id, so `TitleWarning` stayed quiet.
- **The fix is a deletion.** Both the `id` prop and the hand-written `aria-describedby` are gone, and Radix wires them. No accessibility behaviour changes — it was already correct — so this is console noise only. It is worth fixing because it is a **false positive on a real warning**: WIC-1851 existed because `CommandPalette` genuinely had no accessible name, and Radix had been saying so on every mount for as long as the component existed. A warning that also fires against correct code is one everybody learns to scroll past.
- **The name assertions could not have caught this.** Measured against the pre-fix component: `toHaveAccessibleName` and `toHaveAccessibleDescription` both **passed**, because the markup really was right. Only the `console.warn` guard and an assertion that `aria-describedby` resolves to Radix's _generated_ id failed. `ApplicationForm.test.tsx` is new and carries both, plus the positive control from `CommandPalette.test.tsx` that mounts a deliberately unnamed dialog and asserts it does warn — without which the guard passes against a broken spy or a Radix version that stopped warning.
- **The other dialogs were swept, not assumed.** All three `Dialog.Content` call sites in `packages/web/src` render a `Dialog.Title`, so there is no SC 4.1.2 defect of the WIC-1851 class outstanding; `ApplicationNew.tsx` was already clean and overrode no ids. `docs/design/ACCESSIBILITY.md` → "Dialogs" no longer names `ApplicationForm` as the standing offender and records why the console guard is not redundant with the name assertions.

### Fixed — every command-palette result announced its type emoji's name instead of its type (2026-08-30)

`CommandPalette` maps each result to a type emoji — 💼 application, 🏢 company, 🕐 recent search, ✨ suggested filter, 📄 fallback — and rendered it in a bare layout `<div>` at all four result-row call sites. With no `aria-hidden` the glyph joined the enclosing button's **accessible name**, so every row was announced as _"briefcase Senior Engineer, button"_. The palette is arrow-key navigated, so that was heard once per `ArrowDown`, not once per page (WIC-1850).

- **`aria-hidden` alone would have been a silent removal, not a fix.** Unlike the ✨ in the entry directly below, this glyph is the _only_ signal distinguishing one result type from another: the background colour is purely visual, and `subtitle` carries no type at all for `suggestion` and `recent` (neither has one) and nothing type-shaped for `application` (it is the company). Hiding it would have dropped a distinction sighted users keep, and nothing in the rendered output would have looked different. So the glyph is hidden **and** replaced with an `sr-only` type label: rows now announce `Application: Senior Engineer Acme Corp`, `Company: Acme Corp 2 applications`, `Recent search: remote backend`, `Suggested filter: Interviewing`.
- **Emitted from one shared `ResultTypeBadge`, not repeated four times.** The two halves are only correct together, and split across four call sites they can drift apart one site at a time. Hoisting it also covers the caller-supplied `result.icon` override, which all four `SUGGESTED_FILTERS` use — a fix applied only to the `switch` would have left exactly those four rows announcing their emoji.
- **Grouping rows under type headings was considered and rejected.** The un-searched view already groups under `Suggested Filters` / `Recent Searches` / `Recent Applications`, but the searched view — the branch where the types actually interleave — is one flat `Results` list with nothing to group by, so grouping would have fixed the branch that needed it least.
- **Tested at the exact accessible name, with a guard against deleting the glyph.** Six cases in `CommandPalette.test.tsx` (new, `npm run test`) cover all four types across both branches, assert each row's exact name, assert the decoration is still rendered and still `aria-hidden`, and sweep every rendered row for a glyph reaching any accessible name. All six fail before the change and pass after. Exactness is load-bearing twice over: a substring matcher passes with the emoji still in the name, and a name-only assertion passes for a "fix" that deleted the glyph and took the sighted user's signal with it.
- **The empty-state 🔍 is hidden too**, with no `sr-only` replacement — "No results found" directly beneath it already says the same thing, which is the decorative case.
- **Not fixed here:** the palette's `Dialog.Content` carries no `Dialog.Title`, so the dialog itself has no accessible name and Radix warns about it on every mount. Filed as WIC-1851 rather than widened into this change.
- The rule this case extends is now in `docs/design/ACCESSIBILITY.md` → "An Emoji Is Not the Sole Indicator Either", which states the decorative/load-bearing split, the verification both halves need, and why `jsx-a11y` cannot enforce it.

### Fixed — a decorative ✨ was read as part of every predefined filter shortcut's name (2026-08-30)

The four predefined shortcuts in `SavedFilterShortcuts` render a ✨ inside the button to mark them as built-in. It carried no `aria-hidden`, so it joined the button's **accessible name**: the row exposed `✨Needs Follow-up`, `✨Interviewing`, `✨Applied` and `✨Active Offers`, and a screen reader announced the emoji's Unicode name before every label — _"sparkles Interviewing, button"_ (WIC-1846).

- **The decoration was never available to the users it was announced to.** `isPredefined` is already conveyed non-visually by the absence of the delete control beside the button, so the emoji added a spoken word per shortcut and no information. `aria-hidden="true"` on the span leaves it rendered and removes it from the name; nothing about the visual row changes.
- **It had already bent the tests around itself, which is how it surfaced.** `FilterPanel.test.tsx` could not query these buttons by the names anyone calls them: an exact `{ name: 'Interviewing' }` found nothing, so the helper matched on a substring regex and carried a comment explaining why. `SavedFilterShortcuts.test.tsx` went further and needed a _function_ matcher for `Applied`, because a substring or end-anchored matcher also accepts `Recently Applied` — the label WIC-1775 had just removed for promising a window its filter never measured. Both workarounds are deleted here in favour of exact `FILTER_SHORTCUT_LABELS` names, which is the stricter assertion as well as the simpler one.
- **Tested against deleting the decoration, not just hiding it.** Five new cases in `SavedFilterShortcuts.test.tsx` (`npm run test`): four assert each label is the button's exact accessible name, and one asserts the marker is still in the DOM and still `aria-hidden`, so a "fix" that dropped the span fails. All five fail before the change and pass after.
- **Same defect class as the decorative ✓ in STAR fields, three entries above.** Purely decorative glyphs inside an interactive element need `aria-hidden`; the general rule is `docs/design/ACCESSIBILITY.md`. Not fixed here: `CommandPalette.tsx` renders result-type emoji (💼🏢🕐✨📄) inside four button/option rows with the same omission — filed separately rather than widened into this change.

### Fixed — The applications filter panel went stale on a shortcut and silently dropped filters (2026-08-27)

`/applications` had two writers for one piece of filter state. `ApplicationsList` owns `filters`; `SavedFilterShortcuts` writes it through `onApplyFilter`, and `FilterPanel` writes it through `onFilterChange`. `FilterPanel` also copied the `activeFilters` prop into four `useState`s, whose initialisers run on first mount only — so once the panel was open, every shortcut write was invisible to it (WIC-1612).

- **The worst symptom was silent data loss, not a stale display.** With the panel open and a shortcut applied, ticking one more status spread the panel's own stale `[]`: one click added `offer` and discarded `interview` and `phone_screen`, filters the user never touched. No error, no undo — the board just changed underneath them.
- **The panel also denied that any filter existed.** `hasActiveFilters` was computed from the same stale copies, so the chip row and **Clear All** — the only control that can undo a shortcut — never rendered over a list that really was filtered. `SavedFilterShortcuts` computes the same predicate from the fresh prop, so it offered "+ Save Current" at the exact moment the panel below it showed nothing active.
- **`FilterPanel` now holds no state at all.** All four `useState`s are deleted and derived from the prop; `onFilterChange` is the only writer. The handlers needed no change — they already spread `activeFilters` rather than local state — so this deletes state rather than adding a sync effect that could itself fall behind.
- **The debounce moved to the page rather than staying as a resync.** `search` was the one field with an honest reason to be local: `useDebounce` has to hold uncommitted keystrokes. The obvious remedy — a `useEffect` resync on `activeFilters.search` — is rejected by this repo's own `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` lint rule, so the hook was lifted to `packages/web/src/hooks/useDebounce.ts` and now sits in `ApplicationsList` between the committed filters and the API. The box stays responsive, the network still gets one request per settled search rather than one per character, and the panel is left fully controlled.
- **Tested, where there was no test at all.** `FilterPanel.tsx`, `SavedFilterShortcuts.tsx` and `ApplicationsList.tsx` had zero test cover. New `components/FilterPanel.test.tsx` (13 cases) drives the **real composition** — the actual page over the actual shortcuts bar and panel — because that is the only place the defect exists; a hand-built stand-in host proves only that the component obeys the stand-in. Page state is read back off the request the page issues, i.e. observed entirely outside `FilterPanel`, so a panel that merely tells itself a consistent story cannot satisfy it. Pre-fix the file was **10 failed / 3 passed**, and none of those three greens is defect cover: one is a regression pin on handlers that were already correct pre-fix (they always spread `activeFilters` rather than local state), and the other two cover behaviour the debounce move had to _preserve_, so they are green on both trees by design. All three are labelled as such in the file, so the discrimination the suite actually has is not overstated.
- **Known residual, measured on both trees and left deliberately.** With a search already _settled_, applying a shortcut fires one extra request carrying both — `?status=interview,phone_screen&search=goo` — for up to 300ms, because `debouncedSearch` lags the `filters.search` that the shortcut clears instantly. It then self-corrects to `?status=interview,phone_screen`, and no state is damaged, so it is well inside the trade the debounce move makes; it is a transient echo of the same panel-disagrees-with-the-list family this entry is about, and it is **introduced** by that move rather than inherited — the pre-fix tree fires no such request. What the pre-fix tree did instead was the harmful version, and that one is fixed: characters typed in the 300ms _before_ a shortcut click used to survive it, leaving the box reading `goo` and the committed request `?status=interview,phone_screen&search=goo`. On this tree the box clears with the rest of the filters and no request ever carries the abandoned search.
- **Second instance of a class with one more member.** `OutreachComposer.tsx` (5 sites) has the same shape and is owned by WIC-1583; a lint rule covering all nine sites is filed separately, because shipping it here would knowingly red CI until that card lands.

### Fixed — The organic-traffic watcher's two PostHog fetches share one fault tuple, so exit `10` survives a network fault (2026-08-29)

The entry below fixed the except tuple in `organic_watch.py`'s `prod_db_health()`. The watcher's two `run()` call sites had the same gap and were left out of that PR's scope: the candidate-detail fetch caught only `(URLError, HTTPError, RuntimeError, KeyError)`, through which **12 of 16 measured fault classes escaped** (WIC-1680).

- **Weaker consequence than the entry below, deliberately stated as such.** That handler runs _after_ the `CANDIDATE ORGANIC TRAFFIC` headline prints and _before_ `return 10`, so an escape never hid a candidate from a human reading stdout. It lost the detail rows (the adjudication evidence), the probe-registration guidance, and turned exit `10` — which a heartbeat branches on — into a traceback exit `1`. Same inversion as WIC-1636, one branch later. Nothing in the repo consumes exit `10` today, which is why this followed rather than blocked PR #207.
- **`OSError` is load-bearing, and the original write-up missed it.** The suggested fix was `http.client.HTTPException` + `ValueError`. Measured, that closes only 8 of the 12: `ssl.SSLError`, `socket.gaierror`, `ConnectionResetError` and `TimeoutError` are `OSError` subclasses reachable through neither, and would have kept escaping a fix everyone believed was complete. The tuple now matches the one `prod_db_health()` already carries.
- **One named `QUERY_FAULTS` constant, used by both call sites.** The two tuples drifting apart _is_ the defect; a shared constant is what stops it recurring. The aggregate site adds `IndexError` locally, the one class it needs and the candidate site cannot raise. `urllib.error.HTTPError` is dropped as redundant — it subclasses `URLError`, and naming it only made the tuple look exhaustive when it was not.
- **Resource exhaustion still escapes, and a negative control pins that.** `MemoryError` must not be caught; a suite asserting only "nothing escapes" would pass while the tuple quietly became `except Exception`. Noted honestly: `RecursionError` _is_ caught, because it subclasses the `RuntimeError` that `run()` itself raises on a missing API key — incidental and not removable without a re-raise, not a claim that recursion faults are handled.
- **The tests assert the exit code, not the tuple.** `--selftest` drives every fault through real `main()` control flow with `urlopen`'s callers stubbed, because asserting `isinstance(exc, QUERY_FAULTS)` would pass against whatever tuple the handler happened to name — including the broken one. Both legs are covered: candidate detail must still return `10`, aggregate must return `1` having printed `CHECK FAILED` rather than dying in a traceback (both exit `1`, so only driving `main()` tells them apart). The suite goes 23 → 58 cases; against the pre-fix tuple it fails 24, and against the incomplete suggested fix it fails 8.
- **Watcher behaviour is otherwise unchanged.** No query, predicate, verdict, or exit-code semantics were touched.




### Fixed — `reviseCoverLetter` no longer persists STAR entry ids it could not resolve

`POST /cover-letters/:id/revise` fetched the selected STAR entries and then wrote the *caller's* id
list into `selected_star_entry_ids` regardless of what that fetch returned, so an id resolving to no
row was still stored. `generateCoverLetter` has always rejected that input with `STAR_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND`
(404); the revise path now does the same, and throws before the model call rather than after it.

- **The check covers the caller-supplied list only, not the stored fallback.** When the request omits
  `selectedStarEntryIds` the service falls back to the ids already on the row, and validating *that*
  would make a letter which already stores an unresolvable id impossible to revise ever again —
  including by an instructions-only edit that never mentions STAR entries. Those rows exist precisely
  because this write path minted them, so the guard is scoped to close the write vector without
  stranding what it already wrote. A test pins the narrowing: widening the guard to the fallback list
  turns it red.
- **An explicit empty list still clears the row.** `[]` is a request, not an omission, and is
  distinguished from the fallback case.
- **This composes with the owner-scoping fix on PR #159 (WIC-1437) and does not depend on it.** Here
  "did not resolve" means "does not exist", because the catalog read on `main` carries no owner term.
  Once #159 adds one, another user's id also stops resolving and this same guard rejects it with no
  further change — which is why the check is computed from the rows the fetch returned rather than
  from an existence query of its own.

### Fixed — Route 2 (console JSON import) can now emit a synthetic-filtered pack, reusing Route 1's rewriter (2026-08-30)

`make_console_pack.py` built `dashboard-templates.json` straight from the unfiltered payloads, and the runbook stated Route 2 "carries NO synthetic exclusion, and that is deliberate" — so an operator who imported the committed JSON got 17 tiles counting probe residue as product usage.
